name: Educational Email 8
text:
Hi {first_name},

Since returning home from Kuwait last week, the topic of travel and jet lag has been at the forefront of my mind.  









If you’ve done some traveling, you can relate when I say, “jet lag is seriously no fun.” 




What are some common symptoms of jet lag?




Disturbed sleep
Daytime fatigue
Difficulty concentrating
Stomach problems
Mood changes




Any time we travel across time zones, we experience some disruption in our body’s natural 24 hours circadian rhythm cycle and internal processes. Often times it can be quite tough and a longer process than we’d hope to recover from these challenges.










I’ve created a series of tips that you can use the next time you travel to help mitigate this:




Avoid airplane food


Explore fasting during a portion of your travel day
a) If you are accustomed to fasting, and typically have stable blood sugar levels, explore fasting on the flight or travel day. When you arrive at your destination, try to get on the new time zone’s schedule of eating for your next meal. For example, if you land at 10 pm, skip dinner and start your meals again with breakfast the following day. 


Perform morning cardio 
a) If there’s a cardio machine in your hotel, or the weather is nice (best option), go for a 15-20 jog. This will help raise your cortisol levels, so it's more in sync with the rhythm of new time zone.


Take 3 minute+ cold showers
a) Not only will this wake you up ; ) but it can help to balance your hormonal system.


Peppermint oil in the morning
a) An uplifting and energizing essential oil you can place behind your neck and breathe in deeply for five breaths (I found out about Essential Oil Wizardry from the Living 4D Podcast with Paul Chek and Dr. Nick Berry and I am loving it).


Lavender oil in the evening
a) Place behind your neck, and on the soles of your feet


Camomile tea before bed
a) Settles the stomach and is excellent for calming the body 


Sauna the day you arrive
a) If you can locate a sauna, aim to get a good 20-30 minute sweat in and enjoy the relaxation, detoxification, and quiet space to enjoy meditation or a gentle stretching routine.


Perform a 5-10 minute morning or evening meditation outside barefoot  
a) This will help ground and connect you to the new environment as you relax your mind from the busy travel day.


Stay hydrated
a) Aim to drink ½ your body weight in ounces of water at a minimum, and remember to drink on the plane.


Schedule a float (sensory deprivation tank) session when you arrive home
a) One of the very best tools for supporting deep rest and recovery following travel is a float. Schedule a 60-minute session, and when you do, please let me know afterward how it went!



        Post-flight float at Balance Float in Redwood City, CA







Bonus Tip - there has been one supplement that was recently recommended to me by a close friend since returning home from Kuwait. Being very selective when it comes to supplements, I am quite happy with how it's been helping me recover from jet lag this past week. You can find it easily on Amazon -  H2 Elite. The company that makes it is Quicksilver Scientific. 




I hope you enjoyed these tips and give a few a try the next time you travel. Feel free to share with a friend or family member whom could benefit : )




Wishing you a great day,

Mike





Reference: https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/jet-lag/symptoms-causes/syc-20374027

name: Waitlist Update
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I hope this message finds you well. I'm reaching out today to share some exciting updates about the upcoming 30-Day Bulgarian Bag Complete Online Program - Athleticism for Life.

 

Let me start by expressing my appreciation for being a forward-thinker who embraces unconventional approaches.

 

About a decade ago, I came across a YouTube video featuring Ivan Ivanov using the Bag, and I immediately recognized its unique qualities. The movement skills, creativity, and athleticism (especially with rotational movements) were exactly what I had been looking for.

 

However, finding comprehensive education on the subject proved to be a challenge at the time.

 

To address this gap, I made multiple trips to Suples HQ in Boise, Idaho, over the years and took certifications to learn directly from the creator.

 

Since then, I've been fortunate to share the Bulgarian Bag, Ivan's system, and my unique approach with people worldwide.

 

Finally, the time has come to introduce a program for you! This marks the first Suples Approved Program, offering you the opportunity to learn the movements and techniques I've learned from Ivan, in addition to my own perspective and holistic training method.

 

This program goes beyond just Bulgarian Bag training. When pre-orders open this Friday, you'll see exactly what I mean.

 

As incredible as the Bulgarian Bag is, or even the Kettlebell, there are many other aspects of training that are crucial for harnessing athleticism throughout life.

And what I love is sharing complete training methods and systems that deliver lasting results.

 

I'm thrilled and honored for you to elevate your performance, body, and overall training to new levels.

 

Stay tuned for more updates in the coming days. Here's what you can expect:

 

Pre-Orders: Available for 4 days starting this Friday (big discounted pricing).
Program Access: January 1st.

In the meantime, if you have any questions or want to order a bag to get ready, use code TEAMSALEMI10 on my site for a 10% discount (valid in the US). 

 

Get ready to capture your pre-order opportunity this Friday!

Best, Mike

name: Holiday Message
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

As we embrace both the joy and potential challenges that the holiday season brings, I want to take a moment to express my gratitude for your presence in my community.

 

This time of year has especially brought a deep sense of connection as I serve my community. Your trust and commitment to this journey has made it even more special.

 

As we navigate through the holidays, I encourage all of us to keep our hearts open, even when faced with challenges that may leave us wanting to "collapse", hide, or run metaphorically.

 

Staying heart opened could look like approaching situations with greater understanding before passing judgment, choosing compassion, or simply establishing clear boundaries. Recognizing that, at times, setting boundaries is one of the most loving things we can do for ourselves and others.

 

Wishing you the very best today, and I hope you find moments to keep your heart open.

 

Warm regards,

Mike

 

P.S. Do stay tuned for tomorrow's special pre-order offer on the Bulgarian Bag program and exclusive 50% discounts on all my programs : ) 🎁

name: Educational Email 8 clone
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

By looking at these photos, it would be hard to tell just what this group had endured a few hours earlier.⁠

 








I’m a big proponent that we all need to test ourselves in life.⁠

 

Sometimes these tests are brought to our doorstep without notice, and other times we seek them out.⁠

 

In either situation, we have a choice with how we will respond. Will we rise, or will we crumble?⁠

 

The result we experience afterward is less important. What is critical, however, is how we stand up and continue moving forward in the process.⁠

 

This group of trainers and coaches at Crossfit Foggy Bottom in Washington, DC did just that.⁠

 

Their smiles speak of:⁠

 

⁠- Joy⁠

- Respect for self⁠

- Brotherhood ⁠

- Sisterhood⁠

- Teamwork⁠

- Hard work⁠

- Commitment ⁠

 

⁠No matter the challenge, if you can remember to smile even for a moment, I guarantee that a seemingly insurmountable struggle will begin to soften.⁠


 

And when you get through it, you will respect yourself more in the end.⁠

 

You will have just endured your test, your rite of passage, and HELL YES to that!⁠

 

So, where are you rising up in your life right now?⁠

 

Where are you falling short?⁠

 

Are you being unreasonable with your goals, or playing it small because that is the safe route?⁠

 

⁠I invite you to consider these questions and write them down. The act of writing will make the ideas floating around in your head into more real. 




I encourage you to be unreasonable with your goals. Go for what you want, and even if you fall short, the process is truly the gift waiting for you.⁠

 

⁠Just remember these two things: ⁠

1. Bringing a smile to a difficult situation can change instantly how you feel and move through it.⁠

2. It’s OK to ask for help when you need it.⁠

 

 

 

Lastly, big respect for this group of warriors this weekend. Each of you inspired me in some way and I am grateful you chose me as your coach. Thank you!⁠

 

Wishing you a great day!
Mike Salemi
 

P.S.

{first_name}, I’m stoked to share that since the announcement of the Kettlebell Lifestyle Transformation Program, there’s been a huge positive response from people excited to get their hands on this puppy! To further reward all those who jump on board for the beta-release, I’m going to include more resources to elevate your health and performance even more. Tomorrow’s email will touch on the massive gift I have planned for the Kettlebell Lifestyle family.


Learn More about Kettlebell Lifestyle™

You will have just endured your test, your rite of passage, and HELL YES to that!⁠




So, where are you rising up in your life right now?⁠




Where are you falling short?⁠




Are you being unreasonable with your goals, or playing it small because that is the safe route?⁠




⁠I invite you to consider these questions and write them down. The act of writing will make the ideas floating around in your head into more real. 




I encourage you to be unreasonable with your goals. Go for what you want, and even if you fall short, the process is truly the gift waiting for you.⁠




⁠Just remember these two things: ⁠

1. Bringing a smile to a difficult situation can change instantly how you feel and move through it.⁠

2. It’s OK to ask for help when you need it.⁠










Lastly, big respect for this group of warriors this weekend. Each of you inspired me in some way and I am grateful you chose me as your coach. Thank you!⁠




Wishing you a great day!
Mike Salemi

name: Sacred Hunting
text:
Hi {first_name},




I am honored to extend a personal invitation to a special upcoming event – our Sacred Hunting Experience in the heart of Texas from February 29th to March 3rd.




Sacred Rituals:


This is not just a hunting trip; it is a carefully crafted series of sacred rituals meant to guide you on a profound journey of self-discovery and transformation. Held in the landscape of Texas, this experience is an opportunity to reconnect with your primal essence and tap into the wisdom of the natural world. One of these rituals is a private Sweat Lodge, and I will discuss a few of the others below.




Men's Only Container:


In the spirit of fostering authentic connections and brotherhood, our Sacred Hunting Experience is a men's only event. This intentional container creates a space where participants can freely express themselves, forge deep connections, and embark on a shared journey of growth.




Sacred Plant Medicine:


Part of this approach is the mindful use of sacred plant medicine, artfully integrated to enhance the spiritual and transformative aspects of the journey. This practice serves as a gateway to self-awareness, offering a unique opportunity for personal reflection and communion with the natural world. Your guide for this will be Mansal Denton.




Beyond the Hunt


While hunting is a pivotal part of the experience, our journey encompasses much more. From mindfulness practices to group discussions and guided reflections, we offer a holistic exploration of your identity, purpose, and potential.




Spot and Stalk Hunting


The style of hunting on this trip employs the "spot and stalk" method—a practice that combines observation and patience to connect with the wild. This method is not only in alignment with ethical hunting principles but also provides a beginner-friendly introduction to the art of hunting. We will be on the move, following the animals as we hunt.




Ideal for Beginners


Whether you're a seasoned hunter or a complete novice, our experience is tailored to meet you where you are. Expert guides, including Mansal Denton, Mike Bledsoe, and others, will provide comprehensive support and guidance, ensuring that every participant feels empowered and comfortable throughout the trip. Also, note that this is a rifle hunt.




Bonuses


To enhance your preparation for this unique experience, everyone attending will receive complimentary access to my new Bulgarian Bag online program. This program is designed to physically prepare you for the challenges of the hunt, promoting strength, agility, and resilience.




In addition to the physical preparation, I am stoked to announce that I will be guiding breathwork at various points throughout the trip. This will be a powerful complement to our experience together.




Save the Date and Hop on a Call with Mansal Today


Mark your calendar for February 29th to March 3rd. There is preparation both mentally, physically, and logistically for this hunting trip. If you are indeed interested, apply ASAP to get all the details and hop on a call with Mansal.




Click here to visit Sacred Hunting and apply today for our Feb 29-Mar 3rd experience.




Hope to have you join in this special experience,


Mike

name: A4L Phase 2 Unlocked
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I hope you had an incredible weekend! I just returned from two days of badass training at Suples HQ in Boise, Idaho, and it was a phenomenal experience. I am stoked to share that I am now one of the very few US coaches authorized to teach both Level I and Level II Certification (1:1 and in groups)! It has been a long time coming, and I feel honored to be able to share this knowledge with you in various capacities.

 

Regarding A4L - Phase II is now unlocked! You can explore new workouts and discover additional bonus materials, including extra workouts and podcasts, in the "What's Next" section.

 

Furthermore, I want to let you know that in the coming weeks, I will be making a few small improvements to your program. With myself and my family being sick for over a week before the New Year, and my videographer getting sick as well, we managed to pull off getting the program to you just in time for January 1st.

 

Stay tuned for these enhancements that aim to make your experience even better. For example, the Workout Library will soon include an archive of workouts without the warm-up and cool-down if you prefer to access just those. Additionally, I've already added a shorter warm-up in the Warm-Up drop-down (in the Preparation & Recovery Tab), along with a few other small improvements.

 

You were among the very first people to receive this program, which tells me that you are genuinely interested in learning the Bulgarian Bag, elevating your movement, and learning from or supporting me in the process.

 

In doing so, you are also supporting my family and giving me an opportunity to make a larger impact in the world, for which I feel blessed and grateful. Thanks for being on this path with me, and for being simply...AWESOME : )

 

All the best, 

Mike

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

We're down to our last spot for the upcoming Sacred Hunting Experience in Texas at the end of February, and if you've been curious about this unique opportunity, here's the lowdown:

 

What's in it for you?

 

Building Confidence: Hunt your own food and increase your skillset as a provider.
Nature Connection: Strengthen your bond with the great outdoors and feel a connection to nature free from distractions
Purpose & Brotherhood: Uncover a lasting sense of purpose and primal brotherhood.

Hear from Past Attendees:

 

"It's a powerful experience to connect with the land... spiritually, I had a really big breakthrough just being in that container..."

- Brandon E

 

"Some of the most important men's work... world's work, really... this is something that felt really important for me to connect with my primal roots..."

- Jordan B

 

"Seeing her approach death was an emotional experience...."

- Tim K

 

What is Sacred Hunting?

More than just a hunt, it's a transformation experience focusing on self-growth and an eco-spiritual connection to nature. This includes a Sacred Ceremony with Power Plants, where you'll participate in a meticulously guided ceremony that's been used for healing, expansion, and more for thousands of years.

 

You'll also rediscover ancient practices and intentions to reclaim gratitude and deep presence. This experience involves ethical hunting with a tribe of men, forging bonds around the fire, and much more.

 

We've got only ONE spot left for our exclusive Feb. 29-Mar 3d hunt in Texas. If you feel that inner calling to explore further and join us, hit reply, and I'll be stoked to provide more details - simply reply to this email for more details. 

 

Best Regards,

name: Educational Email 11
text:
“Ouch!” 

 

Have you ever made this sound when cleaning a kettlebell?

 

{first_name}, you know, when the kettlebell flips over your arm and painfully bangs onto your wrist?

 

If not, can you think of someone you know who is going through this challenge right now? 

 

I was thinking today, and I'm not sure if I’ve ever met a person who didn’t have to go through this learning process, at least for a brief time.

 

While there are coaches out there who may tell you to "suck it up", I’m here to share that there are things you can do to minimize this issue and improve faster. 

 

Now, in terms of wearing supportive gear, I do support the use of wrist bands in certain times, especially if you’re completely new to clean training (to soften the landing). However, if it becomes a crutch for continuing with a faulty movement pattern, that’s when I’m not super cool with it.

 

You see, I want your technique to be the saving grace of your lifting, and not have you over-rely on supportive gear. 

 

 

That's because the issues you experience now on the clean, will also impact all variations of this movement, as well as others that build upon it. For example, the kettlebell snatch, or any sequence of exercises that pick-up from when you finish the clean (the rack position), such as:

 

Clean and Press
Clean and Jerk
Clean and Squat
Clean > Press > Windmill Combo

 

One thing I’ve learned over the years is that many times the same drill to fix a specific issue does not always work. 

 

That said, this morning I woke up feeling inspired after having recently coached a lifter through this very problem while performing an advanced progression of the exercise. 

 

So, I went down into my garage to record two drills that you can utilize right now to help remedy this. 

 

The first drill is called an Assisted Clean, and the second is called a Swing Low Pull.

 

This video is now up on my IGTV, click here to view it.

 

You’ll be learning the Swing Low Pull within a 3 movement sequence. The purpose of this is to help you transfer key elements from your swing into your clean, while keeping the kettlebell close to the body. 

 

By practicing these drills, the kettlebell will be traveling around your arm and land smoothly and (quietly ; ) onto your forearm.

 

I hope you enjoy this video and implement these drills right away!

 

Wishing you all the best,

 

Mike


 

P.S.

You’re probably aware that high-performance training of any type involves more than what you do in the gym. In fact, MUCH more. That’s why in the upcoming Kettlebell Lifestyle program you will be supported by more than 8 health and wellness experts that know exactly how to facilitate lasting change at the deepest level. 

 

Tomorrow you’ll get an inside sneak peek at some of these special people here to help ensure your success...you may even recognize a few of them 

; ) Stay tuned, great stuff is coming!

name: Men's Reset Retreat 1: Needs
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Let's cut right to the chase.

 

The belief that "my needs don’t matter" as a man is utter nonsense.

 

It's a silent force that often dictates our actions, creeping into our minds and convincing us that putting everyone else's needs before our own is the noble thing to do.

 

But here's the truth: neglecting our own needs eventually leads to dissatisfaction, burnout, and a life that lacks fulfillment.

 

Think about it - when was the last time you truly prioritized yourself? When did you last acknowledge your desires and take meaningful steps to fulfill them?

 

For many of us, the answer isn't as clear as it should be.

 

We push aside our passions, neglect our physical health, and bury our deepest desires under layers of responsibilities and expectations.

 

And the result? Relationships suffer, creativity stagnates, and we find ourselves trapped in a cycle of mediocrity.

 

But here's the kicker - you are solely responsible for your own happiness and well-being. No one else can fulfill your needs but you.

 

It's time for a change. It's time for a total body RESET.

A chance to break free from the confines of routine and rediscover what it means to truly live.

 

If you're ready to take that first step, ask yourself these three questions:

What words have you left unsaid that are fueling resentment within yourself or towards others?
What essential needs are you neglecting?
What's holding you back from taking that crucial first step towards meeting your needs?

Recognizing and meeting our needs isn't just an act of self-care - it's a catalyst for personal growth and stronger, more fulfilling relationships.

 

That's why I'm stoked to invite you to the Men of Movement Retreat on May 17-19th.

 

This retreat is all about reclaiming your vitality, reigniting your passions, and connecting with like-minded men who are on a similar journey.

 

We've curated an experience unlike any other, with personalized sessions led by experts in bodywork, Chinese medicine, functional medicine, myself, and more.

 

You'll receive tailored training programs, rising and evening mini-practices/rituals, learn invaluable techniques for longevity, and have the opportunity to address any injuries or restrictions holding you back.

 

But most importantly, you'll be part of a supportive community dedicated to helping you thrive.

 

If you've been running yourself into the ground or simply crave a reset to realign with your true purpose, this retreat is for you.

 

Join us in the breathtaking setting of Mount Shasta, CA, and go on a journey of renewal and transformation.

 

Space is limited, so if you're even remotely interested, don't hesitate to reach out.

 

Simply book a call on my calendar by clicking here, or respond to this email with "I'm interested," and I'll provide you with more details.

 

Here's to prioritizing your needs, reclaiming your vitality, and living a life filled with purpose and joy.

 

With love and respect,

Mike

 

P.S. 

I just arrived home yesterday from an incredible Sacred Hunting Experience in Texas. I was so moved by this one, and the men who attended. In the coming weeks I'll share these reflections in an email and likely a podcast, so please stay tuned.

name: Men's Reset Retreat
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I returned home late Monday night after spending six days in the California desert (Death Valley area), and man, what a game-changer.

 

Surrounded by 70 men all willing to dive deep, doing my own personal work has left me still beyond capacity with soul nourishment.

 

 

Being out in that quiet desert space, everything intensified—my thoughts, emotions, sensations, reflections—all of it.

 

I had never experienced the desert before and being with no cell or wifi, I got to feel part of myself that had been dormant. 

 

I'll be dropping a podcast soon to share some of my major takeaways and what went down, but one thing in particular hit me hard was the struggle many of us men face..

 

Balancing providing for family while striving to be our best selves in all aspects of life, all while maintaining the life force it takes to do it well—it's a constant battle for many of us.

 

As was discussed at the event with leader and head, John Wineland, we have two components to take into account as we self assess as men - our intent and our energy.

 

Intent keeps us grounded, like an anchor, focused, and on a trajectory.

 

And energy is what flows in and through us as we walk the path.

 

Too many times to count, many of us men may have shown up in life with strong intentions, but weak energy.

 

And that lack has a significant impact.

 

The quality of change we can create in life, and more importantly, sustain that level of change, largely depends on the energy, and flow of it, we have on board.

 

But too often, as men, we're running on empty.

 

Does that resonate?

 

It's sometimes a harsh reality we don't want to confront, but it's often the truth.

 

If we don't come to terms with it, who suffers?

 

Everyone in our life.

 

That's why I'm evolving a few things. 

 

One is how I plan  to run the upcoming Men of Movement Retreat to target a different issue....

 

This experience is called - RESET.

 

By getting out in nature, while eating top-quality food, we'll be addressing key things such as:

Sleep challenges
Nutritional deficits
Limiting beliefs
Physical pain
Movement restrictions
Energy slumps
A craving for brotherhood
And more

All of these will affect the way we show up in the world.

 

Because let's face it, our energy levels affect everything.

 

This experience is going to be smaller, intimate, and personalized AF.

 

Each guy will get the full treatment—mind, body, and spirit reset with 1:1 sessions from myself and each facilitator present. 

 

Click this link to learn more details regarding this Men of Movement RESET Retreat.

 

Also, in this link is an effective six-minute breathwork routine you can use to cleanse and clear your body/mind whenever you feel stagnant.

 

Let's do this!

-Mike

 

P.S.

My NEW free online men's community just launched and in just one day we have 25 men in the group! You will also find out info on how to sign up all on the same link I mentioned above, just scroll down under the event information area.

name: Educational Email 12
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

What’s the biggest reason why most people don’t experience the results they expect from their training?

 

Is it because they don’t have a solid plan?

 

Is it because they don't have the finances to hire a skilled coach?

 

Are they lacking motivation or a clear reason for why they’re training in the first place?

 

Well, I’d say all of the above and then some. 

 

Remember, we are all HUMAN and not robots.

 

Even with a well thought out plan, sometimes life gets in the way and throws us curve balls. 

 

When I was first laying out the structure for the Kettlebell Lifestyle Program, the original idea was to create an 8-week phased workout program. This would be complete with detailed instruction for beginners and intermediate folks interested in moving more safely with kettlebells, improving skill level, and elevating fitness. 

 

However, after the weeks went on and the meat of the program started coming together, I was still not happy.

 

I felt that something was missing, something essential.

 

Then it hit me, I absolutely had to include a lifestyle component to the program - especially because I know at least part of your goals has to do with longevity and wellness if you are receiving these emails. 

 

The truth is that Kettlebell training, and any form of physical exercise, HAS to be about more than training. This is because life is about more than the time you spend moving heavy objects in the gym, no matter how rad said objects might be ; ) #truth

 

In Kettlebell Lifestyle, you will receive modification suggestions to your program, as well as emails and videos that can help you foster high performance for decades to come. 

 

To support you at the deepest level, I contacted a handful of brilliant minds in the health, wellness, and performance space to ask if they'd be willing to contribute to your success...and they were all STOKED to take a part :)

 

Here are just 5 of them, maybe you can recognize a few? ; ).

 

 

Paul Chek

Holistic Health Practitioner & Expert

www.chekinstitute.com

 

 

Mark England 

TEDx Speaker, Public Speaking Coach,  and Co-founder of Enlifted & Procabulary 

https://procabulary.org

 

 

Jator Pierre

Health and Wellness Expert, Board Certified Health and Wellness Coach, CHEK Institute Faculty

www.wehlc.com

 

 

Danielle Cook Kawash

Registered Dietician, Board Certified Health and Wellness Coach 

https://danielleckawashrd.com

 

Warren Williams

Health and Wellness Expert, CHEK Institute Faculty

name: Dads To Be
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In over 15 years of competing as an elite athlete, what has become crystal clear to me is that the real event I was training for was...fatherhood.

 

Being a new dad has stretched me in ways I never thought possible. And with that, I woke up today inspired to share some real-talk about a few things I wish I'd known before becoming a dad.

 

1. Seek Out Fathers Who Inspire You

Connect with fathers who embody the various qualities you aspire to. These men can provide invaluable advice, support, and encouragement as you navigate the highs and lows of fatherhood. We all need a tribe, and it's important to know you are not alone in this.

 

2. Prioritize Your Health and Vitality

Your life force directly impacts your ability to be present and engaged as a father. As much as my wife and I had focused on the foundations of health (nutrition, hydration, sleep, movement, etc.) as an integral part of our lifestyle already, I underestimated how much being a new dad would require of me.

 

Making self-care a priority by prioritizing sleep, nourishing your body with nutrient-dense food, drinking quality water, breathing lower and slow, and knowing what type of movement you need, I've found to be essential. This investment will pay many times over in your ability to show up in a powerful way.

 

3. Nurture The Relationship

The best advice I was in fact given early on came from my friend, Dr. Nathan Riley. He mentioned to me on our podcast together, The Path Ep. 10: The Ceremony of Birth & Parenting, that the birth experience would be relatively straight forward. The real work would be with my relationship with Lauren afterward. 

 

Take time to communicate openly and honestly about your fears, dreams, and aspirations. Cultivate a strong connection with your partner, and I suggest exploring helpful communication frameworks such as Nioviolent Communication or Imago Dialogue.

 

4. Practice Self-Regulation and Capacity

Learning to regulate your nervous system and inner experience is crucial for being a safe, grounded place your family can land. I can't emphasize this one enough. Having a daily practice of up to 20 minutes that includes some combination of breath, movement, and meditation will become an anchor when times are challenging. This has been quite possibly the one thing that has helped me cultivate patience and presence most in my relationship and experience being a dad to Luca.

 

5. Remember That You Can Have ANY Relationship You Want With Your Child 

The common saying I had heard around the first two years being "Papa doesn't matter," and "it's all about mom, you just provide financially" to me is BS. What a child craves more than anything is your presence. To me, presence is the currency of fatherhood.

 

Creatively explore ways to engage and love on your partner and child, such as with touch, reading, singing, drumming, etc. Your bond will only grow, and you can start anytime in any way that feels good to you.

 

I hope this helps you, or a soon-to-be dad you may know.

 

Wishing you a kickass day,

Mike

name: Mike@mikesalemi.io
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

It’s estimated that 80% of Americans will suffer at least one episode of low back pain in their lifetime.

Both structurally and energetically, the spine is massively important.

Having a well functioning spine can be the difference between a vital, pain-free life, and one that feels restricted and bogged down.

Below is a brief routine that you can use as a daily warm-up for your spine done by itself, or as a warm-up for things such as workouts, stretching, meditation, and really any activity that you’d like to do - I've done it just about every day for the last 5 years!

 

Click here to watch that video.

Also, here are the exercises included in this warm-up, feel free to do as many repetitions as needed to feel an improvement in how well your spine is moving and feeling. Approximately 10 to 50 reps per exercise is a reasonable range.

The exercises included are as follows:

1. Marching In Place (to ⬆️core temp.)
2. Pelvic Rocks
3. Spinal Roll-downs
4. Translations
5. Archer Rotations
6. Positional awareness while standing, breathing, and continually growing tall

I hope you enjoy this warm up and adding it to your practice.

Do let me know how it goes!

Wishing you a beautiful day 👊

 

-Mike

name: Facebook Group Males
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

What do men really need?

 

You may have heard me talk about this before, but it's worth emphasizing: men are in dire need of solid male mentors, role models, and healthy connections with other men.

 

What occurs when a man grows up without a father figure?

 

Considering that the majority of men today are raised by women (and let me be clear, this is not a slight against women or mothers), there's a particular kind of nourishment that only a father can provide.

 

There's a deep wound in the male psyche, as respected author, poet, and men’s work leader Robert Bly would say in the absence of the father. Society as a whole is lacking that paternal presence, and it affects his maturity and sense of wholeness.

 

Maybe a father was physically present but not emotionally available. I see and hear this a lot with the men I work with.

 

Bly describes how there is a collective grief among men because of this absence.

 

If you've had a father, even a good one, chances are high that they weren't there for you in all the ways you wanted or needed. And this isn’t about blaming fathers — it would be nearly impossible for fathers to meet every single one of their child's needs.

 

Additionally, in nearly every society where boys were initiated into men, there needed to be a separation from the father. To put it bluntly, it's about metaphorically "killing the father" to psychologically transition into manhood. Unless we do that, we'll always remain children. Part of the work of individuation is where we learn to father ourselves as men, and make some form of peace with our fathers/father figures.

 

Carl Jung shared that individuation involved becoming your own person, with your own beliefs and ideals that might be separate from those of your parents and society.

 

And that's precisely why men need real men around, to model it, and with us along our journey.

 

What we tend to see in society is children in adult bodies seeking guidance from other children in adult bodies. There are few elders left, and even those who exist often go unnoticed or lack the respect they deserve.

 

After much reflection, this is one of the main reasons why I've started a free online community for men.

 

While there's no financial cost, the price of admission is participation and engagement. There are enough "dead" groups out there. We only grow if we participate, contribute, and become a stand for one another.

 

Every week, I'll be going live on Wednesdays at 10:30 am PST. The calls are archived, and throughout the week, there will be prompts, mini challenges, book explorations, and discussions. 

 

The focus is around education and brotherhood.

 

We’ll see where this journey takes us, but in just two weeks, we've already gathered about 35 members, and I'm loving the energy that is starting to build.

 

I’ll be putting up a poll in the group tomorrow for members to choose the best days and times that work for them to select a group practice call in the next few weeks. This is an added bonus, and I'll be leading you through some of the work I guide men through at our in-person events.

 

Right now, I'm running the group through Facebook to make it simple.

 

If this sounds like something you want to be a part of, click here and scroll down on the Group Sign Up Form, and you’ll go through a brief approval process before joining the group.

 

All my best,

Mike

 

P.S. Did you know that our upcoming Men of Movement: Reset Retreat is a different style and format than what we've run in the past? This one will be more focused on physical vitality as a chief component to healthy masculinity. The event will take place Friday-Sunday in Mt. Shasta, CA from May 17-19th. Click here for more info.

name: It''s not fair
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

Ever been hit with that gut punch of responsibility, especially when you're trying to be the rock in your relationship?

 

Here's the raw truth: being a real leader in a relationship isn't for the faint-hearted. It can sometimes feel like you're diving into a battlefield, no matter how heavy the odds, leadership in the moment falls on you.

 

When life's smooth sailing, sure, it's a breeze basically. But when things hit the fan, and emotions run wild, that's when the real test begins.

 

And here's the kicker: even when it's not your fault, if you aim to embody good masculine leadership in the relationship, then it's on you to step up and lead, that's just the way it is.

 

Now, I'm not trying to preach to you. But if you want to be the kind of man who steers the ship, it's time to roll up your sleeves and own it.

Here's the deal: using your masculine energy in leadership means utilizing structure to create an intentional space where the flow of energy can move as optimally as possible.

 

That might mean setting a time for you and your partner to have a heart-to-heart, leading with a helpful communication framework such as Nonviolent Communication or the Imago Dialogue, or just creating an environment where you both feel safe to speak your minds and hearts.

 

Even if life throws you a curveball, it's still on whoever is "holding the masculine" in a relationship to step up to the plate and swing.

 

I know it's a lot to take in.

 

My invitation would be to sit with this, and if it resonates, then go through a check-in/evaluation of how your current situation, or future challenge could be lead in that very moment with more structure, presence, intention, and breath.

 

Leaning In,

Mike

name: It''s not fair clone
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

When did men start selling themselves short?

 

Look, I get it...

 

There are a variety of reasons that point to why this is happening:

Many men grow up without a father or father figure present, and even when they are, they often aren't emotionally available.
Historically, there was a shift during the industrial age, where children and adolescents didn't spend nearly as much time with their dads - observing, learning, and getting the nourishment from spending time alongside their father.
Society tends to label masculinity as "toxic."
There's even confusion about what being a man means today.

We can see that many men have lost touch with their innate masculine essence. As society at large, we've forgotten the ancient rites of passage and rituals that once guided us into manhood. We've become disconnected from our primal instincts and emotions, leading to a sense of emptiness and aimlessness.

 

The pattern I see, where many men diminish their role in the family unit and in society at large, needs to come to an end.

 

Witnessing men who are rising up, and who are each day coming to the recognition that THEY DO MATTER, and their role is crucial, is beyond inspiring. 

 

Masculine leadership, when healthy, is a gift. When embodying a healthy masculine form, you'll notice how people around you begin to relax, begin to feel safer. There's a directive force to life. There is more integrity all around.

 

A big part of how this has continued to come to my awareness at first surprised me and was not what I expected.

Exploring with curiosity and courage those core beliefs holding men back.

Embracing ritual to infuse intentionality into daily life.
Nourishing the body and soul with a purpose.
Building a supportive community where egos are left at the door.

 

I won't sugarcoat it; it's not easy. But trust me, it's worth it.

previewHtml:

name: Take Responsibility
text:
Hey {first_name},




Take a moment to consider this: you are the writer, director, producer, and actor of your life.




Sit with that for just a moment.





It's a powerful realization, is it not?




When I first contemplated this idea, I experienced two contrasting emotions simultaneously.




On one hand, I felt empowered beyond measure.




Yet, on the other hand, I felt a surge of responsibility wash over me.




The realization dawned on me that it's entirely up to me to craft the life I deeply want.




A life that I am willing to fight for.




Upon further introspection, I noticed how profoundly the language we use, both with ourselves and others, impacts our ability to shape and live our lives to play all out.




There are common sentiments lately I often hear expressed:

"I'm just getting old..."





"I'm always tired..."





"I've learned to live with the pain..."





"I’ll do that (insert anything for yourself) next week."




It's easy to slip into these patterns of thought and speech, especially when bombarded with mainstream narratives about health, fitness, and what's achievable when we prioritize our well-being.




But here's the crux of the matter—it doesn't have to be this way.




You have the power to script your own narrative.




This isn't about denying the reality of your current circumstances or struggles. It's about acknowledging them and taking ownership of the life you're creating and have allowed to be created—in your work, relationships, health, and every other aspect.




Granted, it may not always seem fair, and that's okay.




I encourage you to embrace those feelings and sensations fully. That is deep work by itself.




Then, from a place of greater clarity and authenticity, take the next step forward.




Sometimes that's all you need to feel into and know.




Just the next step.




Remember, your life is your masterpiece, waiting to be written, directed, produced, and performed by you.




With respect,

Mike

name: Take Responsibility clone
text:
Hey {first_name},

  

I hear it from men nearly every day - they feel pulled in countless directions.

 

Work obligations.

 

Making money.

 

Quality time with their intimate partner.

 

Self-care.

 

Nurturing friendships.

 

Time with their children.

 

The list goes on.

 

For all these reasons, and more, I find it paramount to spend time cultivating a practice of stillness - which is not synonymous with meditation btw.

 

Simply, stillness.

It might be taking a minute to stop to observe the nature around us.

 

It might be taking a pause to stop and listen for the farthest sound you can hear.

 

It might be resting to feel and hear your own heart beat.

 

It might be stopping for a moment, remembering to breathe so that we can regulate our racing minds.

 

Stillness is nourishment.

 

In fact, I believe that many kids today, and even many adults, simply can’t sit still.

 

And many have zero capacity for boredom.

 

Being bored I feel, is actually one of the most underrated gifts we can give ourselves.

 

So what happens then if we don't intentionally create time for nothing, to be still?

 

Simply put, we burn out.

 

Or we become like powder kegs on the inside, waiting to explode.

 

We may appear superficially as stoic, or like we have it all together, but deep down, we know the truth.

 

And here’s the thing I've learned from my own painful experiences: if we don’t stop to be still when we have the conscious choice, life will force us to do so at some point or another.

 

And it doesn’t take much—far less than you might think.

 

Take 10 minutes today. It’s Sunday. Simply be still.

 

Don’t overcomplicate it. Just sit, listen, observe.

 

From this place, I’m willing to bet that everything will become clearer.

 

You will know what you need to do next.

 

You will love more deeply.

 

You will feel more vital.

 

Give yourself this gift.

 

With love,

Mike

 

P.S.

If you know deep down it's time to create space and a practice to help you create more vitality in your life, then I'd love to help. We have our next retreat happening May 17-19th in Mount Shasta, CA. Simply reply with "I'm interested" and I'll get you more details.

name: Achivement
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

Ever find yourself chasing one success after another, only to wonder why the fulfillment never quite arrives?

 

Trust me, you're not alone.

 

In a world where success is often defined by your bank account or your latest accomplishment, it's easy to get caught up in the chase. And don't get me wrong, I'm all for setting goals and kicking butt. But there's a flip side to all this hustle that we don't talk about enough.

 

Take it from someone who's been there (and chats with men frequently on this struggle): the pursuit of success can be an illusion and can come from a deeper, hidden place—a place that whispers, "you're worthless unless you're constantly proving yourself, doing, or achieving something." Sound familiar?

 

I remember when, for SO long, I only felt valued and happy when I hit a won a competition, or when there was a certain weight on the bar. If I didn't hit my goals or achieve, I would go to a dark place inside, and also, as a result of being an achievement fanatic, there were many costs (namely relationships) that suffered.

 

When we tie our worth solely to what we achieve, we miss out on the essence of who we are. We start seeking validation outside ourselves, which can wreak havoc on our relationships and leave us feeling hollow, even when we've ticked off all the boxes society tells us we should.

 

So, what's the antidote?

 

No, it's not giving up on your dreams or pretending achievements don't matter. It's about digging deep and asking yourself some tough questions. Like, why are you really chasing those goals? Who are you doing it for? And most importantly, can you find fulfillment and worthiness within yourself, regardless of the accolades?

 

If this hits close to home for you, I'd love to chat.

 

Whether it's joining us, or passing this along to a man you know for our Men of Movement RESET retreat in Mount Shasta in less than 2 weeks on May 17-19th (trust me, it's going to be a game-changer) or exploring some one-on-one coaching, I'm here to help you find your way back to a life filled with meaning and connection.

 

Simply reply to this email and we'll chat further. 

 

Oh, and if you're curious, we'll be diving even deeper into this topic on next week's Path podcast. So stay tuned!

 

Wishing you a kick-ass weekend ahead,

Mike

name: Relationship
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

I wanted to share something that's been on my heart – some wisdom that's really hit home for me as a new parent, courtesy of my good friend Dr. Nathan Riley.

 

Nathan always said that while the birth experience would be unforgettable, the real test lies in how my wife Lauren and I would navigate our relationship as new parents.

 

And you know what? He hit the nail on the head.

 

Now, don't get me wrong, the birth of our little Luca was pure magic. But since then, we've been swept up in the whirlwind of sleepless nights, endless baby duties, and the shift in responsibilities - here is where I've found Nathan's words ringing truer than ever.

 

Despite the challenges, our love has grown in ways I never could have imagined.

 

In those tough moments, when exhaustion sets in, and when old patterns re-emerge, there still remains a deep bond, one of safety, love and respect.

 

Our relationship has become one of my greatest teachers. It inspires me to be better, and reminds me of the immense responsibility I have as the leader of our family.

 

Sure, there are times when I just want to crawl into a hole and shut down (believe me, it happens more often than I'd like to admit), but I've committed myself to practicing keeping my heart open, even when it feels impossible.

 

And through it all, I'm learning the importance of repair in relationships.

 

In a world where conflict is inevitable, knowing how to "fight fair" and mend things afterward is invaluable.

 

As I reflect on it all, being a father and a husband is a calling that constantly reminds me of the love, respect, and dedication I have for my family and the path we're on together.

 

So here's to embracing the challenges, learning from the stumbles, and being humbled by the incredible power of love.

 

With gratitude and an open heart,

Mike

name: Achivement clone
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

It’s been over a week since returning home from Mt. Shasta, and among the many things that took place, there was one thing that I personally experienced that still has my jaw dropping.

 

While I’ll be giving a proper recap of the event on my podcast soon, there was something that happened on the final day that I'll detail here..

 

This particular retreat focused on delivering a personalized deep dive into increasing the men’s life force, and unlocking the power that lay dormant inside.

 

And after everyone had left on Sunday, and while the facilitators and I were cleaning up, I had the opportunity to first get some hands-on bodywork on my knee by Soma Therapist and facilitator, Justin Brien.

 

For a little context before going further - my knee has been in some degree of pain off and on, and to varying degrees, for nearly 7 years.

 

It’s a repetitive stress injury to my LCL. I’ve known how to manage it, but I’ve not experienced full resolution, especially in times when I’m not diligent with my maintenance program, or when I push my body hard in training.

 

I know full well there is a mechanical issue going in and around the knee, and yet I’ve always believed there was more to the story - especially after years of doing this type of men's work, and considering the amount of rehab I’ve already done on it.

 

You see, I’ve continuously been curious regarding what pain symbolizes and what it can point us towards.

 

My knee pain is on the right side, which is associated with the masculine principle.

 

Additionally, depending on the source you read, one theme of the knees is our willingness to concede or resist life. For instance, one needs to surrender in life in order to bend and move with fluidity and also to concede one’s position.

 

Knee pain can hint at times or situations where we are stubborn, prideful, inflexible, obstinate, or self-righteous.

 

Being very honest with you, my tendency towards rigidness and my harsh critic to live up to the perception of family values of success, I imagine are highly connected to it. It's a heavy weight I've beared for a long time.

 

To go further, the left knee is more indicative of moving forward; the right knee is indicative of judgments of actions taken or not taken in the moving forward process.

 

Time and time again, I have been surprised by the underlying theme, blockage, trauma, story, or whatever you call it, connected to the physical pain in my body.

 

This has been true in my life, as well as for clients.

 

Remember, pain is inevitable; that’s just a fact of life.

 

However, our resistance to pain is what makes it suffering.

 

And often, pain is there to teach us something.

 

Now, with that context, back to the story…

 

After Justin had treated my knee, Dr. Jonny Suarez, another legit facilitator at the event, gave me one highly specific rehab exercise to do, just one.

 

Immediately, I could tell that something big was shifting.

 

I’ve done countless exercises over the years, and since the retreat, I’ve been shocked that 99% of my knee pain is gone - GONE. It’s been nearly 10 days and I am walking down stairs pain-free, doing lateral lunges pain-free, and more. Thank you Dr. Jonny!

 

To top this off, two days later, a man in my life, who I hold very dear, said something to me that I don't recall him saying before.

 

He told me he was proud of me.

 

Now, I'm well aware of the self-seduction that can come from placing our worth on external validation. That said, this one hit very close to home for reasons I won’t share here - suffice to say, it meant a LOT.

 

Additionally, I started seeing major takeoffs in my business as well.

 

I’ve been borderline baffled.

 

Why, after 7 years, has the knee pain gone away?

 

Was it the exercise I was given?

 

Quite possibly.

 

However, why now?

 

Well, for the last 6 months, I have also been in a program called EMLT - Embodied Men's Leadership Training led by John Wineland.

 

It is a very intense and immersive training.

 

Much of the work of stepping into powerful masculine leadership has to do with healing our lineage, especially the masculine line.

 

To top it off, any time we do this work in a group, for instance at the Men of Movement Retreat, there is a collective energy that emerges and takes shape.

 

And this event in particular had so much to do with healing the body, and the stories beneath.

 

Thus, I believe everything came together at this point in my life right now.

 

And the result?

 

I feel much freer in my body, in my heart, and in my mind.

 

It’s like a pressure valve has been released.

 

I am proud of myself for being committed to the process, remaining curious, not giving up, and surrounding myself with men who have dedicated their lives to their craft.

 

THIS is the WORK.

 

Oftentimes nobody sees it, and even the closest people to us have no idea about the voices inside and the pain we feel inside.

 

So, what can you do? Well, one thing is to remember to remain curious.

 

Curiosity is medicine.

 

Especially when we are willing to question our perception of reality, which may or may not, in fact, be true.

 

Wishing you the best day ever, and stay curious my friend,

Mike.

 

P.S. Now that the retreat is over, I am opening 5 NEW 1:1 coaching spots for men. I've designed a POWERFUL new format in which I am coaching that I am pumped about and have already been rolling out with impressive results. I’ll be sharing more very soon, however, if you already know that you, or someone close to you, would like to explore 1:1 coaching with me, simply reply to this email with “CURIOUS” and we’ll find a time to connect. I'll share more details, and we’ll determine if we are a good fit to work together towards creating and embodying more of the life you'd love to lead.

name: 1:1 Coaching
text:
Hey {first_name},


"I feel empty..."


This was the exact phrase a former client said to me during a coaching call. He had everything society defines as success: fitness, style, cars, houses, and a new boat. He was desired by women and had many friends.

 

Yet, despite checking all these boxes, he still felt utterly “empty” inside.


For privacy, let’s call him "John."


John felt happiest when recognized for his achievements (rather than for who he was apart from them). He excelled at emulating the most successful people around him, acquiring the same material possessions and adopting their habits. However, by focusing on societal definitions of success, he never discovered what truly mattered to him.

 

He rarely let anyone into his heart by being vulnerable and saw emotions as speed bumps on his way to the top.


He emphasized who he thought he needed to be, never asking himself the critical question, “What do I really want?”


When I asked him that question, it stumped him. It was scary for him to even consider it authentically.

 

It was a blind spot.


Through guided exploration, structured embodiment practices, and coaching, we focused on opening his heart to himself and clarifying what he truly wanted in life: to bring his authentic self to the world and a future relationship.
 

While John's story is unique, parts of it may resonate with you. We all have core beliefs formed in childhood that get reinforced over time. Deep down, we all want to feel loved, adequate, safe, and complete, knowing that we are enough. The truth is, we are already that; we've just been conditioned to forget it.


In my opinion, life’s work is to continually return to the visceral knowing of our essential nature.


Working with clients like John is confirmation of why I do what I do.


If you resonate with John’s story, I’d love to hear about it.


Wishing you all the best,
Mike


P.S. My role as a coach is to be your corner man - to call you up when you're playing small, hold space for you when you need a brother, and celebrate your wins. subject: I feel empty
previewHtml:
Hey {first_name},


"I feel empty..."


This was the exact phrase a former client said to me during a coaching call. He had everything society defines as success: fitness, style, cars, houses, and a new boat. He was desired by women and had many friends.

 

Yet, despite checking all these boxes, he still felt utterly “empty” inside.


For privacy, let’s call him "John."


John felt happiest when recognized for his achievements (rather than for who he was apart from them). He excelled at emulating the most successful people around him, acquiring the same material possessions and adopting their habits. However, by focusing on societal definitions of success, he never discovered what truly mattered to him.

 

He rarely let anyone into his heart by being vulnerable and saw emotions as speed bumps on his way to the top.


He emphasized who he thought he needed to be, never asking himself the critical question, “What do I really want?”


When I asked him that question, it stumped him. It was scary for him to even consider it authentically.

 

It was a blind spot.


Through guided exploration, structured embodiment practices, and coaching, we focused on opening his heart to himself and clarifying what he truly wanted in life: to bring his authentic self to the world and a future relationship.
 

While John's story is unique, parts of it may resonate with you. We all have core beliefs formed in childhood that get reinforced over time. Deep down, we all want to feel loved, adequate, safe, and complete, knowing that we are enough. The truth is, we are already that; we've just been conditioned to forget it.


In my opinion, life’s work is to continually return to the visceral knowing of our essential nature.


Working with clients like John is confirmation of why I do what I do.


If you resonate with John’s story, I’d love to hear about it.


Wishing you all the best,
Mike


P.S. My role as a coach is to be your corner man - to call you up when you're playing small, hold space for you when you need a brother, and celebrate your wins. Together, we’ll unlock your potential and help you live a more fulfilling and empowered life. Simply reply to this email with “I'm Interested” and I’ll get you more information.

text:
Hi {first_name},




Today's conversation explores the challenges of balancing personal routines and responsibilities as a parent, the importance of connection, and the impact of lifestyle choices on male vitality and testosterone levels. In this conversation, Mike and guest, Jonas Jonason discuss the importance of finding balance in life and managing stress to improve overall well-being. Jonas is an expert in functional medicine, functional movement, and high performance. He owns one of the top training facilities in Sweden and educates all over the world. Both these men discuss the importance of aligning work with personal values and finding a rhythm that allows for both productivity and self-care. They also touch on the importance of nature and seasonal changes as a guide for life balance.

name: Episode 113 Light
text:
Hi {first_name},




Dr. Alexis Cowan is on the show today where we discuss the importance of light and dark in regulating our biology, as well as the impact of artificial light on our health. She has a PhD in molecular biology from Princeton University, and is a true expert on the topic of light. In our show, she emphasizes the need for both dark darkness at night and bright light from the sun during the day. She explains how different frequencies of light interact with our bodies and the effects they have. Dr. Cowan also provides recommendations for optimizing light exposure, such as using blue-blocking glasses, blocking indicator lights in the sleeping environment, and spending time outside in nature.

name: Hip Stretch
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I hope you're doing well!

 

Recently, I led a recovery workshop for the Santa Clara County Sheriff's Department, and there was one particular part of the session I wanted to share with you—something that could make a big difference if you're dealing with any lower back pain or discomfort.

 

Often, tightness or imbalances in the hips can contribute to issues in the spine, so it's worth focusing on that area. Below is a thorough follow-along video demonstrating a deep hip stretch that targets a muscle called the obturator internus.

 

This myofascial stretch (focused on internal rotation) can help improve hip mobility and, as a result, alleviate some of that back tension.

 

You can check out the video here.

 

In the video, I walk you through each step, and I give recommendations for various levels of progression. Longer durations are favorable while also focusing on slow, deep breathing. This can be especially effective if done regularly, either after a workout or even before bed.

 

Let me know if you try it out and how it goes for you!

 

Best regards,
Mike

name: Paul Chek Annoucement Thursday
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I’m excited to share that the legendary Paul Chek is returning to The Path Podcast this Thursday for another DEEP conversation. This episode is one you won’t want to miss as we explore the concept of embodiment and the journey of personal evolution through his Four Life Process Archetypes and the Tarot.

 

In our discussion, here are just a few of the areas we dive into:

Embodiment and Alignment: How to align your external presentation with your internal truth, and why this is crucial for avoiding anxiety and burnout.
The Warrior Archetype: The importance of rejecting societal norms, fighting for equality and justice, and the unique challenges warriors face.
The Hierophant’s Guidance: The essential role of the hierophant archetype in guiding the journey, helping you to navigate your inner dynamics holisticlaly, and develop authentic mastery.
Midlife Crisis and the Wise Man/Woman Archetype: Understanding the choice point as an opportunity for spiritual growth and the transition to wisdom.

Paul’s insights are as deep and impactful as ever, and this conversation is packed with practical advice, powerful stories, and a lot of heart.

 

There was so much value in this one—nearly 3 hours of content!—that I decided to break it into two parts. Part one will release this Thursday, and part two the following Thursday.

 

Whether you’re on your own journey of personal growth or simply looking to gain new perspectives, there’s something in this episode for you.

 

I just shared a sneak peek clip on social media (with more to come!), and you can check it out here where Paul talks about "What Initiation is Really About."

 

Looking forward to sharing Part I with Paul Chek this Thursday!

Stay tuned and stay strong,
Mike

name: PTIA 2
text:
Hi {first_name}

 

A few months back, around 1am, I found myself lying awake in bed. Not because I didn’t have an evening wind-down routine, but rather because, even with that, my mind just wouldn’t stop racing.

 

I was at my limit point with responsibilities—hustling and catching up following busy work travel, helping care for a sick 18 month-old, making an effort to be there for my wife the best I could, and feeling the weight of it all.

 

Even as a coach, there are times when I hit my upper limit of what I can effectively manage. As a result, I, like many men, tend to hold things in.

 

I have a pattern of internalizing my emotions, putting on a facade, so I can "be the strong one." Now, while I love being the leader of my family and I have cultivated a high capacity to hold much of what life asks of me, neglecting my needs hit a saturation point, and I the emotions continued to build, and my mind continued to race.

 

Eventually, it exceeded my capacity, and there I was, lying in bed, unable to downregulate, my mind speaking with thoughts like:

"You should be able to do it all."
"You should be making more money."
"You should be able to handle this."
"You shouldn't feel angry."
"You shouldn't feel overwhelmed."

As you can see, the "shoulds' of my inner critic were blaring on loudspeaker, and creating pressure internally.

 

In times like these, I have a few things I've found to be helpful, and I want to share them with you here.

 

First, I confronted my inner critic, and I said inside, "enough", in a kind yet firm voice to create a pattern break, and stand up to that part of myself that can be abusive at times.

 

Second, I got up, went outside, and chose to lay down on the cool grass. 

 

Third, within about 10 minutes of lying there and saying a prayer for support, I started to feel held, and things began to slow down.

 

I felt the cooling nature of the earth soothing, and opening my body and mind.

 

When things are at their most stressful, sometimes the answer is this: do nothing. Sit or lie down, and allow.

 

Sometimes it's a mix of allowing it all to happen, while at the same time being a stand for YOU. By that I mean, in this case my inner critic was actually not helpful and only exacerbating the stories and internalization of what really needed to be felt - the emotions (frustration and anger mainly in this case), and allowing them to be there and move through.

 

 As I sat up, the fourth step was I went inside my home and I did a process I guide clients through called Storywork, where you write down the specific event, situation, or moment that has an energetic grip on you, and with the breath as well as a specific structure, things then really started to slow down.

 

After this, I felt like a massive weight had been lifted in real time, and I was able to not only go to sleep, but do so feeling as if a substantial healing had taken place. 

 

Now let me ask you this, have you ever found yourself lying awake at night, unable to turn off your thoughts?

 

You’re not alone. Many men struggle with sleepless nights, and often, it’s not just about stress but deeper issues that need addressing.

 

Here's a few to consider...

 

Why Men Lie Awake:

Isolation: Feeling disconnected from other men, lacking deep, supportive relationships
Unresolved and Supressed Emotions: Bottling up feelings can create an internal pressure cooker that keeps you up.
Inner Critic: A harsh internal dialogue that foster self-doubt and perfectionism.
Unmet Expectations: The weight of societal and self-imposed expectations can lead to anxiety and restlessness.
Lack of Purpose: When you’re unclear about your direction in life, it’s easy for doubts and fears to surface in the quiet of the night.

 

Here's some things to also consider of what men deeply desire:

 

What Men Crave:

Authentic Connection: A safe space to be yourself and share your struggles without judgment.
Purpose and Direction: Clarity about where you’re going and why it matters.
Inner Peace: The ability to quiet the mind and find contentment, no matter the circumstances.
Emotional Freedom: The ability to express emotions openly without fear of judgment
Growth and Fulfillment: Opportunities to evolve, learn and reach your full potential

These challenges and desires aren’t just isolated thoughts—they’re signals that something needs attention.

 

That’s one reason why I created "The Path to Inspired Action," an 8-week program (Starting Sept. 24th) designed to help men address these deeper issues, find clarity, and live a life of purpose and peace.

 

What You’ll Learn:

How to identify and work with unresolved emotions.
The root of your unconscious motivations in life
Techniques to align your actions with your values, reducing anxiety and increasing fulfillment.
Practical strategies and practices to cultivate inner peace and resilience.

This isn’t just about fixing a problem; it’s about transforming how you approach life and getting to the root of why you're up ruminating in the first place.

 

If you’re tired of lying awake at night, wondering if there’s more out there for you, this program might be exactly what you need.

 

If you’re interested in learning more, let’s connect. I’m here to support you on this journey.

 

Respond to this email with "PATH" and I'll get you all the details.

 

All the best,
Mike

 

Yours in Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S

Last week's podcast with Paul Chek was among my most downloaded show on The Path and the feedback has been excellent. Part II is dropping this Thursday where we dive deep into the topic of masculinity and manhood. Get ready for another banger coming soon!

name: PTIA 3 Watery Men
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Ever heard, or felt this, before about yourself, or a man you know?

 

Being a "watery" man in life can mean multiple things...being unreliable, frequently changing plans, failing to honor commitments, and often getting lost in distractions or emotions are a few.

It suggests a lack of discipline, structure, and grounding.

I, too, have had moments of "wateryness." Times when I failed to uphold my schedule or overcommitted myself, leading to disappointments and missed responsibilities. 

 

It's important to acknowledge that unforeseen circumstances can disrupt our plans, BUT what I'm addressing is a deeper, more pervasive pattern.

 

This is about not honoring our commitments, not taking full responsibility for our actions, and letting our words diverge from our deeds. 

 

Many men feel ashamed of this, leading them to shrink, hide, or escape, pretending nothing happened.

 

It can be tough to take responsibility and accountability for these behaviors, I get it, but it's also true and very likely that this pattern has persisted for too long, leaving those close to you craving more reliability and leadership.

 

Watery men are difficult to trust. They are often unreliable in many aspects of life. 

 

The path to change this pattern is clear:

DECIDE you want and are ready for something different - don’t BS yourself here.
SEEK out other men who can hold you accountable, and even guide you through this. 
COMMIT to the practice of transforming these behaviors, and more important what is driving them.

While this journey isn't easy, it's definitely possible. 

I've seen it in myself and in many other men—the shift from being unreliable to becoming a solid, clear, and action-oriented man.

 

This transformation is at the core of my upcoming Path to Inspired Action 8-week Online Group Men's Program, starting in just 3 weeks. My mission is to help men step into their greatness by getting honest about where they're playing small and causing harm to themselves and others.

 

There's no judgment here. If you've recognized "watery" patterns in your life and want to change this story and become a more trustworthy, confident, and empowered man, I'm here to support.

 

Learn more about The Path to Inspired Action Program here.

 

If you're ready to take the first step, either reply with "PATH" or book a quick call with me through the provided link.

 

We start on September 24th. 

 

I'm honored to invite you or any men you know, to take the next step on this new journey of aligned and inspired action in life—a journey where the whole world can benefit.

 

With respect,

Mike

 

Yours in Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S

Last week, Part II of my episode with Paul Chek on The Path Podcast, called "The Path to True Manhood" was a GREAT deep dive into the exact thing I am talking about above in this email. name: PTIA 4 Vulnerability
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

There was a time when thinking about strength, all that mattered to me was the number on the bar or a record set.


And for a while, that worked.

 

I saw the fruits of countless hours of hard training, developed solid levels of discipline early on in life, and was celebrated by my peers,

 

But then something started changing...

 

I started maturing.

 

I began to realize that while physical strength is certainly important for a man, there are other forms of strength that are equally, if not more, important.

 

Whether it was friendships ending, the loss of loved ones in the family, financial challenges, or the breakdown of intimate relationships, as I gained more life experience, I realized that my emotional strength, capacity, range, and maturity were areas I needed to foster and develop.

 

The truth is, the weight of emotions can crush a man much harder—and for much longer—than any failed attempt in the gym.

 

That said, there are strong parallels between the physical strength we build in the weight room and the emotional strength we cultivate in life.

 

Both require discipline, courage, a solid plan, commitment, and sometimes the help of others.

 

Yet one of the most overlooked paths for men to build inner strength is through vulnerability.

 

In a world where we're told to "man up" and push through challenges, we forget that one of the greatest acts of courage is facing what's inside of us.

 

We all carry wounds, fears, and insecurities, but many of us bury them under layers of busyness, distraction, or anger.

 

Here’s the key...

True strength isn’t about avoiding discomfort – it’s about confronting it.

 

For men to thrive, we need to develop emotional intelligence. This means:

Recognizing when you're feeling overwhelmed, stressed, or triggered.
Allowing those emotions to be there, rather than suppressing them.
Exploring what's at the root of them.
Learning to work with them in healthy ways – some could involve sharing with another man you trust, doing some breathwork, setting a timer for 60 seconds and giving yourself permission to have a full embodied release of the emotion, experimenting with a particular meditation, or any number of other tools.

Here’s a simple practice you can start today:

Pause when you're feeling emotionally charged.
Ask yourself, "What am I truly feeling right now?"
Name it – is it fear, frustration, sadness, or something else?
Breathe into that feeling without judgment - don't rush this part.
If you're ready, share it with someone you trust.

If you are going to share it, it's good practice to always ask this person (or group of men) first if they'd be open to supporting you. AND be clear about what type of support you are requesting...this could be to simply listen, offer a reflection, or give feedback.

 

This small process and act can create a ripple effect in all areas of your life.

 

It's easy to stay guarded, but the men who truly grow and succeed are those willing to do the inner work.

 

Take a step today. Face the emotions that may have been holding you back. It’s one of the most powerful things you can do for yourself and those around you.

 

With all that said, I also realize how powerful and needed it is to be guided through a process where all parts of you can be welcomed and honed.

 

In a group of men, all there to grow from the inside out just as much as from the outside in, there is deep medicine in that.

 

My upcoming group online program for men, The Path to Inspired Action, starting on October 1st, will guide a small group of motivated men through an intentional process I’ve led many others through.

 

We’ll work together to uncover where you’ve felt stuck, blocked, or less than and ultimately, as we shift those patterns, create a playbook for the man you are destined to become (with accountability along the way) - one who lives his days with aligned and inspired action.

 

If you're feeling the call to lean in and level up, click here for more details about this program.

 

Stay strong, and embrace the challenge,


  


Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S

There are only a handful of spots remaining in each, so if this is calling you, now is the time to take that step forward.
