name: Pre-order Date
text:
{first_name},

 

You’re receiving this email because Kettlebell Lifestyle is right around the corner. I’m so excited you are joining this movement, and I want to welcome you properly! : )

 

Upon getting access, from the initial videos and intro questionnaire, you’ll see just how different this course is.

 

I could have spent 1/10th the amount of time creating it, and it would still be a valuable program; however, I just couldn’t do that. It’s literally like a small college course in optimizing health and performance for your body. 

 

There is so much going into this program to make it as amazing as possible for you. With that said, it’s taking a bit more time than originally anticipated. 

 

You will be sent your access details on Sunday, March 8th.

 

I know I promised the original release date to be at the end of February and my sincere apologies for this small delay. For you being so patient, as well as being one of the founding members of Kettlebell Lifestyle, I’ve got a special surprise for you. 

 

Regarding the 10 weeks of weekly group coaching that I was planning on doing for 30 minutes, I’ve decided this will be 1 hour each - still for free. This coaching would cost well over $2000 to work with me individually for this amount of hours, and I’d like to express my thanks to you and include it at no cost.

 

My main objective with this program and teaching system has always been to change the way people view and approach training as a whole. To be equally performance AND health driven. 

 

To get the most out of this program, please remember these three things:

 

Trust the process
Stick with it, and fill out the daily readiness questionnaires to get the most personalization possible
Know that it’s ok to back off on your workouts and focus on more rest, and restorative activities as may be suggested in the program 

 

This program works, I can promise you that. What I’m teaching you has helped me win a World Championship in two different sports, as well and coached hundreds of one-on-one clients, and thousands of students around the world over the last 15+ years.

 

Here an idea of what to expect over the 9 weeks*:

 

WEEK 1: On Ramp 

 

Philosophy, Expectations & Results
Finding your Baseline (Intake Questionnaire)
Morning Routine
Warming Up
Working In Exercise
Stretching Review & Testing
(Optional) Mini Starter Workout
Review Key Exercise Tutorials in Phase I
Bonus Industry Expert Interview on Goal Setting

 

 

In this phase, the main focus is actually not kettlebells (other than reviewing/practicing the kettlebell tutorials, and the mini starter workout if you'd like). This was done for a specific reason. The primary focus during the On Ramp Phase is to learn and create habits around performing your morning routine, warm up, and stretches. These three elements, in addition to preparing mentally for next ~8 weeks, are truly the keys to long-term high performance.

 

 

WEEKS 2-3: Phase I Reset & Foundations 

 

Continue with Daily Morning Routine
Continue Warming Up Sequence
Continue Working In Exercise
Start Workouts A & B
Training days are approximately 3-4x/week 
New Exercise Tutorials
Follow Your Personalized Stretching Plan
Weekly Personalized Lifestyle Support Videos
 

 

WEEK 4-6: Phase II Base Conditioning & Skill Development

 

New Morning Routine
New Working In Exercise
Continue Warming Up Sequence
Three New Workouts A, B & C
Training days are approximately 4x/week (3 kettlebell workouts, and 1 kettlebell skill development day)
New Skill Development Day
New Exercise Tutorials
Stretching Plan Updated
Weekly Personalized Lifestyle Support Videos

 

WEEK 7-9: Phase III, Performance

 

New Morning Routine
New Working In Exercise
Continue Warming Up Sequence
Two New Workouts A & B
Training days are approximately 4x/week (3 kettlebell workouts, and 1 kettlebell skill development day)
New Skill Development Day
New Exercise Tutorials 
Stretching Plan Updated
Weekly Personalized Lifestyle Support Videos
Kettlebell Surprise Challenge

 

*This program can last longer than 9 weeks due to it being personalized and dynamic in nature. It is also designed so that you can go through it as many times as you’d like.

 

It's my honor to be YOUR coach and to help you transform your life.

 

I look forward to your diving into the program on Sunday, March 8th.

 

Also, I can’t wait to see you on our first Live Webinar Tuesday, March 10th at 12:00pm PST.

 

I will send out details with a webinar link in the days leading up to our call. 

 

See you soon!

Mike

name: Retreat Doors Close
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In just 10 days, we’ll be gathering in the powerful landscape of Mount Shasta, California for the Hold Your Ground: Men of Movement Retreat. With doors closing this Thursday, this is your last chance to join us for an experience that could reshape how you move through life.

 

If you've been feeling isolated, overwhelmed by the constant need to have it all together, or like you’re always carrying the weight alone, this is your opportunity to do something different.

 

This retreat isn’t about pushing you to meet society’s expectations of who you should be. It’s about confronting the lone wolf mentality, challenging the pressures placed on you, and giving you the tools to step into a more grounded version of yourself.

 

Here’s just some of what we’ll focus on:

name: Episode 122 Vincent Larviee
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In this recent episode of The Path, our guest is elite coach Vincent Larivée. Together we dive into the evolving world of youth sports and athlete development, exploring the essential balance between performance and holistic health. We discuss the impact of modern distractions, rising injury trends, and the foundational role of nutrition, sleep, and emotional resilience for young athletes. Vincent offers valuable insights on identifying talent, fostering coachability, and embracing competition as a tool for personal growth.

 

Vincent is a multi-time world beach volleyball competitor, a two time olympic coach, and the current provincial coach in Quebec preparing athletes for the national team. The episode emphasizes the importance of creating supportive environments that prioritize well-being, the ripple effects of coaching, and the role parents play in modeling healthy habits and self-care. Vincent advocates for a holistic approach to athletic training, family dynamics, and the joys of high-performance sports. His wisdom here is refreshing and how he ties it all together to build well balanced humans is inspiring.

text:
Hi {first_name},




Today kicks off my 7 Days of Specials for Black Friday, where each day brings a unique offer designed to help you grow and thrive.




We’re starting with one of the most impactful tools for personal transformation: the Enneagram.




Today's Offer - 45% Savings!

For just $197 (normally $357), you’ll receive:

Inner Compass Enneagram Assessment – an in-depth evaluation of your core motivations, instincts, and emotional patterns.
90-Minute Personalized Enneagram Session with me – where we’ll interpret your results, explore the root causes of your challenges, and craft a personalized path forward. Click here jump on this offer today.

What is Inner Compass Enneagram Assessment?

Inner Compass is not your average personality test. It’s a holistic framework that uncovers the patterns driving your behaviors and decisions, giving you clarity on how to navigate life with purpose.




Developed by Jason Olivea, Inner Compass is the tool I’ve relied on in all my coaching programs, retreats, and personal growth. Over the past 3+ years, I’ve worked closely with Jason to go DEEP with this approach, ensuring I can deliver meaningful insights tailored to you.




The Enneagram assessment identifies:

Your Type: The unique lens through which you see yourself and the world.
Your Core Patterns: Automatic beliefs and behaviors that shape your decisions.
Your Growth Path: Specific steps to overcome obstacles and unlock your potential.

Your 90-Minute Session with Me

This personalized session is designed to go beyond surface-level results. Together, we’ll:

Uncover Root Issues: Explore the core motivations and fears that drive your habits.
Break Limiting Patterns: Identify beliefs that no longer serve you and develop practical strategies to shift them.
Craft Your Path Forward: Develop an actionable, tailored plan to help you achieve clarity, confidence, and transformation.




This is a fully personalized experience—not just about learning your type, but understanding how it shapes your relationships, work, and self-perception.




**Click Here to Explore 7 Days of Specials**




What Struggles Does the Enneagram Help With?

Each Enneagram type experiences life through a specific lens, which can reveal both strengths and struggles.


Here’s a snapshot of the challenges each type may face:

Type 1 (The Improver): Struggles with self-criticism, perfectionism, and always feeling like they “should” be doing more.
Type 2 (The Helper): Often prioritizes others' needs to feel loved, leading to burnout and resentment.
Type 3 (The Achiever): Measures worth by productivity and success, struggling to slow down or feel fulfilled.
Type 4 (The Individualist): Can feel stuck in comparison and self-doubt, longing for authenticity yet fearing they’ll never find it.
Type 5 (The Investigator): May withdraw to conserve energy, struggling to connect deeply or trust their contributions are enough.
Type 6 (The Loyalist): Worries about worst-case scenarios and seeks external security, often at the expense of their inner peace.
Type 7 (The Enthusiast): Avoids pain through distraction, constantly chasing the next adventure while struggling with commitment or discipline.
Type 8 (The Challenger): Protects themselves by being overly strong or dominant, but may struggle with vulnerability and trust.
Type 9 (The Peacemaker): Avoids conflict by minimizing their own needs, often feeling unseen or disconnected from their purpose.

Through the Enneagram, we’ll uncover how these patterns are showing up for you, what you're looking to get most out of our sesison together, and create a plan to help you grow beyond these patterns and challenges showing in your life.




Added Value – Learn More About the Enneagram on The Path Podcast with Mike Salemi

I’ve had the opportunity of discussing this tool in depth on my podcast numerous times.




Check out these powerful episodes:

Ep. 34: The Enneagram Explained: Alleviating Emotional Suffering with Inner Compass Assessment Creator, Jason Olivea
Ep. 116: Overcoming Procrastination with the Enneagram
Ep. 102: The High Achievers Dilemma: The Shadow of Success
Ep. 82: Unpacking the Perfectionist's Dilemma using the Enneagram

Why Start Today?

This exclusive offer is only available today, Tuesday, November 26th - December 2nd.




**Click Here to Explore 7 Days of Specials**




This is your chance to gain clarity, break free from limiting beliefs, and step into your next level of growth.

  

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Day 2: BF Breathwork
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Life can get heavy....the stress of providing for family, keeping up with work demands, and trying to stay present for the people you care about—it all adds up. I get it, trust me.

 

For most men, there’s no manual on how to handle it all, let alone how to process the tension that builds over time.

 

We carry the stress and tension in our traps, our breath gets shallow, and our ability to focus starts to slip. Over time, this can leave us feeling stuck, disconnected, or just... off.

 

Any of that resonate?

 

Breathwork as a whole has been one of the single most powerful and reliable tools I've used personally and in my work to help create massive shifts in men's lives. 

 

This is one reason why I created a Somatic Breathwork for Men Online Group Experience happening on December 29th from 9-11am PST.

 

This isn’t just a workshop—it’s a space to reset, reconnect, and leave lighter than you came in.

 

Why Somatic Release Breathwork?

It's not hard to grasp that as humans we store stress, frustration, and even emotional pain in our bodies. And, it doesn’t go away by ignoring it—it may show up up as tension, reactivity, overwhelm, or even a constant feeling of being “on edge.”

 

Somatic breathwork is one of the most effective ways to release that built-up tension and regulate your nervous system. It’s a practice that helps you:

Let go of what’s weighing you down.
Quiet the mental chatter so you can find clarity.
Feel more grounded and in control, even during challenging times.

This isn’t about “fixing” you.

 

It’s about helping you reconnect with yourself in a way that makes life feel a little lighter, more empowering, and manageable.

 

This is a 2-hour experience that combines breathwork, brief mindset work, and connection with other men.

 

Workshop Details

What: Somatic Breathwork for Men – Online Group Experience
When: December 29th, 9-11am PST
Where: Online (Recording available for 1 week)
Regular Price: $139
Black Friday Special: $39 (72% off!)

Sign Up Here and Claim Your Spot




Why It Matters

Most men don’t give themselves the time or space to process what they’re carrying. This workshop is an opportunity to do just that—and it can change the way you show up in every area of your life.

 

Whether you’ve done breathwork before or this is completely new to you, this experience will meet you where you are and help you take a meaningful step forward.

 

Claim Your Spot Here, and save over 70%!

 

Let’s finish the year stronger, together.

  

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Day 3: BF Kettlebells
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

First off, thank you. Whether you’ve been following my work for years or just recently joined this community, I’m deeply grateful to be a part of your journey. The fact that you’re here—taking steps to grow stronger, move better, and show up for yourself—means everything.

 

When I first picked up a kettlebell, I was blown away by how much power, strength, and precision it demanded. It wasn’t just a tool—it was a challenge. A mirror.

Kettlebells have this unique ability to expose your weaknesses while building resilience, strength, and mobility like nothing else. But without proper technique and programming, they can also leave you frustrated, stuck, or even injured.

 

That’s why I created two programs to meet you wherever you are in your kettlebell journey. Whether you’re perfecting the basics or ready to integrate kettlebells into a long-term lifestyle, these programs will guide you every step of the way.

name: Day 5: BF A4L
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Years ago, I sat down with Ivan Ivanov, the creator of the Bulgarian Bag and a former Olympic wrestling coach. Ivan shared how the bag was born out of necessity. He needed a tool that could prepare wrestlers not just for brute strength, but for agility, rotational power, durability, and endurance—something dynamic enough to translate to the movements and demands they’d face on the mats.

 

What stood out to me wasn’t just the tool itself but Ivan’s vision: training should develop a body that is resilient, adaptable, and ready for life’s demands.

 

This philosophy deeply resonated with my own journey as a world champion athlete and my studies with Paul Chek, a pioneer in holistic health and performance. Together, these experiences inspired me to create Athleticism for Life: The 30-Day Bulgarian Bag Program.

 

This program doesn’t just teach you how to use the bag; it offers a holistic system for building strength, vitality, and resilience that extends beyond the gym.

 

Here’s why it matters:

Many people feel stuck in repetitive workouts that don’t carry over to real-life movement.
Stiffness, fatigue, and a lack of connection to the body leave them feeling worn down and frustrated.
Training often focuses on strength without considering durability, joint health, or recovery.

Athleticism for Life is the solution.

Over 30 days, you’ll experience a program designed to improve not just your physical strength but also your mobility, endurance, and mental clarity.

 

The Bulgarian Bag is the primary tool, but the methods include:

Rotational and dynamic movements to unlock functional strength.
Intentional breathwork to connect mind and body for better performance and recovery.
Mobility and recovery practices to ensure you’re building strength that lasts.

Additionally, it has been designed with TONS of progressions within each workout so you'll continually notice benefits each time you go through it.

This is for you if:

You’re tired of cookie-cutter workouts and want a smarter way to train.
You’re looking to integrate holistic training principles into your routine.
You want to move better, feel stronger, and live with more energy.

Black Friday Special:
The full program is normally $250, but for this week only, you can join for just $175.

 

This offer ends at midnight on December 2nd.

 

Click Here to Hop In Your Program

Use Code: A4L30

 

This isn’t just another program—it’s a step toward reclaiming your strength and vitality, guided by proven methods and decades of experience.

 

I hope to see you inside.

  

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Day 6: BF Retreats
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Men need men.

 

In a world that often isolates us, there’s immense value in stepping out of the grind and into spaces where we can reconnect with nature, rediscover our primal power, and forge deep bonds with other men.

 

These three exclusive retreats are life-changing immersions. Each retreat is designed to help you reclaim your strength, purpose, and clarity through connection, growth, and guidance.

Location: Texas

Details: This is a sacred rite of passage. Led by expert guides, this experience will connect you to the land, the animal, and yourself through ceremonies, mindfulness, and skill-building. It’s an intimate and profound journey available only to my community.

Isolation isn’t the answer. This is your opportunity to connect with a brotherhood of men, step into the wild, and transform your life.

name: Relational Confliect
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

About three years ago, I was visiting friends in Texas. We ended up at a small gathering at one of their friends’ homes—a beautiful, upscale high-rise downtown. The food was amazing, and the conversations were engaging and nourishing.

 

But there was one moment from that night that has stuck with me ever since.

 

A couple at the gathering, married for over 15 years, mentioned something that completely caught me off guard:

 

They said they’ve never had a fight in all those years.

 

First thought? No way—that’s gotta be BS.

 

Second thought? Judgment time. I was secretly rolling my eyes and thinking, How is that even possible?

 

Third thought? They must be delusional. Harsh, I know, but that’s where my mind went.

 

You see, I couldn’t fathom a relationship without conflict. Not then, not now.

 

Now, maybe they were using the word "fight" differently than I would, but let’s be real—if there’s no conflict, something’s likely being swept under the rug. And that’s where the real trouble begins.

 

Why Conflict Matters

 

Here’s the thing: I believe conflict is crucial in relationships.

 

The key is fighting fair—approaching conflict productively and with love. Yet many men struggle with this. Whether it’s the "nice guy" tendency to avoid conflict altogether or passive-aggressive behavior that sidesteps confrontation, these patterns can lead to disconnection and resentment.

 

Growing up, I deeply resonated with the "nice guy" role. I’d avoid conflict because it felt unsafe, always trying to spin things positively to keep the peace. But what I’ve learned—through my own growth and in my relationship with Lauren—is that avoiding conflict doesn’t keep the peace. It just delays the storm.

 

Building Healthy Conflict Skills

 

Here are a few things that have helped me (and might help you, too):

 

1. Set Rules for Conflict

Agree on boundaries with your partner. For example, no name-calling or cheap shots, ever

2. Learn Productive Frameworks

Tools like nonviolent communication, Imago dialogue, or authentic relating can help clear emotional charges, avoid judgment, and create space for repair.

3. Master the Art of Repair

Repairing after conflict is one of the most important skills you can develop in a committed relationship. It’s not about avoiding conflict but addressing it with the intention of strengthening the connection.

 

The Real Problem with Avoiding Conflict

 

The desire to "keep the peace" often backfires. When we avoid addressing issues that need attention, we miss an opportunity to build deeper intimacy and connection. Worse, we reinforce dysfunctional patterns and allow resentment to grow.

 

And resentment? That’s poison for any relationship. It creates emotional distance, breeds miscommunication, and erodes trust and intimacy over time.

 

A Commitment to Love

 

Reflecting on that story from Texas, I still believe conflict is healthy—and necessary—in relationships.

 

But as men, it’s up to us to lead with love, even in the messy, uncomfortable moments. When handled productively, conflict can elevate the entire relationship.

 

Lauren and I recently recorded a podcast episode about our family’s core values and how we’ve navigated conflict (for better and worse) over the past few years. If that sounds like something you’d enjoy, you can check it out here.

 

It’s not about being perfect. It’s about moving in the same direction as your partner and committing to love, even when it’s uncomfortable.

 

When you lead with an open heart and a clear intention, conflict becomes an opportunity for growth—and one of the greatest gifts you can bring to your relationship.

 

With respect,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Multi-Tasking
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

A few weeks ago, I sat down with my journal and asked myself, What’s the one thing I can focus on right now that would make the biggest difference in my life?

 

It sounds simple, but getting to the answer wasn’t easy. My mind immediately started juggling a dozen different ideas—family commitments, work projects, personal goals. It’s like part of me wanted to hold onto the belief that I could tackle everything at once.

 

But here’s the truth I’ve learned the hard way: trying to do everything usually means doing nothing well.

 

I’ve been familiar with the concept of focusing on “the one thing” for years (there’s even a great book by that name by Gary Keller and Jay Papasan), but living it? That’s where it gets tricky.

 

Here’s the core idea: Your one thing is the single, most important task that drives everything else forward. It’s the action that creates momentum, clarity, and results.

 

When you focus on your one thing, everything else either falls into place or becomes unnecessary.

 

For me, it took some deep reflection to figure out what my one thing was in different areas of my life.

 

In my work, it’s simple: how many genuine connections and offers I make daily. That’s the clearest way to drive financial growth, serve more men, and make the kind of impact I care about.

 

In my relationship, Lauren and I have committed to tackling something we’ve avoided for years—our money patterns. We’ve signed up for a financial course together, which has sparked some tough but transformative conversations.

 

And in my personal life, it’s my daily practice: 10 minutes minimum of movement, meditation, and breathwork. Without that foundation, I’d be running on fumes and wouldn’t be able to show up fully for anyone else.

 

Now, none of this clarity would have been possible if I stayed stuck in the biggest productivity lie: the myth of multitasking.

 

The Lie of Multitasking

Multitasking sells itself as a productivity hack. It makes you feel like you’re getting more done. But here’s what’s really happening:

You’re not multitasking—you’re task-switching. Your brain isn’t built to focus on two complex tasks at once. Instead, it jumps back and forth, losing efficiency and energy every time.
You’re draining your mental energy. Each switch burns more focus, leaving you tired, distracted, and more likely to make mistakes.
You’re stuck in shallow work. Multitasking keeps you skimming the surface, never diving deep enough to create real progress or results.

 

In fact, studies show that multitasking can reduce your productivity by up to 40%. Think about that—almost half your energy and time wasted because your attention is divided.

 

So, what’s the alternative?

 

It’s focusing on your one thing. Instead of spreading your energy across ten different tasks, you zero in on the one that truly moves the needle.

 

Here’s how to get started:

Ask the question: What’s the one thing I can do today that makes everything else easier or unnecessary? I would suggest doing some type of grounding practice right before this, and getting as still and quiet as possible to tune into your deeper inner wisdom.
Block out distractions: Turn off your notifications, close unnecessary tabs, and commit to working deeply on your one thing. I enjoy creating uninterrupted blocks of time during the day for my one thing and daily "big 3" in my calendar.
Trust the process: By focusing on less, you’ll achieve more—and feel more energized doing it. It does take some self-restraint to curb the desire to dive into a million things, all of which appear as important. Yet, I promise you focusing on what's actually important, rather than urgent will go longer than you might think.

 

The key is to remind yourself: doing more isn’t the goal. Doing what matters is.

 

What’s your one thing right now? If you're open to it, reply with yours and let me know—I’d love to hear what you’re focusing on using discernment and alignment with what's most important to you.




Best,


  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Sarcasm
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Sarcasm can be tricky in relationships—sometimes it’s playful, and other times it cuts deeper than intended.

 

Last week, I sat down with clinical psychologist Dr. Edmund Knighton for a podcast, and after the show, I was so intrigued by something that he shared on sarcasm, we hopped back on and did an entire segment on it that I'm excited to share with you today.

 

In this 10 minute clip we dive into the role of sarcasm in relationships, exploring its potential to either strengthen connections or create distance. Dr. Knighton shares his unique insights on humor, emotional intelligence, and how to navigate communication with authenticity and care.

 

Here are a few key takeaways:

Sarcasm often reflects unrecognized shadows in relationships.
Humor can reveal truths that deserve attention and care.
Childlike humor creates joy and deeper connection.
Sarcasm, when rooted in love and intention, can be a gift—but only if both partners understand it.

 

🎥 Watch the clip now on YouTube of this insightful conversation by clicking here.

 

And don’t miss the full podcast episode dropping this Thursday, where we go even deeper into topics like:

An easy, potent practice you can do to cultivate equanimity even in challenging situations.
Rudolf Steiner's levels of self-mastery
The Being Human Program
Movement and creativity
Navigating ambition and family life

This is one of the most thought-provoking conversations I’ve had on humor, relationships, and personal growth.

 

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts!

 

In service,

Mike

name: Time Blocking
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

A few weeks ago, I found myself sitting at my desk, staring at a to-do list that seemed to grow every time I blinked. I had emails to respond to, social media notifications piling up, and half a dozen “urgent” tasks pulling me in different directions.

 

I started working on one thing, then another, but nothing was actually getting done. By the end of the day, I was exhausted, frustrated, and questioning where all my time had gone.

 

One of the biggest frustrations I’ve had with myself over the years is this: I know I’m a hard worker, and I can get a lot of stuff done. But I’ve realized that busyness doesn’t equal success. I'll say that again: busyness doesn't equal success. That was a really tough pill for me to swallow and sit with if I'm being totally honest right now.

 

It’s discernment and consistent, focused action that truly moves the needle.

 

That night, I picked up The One Thing  - a book I recently shared in one of my prior emails to you discussing the myth of multitasking. One concept immediately grabbed my attention: time blocking. I realized I wasn’t just scattered—I was leaking energy.

 

Distraction had become the enemy of my focus, my presence, and ultimately, my purpose.

 

Since then, I’ve made time blocking a daily practice. It’s simple, but it’s not always easy. The idea is to dedicate uninterrupted time to your one thing—the task that makes everything else easier or unnecessary.

 

For me, the key shift was asking this question: What’s the ONE thing I can do right now that would make the biggest difference?

 

At first, the book's suggestion to block four hours seemed impossible! But as I leaned into it, I realized that when you define your one thing, the impact is remarkable. Those four hours aren’t just time on a calendar—they’re a commitment to your priorities, your energy, and your vision. 

 

Now, the truth is not everyday do I block off four hours, due to the responsibilities of being a young dad, coaching clients, having a firm cut off time for work so I can be with family, etc. However, I AM making a gesture towards it and there IS a time block made in my planner each day for my one thing. 

 

What surprised me most was how much I was losing to small distractions:

Scrolling through Instagram.
Checking emails every 15 minutes.
Wandering off to grab water when I could have planned ahead.

These weren’t just “little” things—they were cracks in my focus that drained my energy and held me back from showing up fully as the man I want to be.

 

Many men struggle with this. We get caught up in the grind, pulled in a hundred directions, and wonder why we feel depleted. Concentration is a skill, and it’s one of the most important skills we can develop.

 

Time blocking has helped me reclaim my energy and channel it into what matters most. It’s not just about getting things done—it’s about becoming a more focused, present, and powerful man in all areas of life.

 

If this resonates with you, start small if needed, but start.

 

With focus and strength,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

PS


I’ve been working on something close to my heart for men—something designed to help reclaim vitality, focus, and power. I’ll share more soon—stay tuned.

name: Discipline - Soft Launch VMC
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Discipline is often misunderstood.

 

Most people think it’s about willpower—forcing yourself through resistance, grinding day after day. But that’s not how it works.

 

In my opinion, discipline at its core, is a practice of integrity. It’s about choosing actions that align not just with your goals, but with the person you’re committed to becoming—even when it’s hard.

 

At first, discipline does feel like effort. You have to consciously choose the things that matter, even when they’re uncomfortable. You might wrestle with old habits, face resistance, or doubt your capacity to stick with it.

 

But when you stay consistent, something shifts.

 

Here’s the truth:

Discipline doesn’t mean doing more; it means choosing what matters, consistently.
Small, deliberate actions—taken daily—rewire you at your core.
Over time, the need to “force” yourself fades. You stop fighting resistance because your choices come from a place of clarity and alignment.

But let’s talk about something most people don’t admit: discipline doesn’t become effortless.

 

Even when you’ve built strong habits, life will challenge you. Stress, doubt, distractions—they’ll show up and test your foundation. But this is where true discipline shows its power.

 

When discipline is rooted in who you are, it becomes your anchor. It’s not about perfection or never slipping—it’s about having the capacity to reset, to recalibrate, and to realign when life pulls you off course.

 

Discipline is less about what you do and more about the relationship you create with yourself. It’s showing up again and again, in ways that build trust within.

 

And here’s the truth: you don’t have to figure it out alone.

 

Over the past year, I’ve been working on a new way to support men—bringing together everything I’ve learned about living with clarity, strength, and purpose.

 

It’s not about doing more. It’s about learning to show up differently—in your work, your relationships, and in how you lead yourself.

 

If this resonates with you, and you want to hear more about what I’ve been building, just reply with “Tell me more.”

 

Let’s explore what’s possible, together.

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: The Victim Trap
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Imagine this:

 

You wake up already feeling behind. The weight of your to-do list presses on your chest before your feet hit the floor. By the time the day is over, you’ve given everything you’ve got—to work, to your family, to the endless demands pulling you in a thousand directions.

 

And yet, deep down, there’s this gnawing frustration: “Why does it feel like no matter how much I do, it’s never enough?”

 

You tell yourself things will get better once you check that next box or hit that next milestone. You keep pushing, thinking, “If I can just do more, give more, or try harder, things will finally fall into place.”

 

But here’s the hard truth: that cycle never ends.

 

Beneath it all is often something deeper—a pattern that keeps so many people stuck and exhausted.

 

This is what I call The Victim Trap.

 

It doesn’t look like blame at first—it looks like justification. It feels like:

“I have to do it all because no one else will.”
“If my circumstances were different, I could finally [insert goal here].”
“I’m so drained, but I don’t want to disappoint anyone.”

The Victim Trap is sneaky because it convinces you that you’re doing everything right. But in reality, it’s pulling you further from your power.

 

Here’s the hard truth: when you live in the Victim Trap, you hand over your control. Life happens to you, not through you.

 

And it all starts with your words.

 

As mentor and friend Mark England teaches, the language you use creates your reality. Victim language is heavy, constricting, and full of absolutes like:

“I have to.”
“They made me feel this way.”
“There’s nothing I can do.”

But here’s the good news: just as your words can trap you, they can also set you free.

 

Here’s how to start breaking the cycle:

Slow down your words. Write down the story you’re telling yourself about your current situation. Get it out of your head and onto paper.
Look for absolutes. Highlight the have to’s, can’t’s, and should’s. These are the red flags of victim language.
Reframe your story. Replace those absolutes with empowering choices. For example:
Victim: “I have to stay late because no one else will do their part.”
Empowered: “I’m choosing to stay late because this project matters to me, and I can also set boundaries moving forward.”

This isn’t about ignoring challenges or pretending everything is easy. It’s about reclaiming your power to choose how you respond to life.

 

Every powerful man I’ve met has mastered one thing: the ability to recognize his patterns and take action to change them.

 

In the new The Vital Man Collective, this is one of the foundational skills we teach—how to rewrite the stories keeping you stuck. Because freedom starts with the words you choose.

 

When you change your words, you change your perspective. And when you change your perspective, you change your life.

 

With love and respect,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S. If you'd like details on the Vital Man Collective, reply "Vital" and I'll shoot them on over.

name: Doing things Differently
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Growing up with an immigrant father, I was shaped by his relentless drive and the example he set through his work. My dad didn’t just go through life; he built it. From pulling espresso shots while standing on a milk crate at the age of 9 in Sicily, to becoming the head pastry chef at a busy Italian grocery store when he moved to the States, he embodied what it meant to create something with his own hands.

 

But it wasn’t just about business. It was about carving a path, no matter the odds, and doing it with integrity. I saw that firsthand. He was always willing to disrupt the status quo, and whether it was working in the kitchen, running a landscaping business, or building a marble and granite company, he put in the work—no shortcuts. It wasn’t just for him—it was for his family.

 

What I really took from him wasn’t just the business work ethic. It was the commitment to craft, the courage to take risks, and the unwavering determination to provide and protect what matters most. He taught me the value of building something meaningful, even when the world says it's easier to take a more predictable route.

 

This week, as I prepare to launch the Vital Man Collective, I’m reminded of the impact my father had on me as a man. Over the last five years of focusing on men’s work—leading retreats, running online programs, coaching men one-on-one, and participating in various men's groups and immersive experiences—I’ve seen firsthand some of the challenges men face when entering this work.

 

For one, what exactly is "men’s work"? Ask 100 different people, and you’ll likely get 100 different answers. I, too, have contributed to this confusion.

 

In my experience, I’ve found a few common barriers that prevent men from getting the support they need:

High upfront price points that make it difficult to access the value of this work and determine if it's a good fit for them.
Start dates for programs that often don’t align with when men need help the most.
A lack of ongoing accountability, support, and community after a program/group ends.
"Leaky" containers where men don’t feel supported enough to open up and dive deep.
The lack of action. Awareness is great, but if your life doesn’t change, what's the point?

 

After countless hours of reflection and discussion, I’ve come to a conclusion. The solution is the Vital Man Collective.

 

This is a unique blend of a deep, supportive community, a men's group, access to all of my past work (programs, workshops, etc.), and everything I create moving forward!

 

I will tell you straight up, the men who join the VMC will regularly be challenged - however, I can assure you it will come from a place of respect, love, and a desire to see each man lead their life in the biggest way possible.

 

The VMC for men who are ready to step into their authentic power with integrity and alignment—free from burnout and the constant need for external validation.

 

I’m excited to offer the first kickoff workshop call for FREE, on Tuesday, February 4th from 5-7pm PST.

 

Whether you sign up for the program or not, I promise you will walk away with something valuable if you show up with an open mind and heart.

 

In this first workshop, I’ll lead powerful group breathwork practices and guide a process called Storywork to help men let go of the heavy packs they so often carry.

 

If you’d like more information on the Vital Man Collective, or to join the first workshop call for free on February 4th, simply reply with the word "VITAL'.

 

This new offering is about helping men create the energy to sustain change and step into life powerfully and authentically. 

 

If you or a man you know would benefit from this, shoot me a reply.

 

With love and respect,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: VMC Workshop Launch
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

A lot of men pride themselves on doing a lot. They take on more responsibilities, push harder in their careers, train their bodies, and aim to be great partners, fathers, and leaders.

 

Now, don’t get me wrong— parts of me do this too. And in fact, I believe responsibility is a key to stepping into our power as men.

 

Heck, having a child has been one of my biggest opportunities to grow as a man—in leadership, in love, and so much more.

 

But here’s the thing—effort isn’t the same as direction.

 

A man who’s constantly moving but unclear on his deeper why, his vision, or his center eventually burns out. He works harder but feels less fulfilled. He jumps from one challenge to the next, hoping that the next thing will be the answer.

 

That’s why I created The Vital Man Collective—a new space for men who want more than just surface-level motivation. And next Tuesday, from 5-7pmPST, I’m hosting Call #1 as a free workshop where you, or a man you know, can experience it firsthand.

 

What You’ll Get in This 2-Hour Workshop:

Breathwork & Embodiment Practices – Train your nervous system to hold more energy and presence, so you don’t shut down or lash out under stress.
Identifying & Breaking Stuck Patterns – Recognize and work as a group on the hidden stories that cause burnout, overthinking, and self-doubt, and begin to shift them in real time.
A New Relationship with Challenge – Develop a mindset where resistance becomes fuel, rather than something that drains you.

 

This isn’t just another call. It’s an experience—something you’ll feel in your body immediately.

 

And it’s completely free, so whether you sign up for the VMC or not, if you show up with an open heart and mind, you will walk away with something real.

 

👉 Click Here to Register for the Free Workshop

 

If you’ve been looking for a way to step into deeper strength, purpose, and clarity—this is it.

 

And if you know a man who needs this, send this his way.

 

With love and respect,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: What Makes a Week Man P1
text:
Hey {first_name},




Most men don’t set out to be weak.




But weakness doesn’t happen all at once—it creeps in. One compromise here. One excuse there. Before you know it, you’ve lost your edge.




Here’s just some of what makes a weak man:




A weak man is a reactive man. He’s emotional and impulsive, blaming others instead of leading himself.
A weak man is easily distracted. He jumps from one thing to the next, never fully present. His attention span is shorter than his patience.
A weak man avoids discomfort. He seeks short-term ease instead of long-term strength. If it’s hard, he backs down.
A weak man struggles to commit. He keeps one foot out the door—whether in relationships, business, or personal growth—so he always has an escape.
A weak man has no boundaries and is a people pleaser. He gives his time and energy away because he’s afraid to say no.
A weak man rarely keeps his word. He makes promises but doesn’t follow through. Eventually, no one—including himself—trusts him.
A weak man blames others for his shortcomings. He points the finger instead of taking responsibility and lives in the victim mentality.
A weak man is physically weak. He neglects his body, ignoring the fact that strength is the foundation of all discipline.
A weak man avoids feedback. He’d rather be comfortable than face the truth about where he needs to grow.




Here’s the worst part: Most weak men don’t even know they’re weak.




They justify it:

“I don’t have time.”
“I don’t want to be selfish.”
“It’s not the right moment.”




But the truth is simple: Weakness is a choice. And so is strength.




Now what?




You’ve got two options:

Get defensive, close this email, and pretend none of this applies.
Be brutally honest. Ask yourself: Where am I living like a weak man? Where am I tolerating these patterns in myself?

If you’re ready to actually do something about it, keep an eye on your inbox.




Tomorrow, I’ll show you exactly what it takes to become a strong man.

No fluff. No nonsense. Just the real work.

name: Kettlebell Jerk - Power
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

Staying on theme with our recent discussions about weak vs. powerful men, today we’re diving into physical training with kettlebells.

 

The kettlebell jerk isn’t just another overhead movement—it’s a true test of power and efficiency. Unlike a strict press, where the shoulders do all the work, the jerk harnesses full-body force to drive the kettlebells overhead with minimal effort. It requires timing, coordination, and explosive leg drive, making it one of the most effective lifts for athletic power.

 

Execution is everything. Every phase must be precise—rack position, leg drive, and drop speed. Common mistakes like over-relying on the arms or losing position will rob you of efficiency and keep you stuck.

 

This breakdown will take you through each phase step-by-step, along with the biggest mistakes lifters make (and how to fix them). If you want to move with power instead of just muscling through reps, keep reading.

 

The Kettlebell Jerk

 Step-by-Step Breakdown of the Kettlebell Jerk

 

1. Rack Position 

Clean the kettlebell(s) into a solid, stable rack.
Shoulder depressed down, with your lat and core active
Elbows rest against the torso, wrist neutral, grip firm but not overactive.

2. The Dip

Bend the knees slightly forward—no hip hinge
Keep the torso vertical (weight centered between the heel and midfoot)
The dip is quick and controlled

3. The Drive

Drive through the legs, extending the knees, hips, and ankles powerfully.
The goal is to propel the kettlebell upward primarily with leg power, rather than pressing with the arms.

4. The Drop (a.k.a Undersquat)

As the bells float from the leg drive, perform a quick second dip under the weight.
Punch the arms fast to enter the lockout position 
Keep the torso vertical when receiving the weight
This second dip allows you to "catch" the bells overhead without excessive pressing.

5. Lockout (a.k.a Fixation)

Stand up strong with the kettlebell locked overhead.
Biceps close to ears, arms straight, and shoulders stable.

 

Common Mistakes & Fixes

Dipping Too Low – Stay shallow and vertical to keep the energy direct. A deep dip wastes power and disrupts mechanics.
Pressing Instead of Jerking – The legs do the work—the arms should only catch and stabilize. If your shoulders burn out quickly, you’re likely pressing too much.
Not Dropping Fast Enough – Speed under the bells is key. A slow second dip forces unnecessary strain on the upper body. Work on a quick, sharp drop to reduce effort.
Losing Rack Position – Keep the elbows tight, core active, and kettlebells stacked before launching into the movement. A weak or loose rack will throw off every phase of the lift.
Poor Lockout Position – A weak or misaligned overhead position leads to instability and inefficiency. The kettlebells should sit directly over your shoulders and hips, with wrists neutral, elbows locked, and lats active. If your arms are bent or the bells drift forward, adjust your posture and reinforce a strong stacked position before moving on.

Mastering the kettlebell jerk takes patience and attention to detail, but once dialed in, it becomes one of the most powerful and efficient movements for building power, power-endurance, and explosiveness. Focus on technique, eliminate wasted effort, and develop the ability to generate force with precision.

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

PS

If you’re in, click here to register.

name: What Makes a Week Man P1 clone 2
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

Most men like to think they’re strong. They tell themselves they’re disciplined, committed, and capable.

 

But when it comes down to it, real strength isn’t built in big moments—it’s revealed in the small, daily choices.

 

It’s whether you follow through when no one is watching.


It’s whether you stand firm when it would be easier to cave.


It’s whether you face discomfort or find another excuse to avoid it.

 

And the truth? Most men struggle with these things at some level.

 

That’s not a judgment—it’s reality. And the difference between staying stuck and stepping up is being willing to see where you can grow and actually do something about it.

  

11 Things Most Men Can’t Do:

 

1. Say "No" Without Apologizing or Over-Explaining.
Most men struggle with this. They say “yes” when they should say “no,” fearing judgment or rejection. A strong man sets boundaries and enforces them without guilt.

 

2. Sit in Silence for 10 Minutes Without Distraction.
Most men reach for their phone the second they feel bored or uncomfortable. A strong man trains his mind like his body—by sitting with discomfort, not running from it.

 

3. Look in the Mirror and Say, "I am 100% Responsible for My Life."
Most men blame their job, their upbringing, their partner, or their circumstances for where they

 

4. Follow Through When No One is Watching.
It’s easy to show up when someone’s holding you accountable. But will you train when no one is checking? Will you finish what you started, even when it’s inconvenient?

 

5. Ask for Help Without Feeling Weak.
Too many men believe they should handle everything alone. A strong man understands that real growth comes from seeking guidance and surrounding himself with the right people.

 

6. Train for Strength, Not Just Looks.
Most men chase the pump but can’t move well or sustain power. A strong man trains for real-world capability—whether that’s carrying, climbing, or simply moving heavy sh*t.

 

7. Hold Eye Contact in a Hard Conversation.
Avoiding eye contact = avoiding presence. A powerful man holds his ground, listens fully, and responds with clarity—even in the uncomfortable moments.

 

8 Make a Hard Decision and Stand By It.
Most men hesitate, waiting for perfect conditions or permission. A strong man makes the call, owns the outcome, and keeps moving forward.

 

9. Step into Cold Water Without Hesitation.
This isn’t just about cold plunges—it’s about taking action without bargaining with yourself. A strong man moves—into discomfort, into challenge, into action.

 

10. Look in the Mirror and Say, "I Love Myself"—And Mean It.
Most men can’t even meet their own eyes in the mirror. They see flaws, regrets, the weight of expectations they haven’t met. A strong man does the work to respect and trust himself fully—without needing anyone else’s validation.

 

11. Walk into a Room and Carry Presence Without Saying a Word.
Weak men overcompensate—talking too much, seeking validation. A powerful man’s presence is felt through his actions, discipline, and energy—not forced words.

 

Be honest—How many of these can you actually do?

 

If reading this list made you pause, that’s a good thing.

 

That hesitation is an invitation.

 

A moment to recognize where you can step up.

 

Tonight, I’m leading a free men’s workshop at 5 PM PST for men who are serious about stepping into strength, discipline, and ownership.

 

If you’re ready to stop hesitating and start moving, DM me "VITAL" and I’ll send you the details.

 

Let’s go.

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Balancing
text:
Hey {first_name},




There will always be more to do. More responsibilities, more expectations, more people pulling at you. The weight of showing up for others—whether as a partner, a parent, a leader—never fully disappears. But trying to carry it all at once? That’s what leads to exhaustion, resentment, and burnout.




Not every ball you’re juggling is made of glass. Some can drop. Some need to drop so that the most important ones—your health, your integrity, your relationships—don’t shatter.




If today was your last, what needed to happen?


What words needed to be said?


Who needed to feel your presence, not just your productivity?




This isn’t about doing less for the sake of ease. It’s about doing what actually matters.




A skilled warrior doesn’t waste energy swinging wildly at every target. They move with precision, striking only where it counts. The same is true for life. Some fights are worth engaging in. Some expectations are worth releasing. And some moments—if missed—can’t be reclaimed.




Sometimes, the most important thing you do in a day isn’t checking another box on the to-do list. It’s choosing to be present. To pause. To say, I love you. To own a mistake before the weight of it grows too heavy. To recognize that you don’t have to do it all—just the things that actually shape the life you want to live.




Tonight, when your head hits the pillow, ask yourself: Did I take care of what truly mattered?


Not everything. Not perfectly. But the things that count.




Because that’s what real balance is.




With you on the path,

  

Mike Salemi

name: Spartan
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

What if your entire childhood was designed to make you unshakable?

 

In ancient Sparta, boys entered the Agoge at age seven—a training system built to forge warriors feared across the known world.

 

Softness wasn’t an option.

 

They slept on the ground. They trained relentlessly. They endured hunger—not because suffering was the goal, but because they understood strength comes through challenge, not comfort.

 

But here’s what most people miss:

Spartans weren’t mindless brutes pushing through pain just to suffer. They were calculated, disciplined, and intentional in their training. Their hardships were designed to prepare them for what life would demand of them—not break them.

 

That’s the lesson.

 

"You have power over your mind—not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength." — Marcus Aurelius, Meditations

 

Today, men aren’t fighting with shields and spears, but the battles are still real—distraction, doubt, responsibility, the pressure to perform. The world doesn’t demand discipline from you, which is exactly why you must choose it.

 

Because discipline isn’t restriction. It’s freedom. It’s readiness. It’s knowing that no matter what happens, you’ve built the strength to handle it.

 

So here’s your challenge:

For the next 7 days, build your modern Agoge.

Wake up 30 minutes earlier.
Train with focus, not just intensity.
Breathe deeper when stress hits.
Make the hard decision you’ve been putting off.

 

Strength isn’t found—it’s built.

 


Stay strong,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: If fell like I've lost myself
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

A man inside The Vital Man Collective recently said something that I deeply resonated with from my own journey in prior years:

 

"I do everything I can to be a good man. I show up. I work hard. I try to make the people in my life happy. But no matter how much I give, it never feels like enough."

 

Maybe you or a man you know has felt that, too.

 

You pride yourself on being solid, someone people can count on. You handle responsibilities. You don’t cause problems. You try to be the guy who makes things easier for everyone else.

 

And yet, at some point, you start to notice the cost.

 

You hold back what you really think because you don’t want to create conflict.


You suppress your needs because you tell yourself they aren’t as important.


You carry an unspoken resentment because you give, and give, and give… but it never seems to come back to you in the way you hope.

 

This is the weight of Nice Guy Syndrome.

 

And it has nothing to do with kindness.

 

The Truth About ‘Nice Guys’

A lot of men confuse being a good man with being a man who shrinks himself to avoid discomfort.

 

They think:

“If I keep people happy, they’ll appreciate me.”
“If I avoid conflict, things will go smoothly.”
“If I put others first, eventually things will balance out.”

 

But here’s what actually happens:

People don’t respect a man who constantly abandons himself.
Avoiding conflict doesn’t make it disappear—it just shows up in other ways.
The longer you suppress your own needs, the harder it becomes to even recognize what they are.

 

John Wineland talks about the false virtue of niceness—how so many men wear it like a badge of honor, but in reality, it’s a cover for fear.

 

The fear of being too much.
The fear of being seen as selfish.
The fear of being rejected for standing firm.

 

And so instead, these men become agreeable, accommodating, and easy to be around.

 

Not because it’s who they truly are.
But because they believe it’s what will make them acceptable.

 

And yet—deep down—they feel the cost of it.

 

They know they’re holding back.
They know they’ve made themselves smaller.
They know they’ve betrayed themselves in small, subtle ways over time.

 

A man can only do this for so long before he starts to break under the weight of it.

 

What Happens When a Man Reclaims His Power?

 

The moment a man stops living for other people’s approval, something shifts.

 

He stops sugarcoating his words and starts speaking clearly and directly.
He stops explaining himself when he sets a boundary.
He stops overextending himself in relationships that only drain him.

 

And ironically?

 

That’s the moment people actually start respecting him.

 

Because people don’t trust a man who betrays himself.

 

A Challenge for You

For the next 24 hours, I want you to pay attention to the moments when you feel the urge to soften your words, backtrack, or accommodate someone else at your own expense.

 

Where do you hold back your truth?
Where do you avoid discomfort?
Where do you downplay your needs, even when you feel them deeply?

 

And then—just once—choose a different response.

 

Say what you actually mean.
Hold your boundary without apologizing for it.
Let someone feel uncomfortable with your truth, and stand firm in it.

 

At first, it might feel unnatural.

 

But if you sit with it, you’ll feel something stronger beneath the discomfort:

Your own power.

 

With respect,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Pain is a Signal, Not the Problem
text:
Hey {first_name},

 

Pain is a signal, not the problem.

 

Most people think of pain as something to fix, suppress, or push through. But pain is simply the body’s way of telling you something is out of alignment. And whether it’s your back, knees, shoulders—or even your energy—the real cause often isn’t where you feel it.

 

Take back pain, for example. You might assume the issue is in your lower back, but in reality, the problem could be in your feet, hips, breathing patterns, or even your diet. If one area is out of sync, everything else has to compensate. That’s when movement becomes inefficient, tension builds up, and pain shows up.

 

Integrity, it's more than just a word.

 

This month inside The Vital Man Collective, our focus is integrity—and there are many ways to look at it. Three in particular shape how we show up in the world:

Word: Do you follow through on what you say, even to yourself? If you commit to something, do you honor it
Heart: Do you act in alignment with what you truly believe, or do you let fear, approval-seeking, or pressure pull you off course?
Body: Are you moving efficiently, or are old patterns of stress, misalignment, and imbalance leading to unnecessary pain and tension?

We recently had guest presenter Justin Brien, a certifying instructor for Guy Voyer and ELDOA, speak to the group about The Gravity Line—the principle that proper alignment allows for more efficient movement and reduces unnecessary strain.

 

When your head, ribs, pelvis, knees, and feet are stacked properly, movement becomes effortless. There’s no wasted energy, no unnecessary tension. But when you’re off-center? The body knows—and it lets you know through discomfort, fatigue, or injury.

 

It’s the same in life.

 

Ever notice how a tough conversation, financial stress, or an overwhelming to-do list can leave you feeling just as drained as physical pain? That’s because efficiency and integrity don’t just apply to movement—they apply to how you manage energy in every area of your life.

 

When you know how to dynamically center—physically, mentally, and energetically—you move through challenges with greater clarity and purpose. When you’re off-center, everything feels harder than it needs to be, and you get pulled into old, dysfunctional patterns.

 

This is where the gold is.

 

Can you develop enough awareness to know where your energetic center is moment to moment?

 

Do you have the sensitivity to discern which people, conversations, and tasks pull you out—causing a collapse of your power?

 

And most importantly, do you know how to bring yourself back?

 

This can be trained—and in my opinion, it should be trained, especially in men who seek to show up most powerfully and lovingly in life.

 

So Here’s My Invitation to You:

Where are you experiencing pain—physically or otherwise?
What’s pulling you out of alignment?
What’s one small shift you can make to regain your center?

 

Inside The Vital Man Collective, we bridge physical integrity with internal integrity, so that pain, tension, and misalignment—whether in the body or in life—don’t hold you back. If you’re ready to restore efficiency, integrity, and power in how you move and live, join us.

 

If you or a man you know could benefit from stepping into greater integrity—physically, mentally, and emotionally—alongside a group of men committed to real conversations and powerful shifts, simply reply to this email with "I'm Interested." I'll send over the details about The Vital Man Collective.

 

Stay strong,

  

Mike Salemi
Men's Coach & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S.

Tomorrow, an epic podcast drops with Michael Chernow—one of the most inspiring conversations I’ve had on overcoming serious adversity, conscious fatherhood, and showing up under the responsibility and pressure of being a high-level entrepreneur and business owner. You won’t want to miss this one!

name: Language Game
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Mindset. It’s a word that gets thrown around all the time, but most definitions overcomplicate it.

 

Mark England, a friend and mentor, has the simplest, cleanest definition I’ve ever heard:

 

Mindset is the story we tell ourselves, and the words we use to tell that story.

 

That’s it.

 

And here’s the thing—we are always telling ourselves a story.

 

A story about the past.
A story about the future.
A story about why we’re stuck.

A story about how our partner criticizes us.
A story about fear, judgment, anger, resentment.

 

Sometimes these stories serve us. Sometimes they keep us trapped.

 

If you want to experience a shift in mindset, don’t start with “thinking positive.”





Start with the raw materials of your stories—the words themselves.

 

A Simple Game

Today, I want to invite you to a simple, but powerful exercise. This isn’t about fake positivity. It’s about precision and awareness—seeing how even the smallest change in language can shift how you feel, breathe, and move through the world.

 

To keep things simple, I'm going to pull out one particular sentence that came up recently with a client, and we are going to work with it together in realtime.

 

Here’s how it works:

Read each sentence out loud.
Pause and check in with yourself briefly: How does it feel? What's the vibe?
Move to the next sentence and repeat. Notice even the micro shifts - in your breath, your posture, or your internal dialogue. 
Bonus: Take one full breath before reading the next statement

 

The Language Game

 

READ: "When will I ever just get over this fear?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 
READ: "When will I get over this fear?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "What if I get over this fear?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.


READ: "What if I get over this story?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "I could get over this story."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "I can get over this story."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.


READ: "I can welcome parts of this story."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.


READ: "I can welcome parts of me."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "I can welcome me."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

Did you notice any difference?

 

At the start, the words likely felt heavy - restrictive, trapped, almost impossible.

 

As you moved down, the weight started to lift. The breath slowed. A subtle shift happened.

 

The fear is still there, but instead of fighting it, you may find yourself expanding beyond it, welcoming more of your experience. 

 

This is one small example of how you can work with language - especially in the context of a story where there is a lot of energetic charge connected to it. 

 

We’re not forcing positivity here. We’re choosing our words with intention, slowing down, breathing deep, and exploring new possibilities incrementally - without being overly attached. 

 

And in doing so, we create space, clarity, and new possibilities.

 

If you did indeed give this game a try, reply and let me know what you noticed, I'd love to hear about it.

 

Yours in Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi

subject: What If One Word Could Change Everything?
previewHtml:
Hi {first_name},

 

Mindset. It’s a word that gets thrown around all the time, but most definitions overcomplicate it.

 

Mark England, a friend and mentor, has the simplest, cleanest definition I’ve ever heard:

 

Mindset is the story we tell ourselves, and the words we use to tell that story.

 

That’s it.

 

And here’s the thing—we are always telling ourselves a story.

 

A story about the past.
A story about the future.
A story about why we’re stuck.

A story about how our partner criticizes us.
A story about fear, judgment, anger, resentment.

 

Sometimes these stories serve us. Sometimes they keep us trapped.

 

If you want to experience a shift in mindset, don’t start with “thinking positive.”


Start with the raw materials of your stories—the words themselves.

 

A Simple Game

Today, I want to invite you to a simple, but powerful exercise. This isn’t about fake positivity. It’s about precision and awareness—seeing how even the smallest change in language can shift how you feel, breathe, and move through the world.

 

To keep things simple, I'm going to pull out one particular sentence that came up recently with a client, and we are going to work with it together in realtime.

 

Here’s how it works:

  • Read each sentence out loud.
  • Pause and check in with yourself briefly: How does it feel? What's the vibe?
  • Move to the next sentence and repeat. Notice even the micro shifts - in your breath, your posture, or your internal dialogue. 
  • Bonus: Take one full breath before reading the next statement

 

The Language Game

 

READ: "When will I ever just get over this fear?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 
READ: "When will I get over this fear?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "What if I get over this fear?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.


READ: "What if I get over this story?"

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "I could get over this story."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "I can get over this story."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.


READ: "I can welcome parts of this story."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.


READ: "I can welcome parts of me."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

READ: "I can welcome me."

Stop. Check In. Breathe.

 

Did you notice any difference?

 

At the start, the words likely felt heavy - restrictive, trapped, almost impossible.

 

As you moved down, the weight started to lift. The breath slowed. A subtle shift happened.

 

The fear is still there, but instead of fighting it, you may find yourself expanding beyond it, welcoming more of your experience. 

 

This is one small example of how you can work with language - especially in the context of a story where there is a lot of energetic charge connected to it. 

 

We’re not forcing positivity here. We’re choosing our words with intention, slowing down, breathing deep, and exploring new possibilities incrementally - without being overly attached. 

 

And in doing so, we create space, clarity, and new possibilities.

 

If you did indeed give this game a try, reply and let me know what you noticed, I'd love to hear about it.

 

Yours in Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

name: Rotation
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Most training programs focus on linear movements—squats, deadlifts, presses. And for good reason. These lifts help build the foundational strength we need for overall durability and power.

 

They align with many of our body's primal movement patterns—push, pull, squat, hinge, lunge, twist, and gait.

 

But here’s the thing… one of these patterns is almost always neglected.

 

Rotation.

 

Why Rotational Strength Matters More Than You Think

Most of the power we generate—whether in sports, daily movement, or simply staying strong for life—comes from rotation. It’s the missing link between raw strength and real-world functionality.

 

Think about it: when you throw a bag of dog food into the back of your car, catch yourself from slipping on a wet floor, carry a heavy suitcase up a flight of stairs, toss your kid in the air and catch them, or pull something down from a high shelf while rotating your torso, your body isn’t working in isolated, linear patterns—it’s relying on rotational strength, core stability, and grip endurance to generate and control force efficiently.

 

Yet, most training programs overemphasize sagittal-plane lifts (squats, deadlifts, presses) while neglecting transverse-plane strength, where true athleticism and injury prevention are built. If you’re only training in straight lines, you’re leaving a massive gap in your strength, mobility, and durability.

 

For those who understand functional movement, rotation isn’t optional—it’s foundational. Without it, strength becomes rigid, power lacks fluidity, and injury risk skyrockets.

CHEK Faculty Matt Wallden states that 80% of power in sports comes from rotational force.
Back injuries account for nearly 20% of all workplace injuries, often due to improper lifting techniques and uncontrolled twisting.
About 80% of Americans will experience at least one bout of back pain in their life. 

And Paul Chek says it best—“You can't fire a cannon from a canoe.” If your core can’t stabilize and transfer rotational power, your strength won’t carry over into real-world movement.

 

What I Personally Do

Well, one of the things I can tell you is I keep portable training tools on hand. I have a Bulgarian Bag in my office and use it almost daily. If you’ve never trained with one, it’s a tool built for rotation, grip endurance, and muscular stamina—all in one.

 

As a father, this isn’t just theory—it’s real life. When I pick up my son, carry him on one side, twist to put him in the car, or chase him around, my body isn’t just moving up and down—it’s shifting, rotating, and adjusting in multiple directions. Training this way means I can do all of it without pain, stiffness, or feeling worn down.

 

How You Can Start

Even just 5 minutes of Bulgarian bag training will:

Develop grip endurance (your grip is your nervous system’s first line of strength).
Strengthen your trunk for real-world power (not just static planks).
Improve spinal movement and durability (key for injury prevention).
Increase conditioning without beating up your joints.

The Bulgarian Bag in Action

When I teach certifications on the bag (by the way, at the end of 2025, I’ll be running Level I & Level II Bulgarian Bag Certifications in California), one thing always stands out—how much intelligent training you can get out of such a simple tool.

 

We put in a ton of practice. The kind that builds true functional strength—rotational control, grip endurance, and core stability.

 

And the best part? Participants wake up the next day feeling better, not wrecked. More mobile, strong, and connected, instead of beaten down. That’s the kind of training that translates beyond the gym and into life.

 

Have Questions?

If you’re wondering how the Bulgarian Bag can fit into your training for rotation, grip, and muscular endurance, reply to this email—I’ll get back to you in the coming days.

 

Stay strong,

 

Yours in Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

PS

If you want to get rolling training with the Bulgarian Bag on your own, for the next 48 hours, I’m offering 30% off my 30-day Bulgarian Bag program inside Athleticism 4Life (A4L).

 

Use code ROTATION at checkout, by clicking here.

name: Creating Structure
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

During a unique time like this, when there is lots of fear and uncertainty going on, I can fully understand how challenging it is to maintain some sort of structure in life.

 

One thing I do know, however, is that it couldn’t be more important to take care of our physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual health right now. 

 

To support you, I wanted to share a few updates and practices that may help.

 

While the quarantine is in effect, I will be going live daily at 9:30am PST

 (11:30am CST / 12:30pm EST) and offering free movement and resiliency sessions on Instagram Live @Mike.Salemi. So far, people from around the world have been joining, and I'd love to see you there too!

 

Each of these sessions will require minimal equipment and involve things like bodyweight training, single kettlebell training, stretching, active mediation, and more.

 

Although each day at 9:30amPST these sessions will be live, the recordings will be up for 24 hours so you can watch them at a later time. Also, I am working on filming short snippets of the movement sessions and putting them on my main Instagram feed so that even beyond the 24 hour window, you can still catch them.

 

I am here with you, and more than ever I believe that self-discipline is needed for our overall health. 

That's why on Wednesday, March 25th, I am bringing on close friend and Former UFC Fighter Charlie “The Spaniard” Brenneman for what we are calling "Train & Hang" with Charlie and Mike. Charlie is the epitome of a disciplined athlete and human and I've always admired his high level of self-discipline. On IG at @Mike.Salemi, Charlie will lead us through a ~20-minute bodyweight workout, and we'll follow this up with a conversation on the topic of discipline. 

 

And tomorrow, Tuesday at 4:30pm PST (6:30pmCST & 7:30pmEST), I will be going live on his Instagram, @charliespaniard, where we'll be discussing mindset and happiness. I would love to have you join!

 

On a related note, one thing I was reflecting upon this morning was that since childhood, I've always been quite structured in the pursuit of goals and dreams.  I even recall in middle school, I'd get SO excited when the school would hand us our yearly planners. I would organize my day, weeks, and months and create a structured plan for the success I wanted to experience. This habit has carried over into my training and is something I've continued for years via my workout logs. 

 

I am attaching here a downloadable PDF I created as a gift you can print out and place on your desk, fridge, or kitchen counter. It is a blank fillable weekly calendar to help you create more structure in your day while being at home. 

 

Below you will find a link to an excellent blog post and accompanying video from Holistic Health Practitioner Paul Chek. It is full of practical tips covering what you can do for yourself right now health wise.

Click here to read and watch.

 

Also, here is an article that a colleague of mine, Danielle Cook Kawash, RD created, which has lots of gems in it that you can use to improve your immune system.

 

I hope any and/or all of these resources aid in the flow of your day, help ground you, and promote greater stability, health and wellbeing.

 

Let this be a time for reflection, family, self-care, and one where we come out stronger than when we came in.

 

To Racap:

Every day receive free health and performance sessions at 9:30am PST on  Instagram Live @Mike.Salemi
Tuesday 3/24 check out @charliespaniard's Instagram for our conversation on mindset and happiness.
Wednesday 3/25 join Charlie and I as we “Train & Hang” for a bodyweight workout and talk discipline
Download the attached free daily & weekly PDF planner I've created to support you in creating more positive structure in your life to help you thrive
View Paul Chek Blog for health tips related to the Coronavirus
View Registered Dietician and Health Coach, Danielle Cook Kawash's blog article on things you can do to boost your immune system.

 

Sending good energy to you and your family,

Mike

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

"I feel like I've lost myself over the years. I don't even know who I am anymore."

 

I've heard this numerous times from men in my groups—and I’ve been there myself. Life transitions like fatherhood, career shifts, breakups, and injuries can leave you feeling disconnected from your fire, your passion, and even your sense of self.
