name: Primal Reset
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

This past weekend, I co-led a men’s workshop deep in the redwoods—a space I return to again and again because it strips away the noise and reveals what’s real. But this time, something was different.

 

The land itself felt like it was in transition—cloudy, quiet, holding something just beneath the surface. And as I spoke with the men who showed up, I saw the same.

 

There was a theme of being caught in the loop of working hard, providing, and achieving—yet feeling deeply frustrated and angry when it led to undesirable and even dysfunctional results. Some felt like they were failing as fathers or partners. Others were realizing that success on paper wasn’t bringing them the joy, clarity, or fulfillment they had expected. And yet, a part of them kept repeating the cycle—because they had grown so accustomed to the familiar feeling of "failing" that they had become addicted to the shame that came with it.

Before hiking in silence, I shared something simple but powerful:

 

The difference between processing vs. dwelling.

 

Dwelling is the downward spiral—shame, blame, control, running the same script over and over again. Processing is different. It’s about fully feeling what’s real while staying connected to yourself, your heart, and your direction forward—not getting stuck in the past.

 

I felt it in myself, too. My son had been sick with a cold for weeks, sleep had been rough, responsibilities shifted—and yet, just five hours in nature, breathing, moving, and being with men, gave me the space to recalibrate.

 

This is what so many men are missing.

 

Which is why, this May, I’m hosting The Primal Reset Retreat—a four-day experience in Mount Shasta, CA in collaboration with Tim Corcoran, a masterful guide with over 50 years of experience leading men through wilderness rites of passage.

 

We’ll be:

Learning RAD survival skills like fire-making and primal movement—reconnecting with our bodies and instincts.
Going on a mini half day vision quest—a guided experience that presses pause on the relentless pace of life so you can hear what’s next.
Sitting around the fire in deep conversation—no filters, no distractions, just real brotherhood.
Breaking the patterns that have kept you stuck

This isn’t a retreat where you check out of life. It’s one where you step back in—with clarity, presence, and a fire inside you that you haven’t felt in a long time.

 

Dates: Saturday to Tuesday, May 17-20
Accommodations: Handmade teepees or cabins
Bring a friend: Significant discount for both of you

 

Because we’re staying on the land, the cost of this retreat is lower than my usual Men of Movement retreats—but this is still a high-level experience for men ready to go deep. If you feel called to this, don’t wait.

 

The best way to know if this is for you? Let’s talk.


Reply to this email with "I'm Interested" and I'll send you my calendar link to hop on a call. 

 

We all need a reset. I needed it this past week, and I have no doubt you do, too.

 

Let’s do it right.

 

Yours in Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

PS – If this is calling to you, reply with “I’m Interested,” and I’ll send over my calendar link so we can connect. No pressure—just a conversation to see if this is the right experience for you.

name: Primal Reset clone
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

If you're like me, you spend so much time managing life—emails, schedules, notifications.

 

And if we're not mindful, we forget what it feels like to be in life.

 

Nature doesn’t run on to-do lists. The river isn’t rushing to its next meeting. The mountain isn’t trying to be anything other than what it is.

 

And at your deepest core, neither are you.

 

The problem is, most men don’t realize how disconnected they’ve become until they step outside of it. Until they take their shoes off, put their feet in the dirt, and feel something they haven’t felt in years—presence.

 

Science backs this up. Studies show that time in nature lowers cortisol, improves nervous system function, and enhances cognitive clarity. But you don’t need a study to tell you that something shifts when you spend real time outdoors—away from distractions, fully immersed.

 

When you step outside of the noise, something shifts. Your breath slows. Your body settles. And the stress you’ve been carrying starts to feel… like it was never yours to hold in the first place.

 

This isn’t just relaxation. It’s a full-system reset.

 

One practice I've committed to at least once a day is getting outside with my feet in the dirt while breathing consciously.

 

Sometimes this happens when the sun rises. Other times, I eat my lunch outside. And sometimes, I’ll just hang with my pup after work. It could be as little as 60 seconds or as long as an hour or two, depending on my day. But no matter what, I make sure it happens at least once.

 

What I’ve noticed is that my body and spirit crave more of it. That’s why, often in between meetings, I’ll head outside—even for a few seconds. Think of it like the minimum effective dose.

 

I’ve never given someone a 60-second feet-in-the-dirt challenge and had them regret it. Every single time, they’ve said how good it felt. And more often than not, they stayed longer and found creative ways to be outside—to ground, reset, and break out of old patterns.

 

But if you can’t see yourself stepping away from the computer, trust me—start small. Just 60 seconds, at the same time each day for a minimum of 7 days. See what kind of momentum and benefits that creates over time.

 

Try it. You won’t regret it.

 

In Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

We don’t talk enough about the role of elders.


Not just older men—but true elders.

 

The kind of men who’ve spent decades listening to the land.


Who speak with clarity because they’ve been shaped by fire, failure, and solitude.


Men who carry stories that don’t come from books—but from experience.

In traditional cultures, elders weren’t just advisors.


They were initiators. Witnesses. Truth tellers.


They were the ones who marked the turning point between boyhood and manhood—not with shame, but with honor.

 

And for most of us… that moment never came.

 

There’s a story from Lakota tradition about Crazy Horse. As a young man, he went into the wilderness alone for a vision quest. Four days—no food, no distractions—just him, the land, and his prayers. On the final day, he was given a vision that shaped the man he would become: a humble, untouchable protector of his people.

 

When he returned, his community welcomed him back—not just as a boy, but as a man. That kind of recognition lives in the bones.

 

We don’t grow like that today.


But we can.

 

That’s why I'd like to share something with you.

 

There’s a man I know and highly respect—Tim Corcoran, founder of Headwaters Outdoor School.


Tim is what most men have never experienced: a real elder.

 

He’s lived in deep relationship with the land for over six decades.


He’s mentored thousands—young and old—through earth-based teachings, ancestral skills, and personal transformation rooted in nature.

Tim doesn’t need to impress anyone. He’s walked a path of simplicity, strength, and clarity—and you can feel it the moment you meet him. He teaches by presence more than words. And when he does speak, you listen.

 

This spring, I’ve teamed up with  Tim to guide a group of men in a powerful weekend immersion in Mt. Shasta on his sacred land.

 

This experience is a return...a return to something deeper.

 

And if you’ve never had the opportunity to sit with an elder… it’s time.

 

Reply to this email with "ELDER" and I'll get you more info on our May 17-20 special event with Tim and me.

 

In Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi

name: Primal Reset clone clone clone
text:
Hi {first_name},


You went to bed on time.
You clocked your 8 hours.
Maybe even hit “optimal” on your sleep tracker.

 

But you wake up… already tense.
Already behind.
Already in fight mode before your feet hit the ground.

 

If that’s happening, it’s not because you need more sleep.
It’s because your system isn’t getting what it actually needs to recover.

 

Here’s the truth: a lot of high-performing people are stuck in survival mode—and they don’t even know it.

 

Your body might be in bed… but it’s not resting.
It’s still competing.
Still trying to solve.
Still defending.

 

That’s what I call nervous system debt.
And here’s what might be stacking it for you:

 

1. You never hit the brakes.
Even when you stop working, you’re still mentally grinding.

 

Your eyes are closed, but your mind is rehearsing.
You’re running through conversations, deadlines, what-ifs, and worst-case scenarios.

 

You wake up already overstimulated—because you never really dropped out of go-mode. And if your body never gets that “you’re safe now” signal, it can’t let go. It can’t repair. And you start the day already in the red.

 

2. You’re breathing through your mouth while you sleep.
Dry mouth in the morning? That’s not nothing.

 

It means your system is in a mild state of stress all night.
Instead of restoring—your body is just trying to stay afloat.

 

That kind of breathing leads to lighter sleep, less oxygen absorption, and way more morning fatigue. You’re getting sleep… but not depth.

 

3. You’re inflamed—but used to it.
This is the sneaky one.


If your last meal is too close to bedtime (and full of less than ideal foods)—or you’re hitting caffeine late in the day—you’re not setting yourself up to restore.

 

You’re spiking cortisol when it should be winding down.
Your digestion is working overtime.
And your brain never fully gets to shut down and clear out.

 

4. You’re either overtraining… or not moving at all.
If your workouts are too intense, frequent, or unbalanced with no real recovery, you’ll wake up drained.


And if you haven’t moved enough throughout the day, your body holds that stagnant energy overnight.

 

The result’s the same: You wake up groggy, stiff, or wired.

 

The real issue?

For men, they often wait until something breaks.
They normalize tension. They normalize poor sleep.
They tell themselves “it’s just a busy season.”

But for many of you, that “season” has lasted years.

 

So here’s the invitation:

Start paying attention.
To how you feel in the morning.
To how your body actually recovers—not just how long you were in bed.

You don’t need more hacks.


You need to give your system what it’s actually asking for:
Rhythm. Stillness. Breath. Boundaries.

Not forever. Just enough to reset.


This week on the podcast, I go deep into this (and 4 other signs your system’s heading toward burnout). It’s a solo episode—raw and real.

 

In Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi

There’s a pattern I see in a lot of high-functioning people—especially the ones who carry a lot of responsibility, often without saying a word.

 

They’re the ones others rely on.
They’re steady. Reliable. Always there.
They hold space. They hold tension. They hold it all together.

 

And over time, it starts to wear on them.
Not always in loud, dramatic ways.
But in small, persistent ones—the tension that won’t release, the breath that doesn’t quite go all the way in, the growing sense that something’s off.

 

Being the person everyone relies on comes with a cost.
And if that cost isn’t acknowledged, it gets paid through the body, the relationships, the sleep, the joy.

 

Let’s slow this down and look at it.

 

The Pattern Beneath the Pressure

This pattern often shows up in people who take pride in being dependable, helpful, high-achieving.

 

In the Enneagram, this maps onto Type 2s and Type 3s.
You don’t need to know the system to relate to it—just see if this lands:

For Type 2s, the inner drive is often: “If I’m not helping, I’m not valuable.”
For Type 3s: “If I’m not achieving, I’ll lose love or respect.”

So their identity becomes tied to being the one others lean on.
And while that can be a beautiful strength, it can also come at the cost of their own inner life.

 

A Moment I Won’t Forget

At a retreat I was leading, a man in circle said,

“I’m the guy everyone leans on. But I don’t know who’s got me.”

 

That sentence landed hard.


Not because it was unique—but because it was so common.
Every man in that room understood it.
So did I.

 

And chances are, so do many reading this right now.

 

The Body Always Knows

When the nervous system is wired for constant responsibility, it never really turns off.
Even when things are quiet, there’s still a low-level hum underneath. A readiness. A bracing.

 

It often shows up as:

Chronic muscle tension
Shallow breathing
A hard time sleeping
A vague sense of restlessness or resentment

It’s not failure.
It’s the body speaking—asking for a different rhythm.

 

Leadership That Includes You

One of the shifts I guide people through is learning how to lead in a way that includes themselves.

 

That means:

Letting yourself be supported
Learning to regulate without shutting down
Moving from performance into presence

As Connor Beaton puts it:
“Your capacity to lead is only as strong as your capacity to be held.”

 

This is what we train through breath, through movement, and through embodied community.

 

A Reminder That Matters

If your leadership is costing you your aliveness, your peace, or your relationships—it’s not leadership.
It’s sacrifice.

 

You can show up for others without disappearing in the process.
You can be dependable without being depleted.

 

A Simple Reflection

Here’s something worth sitting with today:

Where in your life are you still carrying it all—without allowing yourself to be carried?

 

It’s okay to need support.
It’s okay to not have it all together.
It’s okay to be human.

 

In Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

This is a space to drop the weight, reconnect to your body, and remember who you are without all the noise.
Click here to learn more and grab your spot.

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Most men don’t realize how much they need to unplug—until they do.

 

“I didn’t realize how much I needed this kind of reset—until I got out there.”

 

That’s what I keep hearing from guys after just one day on the land.

name: Everyone Relies on You clone
text:
Hi {first_name},




There’s a reason you feel more tired after scrolling your phone.
There’s a reason you feel more restless after spending a day indoors.




We weren’t designed for the constant noise we live in today — the notifications, the deadlines, the bright screens, the endless inputs.
We were built for the rhythms of the earth.
For sunrises and seasons. For breath and movement. For real connection — to the land, to each other, and to ourselves.




Tim Corcoran, who I’m honored to co-lead my upcoming retreat with, has spent decades guiding men back to these natural rhythms.
He’s the founder of Headwaters Outdoor School in Mt. Shasta and the author of The Earth Caretaker Way — but what matters most is that Tim walks the path himself — rooted, humble, and deeply connected to the land.




He teaches that the body has a memory older than civilization.
It remembers the language of the wind.
It knows the feeling of belonging to the land — not owning it, not managing it, but being a part of it.




When we stay too long in the human-made world, we lose touch with this ancient memory. We begin to mistake busyness for purpose, stimulation for connection, and comfort for vitality.




When life gets too loud, it’s easy to think we need to do more to fix it.



Sometimes, the real medicine is not doing more — it’s creating enough space to finally hear yourself again.


Nature doesn’t yell.
It doesn’t rush.
It doesn’t perform.
It simply is — and when we’re close enough, we start to remember that we are too.

And when you taste that kind of clarity again, it changes the way you move through the rest of your life.




In Health & Happiness,




Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S. This May 17-20th, Tim and I are holding sacred space for men to step away from the noise and reawaken that deeper memory inside. The Primal Reset Retreat isn’t about escape — it’s about reconnection.
If you feel the pull, let’s talk — simply shoot a response to this email and we'll link up for a 30 minute call.

name: Everyone Relies on You clone clone
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Ever get to the end of the day and realize you were moving all day…
…but not actually connected to any of it?

 

You knocked out the tasks.
You showed up for your people.
You kept it all moving.

 

But somewhere in the background, there’s this low hum of disconnection — like your body’s in one place, your mind’s in another, and your spirit’s… on hold.

 

I know that feeling well.

 

And I’ve learned something that’s been opening up new space for me — slowly, quietly, but powerfully.

 

Not every answer comes through thinking.
Some only come when you stop long enough to listen.

 

I want to share something I’ve been exploring — a simple practice called the sit spot.


It’s something I’ve seen Tim Corcoran teach with reverence, and something I’ve started integrating into my own rhythm — not perfectly, but intentionally.

 

Here’s what it is:

You pick a spot in nature — ideally the same place each time.
You go there. And you sit.

That’s it.

 

You could journal, track your breathing, etc.
However, there are going to be many times when the deepest medicine is simply observing.
Presence. Listening. Being.

 

At first, it’s uncomfortable.
I’ve noticed my mind wanting to wander, to fill the space.
But over time — even just a few sessions in — something begins to shift.

 

The pace of the land takes over.
Your breath finds a different rhythm.
And what’s most alive in you starts to surface.

 

Tim teaches that the sit spot isn’t about “tuning out.”
It’s about tuning in — to the land, yes, but also to the parts of you that get buried in the pressure to perform.

 

The more I’ve leaned into it, the more I’ve realized how rare it is for men — especially high-performing men — to simply sit and receive.

But that’s where a deeper kind of clarity lives.

 

Not the kind that comes from a list.
The kind that arrives — when you finally give it space.

 

 

In Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Leadership Coach, & Host of The Path Podcast

P.S.
We’ll be carving out time for this exact kind of practice at the Primal Reset Retreat in Mt. Shasta — including a guided solo land sit led by Tim. Simply respond to this email for details.


And whether you join us or not, I invite you to try it:
Go outside. Sit. Stay.
See what comes up when you stop reaching for answers.

name: Luca and Langauge
text:
Hi {first_name},




When I stepped into fatherhood, I thought I’d be the one doing the teaching.




Turns out—I’m the one being taught.




Every day, my son Luca reveals something new. Sometimes it’s subtle. Sometimes it stops me in my tracks. But what’s becoming more and more clear is just how much this experience is shaping me, not the other way around.




Lately, what’s been coming into sharp focus is how deeply our language—especially the kind we don’t even realize we use—shapes the world around us.




Not just in what we say.
But in how we think, choose, and act.





Because while embodiment is paramount…
Language is one of the key levers that either keeps us stuck or moves us forward.




Now that Luca’s speech is really coming online, I’m watching him pick up not only new words, but new patterns. From me.




Just the other day I asked him if he wanted to go to the park.
He paused and said:
“I guess so… maybe.”




Not a strong yes. Not a no.
Just a soft, uncertain middle ground.
And I could hear it clearly—it wasn’t coming from him.
It was a regurgitation of my words. My patterns.




I’ve used those same phrases in passing, without even thinking.
And now here they were, reflected back to me in his tiny voice.




He’s not just learning to speak.
He’s learning how I speak.
He’s picking up on the way I make decisions.
How I express uncertainty.
How I carry myself in small, day-to-day moments.




And it’s not just about him.

It’s about the reflection he’s giving me—of my own internal dialogue.
My own unconscious language habits.
The ones that sound like:

“I should probably…”
“I think I can…”
“It’s kind of hard…”

Left unexamined, those small phrases become the script.
And the script becomes the story.
And the story becomes the life we live inside of.




This is one of the deepest gifts of fatherhood.
It’s not just about protecting or providing.
It’s about seeing—really seeing—the patterns we carry, and doing the work to shift them so the next generation doesn’t have to.




Because we don’t just pass down traits.
We pass down tone.
We pass down tendencies.
We pass down storylines.




The stories we don’t resolve get recycled.
The words we speak, especially the ones spoken on autopilot, become the environment our children grow up in.




And that’s why I’ve been paying close attention to my language.
Not just for him, but for me.
For the younger version of me that didn’t have this level of awareness.
For the man I’m becoming by choosing a different script.




So here’s something simple to try this week:

Speak like someone is learning how to live from your example.
Because someone is.
Whether it’s your child, your partner, your team—or the younger part of yourself still waiting to be led with clarity.




The words you use shape the space you live in.
Choose them with care.
Choose them with presence.
And when you can—choose the ones that move you (and those you love) forward.




If you ever want support in working through your language or your stories, just reach out—this is the kind of work I love doing with clients.





In Health & Happiness,




Mike Salemi

name: Weights Can't Fix
text:
Hi {first_name},




I grew up in the gym.




It’s where I felt strong. Safe. In control.
And for most of my life, movement has been my medicine.




It’s helped me process pain, regulate stress, stay focused, and build the kind of discipline I’m proud of.




But I’ve also used it to avoid what I wasn’t ready to face.




There were times I’d be in the gym 6–7 days a week—not because my body needed it, but because I didn’t know how to be with the stuff underneath.
The restlessness. The grief. The anger I didn’t have words for.
Movement was my way to not feel those things. And on the surface, it looked healthy.




But here’s what I’ve learned:
Even something as powerful as training can become an escape when we don’t know what to do with our inner world.




This isn’t a knock on working out—I still train hard, and I’ll always believe in the power of physical expression.




But I’m also asking better questions now. Questions like:

Am I moving to connect… or to avoid?
What’s the emotional charge I’m carrying into this workout?
What’s one thing I haven’t slowed down enough to feel this week?
If I had no training today, where would my tension go?

These aren’t comfortable questions—but they’re the ones that change everything.




Because your vitality isn’t just in your deadlift.


It’s in your presence. Your honesty. Your ability to feel and not flinch.




This is the work we do inside The Vital Man Collective. Movement. Breath. Language. Embodiment. And a brotherhood that doesn’t just spot you in the gym—but in life.




If this speaks to you, reply to this email or check out the Strongman Scoreboard. It’s a free 15-minute self-check-in that might show you something you didn’t even know was driving you.




In Health & Happiness,




Mike Salemi

name: Weights Can't Fix clone
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Stillness is one of the most overlooked practices in men’s development.

 

When people talk about “doing the work,” they usually point to emotional expression, i.e. feeling your feelings, getting vulnerable, softening. And for many men, especially those raised to believe emotions make you weak, that work is absolutely necessary.

 

But feeling alone isn’t the full picture. It’s often incomplete without something more foundational: stillness.

 

Stillness is not passive. It’s not zoning out. It’s not a spa-day luxury. It’s a masculine discipline. A way to build presence, sharpen your focus, and reconnect to what actually matters. It’s about slowing down enough to meet what’s real, without escaping or distracting.

 

The truth is, most ambitious men resist stillness. They feel like they’re wasting time. Like they’re losing ground. Like if they’re not moving, they’re falling behind.

 

But here’s what I’ve seen, especially in the men who committed to this inside the men's group I assist alongside Ted Riter called The Wisdom Circle over the last six months. The ones who chose meditation or a daily stillness practice are showing up in a completely different way.

 

They’re calmer. More grounded.
They’re having the hard conversations. Following through.
They’re leading with clarity, not chaos.
They’re not reaching for energy drinks or blood sugar spikes to stay in motion.
They’re not reactive. They’re steady.

 

And it didn’t take hours of meditation to get there. They just built the muscle one small rep at a time.

 

Here are two simple ways to start your own stillness practice:

1. Sit Completely Still

Find a quiet space, ideally outside.
Sit upright and set a timer for 3 minutes.
Don’t move. No scratching, fidgeting, adjusting.
Just breathe. Listen. Feel what’s present.
When your mind wanders (and it will), come back to stillness.

 

This might be the hardest thing you do all day, and the most powerful. You’re not trying to clear your mind. You’re training your nervous system to stay with what is.

 

2. 3-Minute Body Scan

Sit or lie down somewhere comfortable with your eyes closed.
Bring your attention to the crown of your head.
Slowly scan down your body, part by part: jaw, chest, belly, legs, feet.
At each point, simply ask: What do I feel here?
You’re not trying to fix anything. Just notice.
If your mind drifts, gently return to the body.

 

This reconnects you to sensation. It gets you out of your head and into your body, which is where your actual power lives.

 

Stillness builds the kind of leadership most men never access.

 

It creates space to hear what’s really going on inside you. It builds the capacity to hold yourself steady, and to hold those around you when it matters most.

 

If you want to lead with presence, start here.

 

In Health & Happiness,

 

Mike Salemi

name: Beta Launch 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

One thing I’ve reflected upon this week is that I’m in a pretty good spot with my training right now. 

 

You see, I’ve found some things that work for me over the years and, definitely not to brag, but it’s rare that I feel that any training or fitness goal is out of reach...

 

Obviously, flashback. 

 

Because it wasn’t always this way. 

 

Sometimes you hit a plateau with your abilities, then you figure something out, and you "breakthrough" and keep making progress.

 

But what happens when you keep hitting plateaus? 

 

You feel like you’ve solved it… 

 

You’re on your way now… 

 

Then...the same issue crops up. 

 

"But I thought I solved this already!" 

 

If that sounds familiar, welcome to my world a few years back. 

 

When I was competing heavily in Kettlebell Sport, I experienced a forearm and shoulder injury that kept me from reaching my goal of winning the WAKSC World Championships and attaining the elite rank, “Master of Sport”. While this particular injury specifically showed up during my training with Kettlebells, even before this I was prone to overtraining and injuries. 

 

It’s devastating to train so hard month in and month out for a specific goal and continually fall short no matter the effort. I was following a strict training program to the T, and was seeking out nearly every quality practitioner and therapist I could find for years, yet with no significant success. 

 

At wit’s end, something had occurred to me: 

 

"What if there’s a single skill set that could tie all these issues I was having together into a unique solution: a meta-skill?”

 

THAT, I discovered, was exactly what I was looking for: 

 

Long term high performance needs to be multi-faceted because as human beings we are individual and unique from one another.  We need a flexible training approach that considers the entire person - what we eat, how we sleep, how we breathe, how we train, how we recover, and more. 

 

These principles I now know were the key to my progress. 

 

"If I can get this right," I thought, "it could make everything else better… 

 

...but as long as I keep getting it wrong I’m going to keep getting the same things wrong." 

 

Developing my "Meta Skill" entailed diving as deep as possible to understand holistic high performance and create training programs that were incredibly effective, dynamic in nature, and could modify based on how myself, and my clients, were feeling on a given day. This key information would serve as the guide for how hard to go, and how much to back off in training - a major key to longevity in any sport or activity. 

 

With this Skill, I ended up going 100% “kettlebell geek" and 1000% scientific simultaneously! 

 

And two things happened: 

 

1. I discovered that to really build a lean, and functional body that can last for years you need to get super specific and consider: self-awareness, mobility, technique training, phased programming, recovery, active meditation, community AND have an overall flexible program that meets you where you’re at on a given day.  

 

2. My fitness progression had completely changed. I'd gone from being frustrated with fixed workout plans to the opposite. I figured out the key factors that determined what kind of workout I should do on any given day and my results skyrocketed. I could finally boost my fitness, mobility, mindset, and more and avoid training plateaus. 

 

You may already know where this is headed: 

 

Based on personal experience as an athlete and coach to now thousands of people, I set out to give my customers the same experience I had: a focused and longevity based kettlebell program with a single purpose: 

 

Taking you by-the-hand, and leading you, step-by-step, to realizing your potential both in and out of the gym. 

 

After more thought, this program would have to be something that is completely yours, your own custom plan. 

 

It would have to be easy-to-do, and fit into short daily routines and training programs that were under 60 minutes from the moment you put on your minimalist type shoes ; ) to get in the shower and rinse off that well-earned sweat from training. 

 

...additionally,  it would have to have transformational results. 

 

This program is now known as Kettlebell Lifestyle.

 

And it is quickly becoming the most popular all-around functional at-home training program available. 

 

Here’s just a taste of the feedback we got from first-time users: 
 

“Job well done! Kettlebell Lifestyle is absolutely incredible. I’m blown away by its beauty, ease of use, layout, and quality of the coaching and content. This is by far the best online program I have seen on the market. Your hard work and efforts deserve the utmost recognition because this program is a true gift to the fitness community and I am so thankful.” —  Amanda R., Personal Trainer

 

“I would’ve paid you 100 fold just for the stretching. Seriously. Never in my life have I looked forward to stretching. Best part is, none of them are unknown. I was doing these in high school football but now I know what sensation to feel for. You’re a genius.”  — Mark D., Fire Fighter

 

Here’s where I’m going with this: 

 

We’re finally re-opening the beta phase of Kettlebell Lifestyle to the public beginning tomorrow...but only for a short time. 

 

I’ll be back tomorrow with many more details. 

 

For now, if you’ve imagined how much faster you could build a lean, functional body that feels as good as it looks, just mark your calendar ;) 

 

See you tomorrow, 

Mike

name: Beta Launch 2
text:
{first_name}, Want to experience the benefits of a custom training program while you can’t go to the gym? Then you'll absolutely love this! 

 

Kettlebell Lifestyle is a 9 week personalized, multi-level kettlebell, and wellness program. This program will teach you a variety of exciting kettlebell exercises such as: Swing Variations, Squats, Presses, Combination Movements, Cleans, Rotational Movements, elements of the Turkish GetUp, and much more.

 

Also included are morning routines, personalized stretching plans, bodyweight warm-ups, 7 follow-along kettlebell workouts, skill development sessions, detailed exercise tutorials, working in exercises, and bonus lifestyle content from industry experts.

 

The main goals of Kettlebell Lifestyle are to empower you to become highly proficient with a kettlebell, AND give you the tools, tips, and strategies to become fit, healthy, mobile, and resilient today and for years to come.

 

Now, I understand that we don’t all have unlimited time, and that’s why this program has been structured in a very unique way. Due to it being so lifestyle-focused, the program has numerous components such as the morning routines that can be done in less than 10 minutes a day, 18-minute bodyweight joint warm-ups, and under 30-minute kettlebell focused workouts. While the program does layout complete days of training and recovery, you can pick any individual aspect you choose, and based on your time commitment for the day, you can do as little or as much as you like. 

 

Simply put, in minutes of consistent effort each day, this program is going to completely change the way your body looks, feels, and performs. Not to mention you’ll learn LOTS about what a balanced training program should look and feel like.

 

I’ve been teaching fitness and performance now for over 15 years… and for the next 9 weeks, I’m looking for eager people that are willing to put in the hard work and dedication to get the results I know you can achieve. 

 

It won’t be overwhelming… you’re going to know exactly what to do… how long to do it for… and I’ll be with you every step of the way. 

 

In a nutshell, I’ll be your personal performance coach. 

 

Kettlebell Lifestyle [BETA] opens to the public today at 11amPST. 

 

If you’re serious about changing your health, wellness, and performance trajectory forever, don’t miss this opportunity. 

 

Watch for another email in the coming hours - it’ll have a special link you can use to get in on the special. 

 

See you then! 

Mike

name: Beta Launch 3
text:
Hi {first_name},

Just moments ago we opened the doors to Kettlebell Lifestyle [BETA] to the public again... 

 

Sign up between today and the next 7 days, and you’ll get TWO exclusive bonuses.

 

Bonus #1: Group Coaching 

 

Kettlebell Lifestyle group coaching calls are currently underway and happen for 10 total weeks (we are currently on week 4 and recordings are released 24 hours after each call which you will receive). These calls are filled with amazing like-minded and hearted people from around the world interested in creating deep levels of positive change. In each call myself, and Kettlebell Jedi Dr. Drew Vercellino, answer your questions, offer a training/lifestyle teaching segment (last week was RAD btw, and students received a technical analysis of two important lifts), and celebrate your wins for the week.  

 

This bonus has a value of $2500...which you will get for free only if you join within these next 7 days. 

 

Bonus #2: Private Facebook Community

 

To be honest, this Facebook community we’ve been building since the initial beta-launch has become one of my favorite value adds. Seeing incredible people support one another each day, as well as receive valuable coaching tips from Dr. Drew and myself makes this group something extra special. 

 

Now, if you’re anything like I was, you can probably get pretty good at strength training by consuming things on YouTube and reading books… 

 

...but eventually you’re going to feel “stuck”. 

 

And it can be frustrating, because what got you to this point, won’t get you any further. 

 

It’s like downloading a big photo with a dial-up internet speed. First, you get the image in low-resolution… 

 

...and, if you can stand a few feet away and squint at it, it looks pretty good. 

 

But then the image would gradually, row-by-row, enhance. 

 

By the end, you’d have a high-resolution image that looked good even close up. 

 

If you’re sharp, you’ve probably picked up two things: 

 

The first is that a generic done for you workout program is like downloading an image over a dial-up connection. 

 

In the first stages, you’re making big, messy strides, and practically everything you try will work. 

 

Eventually, you reach a point where most of the easy wins are gone. 

 

You now need to go back, and pay attention to detail. 

 

And it’s exactly what Kettlebell Lifestyle is designed to do. 

 

We’ll take one step at a time, so you can see progress build and build. 

 

Unlike trying to slam protein shakes (not my preference haha) or spending hours in the gym, Kettlebell Lifestyle is hyper-focused on this goal: 

 

Applying an individualized, holistic workout program to accelerate full-body functional training and longevity - it truly makes all the guesswork disappear. 

 

You can’t help but make progress if you commit and trust the process... 

 

Oh, and did I mention that the entire program was designed to be done if all you have is just ONE, single kettlebell?! Yup that’s right!

 

But we’re closing the doors SOON... this all ends on May 6th at 11am PST... and the Bonuses will not be offered again. 

 

To make sure you grab Kettlebell Lifestyle [BETA] for lifetime access before the doors close, use this exclusive link for the Group Coaching, Private Facebook Community, and for details and sign up: 

 

www.kettlebelllifestyle.com/pre-order

 

See you inside! 

 

Mike

Now, if you’re anything like I was, you can probably get pretty good at strength training by consuming things on YouTube and reading books… 

 

...but eventually you’re going to feel “stuck”. 

 

And it can be frustrating, because what got you to this point, won’t get you any further. 

 

It’s like downloading a big photo with a dial-up internet speed. First, you get the image in low-resolution… 

 

...and, if you can stand a few feet away and squint at it, it looks pretty good. 

 

But then the image would gradually, row-by-row, enhance. 

 

By the end, you’d have a high-resolution image that looked good even close up. 

 

If you’re sharp, you’ve probably picked up two things: 

 

The first is that a generic done for you workout program is like downloading an image over a dial-up connection. 

 

In the first stages, you’re making big, messy strides, and practically everything you try will work. 

 

Eventually, you reach a point where most of the easy wins are gone. 

 

You now need to go back, and pay attention to detail. 

 

And it’s exactly what Kettlebell Lifestyle is designed to do. 

 

We’ll take one step at a time, so you can see progress build and build. 

 

Unlike trying to slam protein shakes (not my preference haha) or spending hours in the gym, Kettlebell Lifestyle is hyper-focused on this goal: 

 

Applying an individualized, holistic workout program to accelerate full-body functional training and longevity - it truly makes all the guesswork disappear. 

 

You can’t help but make progress if you commit and trust the process... 

 

Oh, and did I mention that the entire program was designed to be done if all you have is just ONE, single kettlebell?! Yup that’s right!

 

But we’re closing the doors SOON... this all ends on May 6th at 11am PST... and the Bonuses will not be offered again. 

 

To make sure you grab Kettlebell Lifestyle [BETA] for lifetime access before the doors close, use this exclusive link for the Group Coaching, Private Facebook Community, and for details and sign up: 

 

www.kettlebelllifestyle.com/pre-order

 

See you inside! 

 

Mike

Is that you? Because if so I am prepared to go all-in on your success.

 

BUT… if not, I totally understand. You see, this program is not for everyone and I’m ok with that. 

 

“Who is program is NOT for?”

Anyone looking for random kettlebell workouts. OR those uninterested in learning the whys behind their movement, training, and wellness as a whole.

 

“So then, who IS it for exactly?”

Kettlebell Lifestyle is an intensive (though not time-intensive, as I’ll explain below) system for gym-goers and movement enthusiasts. It quickly delivers a custom full-body strength & mobility solution, all without starving yourself, killing you in training, or telling you to ignore your internal wisdom to know how hard to go and how much to back off.

 

From constantly hitting plateaus, dealing with injuries & lack of mobility… 

 

...to crushing your strength goals WHILE your mobility soars! 

 

I’d recommend this program to anyone who feels "stuck" at their current level... 

 

...or who is killing it, but just wants that extra edge a "fitness overhaul" like this can provide...

 

"But Mike, will this even work for me?" 

The way the program has been constructed, with a Level I (beginner) and Level II  (intermediate) option, the program is not only for any skill level, but was also created in a way that you can go through it multiple times and continually get better and better results. Kettlebell Lifestyle includes multiple phases of training, each that progress you one step at a time to better health and higher performance.

 

It’s path of the balanced warrior. Are you ready?

 

"But Mike, I’m super stressed with everything happening right now in the world, will I be able to make time for everything you’ll be asking in the Program?" 

Luckily, I anticipated this. While you have well over 60 days of daily programmed movement and recovery practices in the program, you get to choose your journey each day. Even simply the morning routines or warm-ups, that took me years to fine-tune are worth the entire program itself.

HELL YEAH! Nick’s experience is not just unique to him, and as the days and weeks go on, I’ll be sharing many more comments and stories from people actually going through the program to demonstrate just how legit it really is. 

 

So if this feels like the right program for you, there are only 100 spots open and when they are gone, they are gone for good until the program officially launches in approximately 5 weeks at more than double the cost, and will no longer be available for lifetime access.

 

Visit www.kettlebelllifestyle.com to grab yours today. 

 

Excited to support you in your health and performance, 

⁠

previewHtml:
Hi {first_name},

 

My day typically starts the same way each and every day - with a specific morning routine. 

 

The purpose of this morning routine, or sometimes I refer to it as my morning ritual, is to begin each day with intention and perform the one thing that has the power to create a positive impact on everything else that follows. 

 

This particular morning routine I'm speaking of entails something that takes less than 10 minutes to perform and includes a specific warm-up for the body, as well as a sequence of simple, effective breathing exercises. 

 

I find that not only does my body feel looser following, but my energy and mental alertness increases substantially as well. 

 

This is the same routine I've done nearly daily for the last 12 months and is one I share with my one-on-one clients. 

 

If it's one thing that is super important to me, it is that whatever I share and post, has to be something that I actual do, and not simply talk about. 

 

And that's why I'm so pumped to be able to share this with you...

 

Not only does Kettlebell Lifestyle have one sub 10-minute morning routine, but it has three! There is one morning routine for each major phase of training, and each one builds upon the other. 

 

If you're looking for adding a little extra structure to your life during this time in a positive way, these are perfect for you.

 

As I write this email, there is less than 4 hours before Kettlebell Lifestyle [BETA] goes away and your chance to get access to everything in the program with lifetime access, group coaching, and the Facebook community expires.

 

Nows the time, let's DO this! :)

 

Visit: www.kettlebelllifestyle.com to sign up at more than 50% off of the price of what it will be when the program officially launches in about a month. 

 

Stay strong and swing on my friend,

name: Chek Workout #2
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

So you and I can probably agree...Paul is not like anybody else out there.

I mean… 

He's probably the only guy who can lift mammoth-sized stones...

Create works of art that move you to tears...

And talk about the meaning of our existence for what seems like an eternity.

All while wearing a pair of farmer pants and looking good while doing it.

Ok...that last bit might be a bit of stretch depending on your idea of fashion :).

But all joking aside, I've been blessed to know and train with Paul for over 7 years.

And what a magnificent and wild journey it's been (so far).

He's taught me countless lessons.

Some I applied and instantly benefited from (like the concept of working in mentioned last time).

Some I didn't really "get" until months or years down the line when I was ready to fully receive them.

Some I still meditate on to this very day.

Out of these, there are a few that really surprised me.

#1) It doesn't take extensive workouts and hours in the gym to be built like a Beast.  

Let's face it, Paul looks and moves like a beast.

I can safely say he would outperform many elite athletes out there, especially in terms of functional strength.  

Yet...I've never seen him spend more than an hour in the gym for a training session.

So what is it that separates him from anyone else?  

He is very purposeful in his training.

A lot of times, his time in the gym would only be 30 minutes.

 

But none of those 30 minutes are wasted.

 

Every rep is intentional.

 

Every set is intentional.

 

Every minute is intentional.

 

When Paul is training, there is nothing else on his mind.

 

One final thing he does is incorporate movement and strength building into the rest of his day.

 

It's not broken down into separate phases of his day...

It's a Lifestyle.

 

You can see this when he lifts and stacks stones.

 

Each session is a meditation and workout combined.

 

I mean…

 

It sort of has to be when you're lifting stones that are over 200 pounds :).


#2) It takes time to truly learn your athletes.

Even though Paul's initial assessment and program design for my body took several *hours*...

It took him another 3-5+ months(!) to deeply learn and understand my body's response to training.

I know...

That long and is there really that much of a difference?

Yep.

I could literally feel the workouts becoming more effective week by week.

Not only did my body get stronger...

I was able to learn to really feel my own body...something that only comes when you are intentional and purposeful.

I've definitely realized that coaching is as much art as it is science.

Which brings me to...

#3) Art can have a profound impact on healing and your development as an athlete.

 

Before working with Paul initially years ago in 2013...

 

I didn't know how much he used art as healing work in his personal life and professional practice.

 

You could even see a taste of that in the first workout video where we did an art piece together.

 

Why does this matter...?

 

Exercise, like art, is an outward expression of who you are.

 

So...

 

Any blocks or restrictions in either one could impact the other.

 

I've personally gotten a lot of joy, healing, connection, and exploration from the art I've created, both with Paul...

 

And the work I've done at home.

 

So how can you apply it in your own life and training?

 

Produce something every single day. 

 

It could be anything.

 

A stick figure drawing...

 

Drawing shapes and coloring those shapes...

 

A grand and epic painting of the beauty that surrounds all of us...

 

Anything.

 

The most important part of it is doing it with...

 

No judgment.

 

Give yourself permission to just create and express yourself.

Let your inner child just be.

 

If you find that you don't have the time to do it every day, 

 

You might find it helpful to incorporate it as a set in your workout...

 

Which is something that Paul and I actually did in our first workout together (again here's the link for that).

 

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

 

Having Paul as a mentor and friend has definitely been integral to who I am today...

 

It's something I'm really grateful for on the daily.

 

Speaking of being grateful...

 

Thank you so much for joining me and Paul during these two workouts.

 

If you made it all the way down here, don't think I forgot the second workout in our series :).

 

You can find it HERE.

 

I hope both workouts teach you some creative ways to use the kettlebell as well as leaving you feeling more energized and excited about your workouts.

 

Again, let me know if you have any questions.

 

Have a great rest of your day.

 

-Mike

 

P.S. just in case you missed it, here are the links to the:

 

First workout (link) and…

 

Second workout (link).

name: Perfect Morning (chek list) Email 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I don't know about you, but I used to have trouble starting my day off right.

Some days it was a struggle to "get into the groove..."

While other days, I would bounce out of bed like a lion pouncing on its prey.

Eventually, I realized that how I started my morning had a direct effect on how I felt the rest of the day.

So...over the years I've experimented with many routines to "win the day."

Everything from: meditation, working out, and visualization to affirmations, journaling, listening to music, and Qigong.

Out of everything I've tried, there was one overriding principle that led to the most success.

Whatever the routine was, it had to...

Align body, mind, and breath.

If one of these was missing, I noticed a huge decrease in the effectiveness.

If I aligned the body and the mind without the breath...

I wasn't as focused and still found myself a little flustered, especially if I was going through something stressful.

If I aligned the body and the breath without the mind...

My presence and intentions for the day were scattered.

If I aligned the breath and the mind without the body…

I would sometimes feel like a sloth that needed lubricant in his joints (although it's kind of crazy that this hasn't been the case since I've been on the carnivore diet...)

So how long does something like this take to do?

Anywhere from 5-10 minutes.

Of course, when I can, I try to do other things like journal or meditate for a longer period of time.

But, consistently doing just my foundational morning routine has been such a gamechanger for me because it is short (which makes it less intimidating to do) and primes me for the day ahead.

----------------------------------------

What does a simple example look like?

1) A glass of filtered water (I use a system from Nikken that has remineralizing stones because I'm a nerd like that :D).  Make sure to drink a bit at a time 

2) Some light movements (such as marching in place and pelvic rocks), paying special attention to expand the belly on the inhale and drawing the belly towards the spine on the exhale.

3) Box breathing - breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 4 seconds, and exhale for 4 seconds.  Again, paying special attention to expand the belly on the inhale and drawing the belly towards the spine on the exhale. Do this for about 2 minutes.

At each step, be mindful of how your body feels.  

Also, towards the end of the box breathing, visualize how the perfect day would go and...

Set an intention on how you want to show up.

 

--------------------------------------

 

Do you have a morning routine?  If so, what does it look like?

 

Hope this helps you win your mornings and, as a result, win your days!

 

-"Morning" Mike Salemi

 

P.S. if you're at all curious about the carnivore diet, I've been giving my honest thoughts on doing the "right" way (incorporating raw organ meats and nothing but pasture raised/100% grassfed/wild caught meat) on Instagram.  You can find me at @mike.salemi

I don't know about you, but I used to have trouble starting my day off right.

Some days it was a struggle to "get into the groove..."

While other days, I would bounce out of bed like a lion pouncing on its prey.

Eventually, I realized that how I started my morning had a direct effect on how I felt the rest of the day.

So...over the years I've experimented with many routines to "win the day."

Everything from: meditation, working out, and visualization to affirmations, journaling, listening to music, and Qigong.

Out of everything I've tried, there was one overriding principle that led to the most success.

Whatever the routine was, it had to...

Align body, mind, and breath.

If one of these was missing, I noticed a huge decrease in the effectiveness.

If I aligned the body and the mind without the breath...

I wasn't as focused and still found myself a little flustered, especially if I was going through something stressful.

If I aligned the body and the breath without the mind...

My presence and intentions for the day were scattered.

If I aligned the breath and the mind without the body…

I would sometimes feel like a sloth that needed lubricant in his joints (although it's kind of crazy that this hasn't been the case since I've been on the carnivore diet...)

So how long does something like this take to do?

Anywhere from 5-10 minutes.

Of course, when I can, I try to do other things like journal or meditate for a longer period of time.

But, consistently doing just my foundational morning routine has been such a gamechanger for me because it is short (which makes it less intimidating to do) and primes me for the day ahead.

----------------------------------------

What does a simple example look like?

1) A glass of filtered water (I use a system from Nikken that has remineralizing stones because I'm a nerd like that :D).  Make sure to drink a bit at a time 

2) Some light movements (such as marching in place and pelvic rocks), paying special attention to expand the belly on the inhale and drawing the belly towards the spine on the exhale.

3) Box breathing - breathe in for 4 seconds, hold for 4 seconds, and exhale for 4 seconds.  Again, paying special attention to expand the belly on the inhale and drawing the belly towards the spine on the exhale. Do this for about 2 minutes.

At each step, be mindful of how your body feels.  

Also, towards the end of the box breathing, visualize how the perfect day would go and...

Set an intention on how you want to show up.

 

--------------------------------------

 

Do you have a morning routine?  If so, what does it look like?

 

Hope this helps you win your mornings and, as a result, win your days!

 

-"Morning" Mike Salemi

 

P.S. if you're at all curious about the carnivore diet, I've been giving my honest thoughts on doing the "right" way (incorporating raw organ meats and nothing but pasture raised/100% grassfed/wild caught meat) on Instagram.  You can find me at @mike.salemi

name: Back Pain and the Kettlebell Swing
text:
Hey {first_name}, 

 

Hope you're having a great day so far. 

 

Before spending time with family as Uncle "Zio" Mike, I wanted to shoot this over to you before you do your next kettlebell workout. 

 

You see, when it comes to back pain, there are a lot of different factors involved.

 

The way you breathe…

 

What you eat that could cause inflammation within your gut……

 

How tight/weak certain muscles are...

 

However, when it specifically comes to the kettlebell swing movement, there are five common mistakes I see many people do that can lead to back pain.

 

1. Missed Connection

 

What it Looks Like

 

Downswing: Faulty timing occurs when the hips move into flexion too early and space is created between the lower forearms and inner thighs.
Upswing: Faulty timing occurs when the hips lag behind the kettlebell. Proper timing on the upswing involves the forearms being firmly connected from the terminal point of the backswing into the acceleration phase of the upswing.

Notice how my hips have already started to move back way too early here

 

Corrected Form: I hope you can see that I'm still standing pretty straight, even right before the forearms make connection with my thighs

 

Tip(s) to Explore

Be patient during the downswing. Wait with upright posture until the forearms make connection to the pelvis/inner thighs. 
"Connect" and drive lower forearms off the inner thighs, as you accelerate during the upswing

 

2. Pulling with the Arms

 

What It Looks Like

When the arms and shoulders lift the kettlebell up into the top of the swing, the kettlebell appears to be drooping down rather than forming a straight line between the arms and kettlebell.

 

Tip(s) to Explore

Relax arms as much as possible; think of them as your "whips." The swing is primarily a leg-driven movement
Perform Towel Swings, aiming for a straight line from shoulders to the kettlebell

 

3. Loss of Posture (rounding the back)

 

What It Looks Like

At any stage of the Swing, the following can happen:

Rounding the back
Rounding the shoulders
Forward head posture 

Tip(s) to Explore

Set up in the best alignment possible--lift chest, retract shoulder blades slightly, and elongate spine
Return to the Deadlift and/or perform PVC Hinges as an awareness exercise prior to Swing training 
If you are a large lifter with wide shoulders, you may experiment with a slightly flexed elbow style of Swinging, maintaining the shoulder complex in a more favorable position

 

4. Swinging Too Low

 

What It Looks Like

Swinging excessively low to the point that the hands and kettlebell are below the knees. Oftentimes this will be coupled with rounding of the back.

 

Tip(s) to Explore

Place awareness on keeping hands above knees during the swing
Perform swings with a medium-sized Medicine Ball under your body. If you swing too low, the kettlebell will hit the ball

 

5. Overextension

 

What It Looks Like

At the top of the Swing, the hips move into excessive extension, i.e. too much forward projection of hips in relation to the shoulders.

 

Tip(s) to Explore

Have a partner place his/her hand behind your upper back to provide tactile feedback for the correct extension position
Think "stand tall"; elongate spine
Explore increasing engagement of abdominals to bring chest (sternal) position down and forward

With all of these mistakes, this is where you should ideally end up:

 

 

Notice how there is always a straight line from the top of the head to the end of the butt.

 

A big tip for any exercise is to either have a coach or someone else "spot" you for feedback.

 

Or...

 

Record yourself from a side and 3/4 angle and "coach" yourself :).

 

----------------------------------------------------------

 

I hope you're having a great weekend.

 

As always, let me know if you have any questions, I read every single response.

 

-"Zio" Mike Salemi

name: Fight Camp Conditioning
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

When it comes to both injury prevention as well as sports performance, there's certainly a number of different training tools and approaches one can utilize. 

 

Of all of them, however, I'd have to say the kettlebell and Suples Bulgarian Bag are definitely among my favorite top two. 

 

Compared to the Kettlebell, the Bulgarian Bag isn't as well known worldwide yet, however it is a truly a functional, high performance training tool. 

 

Designed and developed by former US Olympic Greco Roman Wrestling Coach and Bulgarian Olympian, Ivan Ivanov, the Bulgarian Bag was developed over 12 years ago and among many things, it is perfect for dynamic rotation training. The rotational (transverse) plane is arguably the most important for success in many sports, yet it is often the one least trained. Remember this - you are most susceptible to experience injury in the plane or pattern of movement that you train the least and/or are weakest in. 

 

In terms of rotational movements used with the Bulgarian Bag, the most quintessential of all is the Suples Spin. Now, after the past few years teaching Bulgarian Bag workshops and certifications, I'd have stay this is also the movement that gives people the most trouble when learning. 

 

That's why I paid a visit some months back to a friend of mine and MMA conditioning expert, Corey Beasley in Southern California to break down a few of the key progressions of this movement.

 

Click here to watch the technique breakdown tutorial.

 

In this video I demonstrate the following Spin progressions:

1. Open Arm Side to Side Swing with Head and Torso Rotation

2. Half Spin

3. Full Spin

 

I hope you take a look at adding more rotational work into your training and have a blast doing so!

 

Wishing you all the best,

Mike

 

 

P.S.

Do you recall my recent email on the Perfect Morning Routine? Well, it received such positive feedback that I've come up with something super exciting related to this that I'll be sharing in the coming days...Get ready!

I will include the workout details at the bottom of this email. Dr. Drew did an additional guided explanation which is up in the Facebook Group. 

 

There are two updates I wanted to share that have to do with the free morning routine challenge I spoke of on the call as well as MTK.

 

I'll be running a free 5 Day Morning Routine Challenge starting on July 15th, where every day I will teach a new 10 minute follow along morning routine. I'll be covering each of the 5 main components of Kettlebell Lifestyle - breathwork, mobility, kettlebell training, stretching, and meditation. You will LOVE this!

 

This challenge will be a way to support as many people as possible towards better health & performance, as well as connect with the perfect type of person who will be a great fit for Kettlebell Lifestyle. These morning routines will have a few aspects related to what you've experienced in KBL, however much of it will be new, plus it will be run live. If you can make it, I'd love to have you join. 

 

 

Here is the link if you're interested in joining: www.kettlebelllifestyle.com/5daychallenge

 

Also, if you happen to know anyone who might benefit I'd be very grateful if you could share the link with them. 

 

When it comes to going deeper with kettlebell training, I did a short overview of my other program Mastering the Kettlebell following the challenge workout on Monday night. If you are interested, until tomorrow morning, you can get 50% off on that! It is hands down the most comprehensive resource on the internet today for kettlebell instruction and coaching. 

 

Here is the recording link to the overview of Mastering the Kettlebell: https://vimeo.com/435104986/59994dc746

Here is your 50% discount code: KBLFAMILY

Go to: programs.mikesalemi.io

 

Additionally, if you have any specific questions on MTK please let me know and I'll do my best to support and even give you a private walkthrough. 

 

---

 

Here is the details from Monday's Challenge Workout (recording is in the FB group)

 

CHALLENGE WORKOUT

 

The idea is to perform as many 3 exercise circuits (1 circuit is one round) as possible. Every time you perform a circuit, you will jump up one level of progression on the following set. Once you've topped out at your personal top-end level of progression, stay there and continue getting as many rounds as possible in during the 18 minute time frame.

All the best,

 

Mike

name: Morning Routine Challenge Annoucement
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Recently I've been experiencing a deeper sense of gratitude, connection, and feeling of relaxed readiness than I can remember in quite some time. ⠀

⠀

From the food I choose to put in my body, to the people I'm spending my time with, to the conversations I'm having both personally and professionally, there is a lot to be thankful for. ⠀

⠀

If I'm to reflect, one element in particular that I feel has been instrumental in helping me feel into and enjoy a more genuine state of self-love and connection is consistency in specific key areas. 

⠀

I'm not saying that I don't have those days where I feel "off", however, there are specific aspects of my life that I realize are absolutely critical for my health, wellbeing, and help facilitate how I can show up best for you. ⠀

⠀

One element in particular, that has helped this tons is my morning routine. While it has evolved over the years, I always have one. ⠀

 

In a prior email I sent out a few weeks back I touched on concepts and elements related to establishing your perfect morning routine and it received so much positive feedback that I wanted to touch on this topic again and share something extra special with you today.

 

While my morning routine can vary day to day, here's what went down this morning:

⠀

1. 6am: woke up & brushed teeth⠀

2. 6:10am: 10 minutes of light mobility & breathwork⠀

3. 6:20am: 2 cups filtered & remineralized water⠀

4. 6:25am: Journaled briefly, sat and reflected⠀

5. 6:25 onward: sipped 1.5 cups of bone broth with grass-fed butter and salt⠀

 

I'm my opinion, a consistent morning routine (even if it only lasts 5 minutes) is the key to: increased energy, feeling a sense of accomplishment, honoring your core values around health, and ensuring you are in the best state possible to show up for yourself, your loved ones, and your work the rest of the day.  

⠀

I do understand that knowing what to do, and taking action on a consistent morning routine, is not always easy to do.

⠀

With this in mind, I just came up with something RAD I'd love to do to support you in.

⠀

Starting July 15th, for FREE, I'm going to teach 5 days of different morning routines Live! Each of these morning routines you can do in less than 10 minutes.

 

These routines will cover 5 key aspects of health, vitality, and performance:

Breathwork
Mobility
Kettlebell training
Stretching
Meditation

If this sounds like something that would light up your spirit and support where you are right now, I'd LOVE to do this with you.⠀

⠀

Click here to sign up for the FREE 5 Day Morning Routine Challenge starting one week from today!

 

Sending good energy,

Mike

name: Email #3 Challenge (Free Group)
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I've never met a person who hasn't wanted to feel accomplished, and move freely in their physical body. 

 

The majority of people I’ve worked with in fact have always expressed a keen interest in exploring ways to improve their mental, physical, and even spiritual well being. 

 

And so, with that said, where is the best place we start when focusing on increasing one's health and vitality?

 

Well, in my opinion, it's with the breath. 

 

Why?

 

Proper breathing is one of the few things you can do that will literally shift your entire physiology (almost instantaneously) for better or worse. Just with the breath, you can enter a state of either feeling hyperactive, or calm and relaxed simply via the pattern/type of breath you utilize.

 

What I’ll be teaching you today is a super valuable series of techniques you can incorporate not just in the morning, but also throughout the day to help you navigate even the most challenging of situations.

 

Before we start however at 9am, I'd invite you to reflect on the following question:

 

Have you ever noticed yourself holding your breath, breathing shallowly,

or experiencing difficulty in taking a complete breath during the day?

 

DAY 1 INSTRUCTIONS: 

 

1. Get your space ready and be sure to log into the Kettlebell Lifestyle Challenge facebook group 5 minutes before we start (be there at 8:55amPST). All morning routines will be streamed here. Click here if you have yet to request access to the FB group.

 

2. For Day 1, you will simply need a cushion to sit comfortably on

 

3. Watch, engage, and participate in the routine

 

4. To enter to win some of the badass prizes we are offering, first, follow @mike.salemi on Instagram. Then, take a selfie pic/video practicing any of the breathing drills from the day and tag @mike.salemi on your IG story or main feed.

 

See you in three hours!!

 

Mike

The majority of people I’ve worked with in fact have always expressed a keen interest in exploring ways to improve their mental, physical, and even spiritual well being. 

 

And so, with that said, where is the best place we start when focusing on increasing one's health and vitality?

 

Well, in my opinion, it's with the breath. 

 

Why?

 

Proper breathing is one of the few things you can do that will literally shift your entire physiology (almost instantaneously) for better or worse. Just with the breath, you can enter a state of either feeling hyperactive, or calm and relaxed simply via the pattern/type of breath you utilize.

 

What I’ll be teaching you today is a super valuable series of techniques you can incorporate not just in the morning, but also throughout the day to help you navigate even the most challenging of situations.

 

Here is your first PDF gift that I'd like you to review prior to the call. Breathing_Morning Routine.pdf

 

Immediately following the call I will stay on Zoom and host an open Q+A to take your questions, as well as review this PDF. 

 

DAY 1 INSTRUCTIONS: 

 

1. Get your space ready and be sure to log into the Zoom Link. Please keep yourself on mute during the session. Also please remain on the Zoom call after we complete the morning routine at 9:20am. I will end and immediately restart the call at 9:20 to host our Q+A since the first part of the call will go directly to Facebook, and the second part Q+A is just for you. 

 

2. For Day 1, you will simply need a cushion to sit comfortably on

 

3. Have your PDF close by and get ready hop in performing the routine (Breathing_Morning Routine.pdf)

 

4. To join the private What'sApp Group, please email your name and number to: Mike@mikesalemi.io with the Subject Line: KBL WhatsApp. I will add you into this group prior to the call.

 

4. To enter to win some of the badass prizes we are offering, first, follow @mike.salemi on Instagram. Then, take a selfie pic/video practicing any of the breathing drills from the day and tag @mike.salemi on your IG story or main feed.

 

See you in three hours!!

 

Mike

text:

Yesterday was about creating space in our breathing muscles and getting you into that state of focus and relaxed readiness. After releasing the diaphragm, you might experience a sense of relief and ease with your breathing. Take advantage of that and keep taking deep breaths throughout the day to remember and lock in that sensation.

 

If you noticed that it was a challenging routine for you but you enjoyed it, continue to use it in your daily practice. Post about your experience in the group, we’d love to hear how you felt!

 

We’re going to take advantage of that moving forward with today's routine of joint mobility. You’ll hear cue’s to breathe in a specific way with the movement and continue to work on what we learned yesterday.

I hope your day went well and you are feeling a bit more freedom of movement throughout your body. HERE is the link to our Facebook group where you can watch the recording.

 

When you perform this routine, while we went a bit over on time with the bonus segment and teaching components, when you perform this on your own in the future, 10-20 reps of each movement is a good range to be in. For our Kettlebell Training Morning Routine coming up, all you'll need is one light kettlebell. Here is my recommendations:

10-25lb bell for most women and a 15-35lb bell for most men.

See you soon!

 

-Mike

name: Email #7.1 Mor Challenge (Free)
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Is stretching worth it?  Or Does stretching really help? 

 

The truth of the matter is that you first have to ask yourself is, help with what? Stretching, just like any other form of exercise, is a tool to achieve a specific goal. 

 

If our goal is to deadlift 500lbs, then stretching as the ONLY means to get there will not suffice. However, it WILL HELP as an additional tool by loosening up soft tissue that can be restricting your movement thus making the lift more difficult.

 

Not everyone wants to deadlift 500lbs. But we can certainly benefit from the stretching for the same reasons of decreasing muscle tension and restricted movement.

 

This is where the longevity and performance pieces blend together.

PS. Stick around till the end of the live as we’ll have a surprise bonus announcement.

text:

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I wanted to say thank you again for being a part of the Kettlebell Lifestyle™ 5 day morning routine Challenge.


It was SO COOL to hear some of the wins and lessons people experienced during this morning routine challenge. Check out some of what was shared on our call today:

 

"I learned that we don't have to step on the gas 100% of the time to feel great. Sometimes it takes 5 minutes of breathing to get there. This is why the simplest routines always work best. It's a humbling process to be honest because I used to have this mindset that being YANG was the only way." 

- Denzel Dion So

 

"The stretching and working in sessions were so transformative. Incorporated them with some of my own movements in my class this morning and my clients LOVED it!"

- Vicky Ferreira

 

"This helped me be more aware of certain parts of my body that needed more attention, such as my neck, pelvis, and spine. Loved the stretches and breathwork, thanks!"

-Gabriel Urquiza

 

"I definitely feel less stressed at work. My day starts on a positive note. I’ve added mindful meditation at night while I’m doing my night time red light therapy. My sleep has been incredible."

- Genevie Perez

name: Two Hand Side to Side Swing
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Questions surrounding rotation training, as well as kettlebells are two super common topics I get asked often related to fitness and performance. 

 

With that said I just created this rad graphic that I wanted to share with you that breaks down one of my favorite rotational kettlebell exercises - the Two Hand Side to Side Kettlebell Swing.

 

In my opinion, performing rotational movements with kettlebells are not always the easiest to execute well. ⁠⠀
⁠⠀
While they certainly are possible and can be a nice addition to a program, I’ve found they typically require a higher level of skill to execute, and of course, well-thought-out progressions to get there safely and optimally.⁠⠀
⁠⠀
This particular movement, the Two Hand Side-to-Side Swing, is one of the movements I enjoy for a few reasons:⁠⠀
⁠⠀
1. Combined frontal (side to side) and rotational plane skill development⁠⠀
2. Teaches counter-balancing a load (using the body to help re-direct the KB, as opposed to unnecessary muscular effort)⁠⠀
3. Combined lower body and upper body movement heavily integrated through a stable, and yet fluid core⁠⠀
4. Trains rotational movement and range precision⁠⠀
 

You can read the full post and watch a mini video demo by clicking here.

 

On Monday, August 3rd at 2pmPST / 5pmEST I'll be hosting an Instagram Live with colleague Dr. Drew Vercellino where we'll break down this movement, as well as take questions on rotation training.

 

Here is a link to my Instagram @mike.salemi so you can tune in Live on Monday. 

 

I hope to see you there!

 

Have a lovely evening,

Mike

 

P.S. 

I'm SO PUMPED that in just a few days Kettlebell Lifestyle puppy is officially coming out and being launched in full capacity. This is only one of over 70 movements that you'll find broken down in much more detailed tutorial videos with me teaching you step-by-step, as well as in multi-level coached follow-along workouts included in Kettlebell Lifestyle. Geeeeeet ready! ; )⁠⠀

name: Youtube Channel Announcement
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

When it comes to my favorite advanced kettlebell exercises, five that immediately come to mind are as follows:

 

1. Double Kettlebell Gorilla Clean

2. Single Kettlebell Countered Sling Shot

3. Double Kettlebell Half Snatch

4. Single Kettlebell Olympic Swing

5. Double Kettlebell Sotts Press

 

Each one of the above exercises requires excellent technical proficiency and are total-body, multi-pattern movements. Master these five, and you will be more fit, mobile, and strong than you could have ever have imagined. 

 

Likely a few of these exercises you may not recognize initially, as I have taken elements of classic movements, incorporated aspects that I felt I needed to up-level my performance, and also make them more fun to learn. 

 

To help you dive into some of these movements optimally, I have an rad update. While I've been meaning for years to re-enliven my Youtube Channel, it's never been a priority, until now! : )

 

I'm super excited to share with you that every Wednesday my plan is to release one new video covering technique training, workouts, tips, interviews and more on Kettlebells, Bulgarian Bags, and other topics pertaining to holistic performance training. 

 

This week covers a breakdown of the Double Kettlebell Gorilla Clean.

 

 

Click here to watch the full tutorial now.

 

This is one particular movement that I've used often over the years when coaching athletes needing to develop the qualities of power and power endurance. 

 

In the video I break down the top three elements to ensure it's success:

1. Maintaining an upright torso position

2. Focus on the raising arm

3. Sync the breath with the movement

 

Click here to watch the full tutorial video

 

Also, please subscribe to my Youtube channel so you can get weekly free content that will leave you looking, feeling, and performing one another level!

 

Wishing you a fantastic Wednesday!

Mike

 

P.S. Stay tuned for next week's video where I cover the Kettlebell Countered Sling Shot! This is hands down one of the exercises I've been working on most in the last year and is an excellent one to building your rotational kettlebell exercise arsenal. This movement has elements inspired from my work with Suples Training Systems (the inventors of the Bulgarian Bag), and I can guarantee you how you'll feel after performing it well is going be incredible. It does take time to master, however, in the tutorial video I'll set you up for success and teach you the developmental elements you'll need to perform it at the highest level.
