name: Youtube 3 - Clean, Back to Basics Part 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

The Kettlebell Clean... you either love it or you hate it.

 

Am I right?

 

What I find is that for those people who hate performing the Clean, it is typically because they have not yet developed the technical skill to do it properly. The unfortunate consequence of this is often bruised forearms.

 

Over time, one of three things will happen:

 

You'll figure out how to remedy the problem
You'll continue bruising your forearms and endure the pain
You'll rarely if ever, return back to the clean

My goal today is to have you understand unique aspects of this movement, and help you avoid points 2 & 3 above. 

 

In this week's Youtube video, I share a simple and effective drill to help you transition from the Swing to the Clean and get you rocking and rolling at a high level. If you can learn the Clean well, what you'll find is you'll be able to enter into the rack position (a key intermediary step in many kettlebell movements) with greater ease and grace. 

 

Click here to watch the full Part I video.

 

If you are enjoying these Youtube videos, I would greatly appreciate it if you would subscribe to my channel and leave a comment on how it is benefitting your training.

 

Stay strong and have an awesome evening,

Mike

 

P.S. Stay tuned for Part II of this series, where I share fundamental concepts of how to perform a different style of kettlebell clean more focused on developing strength endurance!

name: Youtube  - Clean, Back to Basics Part 2
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In last week's Part 1 series covering the Kettlebell Clean, we discussed the mechanics of the Russian (hinge-based) Clean, as well as solving the primary challenge associated with it - banging the kettlebell onto the wrist/forearms. 

 

When done properly, this particular technique is excellent at developing Power-Endurance, as well as the muscles on the backside of your body (hamstrings, glutes, and lower back).

 

There is however, more than one way to skin a cat. Depending on the specific goal or objective for your training, sport, or preferred activity, there is in fact another Clean technique worth considering - the Pendulum Clean.

 

 

The Pendulum Clean is still a "clean" movement - where the kettlebell swings below the waist, through the legs, and finishes in the rack position. However, many details happen in between that make this Clean mechanic very different from its Russian hinge counterpart.

 

You can think of both these techniques as keys that open different doors. 

 

Click here to watch the full tutorial.

 

Why would you consider exploring the Pendulum Clean?

Your goal is maximizing volume, or strength-endurance while aiming to be highly energetically efficient.
You would like to compete in Kettlebell Sport 
You are looking to utilize more of the muscles on the anterior chain (front of the body, i.e. the quads). This clean involves more even load sharing between the anterior and posterior chains. 
You are a trainer, coach, or serious kettlebell enthusiast seeking to understand the different clean techniques and explore how/where they fit into a training plan

Click here to watch the full tutorial.

 

I hope you enjoy exploring this Pendulum Technique in your training!

 

Stay strong,

Mike

 

P.S. I've got a surprise DOPE video coming very soon. It's an instructional training video that has been hidden for nearly a year and just surfaced detailing a fantastic Bulgarian Bag workout. I'll shoot you another email in the next 48 hours with more details so stay tuned.

name: Speed and Power Training
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Less than a year ago, I was on a training trip to Boise, Idaho working with one of my mentors - founder of the Bulgarian Bag, Ivan Ivanov.

 

Ivan was the former US Olympic Greco-Roman Wrestling Coach and an Olympian for Bulgaria. Ivan has a wealth of knowledge and experience working with combat athletes of all types and it's been an absolute pleasure working closely with him these past few years.

 

 

One of the videos we shot, was just released and I wanted to share it with you here. Also, while the title of the Youtube video is "How to Design Speed and Power Training for Wresting", it will be a great fit for any functional athlete.

 

What you’ll see is a four exercise circuit of the following exercises and repetitions.

 

Spin-Arm Throw Combo (2ea)
Arm Throw (3 ea)
Half Swing-Sq (3 ea)
Bent Over Row (12)

Click here to access the workout.

 

The idea is to knock all the reps out as quickly as possible with good technique. One thing to note is that you’ll want to ensure you have good technical proficiency on the movements before trying to increase the speed of each.

 

I hope you enjoy this workout!

name: Training Room and Youtube
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

What can you accomplish in one hour?

 

From time to time, one thing I enjoy doing is testing my focus when it comes to work and productivity.

 

If you're curious about what I mean by "testing my focus," let me explain...

 

You see, I've realized over the years that just because we may be at work for 8 hours a day, that certainly does not mean all those hours are productive and focused. In fact, from what I see with clients, as well as have experienced myself in the past, is that even getting in an hour of focused work can be a challenge.

 

To test my focus and productivity, I will set a timer at varying durations, for example:

15 minutes
30 minutes
60 minutes

The goal is for whatever duration you set, to be as focused as humanly possible during that time frame. This can also be a good way to find your ideal working time before needing a mental break to reset. I find it truly incredible what even just 15 minutes of focused work can do.

 

After each block of time, I will get up, stretch my arms over my head, and sip some water. After longer dedicated work blocks, when I get up I will often listen to my favorite song, perform a stretch, or mini-meditation.  

 

So why am I bringing this all up?

 

Well, mainly because I want to see you operating at a high level of focus, productivity, and performance on a daily basis.

name: Knowledge vs Wisdom
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In a conversation this weekend, the concept of knowledge vs. wisdom came up.

 

Since then, I have been inspired and reflecting much on the difference between the two and how they show up in life - specifically in the realm of health and performance. 

 

Simply stated, knowledge refers mainly to taking in information, whereas wisdom is how we apply that information.

 

Knowledge is more a matter of the mind, whereas wisdom is more a matter of the heart. 

 

This notion was further driven home during a call I had earlier today with an upcoming fitness pro in Norway. We discussed the type of professional he is seeking to become - a heart-centered one who acts from a place primarily of wisdom, rather than purely knowledge. 

 

When it comes to physical training, there certainly are specific training principles/science we know to be true. How we choose exercises, structure training phases, select reps, sets, loads, tempo, etc., are highly important facets to elicit a specific training response. 

 

That said, you can be successful as a coach/trainer while being a bit of both scientist AND artist. In fact, I believe it helps tremendously. 

 

When working with Paul Chek, I observed first hand this very thing at work. Paul would sometimes take hours to create my programs, and although they were VERY scientifically based, steeped in high-level program design principles, there was also a big feeling, meditative and artistic aspect to them.

 

This approach has had a powerful influence on me since 2013, and is how I design programs today and teach on this topic. 

 

When you take this path, you begin integrating the heart with the mind, and turn knowledge into wisdom - this is where the gold is at!

 

However, this does not and cannot happen overnight - it takes countless reps, successes and failures to develop authentic wisdom.

 

This is why I’m stoked to share, while registration for Kettlebell Lifestyle is still closed to the public until late October, this week starts the Kettlebell Lifestyle Masters Program.

 

This Masters Program works hand-in-hand with Kettlebell Lifestyle (which those who sign up for this will receive immediate access), and provides very special 10+ week-long immersion Masters-level experience.

 

This group will be kept SUPER small on purpose.

 

You will be held accountable.

 

You will analyze technique and receive feedback.

 

You will learn the essentials of program design.

 

You will be asked to design workouts.

 

You will meet and be coached weekly by myself and co-facilitator Dr. Drew Vercellino.

 

You will learn strategies and tactics to gain more income by bringing/growing aspects of your business online, all while staying in integrity with your values. 

 

I am holding a live Zoom Call tomorrow, Monday, at 6:15pm PST for approximately 45 minutes, to answer any questions and to help determine if you are a fit for this opportunity.

 

Here is the Zoom Link to join the call at 6:15pm PST on Monday, 9/14: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/5580027238

 

If you cannot make it and would like to watch the recording, please email me and I will send you a link later that evening - group coaching starts this week. 

 

I wish you all the best, and if you’re highly motivated to turn some badass knowledge into applied wisdom you can use to leverage yourself as a kettlebell expert, I’ve got your back. 

 

Talk soon,

 

Mike

name: Youtube- Swing & Spin
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I'm out here in beautiful Eden, Utah for a meeting with some of the best fitness business minds lead by my good friend Mike Bledsoe and his organization, The Strong Coach. 

 

It’s been so nice to re-connect with these friends and get some good movement in together!

 

For today’s YouTube video I asked Ben Walker who is here at the retreat to join me as I share with you a fantastic time efficient workout utilizing two of the best pieces of home workout equipment - the Kettlebell and Suples Bulgarian Bag.

 

With these two tools, I've selected my favorite total body dynamic exercises, the Kettlebell Swing, and Suples Spin. You will train your lower back, glutes, hamstrings, core, shoulders, grip, and more. 

 

In this workout, depending on your fitness and skill level, you can choose the appropriate weight, repetition, and load that best suits where you are right now. 

 

Click here to access the workout

 

Here are a few suggested guidelines:

 

Lower/Medium Conditioning Level

8 Swings
8/8 Spins
4 Sets @60 Sec Rest
Load: Light/Moderate

 

Medium Conditioning Level

10-12 Swings
10/10 Spins
4-6 Sets @45-60 Sec Rest
Load: Moderate

 

High Conditioning Level

12-15 Swings
10-12/10-12 Spins
5-8 Sets @30-60 Sec Rest
Load: Moderate/Heavy

 

While this supersetted workout can be done in a very short amount of time, I highly suggest warming up for 5-15 minutes prior and spending at least 5-10 minutes post-training to cool down and stretch. 

 

Click here to access the workout

 

You should be "in-and-out the door" and completed with everything between 20-35 minutes (depending on how long you spend in each segment).

 

I hope you love incorporating this workout into your training for an incredible time effective, and most importantly, FUN experience with it. 

 

All the best,
Mike

 

P.S. If you are interested in becoming among the best kettlebell practitioners in the world, I have a program for you. My Kettlebell Lifestyle Masters Program, will take 6-8 people through a carefully designed small group experience with myself and Dr. Drew Vercellino. The last day to apply is Sunday so click here and apply now.

name: Double Half Snatch
text:
Hi {first_name}!

 

As we head into the weekend, I wanted to share a video I put together covering one particular lift (actually it's a combination of two lifts in one!) that has been a go-to of mine since my early days of kettlebell training. 

 

The Double Kettlebell Half Snatch is an intermediate level kettlebell movement that is both a power and a strength-based exercise. Most people are surprised at how well-rounded of a training effect they can experience in such a short amount of time, number of sets, reps, and load simply by the nature of this integrated movement. 

 

The goal is to move the kettlebell powerfully from high up under the thighs into the overhead lockout position with power and control.

 

Click here to see the full video demonstration. 




With this unique movement, the raising phase is the most technically critical part - it involves snatching into the overhead position. This is then followed by lowering down to chest level, and then dropping out of the Rack Position as you would a Clean.

 

One added benefit, beyond the strength component of this type of lowering phase, is that the lift has a reduced level of complexity compared to a full snatch. This is why if you are making the transition into either double kettlebell training, or snatch training as a whole, the Half Snatch can be a great option. 

 

Click here to see the full video demonstration. 

 

I hope you have a fantastic weekend and give this movement a try!

 

Mike

 

P.S. To join a private free group I call the "Training Room" where we dive into your questions live on Zoom on training, performance, programming, holistic health, and fitness business please reply to this email expressing to be put on the list. So far we've been having an amazing group of like minded and hearted people from around the world connect, grow together, and get burning questions answered.

name: Double Half Snatch clone
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I hope life is moving through you well! I spent the past weekend in Arnold, California and it was incredibly vitalizing. In this week's YouTube video, with this trip as my inspiration, I share one of the many ways I like to cultivate movement as medicine.

 

I first learned this concept from coach and friend, Paul Chek. In his book How to Eat, Move, and Be Healthy, you'll find invaluable information and guidance on this topic he's coined "Working In". If you don't already have this book in your library, I highly recommend it - in fact, it is my number one recommend book to people I come across!  

 

To me, working in is arguably the most powerful and important thing an athlete or anyone aspiring to improve their performance can do. I honestly believe it saved my lifting carreer and took me to a level of performance that would have been very difficult to achive without it healthfully. Working in (energy cultivating activities) provides the potential to sustain and perform working out (energy expenditure activities) optimally.

 

In this week's video, I share a super simple foundational Kettlebell exercise, along with a complementary bodyweight movement perfect for the health of the spine and building vitality. 

 

Click here to watch the full video to start this vitalizing combo.

 

I hope you have a lovely day and incorporate movement as medicine into your personal practice. I promise you won't regret it!

 

Mike

name: Double Half Snatch clone clone
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

As we progress in our movement practice, one of the things that is often overlooked as it relates to athleticism, fitness, and realizing performance potential is what takes place in the moments in-between repetitions.

 

Transitioning from one repetition to another, and even more so from one movement to another ( such as when we perform exercises in a sequential "flow-like"  fashion ) often requires coordination, patience, rhythm, timing, agility and more. 

 

When it comes to making smooth transitions, specifically with the Bulgarian Bag, there is one in particular that I find as a very effective standalone exercise that also serves as a great way to smoothly transition sides when performing the signature Spin movement. 

 

Click here to watch this week's new Youtube video.

 

Coined the Pummel, this has an excellent application for functional athletes of all types, however especially grapplers and combat athletes. 


The Suples Bulgarian Bag, was invented by Former US Olympic Greco-Roman Wrestling Coach Ivan Ivanov and is something I truly believe in as a complete at-home gym.

 

The vast majority of my training today happens with the Kettlebell (no surprise there haha ; ) and the Bulgarian Bag.

 

This is not by mistake. 

 

They are among two of the very best, results-driven and fun training tools I've ever come across. 

 

Click here to watch the full new Youtube video on making smooth transitions.

 

Wishing you a fantastic day enjoying breathing, moving, and simply being more in your body : )

 

Mike

 

P.S. If you would like to join a free Zoom community call, "The Training Room" that I hold nearly every Thursday, please respond to this email. I'll put you on the list so that when notifications go out for calls you can be informed. Currently, we've held over 6 great sessions with people from all over the world, getting their performance, fitness business, and holistic health questions answered. If you are unable to make the calls at 9:30am PST, I have a free Facebook group where you can watch an archive of the recordings.

name: Strong, Open and Feel Good Challenge
text:
Hi {first_name}!

 

Would you consider your body to be:⁠⠀

 

Strong⁠
Open⁠
Both⁠
Neither⁠

Are you prioritizing one in particular?⁠

⁠

As the saying goes, “where attention goes, energy flows”⁠⠀

⁠

Over the years, I’ve seen if our movement practice does not include both a focus on strength AND in some capacity openness, then we are likely to experience dysfunction and rigidity - the opposite of what it takes to achieve longevity.⁠

⁠

If you’d like to experience better results in your training, all while doing less, sign-ups are now open for a NEW 15 minute, 5 day FEEL GOOD Challenge.

text:

After having returned from a weekend in the forest, my energy is full and spirits are high!

 

Today, I arrived here in Austin, Texas, to celebrate the wedding of a dear friend and record some epic podcasts with people like Paul Chek, and Josh Trent of Wellness Force. Get ready for those to be released in the coming weeks/months : )

 

Let's me just say that I'm PUMPED!

name: Offset Kettlebell Training YT
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Today I’m happy to bring you a fun and challenging way to build core control and strength utilizing kettlebells. 

 

While you likely already know I’m a huge fan of single kettlebell training (mainly due to single kettlebell lifting being so accessible, cost-effective, and portable), there are certainly tremendous benefits and a place for double kettlebell lifting. 

 

In this new video, I share ways to perform offset kettlebell training using two main lifts - one focused on the lower body and one on the upper body. You’ll get a chance to experience the increased demand placed on the entire body that these lifts entail and build crazy levels of old-world strength as a result. 

 

Click here to see this full offset training video and get beastly now! ; )

 

P.S.

I’m thrilled to share that Kettlebell Lifestyle is now available for purchase! End training that burns you out, is one dimensional, and for lack of a better term - boring. Kettlebell Lifestyle teaches you how to get more out of one kettlebell than most people will get from a full gym, plus contains TONS of lifestyle support aspects such as stretching exercises, breath work, mobility training to help bring more balance to your life. 

 

Click here to get started and please share this with any friends or family who may be looking to get more from their at-home workouts right now.

name: Bags and Bells Annoucements
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

One thing that has always amazed me is that as humans, we innately have the ability to recognize beautiful movement when we see it.

 

Often, when a movement or routine looks beautiful, there tends to be exquisite:

Timing
Rhythm
Fluidity

When any of the above are lacking, something will just look or feel off, and the movement will appear less than "beautiful".

 

I'm sure if you've ever seen a clip on TV/Youtube of high-level gymnastics or synchronized swimming, you know what I'm talking about.

 

Here's an example of my dear friend, Sho Nakamori on the Pommel Horse when he was an olympic hopeful. 

 

Moving with rhythm, timing, and fluidity are things that can be developed over time with focused practice. 

 

With this in mind, for today I've broken down the steps to performing two movements I consider to be incredible beautiful when well executed. They are very complementary, so if you'd like to perform them as a back to back superset workout you can and they'll work great to improve your overall athleticism. 

 

RMT (Rotational Movement Training) Clean to Press

 

Start with the Kettlebell in the hang position and body rotated away from the loaded arm (approx. 45 degrees)
With an upright chest, clean the Kettlebell into the rack position as you rotate and pivot the body to the opposite side 
Ensure the shoulder of the loaded arm is depressed, aiming for the elbow to nearly touch the pelvic crest (this is considered the "short" side)
With the elbow of the unloaded arm reaching up to the ceiling, create tension through the lat (considered the "long" side)
Press the Kettlebell overhead as you rotate and pivot the body to the opposite side

 

Bulgarian Bag Snatch

 

Standing behind the Bulgarian Bag, hinge back and maintain your spine while gripping firmly
Swing the Bag through the legs, following it with your head and eyes
Keep the Bag close as it travels up the body
Begin turning/flipping the Bag over the forearms as it approaches chin level
Stand tall with the legs and arms fully locked out and the Bag overhead

With the Kettlebell RMT Clean to Press and Bulgarian Bag Snatch, you'll develop: coordination, rhythm, timing, fluidity, rotational strength, core control, power and more

 

I hope you explore these movements in your training and of course, have a blast doing so!

 

Wishing you a great evening, 

Mike

 

P.S.

Did you know you can now workout online Live with me? 

 

Yup, it's true ; ) I just started a Patreon page offering a weekly Live workout called Bags and Bells that comes out to less than $12 a session!

If you want more training variety, learn how to use the Bulgarian Bag safely, improve fitness with Kettlebells, get a legit, joint-by-joint warm-up, and stand taller and feel amazing with myofascial stretching ELDOAs post-training, my new Bags and Bells class is a great option for you. 

 

Click here for more info - first class starts Wednesday (you can also watch live for 24 hours as well as explore other options)

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

This week I'm excited to switch-up our focus from what's been 12 consistent weeks of Bags, Bells, and Bodyweight content (whew hew!) to share and breakdown the steps to making a perfect espresso shot. 

 

I had a LOT of fun yesterday pulling shot, after shot, after shot LOL, and making a new coffee focused YouTube video - it's all about those Tiger Stripes baby⁠! ? ;)

 

 

⁠

Just like with movement, there is intention, technique, progression, and more all built into the process. ⁠

 

Click here to watch the full Youtube Video.

 

Here's the equipment and coffee used in the video:

Grinder: Compak 3
Espresso Machine: Rocket Giotto 
Coffee: Caffea Organic 
Bottomless Portafilter: Rocket Bottomless Portafilter

If you are in the market for a quality espresso machine that is more economical (as far as good machines go), I honestly loved the Rancilio Silvia for years and have recommended it more than any other machine to friends and family members.

 

The only reason I switched machines to the Rocket is because of the sheer volume of espressos I was pulling on a weekly basis with a house full of room mates and wanted a more commercial machine. 

 

For single family use, you'll love the Rancilio Silvia. Here is a link to that in case you are interested: https://www.seattlecoffeegear.com/rancilio-silvia-espresso-machine

It's simple, durable, and pulls great shots.

 

I hope you enjoy your weekend and put a little extra love, intention and care into your morning beverage ritual : )

 

Mike

 

P.S.

If you enjoyed this week's coffee video, please share this email and subscribe to my Youtube channel to support.

Thank you!

name: 308 Reps
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Yesterday morning I received a direct email from Coach Ivan Ivanov, the inventor of the Suples Bulgarian Bag and key mentor of mine, inviting me to test myself in a max (to the limit!) set of Bulgarian Bag Spins.

 

At first, I thought I should train for this and give myself a few weeks to prepare. 

 

But, then I said to myself, "screw it, let's go right now!" ; )

 

I've not tested myself with the Bag in over a year, and training has been pretty erratic lately, so I was very doubtful I could surpass his BEASTLY 249 rep count.

 

While going for it, I completely lost count but kept going past the point of wanting to quit. 

 

It was a very special moment, as I have not dug that deep for a while, and I remembered during and after the set just how much I missed the feeling of pushing myself beyond my limits and seeing what I had in me. 

 

 

I ended up performing 308 reps, and while at the end, they were NOT pretty reps; however, I gained a new level of self-respect for myself because when it got hard (and it got hard early in the set), I did not quit. THAT is what's most important. That is why it's called a test.

 

I learned that I have MUCH more in me than I thought, and I was so proud of myself. 

 

I remembered the lessons that I've learned multiple times in my life when competing in Powerlifting and Kettlebell Sport. 

 

Our minds can go way further than our physical bodies. 

 

Now, I sit here writing you this email to hopefully inspire a thought and feeling, that you too have more in you than you think. 

 

When you want to quit, just keep telling yourself it will be ok. Tell yourself to simply breathe and move, breathe, and move. 

 

I invite you to join me in this simple, fun, and challenging test.

 

You CAN do it. I believe in you, but that honestly doesn't' really matter much. Because what's most important is that YOU believe in YOU. 

 

Click here to watch the full video of my max effort (nearly dying at the end haha) of this set. 

 

The rules are as follows:

 

Perform 1 max set of Bulgarian Bag Spins
Don't stop moving
You may switch sides at will
Choose a medium-size weight (most men will choose 26lbs, most females 17lbs).

If you do it, please post and tag me as well as @Suples.Training.Systems so we can celebrate your effort with you.

 

I LOVE friendly competition and believe it can truly help us all grow and rise together in a healthy way. 

 

If you need a Bag to get started, here is a discount code you can use (TEAMSALEMI10) when you go to my site if you live in the US: www.mikesalemi.io.

 

I had over 150 people take a wild guess at how many reps I could perform - 83% thought I could do more than 249, and 17% thought I could not. 

 

Again, what people think doesn't really matter. What does, however, is how much we believe in ourselves and our potential. 

 

I have also been getting a good handful of DMs from people in the last 24 hours curious about the benefits of this beautiful, total body movement. So what I will do is in the coming days share about exactly how amazing this movement is and what it's helping you to develop as a more functional athlete and person

 

In my opinion, we ALL are athletes in some capacity, shape, or form, whether we compete in a sport or not. 

 

Also, all have something of value to teach one another, and this test will show you that - I can guarantee you. 

 

When one of us grows and finds deeper meaning into who we are, we all grow together as a community. 

 

With light, strength, love, and spins ; )

Mike

I know this time of the year can be pretty wild, and with all the sales happening this weekend, I imagine your inbox has been flooded. 

 

And while I’d certainly like to share my own rad offers you can hop on as an investment to further your health, fitness, and performance, I also want to take a moment to express my sincere gratitude for you.

 

I am so grateful you’ve chosen to improve yourself by deciding to receive content I share weekly from my heart to hopefully better your quality of life in some way.

 

I hope during the holidays, you’ve been able to take a moment to reflect on the loved ones in your life, and also how amazing YOU are.

 

If you are motivated to continue your study and growth with me (or know any friends who would be a great fit), especially while at home, I’m giving 50% off my two online programs - Kettlebell Lifestyle & Mastering the Kettlebell.

 

Use Code: HOLIDAY50 on either or both of the following image links. 

Also, as an additional bonus, if you purchase both, I am tossing in one month free of my weekly Bags and Bells (Bulgarian Bag and Kettlebell) streaming workout classes! (when you order both I will contact you personally to set you up with these classes). Mike

name: Youtube Arm Bar
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

This week's newest Youtube content brings in Dr. Drew Vercellino to break down the details of one of my old-time favorite kettlebell exercises, the Kettlebell Arm Bar.

 

The Kettlebell Arm Bar requires shoulder stability, strength, endurance, balance, as well as tremendous focus to name a few.

 

In this video, Dr. Drew covers some basics of shoulder anatomy, the KB Arm Bar setup, how to perform the classic movement, as well as three ways to add a bit of variety to it. 

 

Click here and watch "BULLETPROOF Your Shoulders with the KETTLEBELL ARM BAR"

 

I hope you enjoy!

 

Mike

name: Social Media Masterclass
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Last week in the PS section of my email, I shared with you an Instagram Live interview I did with colleague and friend, Ella Mae.

 

Ella is a social media strategist who, above all, teaches people how to build their tribe, business, and brand with integrity using social media.

 

One thing I'm aware of is that many people in my tribe are in the health and fitness field. 

 

These people have AMAZING intentions, are many are incredibly talented at helping people improve their quality of life. 

 

The problem is, many of their potential clients really don't know who they are, how special they are, and most importantly, how they have the skills and abilities that can help. 

 

Why is that?

 

Well, in my experience, a few of the reasons are:

 

They are busy helping people. 
Promoting themselves/their businesses on social media feels awkward/disingenuous to them.
They dislike the fakeness and flashiness that tend to be prevalent with social media.
They think they have to be on it all the time to be successful with it.
They don't understand what content to post or if how what they post could actually turn into getting them more of their ideal clients. 

 

If any of the above sounds like I may be talking about something you can relate to, I have a few rad things to share...

 

First, I invited Ella back for a second interview, and once again, she killed it!

 

Here is a link if you'd like to check out the second Q+A interview.

 

Second, after some reflection, to help support my tribe in using social media in a healthy way to promote their business and themselves while being in integrity, I asked Ella to do me a favor.

 

I asked her to hold a 90-minute social media masterclass exclusively for my community. 

 

So, if you are in the health and fitness industry or simply are interested in building your social presence in a meaningful way that doesn’t feel sleazy, fake, or inauthentic, then this is something I strongly encourage you to consider.

 

This masterclass will happen next Thursday, December 17th, at 12:30 pm PST. 

 

Here is the link to find out all the details.

 

If you have any friends who could benefit from this, please do pass it along, there is going to be TONS of value in it that I'm confident will help. 

 

Wishing you a great day,
Mike

 

 

PS.

In case you missed it, here is a link to the first Instagram Live interview I did with Ella.

name: Birthday Email
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Reflecting on this past year, what I am most grateful for and proud of is fostering a growing community with so many amazing, heart centered people in it.

 

One thing that has become crystal clear to every ounce of my being is this - I am here to serve.

 

It brings me great joy to be able to share tips, techniques, and methods in my emails, videos, and programs geared towards creating a healthy training lifestyle. 

 

As a token of gratitude for your continued support, as well as in celebration for the holidays, I have put together a series of items and gifts for you:  

 

#1: Never Before Seen Breathing & Stabilization Video

The first gift is a new, exclusive video I have yet to share with anyone. I found this in my Kettlebell Lifestyle Program archives, and just discovered that it was never released. It is an excellent tutorial that discusses breathing and stabilization using light loads, heavy loads, and moving at varying speeds. 

 

In it we utilize the Deadlift and Kettlebell Swing to demonstrate this in action. 

Click here for this Breathing and Stabilization Tutorial

 

 

#2: New Podcast with Wellness Force

The second is my most recent podcast with Josh Trent of Wellness Force. In it we discuss ways of increasing vitality at every level, including physical training for spiritual growth. I hope you pull out some gems that will enrich your life. 

 

Podcast Link: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/376-mike-salemi-truth-about-kettlebells-strength-spiritual/id1009470193?i=1000502431815

 

 

#3: Bulgarian Bag Reaction Training Workout

The third is a video with Ivan Ivanov, the inventor of the Suples Bulgarian Bag. It is a workout focused on Reaction Training. This will help to develop your nervous system for more explosive training, especially helpful in many athletic endeavors.

 

Click here for the Reaction Training Workout

*Note, while the workout title says Reaction Training for Wrestlers, even if you are not a wrestler, you'll love and benefit from it, trust me ; )

 

And while we are at it, here a few more gifts... 

 

 

#4: Holiday Discounts

name: Bulgarian Bag Swing Squats
text:
Hi {first_name},

⁠⠀

While there's countless movements that you can do with the Bulgarian Bag, this one in particular, the Swing Squat, is among the most effective for training legs.⁠⠀

⁠⠀

What you'll experience when done correctly is a deep conditioning of the legs (primarily the quads, hamstrings, and glutes) and back, as well as improved coordination. ⁠

⁠⠀

Where I see most people experiencing challenge with this movement is on coordinating the lower and upper body.⁠⠀

⁠⠀

Many times when first learning, people will perform it like a classic swing (just as you would a kettlebell), however, for a proper swing squat, that would be incorrect. With this movement, the goal is when the Bulgarian Bag raises, the hips drop, and visa-versa. ⁠⠀

 

Here is a graphic to illustrate the bottom position of the Swing Squat and where the Bulgarian Bag should ideally finish.

If you would like to see a video of this movement, I recently posted a demonstration in slow-motion on Instagram, which you can watch here, along with four other movements you'll enjoy. 

⁠

The Swing Squat shows up regularly in my Bags and Bells weekly classes, as well as is one of the feature movements in my first virtual workshop of the new year happening tomorrow, January 16th. ⁠

⁠

If you'd like to learn the fundamentals of this incredible training tool, tomorrow I am hosting a virtual workshop. If you own a Bulgarian Bag, or would like try this training in the future, I highly suggest taking advantage of this opportunity to deepen your understanding and ensure you are getting the most out of your training. It will be 90 minutes long and packed with some great gems. Click here for this workshop as well as to see the other killer ones I've got planned.

 

P.S.

Now, anyone who gets my Bags and Bells Elite weekly class, will get my new monthly workshops for FREE as a bonus! That's nearly $1200 in amazing education delivered by top presenters in health and performance as my gift to you for free! If you'd like to get access to tomorrow's workshop and weekly live classes with me, please click here.

name: Bag and Bell  Elite Program-21
text:
Hi {first_name}!

 

I've got some fantastic news that will be super helpful and valuable to your success as you continue training with me.

 

Now, Bags and Bells ELITE includes:

Weekly downloadable Bags and Bells workouts
90 minute monthly workshops with myself and industry experts for free (the next one is on ELDOAs with ELDOA Certifying Instructor, Justin Brien)
Time codes breaking organizing each workout into it's major segments for quick viewing  
A training recommendation plan that will take you through to our next session. This will give you tons of practice, and now if you'd like, Bags and Bells can be your main go-to for all your fitness goals

 

Workout Download

Link: https://vimeo.com/502715087/c248a49b0b

 

Time Codes

1. Core Temp Warm Up: 0:20

2. Joint Warm Up: 3:24

3. Skill Development #1: 13:24

4. Circuit #1: 22:10

5. Skill Development #2: 27:30

6. Circuit #2: 34:49

7. Stretching: 43:30

 

 

Weekly Training Plan Recommendations:

 

WEDNESDAY (1/20): Full Workout

 

THURSDAY (1/21): Stretching Focus

Perform the stretches from yesterday demonstrated at the end of our session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.
*Lat Stretch
Shoulder ELDOA
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the lat stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

FRIDAY (1/22): Skill Development and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Pick the one skill from Circuit #1 OR Circuit #2 that you found challenging or that you’d like to work on.
Perform 1-3 sets of this exercise for 6-10 reps utilizing a light load and resting as needed in between. 
Finish with the L5/S1 ELDOA and rest well before your full workout tomorrow. 

SATURDAY (1/23): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday. 
If you are able to progress, explore so in the following ways:
Add 1-4 repetitions to each exercise
Explore progressing to the next skill progression (based on where you finished on Wednesday)
 Add 1-2 sets to one or both circuits
Add weight (if this is an option for you based on what you have access to at home)

SUNDAY (1/24): Rest and Play!

 

MONDAY (1/25): Skill Development, Circuit #1, and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Pick the one skill from both Circuit #1 AND Circuit #2 that you found challenging or that you’d like to work on. 
Perform 1-3 sets of each of these two exercises for 6-10 reps utilizing a light load and resting as needed in between. 
Once you have done this focused skill work, select either Circuit #1 OR Circuit #2 and perform 1-3 rounds. 

Finish with these three stretches as performed in the workout:

*Lat Stretch
Shoulder ELDOA
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the lat stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

TUESDAY (1/26): Stretching Focus

Perform the stretches from yesterday demonstrated at the end of our session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.
*Lat Stretch
Shoulder ELDOA
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the lat stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

 

I hope you love today's training, practice well before next week, and get some great rest in!

 

 

All the best,

Mike

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Here is your Downloadable Recording from 1/27/21: https://vimeo.com/505331161/1fea117381

 

Time Index:

1. Core Temp Warm Up: 0:37

2. Joint Warm Up: 4:20

3. Technique Portion 1: 20:32

4. Circuit 1: 26:00

5. Technique Portion 2: 32:40

6. Circuit 2: 38:20

7. Stretching: 49:46

 

 

Weekly Training Plan Recommendations:

 

WEDNESDAY (1/27): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (1/28): Stretching Focus

Perform the stretches from yesterday demonstrated at the end of our session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches:

 

1. *Glute Max Deep Myofascial Stretch

2. Hip ELDOA (External Rotation)

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

*Add one additional set to the lat stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

 

FRIDAY (1/29): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Pick either Exercise #1 from Circuit #1 OR Exercise #1 from Circuit #1 that you found challenging or that you’d like to work on.
Perform 2-3 sets of this exercise for 6-10 reps each side utilizing a lighter load and resting as needed in between. Focus on skill improve and technique during these sets. 
Finish with the L5/S1 ELDOA for 1 minute and rest well before your full workout tomorrow. 

 

SATURDAY (1/30): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday. 

If you are able to progress, explore so in the following ways:

 

Add 1-4 repetitions to each exercise
Explore progressing to the next skill progression (based on where you finished on Wednesday)
Add 1-2 sets to one or both circuits
Add weight (if this is an option for you based on what you have access to at home)

 

SUNDAY (1/31): Rest and Play!

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 

If you wish to turn this into more of a training session, continuous steady-state cardio is recommend. Getting in a pool or hiking are an excellent options as example. Keep the total time you are in the pool up to 20 minutes, and hiking between 15 minutes to 1 hour. Have the pace be steady and controlled, resting as needed.

 

Enjoy this day above all and let your energy and how your body feels guide you to the best of your ability. If you do decide to perform cardio, I highly suggest doing your Core Temperature Warm Up and Bodyweight Mobility series from the workout prior to cardio. Once you complete your session, at minimum perform your L5/S1 ELDOA (1 minute), and depending on the time available to you, you can perform your Glute Stretch (3 sets of 30 seconds with 10 second rest in between sides) as well as your Hip ELODA (1 minute each side).

 

 

MONDAY (2/1): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform Exercise #1 from Circuit #1 AND Exercise #1 from Circuit #2
Do 1-2 sets of each of these two exercises for 6-10 reps utilizing a light load and resting as needed in between. Focus on skill improvement and technique above all on these sets
Once you have done this focused skill work, select either Circuit #1 AND Circuit #2 and perform 1-3 rounds of a complete circuit. 

Finish with these three stretches as performed in the workout:

1. *Glute Max Deep Myofascial Stretch

2. Hip ELDOA (External Rotation)

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

*Add one additional set to the lat stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

 

TUESDAY (2/3): Stretching Focus
Perform the stretches from yesterday demonstrated at the end of our session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.

 

1. *Glute Max Deep Myofascial Stretch

2. Hip ELDOA (External Rotation)

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

*Add one additional set to the lat stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

Enjoy your training this week! : )

All the best,

name: Bags and Bells ELITE/Pro Recording 2/3
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout download, time indexed workout, and weekly training plan.

 

2/3/2021 Workout Download:

Link: https://vimeo.com/508083768/4fdd90ab29

 

Time Indexed Workout:

1. Core Temp Warm Up: 1:00

2. Joint Warm Up: 4:20

3. Technique Portion 1: 11:45

4. Circuit 1: 19:35

5. Technique Portion 2: 31:25

6. Circuit 2: 38:50

7. Additional Segmental/Isolated Strengthener: 46:58

8. Stretching: 50:31

9. Q+A: 59:30

 

Weekly Training Plan Recommendations:

 

WEDNESDAY (2/3): Full Workout

**Note — Towel Drill: remembering which arm the towel should be located gave people trouble today. Please to always place the towel in the armpit of the loaded arm, NOT the unloaded for this to be effective. (Reference: 24:41) 

 

THURSDAY (2/4): Stretching Focus

Perform the stretches from yesterday demonstrated at the end of our session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.

 

1. *Gracilis Myofascial Stretch

2. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

*Add one additional set to the Gracilis stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

FRIDAY (2/5): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

 

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Focus on Exercise #1 & #2 in Circuit #1 from our training this week (Level I, this will be either the Waiters Clean with Towel to Forward Lunge (or any regression shown), and for Level II, this will be a Snatch into Forward Lunge (or any regression shown).
With this main movement, you have two options to work with - either increase the repetitions by 2-4, thus between 10-14 on each side, (this would be more of a conditioning focus). You may be able to stay at the same weight, or reduce it by one kettlebell weight if you have it.  OR you can choose to do the same reps that we performed. OR choose to reduce the reps by 2-4, thus between 4-6 on each side (this would be more of a strength focus) and increase the load.
After you perform this exercise, superset it with Butterflies for 15-25 reps
Perform this superset for 2-4 sets. However, be sure to save some energy for tomorrow full workout.
Finish with the L5/S1 ELDOA for 1 minute and rest well before your full workout tomorrow. 

 

 

SATURDAY (2/6): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday. 

 

If you are able to progress, explore so in the following ways:

Add 1-4 repetitions to each main exercise
Explore progressing to the next skill progression (based on where you finished on Wednesday)
Add 1-2 sets to one or both circuits
Add weight (if this is an option for you based on what you have access to at home)

 

 

SUNDAY (2/7): Rest and Play!

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 

 

Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:

 

Hiking for ~45 minutes (long duration cardio, moderate walking pace)
Rowing Machine ~8-15 minutes (cardio focus, moderate pace)
Meditation 5-20 minutes (especially if you are feeling physically or mentally stressed)

 

 

MONDAY (2/8): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform Circuit #2 only from Wednesday’s workout
Do 3-6 rounds of this circuit, resting as needed in between sets for the same reps as on Wednesday

Finish with these three stretches as performed in the workout:

*Gracilis Myofascial Stretch
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the Gracilis stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

 

TUESDAY (2/9): Stretching Focus
Perform the stretches from demonstrated at the end of our live training session.

 

Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.

 

Gracilis Stretch
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the Gracilis stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

Enjoy your training,

Mike

name: Chris Duffin Annoucement
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Believe it or not, yes, there is in fact a human being who can squat AND deadlift 1000lbs...for REPS!

 

His name is Chris Duffin.

 

And what's even more impressive about him in my opinion, is that he is MUCH more than purely a great lifter. 

 

I have been in contact with Chris over the past few months, and while I knew about him for years and appreciated his work, it wasn’t until recently that I started learning more about him.

 

Chris is no stranger to working through challenging adversity in his life. Amidst the adversity he's experienced since childhood, Chris has become a best selling author, engineer, educator, and co-founder of Kabuki Strength. 

 

It takes heart, mind, and spirit to do this, and that's why I am very excited and honored to share that today at 9amPST / 12pmEST I will be interviewing Chris.

 

 

I feel his life experience will be very supportive and inspiring to all of us during these wild times.

 

Tune into Instagram LIVE (@Mike.Salemi), where the topic will be “How to Stay Focused Amidst Adversity." 

 

Hope to see you in a few hours!

 

Mike

 

P.S. 

You're invited! On Feb 20th I am hosting a virtual workshop where you will learn FANTASTIC, detailed postures (called ELDOAs) geared towards reducing pain, compensations in the body, and improving the function of your hips and lower back. If you care about how you feel and perform, you should be there. I'm bringing in ELDOA certifying instructor, Justin Brien, to lead this 90 minute workshop called Pain Free Performance exclusively for my community. Even if you can’t make the live virtual workshop, sign up anyway, trust me. You will have access to the recording and if you only walked away having learned one posture (which takes only one minute a day) I can tell you it will have a positive impact on your life and be well worth it. 

 

Sign up today and take action on having a better functioning body.

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout download, time indexed workout, and weekly training plan.

 

2/10/2021 Workout Download

Link: https://vimeo.com/509905085/1d22c3d09d

 

 

Time Indexed Workout:

1. Core Temp Warm Up: 0:35

2. Joint Warm Up: 4:26

3. Additional: Floor to Stand 2 min Series & Fighter Sit Ups: 10:05

4. Technique 1: 20:00

5. Circuit 1: 27:50

6. Wall Sit: 39: 45

7. Spin Test Explained: 42:15

8. Spin Test: 46:00

9. Stretching: 52:45

 

 

Weekly Training Plan Recommendations:

 

WEDNESDAY (2/10): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (2/11): Stretching Focus

Perform the stretches from yesterday demonstrated at the end of our session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.

Biceps Stretch
C6/C7 ELDOA
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the Biceps stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

 

FRIDAY (2/12): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Focus on Exercise #1 & #2 in Circuit #1 from our training this week (for 2-3 sets)
For the Turkish Get Up, focus more on the bodyweight version for all levels today. Feel each position, and aim to create more space in your joints. Tomorrow, when you do the full workout, you can progress in any way you like that is mentioned (see tomorrow below). I would suggest if you’d like, you can increase the repetitions today by 1-3, and even go up to the full Get Up, however keep the load light or bodyweight so you’re not overly fatigued for tomorrow. 
For Exercise #2, reduce the reps in by 4-6 from what you did on Wednesday, and stick with 2-3 sets, resting as needed after the super set. Keep technique as the main focus and safe your energy for tomorrow. 
Finish with the Biceps Stretch (only 1 set of 45 seconds) & L5/S1 ELDOA for 1 minute and rest well before your full workout tomorrow. 

 

 

SATURDAY (2/13): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday. 
For the Spin Test specifically, aim to beat your time
If you are able to progress on the other exercises, explore so in the following ways:
Add 1-4 repetitions to each main exercise
Explore progressing to the next skill progression (based on where you finished on Wednesday)
For the Turkish Get Up:
Beginners - Progress by first adding a load, and focusing on only going up to the Elbow Post Position. Once you are comfortable with that, you can continue on to the High Hip
Intermediate - Progress to the full Turkish Get Up to the standing position if you are familiar with the addition steps. If not, stick, with the Half Get Up, and increase any of the progressions mentioned in this list
Add 1-2 sets to one or both circuits, and/or the Bodyweight Wall Sit Squat
Add weight (if this is an option for you based on what you have access to at home)

 

 

SUNDAY (2/14): Rest and Play!

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:
Hiking for ~45 minutes (long duration cardio, moderate walking pace)
Rowing Machine ~8-15 minutes (cardio focus, moderate pace)
Meditation 5-20 minutes (especially if you are feeling physically or mentally stressed)

 

 

MONDAY (2/15): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform your Spin Test only from Wednesday’s workout (aim to beat your time)
If you would like, following your Spin Test, you can also perform 1-3 sets of the Static Wall Sit Squats for 1 min (remember to lower down out of the squat when reaching your threshold).

Finish with these stretches as performed in the workout:

Biceps Stretch
C6/C7 ELDOA
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the Biceps stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

 

TUESDAY (2/16): Stretching Focus
Perform the stretches from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.

 

Biceps Stretch
C6/C7 ELDOA
L5/S1 ELDOA

*Add one additional set to the Biceps stretch, and perform 3 sets of 30 seconds with a 10 second rest in between on each side.

 

Enjoy,

Mike

name: Joint Space
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Here's a curious question for ya, "how would you like to age?"

 

I invite you to take a moment and reflect on this.

 

While I was meditating this weekend, I sat with this and a time from my past came up.

 

I was 19 and the “strongest” I've been in my entire life.

 

Squatting and deadlifting over 600lbs, and bench pressing over 450lbs. 

 

I could push a very respectable amount of weight, (which was awesome) however parts of me were frustrated too...

 

 

For my job as a strength coach, I had to demonstrate many athletic movements to my athletes on a daily basis.

 

I LOVED feeling super strong, however, I was stiff, rigid, and my body simply didn’t feel great. Little injuries would pop up, like a strained pec and shoulder, neck tweaks, lower back discomfort when I'd sleep, and more. 

 

If you’re like me then at least a handful of times in your life, you may have said the following:

 

“If I only knew then what I knew now…”

 

And while I do believe that everything happens for a reason, to teach us something our own evolution, there are certain things that I know would have been SO helpful to know.

 

Three of those things with regards to movement are the importance of:

 

Joint space
Excellent body awareness
Strength and control through new ranges of motion

 

When I think of one of the biggest game-changers for me, the addition of a precise and specific postural strengthening program with ELDOAs were it for me. 

 

ELDOAs allowed me to improve all of the above and:

 

Increase recovery
Reduce and eliminate my lower back pain 
Help me get into challenging positions (like a cossack squat) WAY easier
Improve circulation
My overall sense of well being

 

If you want not just to move, but move well and freely as you age, then I highly recommended signing up for an opportunity coming up this weekend. 

 

I’m bringing in ELDOA certifying instructor, Justin Brien, on Saturday 2/20 to teach a 90 minute ELDOA virtual workshop + guided ELDOA workout (note - you can access the recording if you cannot make it live). 

 

 

Here is a personal invitation from Justin, as well as more on this impactful method. 

 

I believe in the results so much that these postures (they only take 1 minute btw!), can provide, that even if it’s not something you may be interested in right now, please do share with any friends and family members who either may be in pain, or looking to level up their performance for the longterm.

 

Click here to register and for more info.

 

Wishing you all the best,
Mike

The rest period will be as needed, and I suggest going one weight lighter if you have it compared to what you will use in tomorrow’s workout
You can also add in 1-2 sets of the Upper Abdominal Roll Ups with Rotations, for 8-10 reps each side following your Kettlebell Skill work

Explore progressing to the next skill progression (based on where you finished on Wednesday)
Add 1-2 sets 
Add weight (if this is an option for you based on what you have access to at home)

Easy morning walk (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes

MONDAY (2/22): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform 2-4 rounds of the Bulgarian Bag and Bodyweight Circuit. Aim to keep the rest periods in between sets between 30-45 seconds. 
Prior to your working sets, perform at least 1-2 technique sets where you focus on only one element you’d like to improve on for that particular exercise. The repetitions should be kept on the lower side for this technique work (approximately 4-8 reps)

Finish with these stretches as performed in the workout:

1. T8/T9 ELDOA

  • Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday.
  • If you are able to progress on any of the exercises, explore so in the following ways:
  1. Add 1-4 repetitions to each main exercise (for Kettlebell Exercise #1, aim to accomplish more reps in the 20-30 second working time frame - depending on what time duration (20 or 30 seconds) you chose based on your level)
  2. Explore progressing to the next skill progression (based on where you finished on Wednesday)
  3. Add 1-2 sets 
  4. Add weight (if this is an option for you based on what you have access to at home)

 

 

SUNDAY (2/21): Rest and Play!

  • A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
  • Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:
  • Easy morning walk (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
  • Rowing Machine 1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time
  • Breathing Squats for 5-20 minutes.These can be found in Paul Chek’s book, How to Eat, Move, and Be Healthy. Or you can go to this link: https://www.paulcheksblog.com/how-to-work-in-with-breathing-squats/

 

 

MONDAY (2/22): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

  • Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
  • Perform 2-4 rounds of the Bulgarian Bag and Bodyweight Circuit. Aim to keep the rest periods in between sets between 30-45 seconds. 
  • Prior to your working sets, perform at least 1-2 technique sets where you focus on only one element you’d like to improve on for that particular exercise. The repetitions should be kept on the lower side for this technique work (approximately 4-8 reps)

Finish with these stretches as performed in the workout:

1. T8/T9 ELDOA

2. C4/C5 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

TUESDAY (2/23): Stretching Focus
Perform the stretches from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to these stretches.

 

1. T8/T9 ELDOA

2. C4/C5 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA
 

 

Enjoy,

Mike

 

 

P.S. Do you have a friend that you'd like to invite to one of our workouts whom you know would dig what we do here? If so, shoot me an email and I'd be happy to offer them a free class so they can see how we roll! ; )

name: ELDOA 2 Annoucement
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Yup, 40%! 

 

Crazy right?

 

Those who know me, are well aware that for a long time (especially when I was competing regularly), the majority of my funds would go to: quality food, hiring great coaches, and self-care to aid in recovery.

 

When competing, with such high training volumes, and at times having to push into the "red zone" to prepare for 10 minutes, continuous Clean and Jerks with double 72lb kettlebells (without setting them down), there were times that my body would “feel” it.

 

And that wasn't always fun.

 

To help combat this, I would often hop in a float tank, get massage therapy, acupuncture, chiropractic adjustments, neurosomatic therapy, ice baths, sauna, and more - all so that I could offset the stresses hard training would put on my body.

 

Whether you’re competing as an athlete or not, what is important is that YOU become your own best therapist.

 

For me, when I added ELDOA strengthening exercises to my program, on top of healthy living practices, I found that my self-care bill dropped approximately 40%! 

 

I can tell you from first-hand experience that seeing this was incredibly empowering. 

 

I was able to gain more control over my healing and recovery.

 

 

One of the best part I like about the ELDOAs are that they only take one minute each to do. 

 

And even if all you do is one each day, over time, this can have a significant positive impact on your health. 

 

This Saturday, I am STOKED to bring in good friend Justin Brien to teach an ELDOA Virtual Workshop and Workout exclusively for my community.

 

And it’s only $97.

 

Improve your recovery
Reduce body pains
Increase Performance
Feel better!

 

Click here to learn more about this 90 minute workshop on 2/20, you won’t regret it.

 

Best,
Mike

name: Goal Setting Workshop 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I know that driven people will sacrifice everything for their goals only to arrive and still not feel satisfied. 

 

I’ve been the same way throughout many points of my life.

 

Back in 2012, I was making my first run at my BIG goal of achieving the Kettlebell Sport Rank - Master of Sport. This elite rank for my bodyweight was 45+ unbroken, Clean and Jerks (no setting the kettlebells down) for 10 minutes with (2) 72lb bells.  

 

This was a HUGE jump for me.

 

 

For four+ months, much of life looked like this:

 

Training my a$$ off 4-5x/week 
Running 30-60 minutes each morning
Eating a super clean (and restrictive) diet to cut nearly 20lbs
Cutting out nearly all social activities with friends

 

At the end, when the competition came, I arrived close to the goal, but didn’t reach it.

 

This story was repeated for nearly 4 more years until I finally was "successful."

 

But success felt empty.

 

The more sacrifice and discipline (and even suffering to some extent) I endured, the larger the gap between surface-level satisfaction, and true fulfillment felt. 

 

It took me a VERY long time to learn how to better set, train for, and enjoy the process of reaching goals.

 

Do you resonate with holding yourself back because the process of accomplishing an important goal is so uncomfortable?

 

Here’s something to meditate on: what could you accomplish if you enjoyed each small step along the way?

 

Imagine arriving at your next goal and being able to celebrate because you’ve enjoyed the process from the start.

 

This month’s 90 minute virtual workshop is going to be fire and I’m bringing in Holistic Health Coach and the yin to my yang, Lauren Rose.

 

Sign up today with a spouse or friend. Use the BOGO offer to send a friend a gift or to make the workshop half price when you go in on it with a friend. 

 

Click here to register, and please email me if you'd like to gift this to a friend and use the Buy One Gift One

FREE offer. 

 

Yours In health,

Mike

name: Rituals Final Email
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

When I was powerlifting, a big goal meant that I was checked out from every non-essential task for weeks. 

 

I didn’t realize it at the time, but I was teaching myself that big goals are terrible things to go after. I taught myself to hold back because the process of accomplishing an important goal was so uncomfortable. 

 

Yes, I got some big lifts, but what could I have accomplished if I had found how to enjoy the process along the way? 

 

More important than my own goal chasing as a twenty-something year old athlete, what could you accomplish if you enjoyed each small step along the way?

 

The workshop this Saturday will show you how to keep your life and relationships prioritized as you chase down goals. 

 

Stop letting your goals drive you crazy 
Make the process of achievement worthwhile regardless of the outcome (teach yourself to enjoy going after what you want)
CRUSH! 

Imagine arriving at your next goal and letting yourself love the achievement because you’ve enjoyed the process from the start.

 

Some of what you’ll learn:

Why goals without values do not work
How some of the most common words destroy your ability to stick with goals
Why rituals aren’t only for hippies...

Sign up today (click here) with a spouse or friend. Use the BOGO offer to send a friend a gift to join you free!

Upon registering you’ll receive a code you can share with your friend/family member.

 

Hope to see you soon!

Mike

 

 

P.S.

Rituals help high performers achieve amazing things by connecting each small action to the larger mission or goal. Top athletes, CEOs, and entrepreneurs ALL use rituals to enhance their life.

name: Bags and Bells ELITE/Pro Plan 3/24
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

 

Please see the below information for your workout download and training plan:

 

3/24/2021 Workout Download:

Link: https://vimeo.com/528433463/bb98ae79cd

 

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (3/24): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (3/25): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

1. Walk It Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Muscle Group Stretches (Hamstrings, Quads, and Upper Body)

 

 

FRIDAY (3/26): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform 1 set of each of the exercises that you will perform in the full workout tomorrow. Rest as needed and treat this is a recovery/preparation type session. I suggest keeping the reps between 8-10 on each or below.
Spins Alternating
Push Up to KB Pull Through
Snatch
Side Handle Single Leg Alternating RDL to Reverse Lunge
KB Goblet Squat with Front Kick
Bulgarian Bag Mtn Climbers (wide around the bag)
Squat and Press

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Walk It Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Muscle Group Stretches (Hamstrings, Quads, and Upper Body)

 

 

SATURDAY (3/27): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday.

 

 

SUNDAY (3/28): Rest and Play!

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:
Easy morning walk (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Rowing Machine 1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time
Sprints of 20 yards x 6-10 sets, resting as needed (if you do this, perform the core temperature warm up and joint mobility beforehand)

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Walk It Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Muscle Group Stretches (Hamstrings, Quads, and Upper Body)

 

 

MONDAY (3/29): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform Tabata Supersets Below:

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (3/31): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (4/1): Recovery Focus

Perform 1-2 Sets of the following exercises for 8-12 reps, resting as needed in between sets
Spinal Good-mornings x 20-30 reps
Abdominal Roll Ups x 8-15 reps
Side of Hip Raises (any position you'd like to work on) x 10-20 reps
Bulgarian Bag Open Arm Side to Side Swing with Rotation x 10-12 each side
Bulgarian Bag Half Spin OR Alternating Half Swing with Rotational Pivot x 8-10 each side

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Outside Hamstring (Bicep Femoris) Stretch

2. T8/T9 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

SATURDAY (4/3): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday.

 

 

SUNDAY (3/28): Rest and Play!

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time
Sprints of 20 yards x 3-8 sets, resting as needed (if you do this, perform the core temperature warm up and joint mobility beforehand)

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Outside Hamstring (Bicep Femoris) Stretch

2. T8/T9 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

MONDAY (3/29): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform this sequence below as a continuous circuit (2-4 sets, resting up to 1 minute after each circuit).
Bulgarian Bag Half Spin OR Alternating Half Swing with Rotational Pivot x 8-10 each side
Kettlebell Overhead Press OR Static Counter Overhead Press OR Alt. Countered Sea Saw Press x 8-10 each side
Side Of Hip Raises (stick with your weakest position x 15-25 each side
Bent Over Bulgarian Bag Rows x 8-12
Abdominal Roll Ups x 8-15

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Outside Hamstring (Bicep Femoris) Stretch

2. T8/T9 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

 

TUESDAY (3/30): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

 

1. Outside Hamstring (Bicep Femoris) Stretch

2. T8/T9 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

Have fun!

Mike

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

If you’ve been on my list for a while then you’ve probably bought at least one of my products… 

 

And if not, that’s ok. Some people need a little more time than others… 

 

But what I hope we’ve developed over time is a sense of trust… 

 

That you trust me to be honest with you and only share things with you that I think will be both interesting and valuable to you.

 

So many people out there will just promote whatever makes them the most money. 

 

Not me. 

 

I’ll only share other people’s stuff if I truly believe that are the real deal.  

 

Like my friend Jator Pierre. 

 

Last week we did a super impactful IG Live talk, where I interviewed him on "How to Become Friends with Fear". This was so valuable and I received very heartfelt messages from people afterwards that let me know it really struck a cord with them. 

 

Here's the full interview "Becoming Friends with Fear" - you'll get tons from it. 

 

Jator is the founder and lead coach at HoL Healing – an alternative and holistic health service focused on helping you towards lasting wellness in your body, mind and heart.  

 

With his team of HoL Certified Coaches, Jator helps people all around the world who feel like there is more to life than they are experiencing right now.  

 

Through a mixture of courses, coaching and private deep work, Jator’s clients are supported to explore and massively improve their health and wellbeing.  

 

The end-result?  

 

They start feeling like themselves again, but better. 

 

Who wouldn’t want to feel like that for a change?! 

 

Jator Pierre is about to launch his new community coaching program, HoL BEING, and to celebrate, he’s giving away access to one of his best training courses to our/my readers – completely free!

Restore Your Power is a self-guided program that can help you say goodbye to fatigue and hello to freedom. 

 

Wishing you a wonderful rest of your day,

Mike

name: Bags and Bells ELITE/Pro Plan 4/7
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout download and training plan:

 

4/7/2021 Workout Download:

Link: https://vimeo.com/534085831/d2eae13d40

 

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (4/7): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (4/8): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

 

1. Biceps Myofascial Stretch

2. Psoas Myofascial Stretch

3. T11/T12 ELDOA

4. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

FRIDAY (4/9): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform 1-3 circuits of the following exercises for 8-10 reps each side, resting as needed in between. Focus on one technique point in each exercise. 
Kettlebell Single Arm Swings OR Floating High Pulls
Bulgarian Bag Back Step (Curtsy Style) Lunges - Bag resting on shoulders

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Psoas Myofascial Stretch

2. T11/T12 ELDOA

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

SATURDAY (4/10): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday. 
Aim to increase how well you performed your 5 minute Snatch/floating high pull/swing/deadlift set via progressing the movement, increasing reps per arm, reducing the times the bell rests on the floor, or the amount of hand switches
For your Bulgarian Bag circuit, aim to add in one additional round if you'd like and can handle the volume well

 

SUNDAY (4/11): Rest and Play!

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time
Sprints of 20 yards x 3-8 sets, resting as needed (if you do this, perform the core temperature warm up and joint mobility beforehand)

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Biceps Myofascial Stretch

2. Psoas Myofascial Stretch

3. T11/T12 ELDOA

4. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

MONDAY (4/12): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform this sequence below as a continuous circuit (3-6 sets, resting up to 30-45 sec after each circuit).
Bulgarian Bag Alt. Curtsy Lunge OR Alt. Overhead Press & Curtsy Lunge x 8-10 each side
Shoulder Front Raises + Hold x (5 reps + 5 sec hold each side)
Inside Grip Bent Over Rows x 10-15

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Biceps Myofascial Stretch

2. Psoas Myofascial Stretch

3. T11/T12 ELDOA

4. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

TUESDAY (4/13): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

 

1. Biceps Myofascial Stretch

2. Psoas Myofascial Stretch

3. T11/T12 ELDOA

4. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

Have a great week and enjoy!

Mike

 

 

P.S.  I'll be bringing in renowned gut health expert, popular podcast host, and author Michael Ruscio on Saturday 24th at 9amPST for you :) You will get this workshop for FREE as being a part of the Elite membership.
