text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your training plan:

 

Also, here is the download link in case you missed it in the prior email: 

https://vimeo.com/536936908/acbe507d1f

 

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (4/14): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (4/15): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

 

1. Quad (Rectus Femoris) Myofascial Stretch

2. T6/T7 ELDOA - perform (2) sets - (1) in each lower body position

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

FRIDAY (4/16): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Once you complete your warm up, perform one set as demonstrated in the workout of the Royal Coil. Hold each side for 5 seconds. 
Perform 1-3 sets of the following exercises for 8-10 reps each side, resting as needed in between. This is not an EMOM, Take your time on each exercise and focus on the precision of each rep as well as the side bending as we went over in the class. Aim to be as powerful as possible on every rep. 
Kettlebell Coiling Swing OR Classic Two Hand Swing
Kettlebell RMT Pivot Press OR Classic Single Arm Overhead Press

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Quad (Rectus Femoris) Myofascial Stretch

2. T6/T7 ELDOA - perform (2) sets - (1) in each lower body position

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

SATURDAY (4/17): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as we did on Wednesday. 
Perform (1) additional complete round of training so it is (4) rounds total
The load is up to you if you would like to change the kettlebell/bag weight if you feel confident

 

SUNDAY (4/18): Rest and Play! 

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Depending on your goals, as well as how you are feeling, I would suggest the following options to also consider:
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time
Sprints of 20 yards x 3-8 sets, resting as needed (if you do this, perform the core temperature warm up and joint mobility beforehand)

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Quad (Rectus Femoris) Myofascial Stretch

2. T6/T7 ELDOA - perform (2) sets - (1) in each lower body position

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

MONDAY (4/19): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Once you complete your warm up, perform one priming set as demonstrated in the workout of the Royal Coil. Hold each side for 5 seconds. 
Perform 2-4 circuit of the all four exercises listed below for 6-8 reps each side, resting as needed in between. While this is not an EMOM, you can take up to 45 seconds rest after each exercise. Because your rest period has increased, if you feel confident in increasing the load you can go for it.  
Kettlebell Coiling Swing OR Classic Two Hand Swing
Kettlebell RMT Pivot Press OR Classic Single Arm Overhead Press
Bulgarian Bag Half Spin Squat Jump OR Half Swing and Squat
Four Point Single Arm Body Row OR Four Point Hold (30 sec)

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Quad (Rectus Femoris) Myofascial Stretch

2. T6/T7 ELDOA - perform (2) sets - (1) in each lower body position

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

TUESDAY (4/20): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

 

1. Quad (Rectus Femoris) Myofascial Stretch

2. T6/T7 ELDOA - perform (2) sets - (1) in each lower body position

3. L5/S1 ELDOA

 

Have a great week!

Mike

name: Gut Health Wksp 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I remember it like yesterday. 

 

I came home from work and baked a small piece of salmon for dinner. Not long after eating, I was hurled over my couch in severe stomach pain. 

 

This pain was so bad that all I wanted to do was go to the hospital.

 

What I came to learn after in-depth testing, was that the main culprit of my stomach pains came from a bacteria infection (H. Pylori). I also discovered that I had a fungal overgrowth, parasite infection, and dysbiosis (imbalance of gut bacteria)

 

Wild right?

 

This was at a time in my early twenties, while I was avidly competing in Powerlifting. 

 

Things got so bad that I had to take nearly 6 months off from training entirely to focus my energy on healing these issues. 

 

For a large majority of the time having gastro-intestinal issues, it really wasn't until I was in physical pain, that I knew something was off. 

 

At that time I was only beginning to learn about holistic health, and didn't have the knowledge yet for what look for - plus being a hard charging 20 year old, I needed something significant to happen for me to wake up. 

 

That is why I am honored to bring Gut Health expert and author Dr. Michael Ruscio on this Saturday (4/24) to lead my 90 minute monthly virtual workshop on the fundamentals gut health, its role in performance, plus a Q+A. 

 

This is a huge opportunity to gain fantastic insights from a leading expert.

 

Dr. Ruscio is the author of Healthy Gut, Healthy You - The personalized plan to transform your health from the inside out, and has a top-rated podcast on functional and integrative medicine.

 

Hear what industry experts are saying about him:

text:

It’s the foundation of your overall health and wellness, and it affects everything from how well you sleep to how much energy you have.

Dr. Ruscio's expertise on the gut has been featured on top podcasts such as Robb Wolf, Tom Bilyeu, Chris Kresser, Mind Pump, CarnivoreMD, the Align Podcast, Paul Chek, and many more!

Here's a live interview he did with Tom Bilyeu called, "Your Diet is Fine, Your Lifestyle Sucks," that was excellent. It will give you lots of gems on gut health and as well as provide you insight into Dr. Ruscio's breath of knowledge and experience. 

 

Come learn about the importance of gut health this Saturday, 4/24, with Dr. Ruscio himself at my 90 minute monthly virtual workshop at 9amPST / 12pm EST. 

 

This event can change your life forever. 

 

Click here to register for this private workshop for only $97*.

 

*Also, you can watch the recording for 72 hours if you cannot attend live.

 

I hope to see you there!

name: Chek Live
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Last week, I was having dinner with a close friend - a high-level, talented practitioner. He's someone who is incredible with movement, bodywork, nutrition & lifestyle coaching, and more.

 

He works with many clients (from moms, to the elderly, all the way up to professional athletes we see on TV) and the results he gets are LEGIT.

 

There's one interesting thing, however, that I've noticed in him, in many of my other friends, and even myself until about 3 years ago....

 

His approach to business could more accurately be described as a passionate "hobby" that generates some income, rather than a sustainable, thriving business. 

 

For me personally, for the first ~12 years as a trainer, I didn't want to acknowledge that business itself was a huge weak link for me.

 

I also refused to look at things like:

My self-limiting beliefs around money
My imposture syndrome
The shame and embarrassment I felt when on putting myself out on social media and promoting what I did
How petrified I was ask for a sale

You see, I identified a coach and teacher but certainly not a businessman. 

 

In over 15 years, I have learned a lot of lessons along the way, and am continually learning more each day about how to build a thriving, healthy, holistic business.

 

I'm excited to share with you some of those lessons, tools, and insights that have helped me grow my business into what it is tomorrow, Friday.

 

I'll be interviewed by the Chek Institute at 1pmPST / 4pmEST on "How to Build a Thriving Coaching Business".

 

If you are a coach, teacher, therapist, or trainer, I'll share from authentic experience the best I can to support you. 

 

Head over to the @chekinstitute Instagram tomorrow.

 

Wishing you a wonderful evening,

Mike


P.S.
In two days (Saturday) the exclusive event is happening with gut health expert and author Dr. Ruscio! He will be hosting our 90 min monthly virtual workshop on how to heal your gut and improve gut health for performance.

Sign up right now by clicking here! 

*You will be able to watch the recording for 72 hours if you cannot attend live

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan 4/24
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your training plan:

 

Also, here is the link in case you missed it in the prior email: 

https://vimeo.com/539777737/dc33c98694

 

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (4/21): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (4/22): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

1. Walk it Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Major Muscle Group Stretches: upper body, quads, hamstrings

 

 

FRIDAY (4/23): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform 2-3 sets of the following exercises for 8-10 reps each side, resting as needed in between focusing on technique:

Side whips OR Suples spins

 

Kettlebell - Reverse Lunge Passes

Cement mixer

 

 

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Walk it Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Major Muscle Group Stretches: upper body, quads, hamstrings

 

 

SATURDAY (4/24): Full Workout

Perform the workout exactly as Bridgette led you through on Wednesday. 

 

SUNDAY (4/25): Rest and Play! 

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Explore the below options depending on your goals and try to remain nasal-diaphragmatic (belly) breathing
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Walk it Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Major Muscle Group Stretches: upper body, quads, hamstrings

 

 

MONDAY (4/26): Skill Development #2 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Once you complete your warm up, perform one priming set as demonstrated in the workout of the Royal Coil. Hold each side for 5 seconds. 
Perform 2-4 rounds of the exercises listed below for 8-12 reps, resting as up to 1 minute after each round:
Suples Clean to Squat
Side Swing Curls
Single Leg KB RDL (4-6 each side)

After this, you can complete 2-3 rounds as a finisher of the below:

Bulgarian Bag Complex Series:

Bent over Rows x 3 reps
Push Ups to Hollow Hold to Bulgarian Bag Get Up to Jump x 3 reps

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

1. Walk it Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Major Muscle Group Stretches: upper body, quads, hamstrings

 

 

TUESDAY (4/27): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

 

1. Walk it Out

2. Sky to Toe Reaches

3. Major Muscle Group Stretches: upper body, quads, hamstrings

 

 

 

Have a great weekend!

Mike

 

 

P.S.  Today is your free workshop with Dr. Ruscio on Gut Health, here is you link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/5580027238

 

It starts in 20 minutes at 10amPST / 1pm EST! : )

name: Hunting 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

A few months ago, you may recall I shared about my first Sacred Hunting Immersive Experience with Mansal Denton and Kyle Kingsbury.

 

 

A few of the reasons why I chose to go on the trip:

To experience first hand where my food comes from
To connect with a group of incredible brothers and be of service with Kambo
To gain greater clarity on my purpose in life
To experience this rite of passage, guided with the utmost respect for the land, animals, and ancestors who came before

I'm honored to announce that Mansal Denton is offering this as a private experience for our community, November 5-7th in the Hill Country of Texas. 

 

This will be a very small intimate group, and there are only 3 spots left. 

 

There is also lots to prepare for ahead of time, which is why I am announcing it now. Mansal has a fantastic online preparation program that will get you ready logistically, as well as support you get the most out of this experience mentally, emotionally, and spiritually. 

 

Additionally, as a special addition, in the 6-8 weeks before you will receive from me, a hunting-specific physical preparation program.

 

Please go to www.SacredHunting.com as soon as possible if you're interested to fill out an application. You will hop on a call with Mansal for more detail and screening to see if you are a good fit for this experience. 

 

If you're ready for a life-changing experience, and to grow as a more whole person, we'd love to have you. 

⁠⠀

Best,

Mike

 

P.S.

This month's 90 minute workout is on the Suples Ball! If you have this training tool, or have been waiting to get one, now is the time. I will teach you the fundamentals, as well as take you through a fun workout at the end. 

Click here for details.

name: Re-looking at Goals
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I remember years ago, when I looked at my fitness and competition goals, with so many of them, I thought this:

 

"If I’m consistent, train my a$$ off, and hit all my numbers (meaning I completed the sets, reps, loads, rest, and tempos my coach laid out for me) then I'd feel great, be happy, and successful.

 

Well, interestingly enough, a number of things happened…

I hit some goals
I didn’t hit others
I felt good about myself most times and built confidence
I also felt sh*tty often and would beat myself mentally and emotionally into the ground for "failures" and any small imperfection
I rarely ever missed a workout
I ended up overtraining 
I learned a TON about pushing myself, and also trusting the process, even when uncertainty was present 

All of this is merely to highlight that whether our goals are performance-based, health, aesthetic, or some combination of all three, to be fit AND feel great, we simply cannot treat our bodies like machines. 

 

There are MANY ways to improve and see progress in other key areas. 

 

 

Here are some questions to reflect on in relation to your workouts:

 

Are you noticing you have more energy to put into family time?
Are you finding you are enjoying your workouts more?
Are you feeling more grounded and centered in your communications?
Do you wake up in the morning with less joint stiffness?
Are you more motivated to eat more regularly and more whole foods?

 

If you answered yes, to any of the above, right on! And if not, now may be a good time to re-assess with fresh eyes what your current workout is doing for you outside of the usual measurements of success. 

 

I hope today's email provided you some guidance or inspiration for looking at how what we choose to do in the gym has a direct impact on the things that also matter to us outside of it. Training has the ability to make us better people at the end of the day, which I've found has much less to do with the exact number of reps, sets, loads, rest, and tempo, and instead a deeper level of honest introspection. 

 

 

In health,

Mike

 

P.S. Tomorrow, Thursday, at 9am PST / 12pm EST I’ll be interviewing former national team member, and 16 year Olympic Weightlifting veteran Chelsea Dillon. We will be talking "Pain and Performance" (on my Instagram: @Mike.Salemi). You’ll love what she has to share!

 

P.P.S  Bulgarian Bag full day Virtual Certification with Suples Pro Trainer Bridgette Yates-Hosick and myself happens on 5/29!!! Click below for more info if you're interested in attending:

https://shop.mikesalemi.io/products/tbfi251dfm2oyfg4rwe6qsw2bg7fbx-g648y

name: Iron Sights Podcast
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Since I transitioned out of my family's business and committed fully to the fitness industry, there has been a few key people who have been in my corner all along the way.

 

Scott Howell is one of those special people. 

 

Our friendship started about four years ago when I was helping the guys at Mind Pump Media with a photoshoot for one of their programs. The shoot was held at Scotts rad facility Red Dot Fitness in San Jose, CA.

 

Upon meeting Scott, I remember he immediately shook my hand and thanked me for what I was doing positively in the industry. His demeanor and words left an impact on me.

 

Since then, I've run numerous trainings for his staff, enjoyed very deep and real conversations with him (he has extensive knowledge on every aspect of fitness and fitness business), and I've shot programs like Kettlebell Lifestyle in his facility.

 

I am SO honored to share he just started an epic podcast with some fantastic guests lined up, and I feel so lucky to have been selected to be one of them. 

 

 

In today's Episode #5, I went to Scott's badass studio, where we talked about many things that I hope you'll find interesting! We discuss the importance of mindset in being the best version of yourself, "the grind," maintaining balance, committing to excellence, and knowing when "less is more" is vital on the road to success.

 

Listen to the episode here.

 

I hope you get lots of value from it,

 

All the best,

Since I transitioned out of my family's business and committed fully to the fitness industry, there has been a few key people who have been in my corner all along the way.

Upon meeting Scott, I remember he immediately shook my hand and thanked me for what I was doing positively in the industry. His demeanor and words left an impact on me.

 

Since then, I've run numerous trainings for his staff, enjoyed very deep and real conversations with him (he has extensive knowledge on every aspect of fitness and fitness business), and I've shot programs like Kettlebell Lifestyle in his facility.

 

I am SO honored to share he just started an epic podcast with some fantastic guests lined up, and I feel so lucky to have been selected to be one of them. 

 

 

In today's Episode #5, I went to Scott's badass studio, where we talked about many things that I hope you'll find interesting! text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout and training plan on 5/26:

https://vimeo.com/555307326/37a09e2328

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (5/26): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (5/27): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Forearm Myofascial Stretches (3 Position: Fingers Back, at a 45 Degree Angle, and Turned in As Much As Possible)
Shoulder ELDOA (2 Position: Fingers Up and Back)
L5/S1 ELDOA

 

FRIDAY (5/28): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform Any Of the Following Exercise Progressions for 6-10 reps each (this can also be used as a technical warm up progression before your training sets)
Two Hand Deadlift
Two Hand Swing
Single Arm Swing
Single Arm Swing Floating High Pull
Alternating Floating Hight Pull x 1 plus Half Snatch x 1
When you are ready to start, perform 1-4 rounds of 6-10 reps of this exercise followed by bodyweight Get Ups for 8-10 reps
Rest period is up to you, since tomorrow will be a full workout, take additional rest here after each round (up to 1 min) so you are fully recovered

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

Forearm Myofascial Stretches (3 Position: Fingers Back, at a 45 Degree Angle, and Turned in As Much As Possible)
Shoulder ELDOA (2 Position: Fingers Up and Back)
L5/S1 ELDOA

 

SATURDAY (5/29): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday. Feel free to add to the below if you'd like to add additional volume:
1-2 additional rounds of the Bulgarian Bag Circuit

 

 

SUNDAY (5/30): Rest and Play! 

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Explore the below options depending on your goals and try to remain nasal-diaphragmatic (belly) breathing
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500-1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

Forearm Myofascial Stretches (3 Position: Fingers Back, at a 45 Degree Angle, and Turned in As Much As Possible)
Shoulder ELDOA (2 Position: Fingers Up and Back)
L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

MONDAY (5/31): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

 

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform 1-6 rounds of 6-10 reps of the following exercises, taking 30-60 seconds rest following each one:
Alternating Pummel OR Alternating Spin-Pummel Combo
Pause Squat OR Pause Squat Thruster with Alternating Rotation
Alternating Shoulder Load

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

Forearm Myofascial Stretches (3 Position: Fingers Back, at a 45 Degree Angle, and Turned in As Much As Possible)
Shoulder ELDOA (2 Position: Fingers Up and Back)
L5/S1 ELDOA

 

 

TUESDAY (6/1): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Forearm Myofascial Stretches (3 Position: Fingers Back, at a 45 Degree Angle, and Turned in As Much As Possible)
Shoulder ELDOA (2 Position: Fingers Up and Back)
L5/S1 ELDOA

 

Enjoy!

Mike

 

P.S. This month Dr. Drew Vercellino will be presenting for our monthly workshop on understanding and helping to resolve migraines on June 19th. Mark the date down, it's going to be chalked full of value! : )

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 6/9
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout and training plan on 6/9 with Bridgette:

https://vimeo.com/561379257/8405f07cc4

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (6/9): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (6/10): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Quads and Hamstrings)
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 minute

 

FRIDAY (6/11): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Today we will focus on KB Snatch or Swing training and technqiue. Once you warm and work up to your desired level of progression/difficulty below, then from there complete 10-15 reps x 4-6 sets at full recovery (as much time as you need for you to feel totally back to normal - don't take more than 4  minutes though). Once you complete these sets perform 3-4 sets of 10 reps of Single Arm Bent Over Rows.  
Two Hand Deadlift
Two Hand Swing 
Single Arm Swing
Single Arm Snatch

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Quads and Hamstrings)
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 minute

 

SATURDAY (6/12): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday 

 

 

SUNDAY (6/13): Rest and Play! 

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Explore the below options depending on your goals and try to remain nasal-diaphragmatic (belly) breathing
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500-1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time

Finish with this cool down:

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Upper Body Stretches (Quads and Hamstrings)
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 minute

 

 

MONDAY (6/14): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

 

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform a Superset (back to back sets of the below two exercises):
Spins 
Kettlebell Swings or Snatches
When you do the above superset, your goal is to complete a total of 80 each.  After each super set, you can rest up to 1 minute before your next combo set. Here's an example of what your first 3 sets might look like:
Set 1: Spins (15/15) + Snatches (10/10) -- REST 30 sec
Set 2: Spins (15/15) + Snatches (10/10) -- REST 30 sec
Set 3 Spins (8/8) + Snatches (10/10) -- REST 30 sec
Continue the above until your total work is 80 Spins and 80 Snatches
Finish with this cool down:
Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Quads and Hamstrings)
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 minute

 

 

TUESDAY (6/15): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Quads and Hamstrings)
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 minute

 

All the best,

Mike

 

P.S. This month Dr. Drew Vercellino will be presenting for our monthly workshop on understanding and helping to resolve migraines on June 19th.  I hope you can make it!

name: Migraine Workshop
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

We know that migraines and headaches of all types massively impact the health and quality of life of countless people in our community and throughout the world.

 

In fact, migraines impact 1 BILLION people worldwide and 39 million men, women and children here in the U.S.

 

While some individuals will experience severe migraines and headaches on a monthly basis, many experience daily debilitating headaches with medications and other remedies doing little to stop the pain and disability.

 

We want that to STOP now.

 

Whether it’s you who are suffering or a child or loved, the information we will be covering has the power to transform your health and lives.

 

For this Saturday’s 90 minute virtual workshop, I'm bringing in expert Dr. Drew Vercellino to share and teach:

✅ The role of your nervous system in headaches and migraines and signs that a common imbalance in that system may be causing your headaches.

✅ One of the most common causes of headaches and migraines (AND also one of the most overlooked causes!)

✅ Ways to improve your nervous system health to decrease headache and migraine frequency and intensity.

✅ Natural solutions to end chronic headaches and migraines for good.

 

The information in this class has been transformational in the lives of so many migraine and headache sufferers.

 

Dr. Drew can’t wait to meet you and is looking forward to helping you get the relief you deserve. 

 

Click here for more information and to register, cost is only $97 and this information is worth the price multiple times over if you suffer or know anyone who suffers from regular headaches or migraines.

 

*If you cannot attend live, you will be able to watch a recording for 72 hours following

 

Hope to see you there!

Mike

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 6/16
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout and training plan on 6/16:

 

https://vimeo.com/564362142/e569803c4e

 

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (6/16): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (6/17): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Biceps Myofascial Stretch x 45 sec x 2
T8/T9 ELDOA (level I) OR T7/T8 ELDOA (level II) x 1 min
C6/C7 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

FRIDAY (6/18): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Today's focus is gong to be on the "Whip" element during your Bulgarian Bag Spin. The whip technique happens as the Bag accelerates past your hip and into the finish position behind the back at shoulder blade level. When you do this your goal is to finish behind the back with the handles pointing upwards. 
Perform the below in a Superset fashion (back to back) with up to 30 second rest
Half Spin OR Full Spin with a Pause: 3-6 sets x 8-12 reps each side
Kettlebell Bent Two Hand Over Row with or without Rotation: 3-6 sets x 12-16 reps

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

Biceps Myofascial Stretch x 45 sec x 2
T8/T9 ELDOA (level I) OR T7/T8 ELDOA (level II) x 1 min
C6/C7 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

SATURDAY (6/19): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday. 
**Remember to do your best to stay only breathing in and out through the nose when you do this workout. Your pacing will be determine by your ability to remain calm and continue breathing through the nose. 

 

 

SUNDAY (6/20): Rest and Play! 

A great option today would be to get outside for unstructured, unbound play. 
Explore the below options depending on your goals and try to remain nasal-diaphragmatic (belly) breathing
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes 
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500-1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time

Finish with this cool down:

Biceps Myofascial Stretch x 45 sec x 2
T8/T9 ELDOA (level I) OR T7/T8 ELDOA (level II) x 1 min
C6/C7 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

 

MONDAY (6/21): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

 

Perform both the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start 
Perform the below in a circuit fashion (back to back) with up to 60 second rest ((aim to maintain breathing only in and out through the nose))
Half Spin OR Full Spin with a Pause: 4-6 sets x 8-15 reps each side
Swing Squat: 4-6 sets x 8-12 reps
Bulgarian Bag Sit Up and Press OR to **Stand and Press: 4-6 sets x 6-10 reps

*This exercise we did not demo however is a progression from the Bulgarian Bag Sit Up to Press you are familiar with. If you have the ability, as you roll your body up, use controlled momentum to rise up onto your feet and stand. Once in the standing position, press overhead and repeat the movement. You will love this one!

Finish with this cool down:
Biceps Myofascial Stretch x 45 sec x 2
T8/T9 ELDOA (level I) OR T7/T8 ELDOA (level II) x 1 min
C6/C7 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

 

TUESDAY (6/22): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Biceps Myofascial Stretch x 45 sec x 2
T8/T9 ELDOA (level I) OR T7/T8 ELDOA (level II) x 1 min
C6/C7 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

All the best,

Mike

 

P.S. This Saturday Dr. Drew Vercellino will be presenting for our monthly workshop on understanding and helping to resolve migraines at 9amPST. Your link will be sent out later today to join! : )

name: Migraine Workshop 2
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Chances are that either someone you know or you yourself have experienced the negative effects of Migraine Headaches. Just in the US alone, they affect over  39 million people!

 

Why are so many people not just affected by Migraines but aren’t finding solutions? 

The answer is quite simple, many health care providers just aren’t aware of other available options, or even worse, don’t want to even entertain the idea of anything working outside of what they know. 

 

You may recall the other day I sent out an email letting you know of a 90 minute virtual workshop happening this Saturday, where I'm bringing in expert Dr. Drew Vercellino to present on this topic exclusively for our community. 

 

You will have the opportunity to ask your questions to Dr. Drew directly. This is a very hands on, interactive workshop with  exercise walk throughs, and direct Q+A included so you walk away with things you can do right now.

 

One of the goals of this workshop is to expose some hidden truths that are so often overlooked and give ideas and strategies to help make changes in people's lives immediately. 

 

Workshop Details:

Date:  Saturday June 19th, 9:00am PST. (90 minutes in duration)

Location: Virtual (72 hour recording link send post workshop)

Cost: $97

 

Not only will we discuss the degree of impact migraines and headaches have on our society, we’ll also cover:

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 6/23
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the below information for your workout and training plan on 6/23 with Bridgette! 

https://vimeo.com/566712476/97b105bfb2

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (6/23): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (6/24): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Groin, Quads, Hamstrings, Rhomboids) and Floor Flow

 

FRIDAY (6/25): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform the following circuit (2-4 rounds, 20 sec on, 20 sec rest):
Spin x 20sec Left (20s REST)
Spin x 20sec Right (20s REST)
Kettlebell Swing OR Swing-Swing Squat Combo x 20sec (20s REST)
Once you've completed the above, rest for 1-2 minutes and then perform 1-3 sets of Single Arm Kettlebell Rows for 10 sec Left Arm + 10 sec Right Arm with 20 second REST

Finish with this cool down as performed in the workout:

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Groin, Quads, Hamstrings, Rhomboids) and Floor Flow

 

SATURDAY (6/26): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday 

 

SUNDAY (6/27): Rest and Play! 

Cycling Sprints (if you've got extra juice ; ): Cycle easy for 5-10 minutes to start. Then once warm, Sprint for 5-10 sec > Cycle Easy Recovery for 50 sec and repeat this superset 6-10x. Complete this session with a 5-10 minute easy cycling cool down. 
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500-1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time

Finish with this cool down:

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Groin, Quads, Hamstrings, Rhomboids) and Floor Flow

 

MONDAY (6/28): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Perform the following circuits as laid out below:
CIRCUIT 1 (2-4 rounds, 30 sec on, 15 sec rest)
Alternating Arm Throw or Shoulder Load x 30sec (15s REST)
Bulgarian Bag Hammer Snatch x 30sec (15s REST)

REST 1-3 Minutes following Circuit 1 before starting Circuit 2

CIRCUT 2 (2-4 rounds, 20 sec on, 10 sec rest)
Kettlebell Lunge and Pass x 30sec (15s REST)
Push Ups x 30sec (15s REST)
Kettlebell Rows: 30sec (15s REST)

Finish with this cool down:

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Groin, Quads, Hamstrings, Rhomboids) and Floor Flow

 

TUESDAY (6/29): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Walk It Out 
Sky to Toe Reaches
Stretches (Groin, Quads, Hamstrings, Rhomboids) and Floor Flow

 

Have a fantastic week!

Mike

Finish with this cool down:

Lat Myofascial Strech x 30 sec x 3 sets
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

MONDAY (7/12): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Perform the following circuits as laid out below:
Superset the following for 2-4 rounds, resting as needed to feel fully recovered before coming back to the Hammer Snatches
Bulgarian Bag Hammer Snatch x 5
Bulgarian Bag Lamb Swing x 8-10 each side
Once you've completed the above perform, the following superset for 2-4 rounds, resting as needed in between:
1. Bent Over Kettlebell Open Palm Grip Row x 8-20 reps with a 10-15 second Hold
2. Wall Sits, Max Duration Hold (remember to lower down to come out of the position once you've hit your fatigue threshold)

Finish with this cool down:

Lat Myofascial Strech x 30 sec x 3 sets
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

Lat Myofascial Strech x 30 sec x 3 sets
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

Have fun!

name: Real Men
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

This is the start of a line I imagine you’ve heard at one time or another. Maybe it was in a movie, during a TV show, or maybe it was even at home.

 

A few common ways I’ve heard this phrase conclude are:

Real men don’t show weakness
Real men don’t express their emotions
Real men don’t cry
And the list goes on...

Well, what does being “real” man mean anyway?

 

My answer? 

 

I don't have the slightest clue lol.

 

BUT, what I do know to be true in my heart, is that a “balanced” man looks and feels like one who embodies:

 

Strength AND Vulnerability

 

I bring this up here because I’m going to share something that in fact scares a part of me to be more vocal about...

 

As you may already know, for so long much of my identity was wrapped up as being an athlete.

 

When I stopped competing 4 years ago, a part of me felt lost and without direction. 

 

During this time, I did, however, find tremendous purpose in teaching.

 

Additionally, as I grew, I also found great fulfillment in holding space and supporting people in their growth in areas outside of physical training.

 

In this moment, I am personally at a transition point in my life. 

 

While I LOVE teaching all things physical movement, I also have felt a deep calling to energize more things that bring our mind, emotions, and spirit into harmony - so that we can be less crushed by our limiting beliefs and live in a way that expresses greater internal freedom.

 

Stay tuned for more content that will not only enhance the ways you train more intentionally, but enliven your entire being.

 

On that note, today I have an extra special treat for you.

 

You see, my buddy, Johnny Elsasser, is as badass as they come. Seriously.

 

He was an elite army ranger, did multiple tours in Iraq, and guarded the US Ambassador to Iraq.

 

In addition to being a beast, Johnny also embodies what I shared earlier as a “balanced man” and has a fantastic podcast called the Art of Masculinity. 

 

I’ll be having Johnny on my Instagram today, Friday at 1pm PST / 4pmEST, and we are going to speak on this very topic. 

 

 

I’m confident everyone who listens will be able to take away valuable gems on things such as:

Leadership
Working through adversity
Grounding yourself
Teamwork
Emotional wellbeing
And More

 

This IG Live will be hosted on: @Mike.Salemi.

 

I look forward to having you join us today and getting to meet such a special human and someone I feel honored to call a friend, Johnny Elsasser.

 

See you at 1pmPST / 4pmEST on Instagram today,

 

Mike

name: Power Email
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Powerlifting is actually strength lifting.

 

Most people training for power with the squat, bench press, and deadlift are not truly training for power. 

 

The definition of power is: (Force x Distance) / Time

 

Time is a HUGE part of the equation above and is a big distinguishing factor, whether you are developing strength or power. Remember this, power movements are to be done QUICK!

 

In my opinion, just about all of us will benefit from power training in our programs if we have achieved:

 

Prerequisite flexibility
Prerequisite stability
Base strength

 

If you’re grinding, it isn’t power.

 

The Olympic Lifts Didn’t Get My Athletes the Best Results

 

When I was a collegiate strength and conditioning coach for Santa Clara university, I trained the men’s tennis team. Tennis in particular requires high amounts of repeated power, as well as agility (ability to change directions) in all planes. 

 

At the time, I was competing in the sport of Olympic Weightlifting and just starting my journey with Kettlebells. Like many coaches, I prescribed the barbell clean, jerk, or snatch to increase power. 

 

It didn’t work very well.

 

Even with these Division I athletes, teaching a group of 8-12 athletes was time-consuming and their skill with these movements was quite low coming in. I never felt I could actually spend enough time with them (session days and durations of gym time were not always consistent nor could be very long) to support them in developing their technique enough to be able to get the most out of it. 

 

Instead, I ended up utilizing kettlebells and medicine balls with MUCH more success and less of a risk of injury.

 

You Want POWER

 

Power training helps develop fast-twitch muscle fibers. Fast-twitch muscles are beneficial to anyone who wants to jump higher, run faster, and throw harder. But power doesn’t only benefit athletes.

 

Training power heightens and enhances the performance of your nervous system as well by improving reaction time, making you more resilient, durable, AND adaptable in daily life.

 

Here are the 3 keys to ensure you are getting the most out of your power training.

 

Have the technical proficiency to perform the movement
Maintain speed throughout the set
Maintain your quality of technique throughout the set

 

If any of these are lacking or are not up to par, then consider strongly revising the approach in any combination of the ways below.

 

Choose a simpler movement you are comfortable with
Reduce the number of reps, load, or sets to the point that you can maintain your speed
Reduce the number of reps, load, or sets to the point that you can maintain your technique

 

Stay tuned for next week's video to discuss this further, as well as for technical coaching on two of my favorite power-producing lifts.

 

Powerful people are quick, springy, agile, and stronger than they look. 

 

Stay strong (and powerful),


 

Mike

 

P.S. I’ll be talking about power and how you can effectively develop it all month. Stay tuned! And if you’ve wondered why I love the kettlebell and Bulgarian Bag so much, power is one of the big reasons. These tools are perfect for keeping speed high with techniques you can master quickly.  

 

P.P.S. Tomorrow, Wed. 7/21 @2pmPST / 5pmEST I will be interviewing owner of the biodynamic farm, Be Here Farm + Nature - Jared Pickard. Jared was a recent guest on Paul Chek's Podcast, which was fantastic! Tomorrow tune into IG Live (@Mike.Salemi) for what will be a great conversation called "Beyond Organic Farming + Holistic Self Care"! : )

  2. Maintain speed throughout the set
  3. Maintain your quality of technique throughout the set

 

If any of these are lacking or are not up to par, then consider strongly revising the approach in any combination of the ways below.

 

  • Choose a simpler movement you are comfortable with
  • Reduce the number of reps, load, or sets to the point that you can maintain your speed
  • Reduce the number of reps, load, or sets to the point that you can maintain your technique

 

Stay tuned for next week's video to discuss this further, as well as for technical coaching on two of my favorite power-producing lifts.

 

Powerful people are quick, springy, agile, and stronger than they look. 

 

Stay strong (and powerful),


 

Mike

 

P.S. I’ll be talking about power and how you can effectively develop it all month. Stay tuned! And if you’ve wondered why I love the kettlebell and Bulgarian Bag so much, power is one of the big reasons. These tools are perfect for keeping speed high with techniques you can master quickly.

Jared was a recent guest on Paul Chek's Podcast, which was fantastic! Tomorrow tune into IG Live (@Mike.Salemi) for what will be a great conversation called "Beyond Organic Farming + Holistic Self Care"! : )

text:

WEDNESDAY (7/21): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (7/22): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Bicep Myofascial Stretch: 3 sets of 30 seconds with 10 second rest
T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

FRIDAY (7/23): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform the following superset for 2-6 rounds, resting as needed in between sets (up to 60 sec):
Bulgarian Bag Half Spin OR Spin with Pause OR Half Spin to Pivot Lunge x 6-10 each side
Side Lying Hip Raises x 15-25 

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

Bicep Myofascial Stretch: 3 sets of 30 seconds with 10 second rest
T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

SATURDAY (7/24): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday 

 

SUNDAY (7/25): Rest and Play! 

Cycling Sprints - if you've got the energy and want to push it. Cycle easy for 5-10 minutes to start. Then once warm, Sprint for 5-10 sec > Cycle Easy Recovery for 50 sec and repeat this superset 6-10x. Complete this session with a 5-10 minute easy cycling cool down.

Bicep Myofascial Stretch: 3 sets of 30 seconds with 10 second rest

Bicep Myofascial Stretch: 3 sets of 30 seconds with 10 second rest
T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Bicep Myofascial Stretch: 3 sets of 30 seconds with 10 second rest
T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

Enjoy!

Mike

name: Not Your Average Band Training
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

While bands are a hidden gem IMO in fitness, it certainly helps to know optimal ways for how to use it to improve movement awareness, skill, and play.

 

Click here for a quick video I created for you demonstrating and breaking down the Pummel to Rotational Lunge.

 

Movement Technique Steps/Tips:

Pull the loaded arm to the centerline of the chest
Pivot and rotate the body 90 deg.
Circle the elbow 
Once you complete the rotation, descend under control
Extend the free arm to aid in rotation
Reverse the steps about and return to the start position

If you’d like to learn a lot more with me and train with the band (shown in this video are Suples H.I.R.T.S. Bands), then next Saturday the 31st I’ll be teaching [online] for 90 minutes how to use the Band for mobility and developing athleticism + we'll get in a workout together, and I'll be taking Q+A.

 

Click here for more information and if you'd like to register for $97. 

 

You will also get to re-watch the workshop for 3 days. 

 

Have a great rest of your day and enjoy!

name: Final Call HIRTS Band Workshop
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Back when I started as a personal trainer, one of my goals was to be a "Swiss-Army Knife" in my craft.

 

To develop as many skills as possible so that I could help as many people as possible with their challenges and objectives was my mission.

 

Without a doubt, the band work that I've implemented in my own training, and that of my clients has not only supported me in becoming a more versatile coach and teacher, but also taken my physical performance to new levels. 

 

If you're thinking, "Mike, it's just training with a band, what could be so special about that?" Well, to be honest, at first I thought the same thing.

 

It wasn't until I spent time studying and learning under Suples Training Systems founder and Olympian Ivan Ivanov, that I really understood the potential of this style of training. 

 

Once I integrated the Suples HIRTS Band training with my own knowledge and experience of supporting the health of our joints, body awareness, rotational training, spinal mechanics, program design, and more, the results I've been getting have continued to grow.

 

Tomorrow, Saturday, at 9amPST/12pmEST I will be teaching a 90 minute online workshop on Band Training for Loaded Mobility and Integrated Athletic Training. 

 

You will learn:

How to maximize and modify athletic band training for all levels
Explosive rotation training
Over 16 movements covered
An integrated workout
Open Q+A
And more

There are still a few hours to sign up, and the cost is $97.

 

If you cannot attend live, you will have the ability to view the workshop for 72 hours.

 

I know you are going to LOVE this stuff, and it would make me truly happy to support you in expanding your skill set with this powerful training.

 

To register, click here.

 

Wishing you a great weekend and I hope to see you soon,

Mike

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 8/4
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the information below for your workout and training plan on 8/4:

https://vimeo.com/583057098/db3cb3c3ba

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (8/4): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (8/5): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Biceps Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
Glute Max Deep Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

FRIDAY (8/6): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start

Super Set 1: Perform 2-4 sets, resting up to 90 seconds after each super set:

Single Arm Kettlebell Snatch OR Single Arm Kettlebell Swings x 5 reps each
Bulgarian Bag Spins OR Half Spins x 6-8 reps each side

Super Set 2: Perform 1 set of the below

Side Lying Inside of Hip (Groin) Raises x 10-15 reps each side
Butterflies x 20-40 reps

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

Biceps Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
Glute Max Deep Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

SATURDAY (8/7): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday 

 

SUNDAY (8/8): Rest and Play! 

Cycling Sprints - if you've got the energy and want to push it. Cycle easy for 5-10 minutes to start. Then once warm, Sprint for 5-10 sec > Cycle Easy Recovery for 50 sec and repeat this superset 6-10x. Complete this session with a 5-10 minute easy cycling cool down. 
Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 
Rowing Machine 500-1000 meter row, while staying nasal breathing the entire time

Finish with this cool down:

Biceps Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
Glute Max Deep Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

MONDAY (8/9): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Super Set 1: Perform 3-8 sets, resting up to 60 seconds after each super set:

Single Arm Kettlebell Swings (For All Levels) x 10 each side
Bulgarian Bag Arm Throw OR Shoulder Load x 8-10 each side

Super Set 2: Perform 1-3 sets, resting as needed after each super set:

Side Lying Outside of Hip (Glute Medius) Raises x Max Tech. each side 
Butterflies: Max Technique 

Finish with this cool down:

Biceps Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
Glute Max Deep Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

TUESDAY (8/10): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

Biceps Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
Glute Max Deep Stretch: 45 seconds x 2 sets (each side) with 10 sec rest
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

Have fun!

Mike

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 8/18
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the information below for your workout and training plan on 8/18:

https://vimeo.com/589057193/b5e818af20

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (8/18): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (8/19): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

L4/L5 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L3/L4 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

FRIDAY (8/20): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start

Circuit: Perform 2-4 sets, resting up to 90 seconds:

Bulgarian Bag Halo OR Halo with Counter Balance x 8-10 each side
Bulgarian Bag Side Swing Squat OR Alternating Swing Squat x 6-15
Lunge Stance Row or Coiled Row x 8-12 ea

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

L4/L5 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L3/L4 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

SATURDAY (8/21): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday 

 

SUNDAY (8/22): Active Rest (OR Complete Off Day)

Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 

Finish with this cool down:

L4/L5 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L3/L4 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

MONDAY (8/23): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Circuit: Perform 3-6 sets of the following, resting up to 60 seconds:

Bulgarian Bag Halo OR Halo with Counter Balance x 4-5 each side
Kettlebell Half Kneeling Press OR Straddle Press x 8-10 ea
Bulgarian Bag Side Swing Squat OR Alternating Swing Squat x 6-15 each side
Lunge Stance Row or Coiled Row x 8-12 ea

Finish with this cool down:

L4/L5 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L3/L4 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

TUESDAY (8/24): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

L4/L5 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L3/L4 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

Have fun this week,

Mike

name: Kettlebell Intelligence Workshop
text:
Hi {first_name}, 

 

The purpose of laying a foundation is so you can build on it.

 

It’s time to build.

 

Progressions increase the complexity of movement, teaching your body to move with more intelligence. Superheroes need to be strong and powerful in any position...you can bet they train with kettlebell progressions ;) 

 

I'm PUMPED to share this a special Workshop with you happening Sunday, August 29th.

 

Stop Boring Workouts: Kettlebell Progressions to Train Like a Superhero

 

We’ll start with foundational KB movements and progress them to become increasingly more technical and athletic (awesome). 

 

2-Hand Swing 
Press 
Squat 
Row 
Windmill 

Those 5 exercises are great, but we’ll go through 4 progressions on each to train stability, mobility, rotation, coordinating momentum, and strength away from the center line.

 

I mean, who doesn’t want to progress their swing to a single-arm, coiled, high-pull with a acceleration - all with the power to make you better in locomotion and any rotational activity! 

 

To cap off the workshop, you’ll receive the design of an intentional AMRAP workout including each progression. The workout is challenging, fun, and perfect for testing your progress over time. 

 

Sign up for the workshop now and stop your boring workouts. 

 

Date: Sunday, August 29th

Time: 9am Pacific/12pm Eastern

Cost: $97

*Recording of workshop is included (available for 72 hours)

 

You are completely protected with my 100% money back guarantee. Register, come to the event, and experience these progressions. If you don’t feel the benefit of these progressions, then I want you to have your money back. Simply send me an email and I’ll refund your money. 

 

Register now.

 

Let’s train like superheroes! 

 

-Mike

  

P.S. Don’t worry if you already have weekend plans. Everyone who registers will get the recording so you won’t miss a thing. Register now and start training like a superhero.

name: Bags and Bells: Mark Interview
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I hope you are well!

 

New Announcement!

We will soon be moving our Bags and Bells Classes to a platform called Mighty Networks - this is so that I can deliver an improved, more valuable experience for being a part of my close community. I’ve wanted to do something like this for so long to share additional things such as complementary training plans, movement tutorials that will remain up, community challenges, and group interaction.  

 

I would greatly appreciate your help with something:

If you could please hop on a brief (15 min max) call with a new member of my team, Mark Laughlin, he will be able to ask you a few questions regarding what you are enjoying most, and as we make this transition, determine what you would benefit most from seeing.

 

Mark has created a special Calendly link here with availability over the next 10ish days. 

 

Link to Set Up a Quick Call with Mark: https://calendly.com/ma-a-laughlin/bagsandbells https://calendly.com/ma-a-laughlin/bagsandbells

 

Thank you in advance, and I can’t wait for what’s ahead!
Mike

name: Breaking the Cycle
text:
“Vulnerability is the courage to experience love in it’s purest form.”
-Lucas Mack

 

Hi {first_name},

 

What are the negative cycles being expressed in your life right now?

 

We all have them, and they can be paralyzing...paralyzing to our ability to trust ourselves deeply, connect with those we care about, and go after our goals and dreams.

 

On this topic, I've invited Lucas Mack, a TedX speaker, podcast host, and healing catalyst for people, especially men who carry concealed trauma, for an IG Live interview today.

 

Lucas' mission is to give people permission to put down their armor and experience the power of vulnerability and unconditional love—initiating their healing and empowering them to live with authenticity and purpose. After healing from his own childhood abuse, he’s been devoted to freeing others from the trauma of the past.

 

This will be a POWERFUL interview.

 

Come join us on Instagram Live (@Mike.Salemi) tonight at 5:00pmPST /  8:00pmEST, on how to stop negative cycles in our life right now. 

 

Hope to see you there,
Mike

 

P.S. There are still a few spots left for this Sunday's 90 minute virtual workshop, “Stop Boring Workouts, Kettlebell Progressions to Train like a Superhero.“

Let’s tap into that athletic intelligence we all have inside together!

Click here for more info and to register.
*Recording available for 72 hours to all participants

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 8/25
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Please see the information below for your workout and training plan on 8/25:

https://vimeo.com/592426846/f921186b41

 

Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (8/25): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (8/26): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

FRIDAY (8/27): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform each progression resting up to 60 seconds in between. For all of this work, begin to think more about your breathing rhythm, and how long it takes you to perform the reps designated. See if you can maintain a consistent number of breaths, as well as the duration of each breath within every rep of each progression. Also, stay nasal breathing throughout. 
KB Deadlift x 10 x 1
KB Two Hand Swing x 10-15 x 1
KB Single Arm Swing x 10-15 ea x 1

 [LEVEL 1 Stop Here, LEVEL 2 Continue On]

KB Clean x 10-12 ea x 1
KB Half Snatch (Snatch Up, Lower Down Like a Press): x 10-12 ea x 1
KB Snatch x 8-10 ea x 1-2
Once you've completed this, perform 1-3 sets of Abdominal Roll Ups for 10-15 quality reps. 

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

SATURDAY (8/28): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday, focusing heavily on your pacing strategy and breathing during the KB Snatch.

 

SUNDAY (8/29): Active Rest (OR Complete Off Day)

Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout
Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 

Finish with this cool down:

T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

MONDAY (8/30): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Station: Perform the following:

KB Single Arm Swings OR KB Snatches x 30-60 seconds duration each arm (i.e. 60-120 seconds total per set of combined arm movements) x  2-4 sets at 1-2 minutes rest. *For Level II, even if you go at a slower pace, challenge yourself to last for 60 sec each arm, i.e a 2 minute set per each arm.

REST Up to 2 Minutes, before starting the circuit below. Rest as needed after each round.

Bulgarian Bag Halo Lamb Swing OR Alt. Lamb Swing x 6-8 each x 1-3
Kettlebell Bent Over Alt. Coiling Row (open palm grip) x 8-10 ea x 1-3
Abdominal Roll Ups x 10-15 x 1-3

Finish with this cool down:

T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

TUESDAY (8/31): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

Have fun this week,

Mike

  2. C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  3. L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

SATURDAY (8/28): Full Workout

  • Perform the workout as on Wednesday, focusing heavily on your pacing strategy and breathing during the KB Snatch.

 

SUNDAY (8/29): Active Rest (OR Complete Off Day)

  • Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout
  • Swimming: 15-20 minutes of pure unstructured movement in the water. Aim to move, wiggle all your joints, and play in the water freely. This is one of the best forms of recovery I've experienced personally over the years. 

Finish with this cool down:

  1. T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  2. C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  3. L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

MONDAY (8/30): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Station: Perform the following:

  1. KB Single Arm Swings OR KB Snatches x 30-60 seconds duration each arm (i.e. 60-120 seconds total per set of combined arm movements) x  2-4 sets at 1-2 minutes rest. *For Level II, even if you go at a slower pace, challenge yourself to last for 60 sec each arm, i.e a 2 minute set per each arm.

REST Up to 2 Minutes, before starting the circuit below. Rest as needed after each round.

  1. Bulgarian Bag Halo Lamb Swing OR Alt. Lamb Swing x 6-8 each x 1-3
  2. Kettlebell Bent Over Alt. Coiling Row (open palm grip) x 8-10 ea x 1-3
  3. Abdominal Roll Ups x 10-15 x 1-3

Finish with this cool down:

  1. T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  2. C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  3. L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

TUESDAY (8/31): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from demonstrated at the end of our live training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down.

  1. T8/T9 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  2. C6//C7 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set
  3. L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min x 1 set

 

Have fun this week,

Mike

name: Kettlebell Intelligence Recording
text:
Hi Everyone,

 

It was an absolute pleasure sharing this month’s workshop focused on Kettlebell Intelligence Training with you.

 

There were a ton of movements covered, 25 in total, all of which progressed in complexity in an intentional manner. 

 

Since there was so much covered, rather than giving it to you for review for 72 hours, I’ve decided that I would like to give it to you for 5 days instead, so you have more adequate time to practice as well as allow your body to recover fully in between sessions as a gift.

 

Here is your Recording: https://us02web.zoom.us/rec/share/Xj_GteuQrGZp3R4ecF1neuawoRan2JJ4R-ZbAUrjyT_xKclsU0vfm8I1wFrpdk6I.vBWW9OtthlB8MFdG

 

Attached you will find the review workout PDF I detailed at the end of the workshop. 

 

This workout is a great way to review, and is quite challenging as a standalone training option that will deliver results for a long time. 

 

*It is set for 18 minutes, but I’ve also done it for between 20-24 minutes if I’m going heavier and taking more rest time in between rounds to recover. 

 

I hope you enjoy it fully!

 

Also, for those of you who would like to go further with this type of training, I instruct each week on Wednesday morning, an array of training with the Kettlebell, Bulgarian Bag, and Bodyweight in a fun and challenging way. If this is something you are interested in, please hit me up, or check out: www.bagsandbells.io.

 

I was thinking lately, and know that getting a Bulgarian Bag is often an obstacle for people, and so what I’d like to offer, for new interested people, is if you purchase a Suples Bulgarian Bag (you can find on my site or www.Suples.com) I will waive your first month of classes so you can put that money towards the Bag. Simply shoot me an email and I’ll hook you up with a code to get a month free once your Bag arrives. 

 

Wishing you a wonderful weekend!

Mike

name: Hold Your Ground Retreat Announcement
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

By and large, a man's worth is judged by how well he holds up or contributes to other people’s values... 

 

Working for what the boss wants
Working to get all the stuff a successful man should have
Looking manly 
Being self-reliant 
Being decisive 

Then there are the opposite demands...

 

Caring about time with your family
Cherishing inner values and not worrying about the small stuff
Valuing your mind instead of your body
Being willing to ask for and receive help
Listen well to others and take their desires into account.

None of the things listed above are bad, HOWEVER being a confident man does not and cannot come from a checklist. 

 

Here’s the truth:

 

Until they’re willing to be laughed at, shunned, or even killed for what they value, men won’t live fully.

 

Trusting yourself about what you truly value and not caving to outside pressure is huge for self-respect.

 

How will your life change when you know yourself well enough to say “no” regardless of the pressure?

 

The good news is, you don’t have to wait to develop yourself until you’re in life and death circumstances. What you need is some intentional discomfort in the right places and the support to make new choices when that discomfort arises. 

 

Here is the plan:

Voluntarily face uncomfortable situations
Connect to your deeper strength that can withstand discomfort
Enjoy the self-respect that comes from sticking to what you authentically value

 

Hold Your Ground Retreat For Men

 

The Hold Your Ground retreat will happen at the very end of October at Belcampo Farms, sitting at the foot of Mount Shasta in Northern California. 

 

If you’re a man who wants to live confidently even when the pressure is on, the Hold Your Ground Retreat is for you. Click here to get the details along with booking a discovery call directly with Mike.

 

-Mike

 

P.S. Men want to feel powerful, but power, at least the kind I want to develop, is something you develop internally. You can’t buy it and you can’t get certified in it. Register for the Hold Your Ground retreat and live powerfully.

name: Content TGU and PS on MoMvmt
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I recall for a long time early on I simply couldn't figure out when moving through the Turkish Get Up (especially during one part in particular), why one of my shoulders would feel unstable, "jammed-up", and lack stability.

 

I came to realize that this point of transition (into what is often called "Elbow Post") is a common challenge many others face as well.

 

The Turkish Get Up offers us a way to move a load from the floor into a standing position safely. It has numerous benefits, such as multi-positional stability, strength, and mobility of the shoulders and hips, plus great core integration, and more. Each of these benefits has the ability to aid in the preparation and conditioning for many work or sports environments.

 

While there are a range of variations to the Get Up, no matter which one you choose (here is a video I did with Mind Pump Media showing 3 different TGU variations), the mistake(s) I describe below apply to nearly all of them.

 

Common Mistakes:

During the raising phase up to the Elbow Post (either of the below):

Base shoulder hikes up too close to the ear
Head and neck projects forward to initiate the movement 

 

During the lowering phase down from the Straight Arm Post:

The planted arm is positioned too close to the hip as it is lowered down to the elbow (causing a bunching up of the body and oftentimes a shift in body position, away from where you started).

 

A Few Tip(s) to Explore:

During the raising phase up to the Elbow Post:

Drive off the heel of the planted leg
Allow torso to rotate slightly (as a result of the leg drive)
Guide kettlebell along a diagonal line towards the belly button 
Drive planted elbow into the ground as the chest lifts

 

During the lowering phase down from the Straight Arm Post:

Readjust the planted hand as needed to create enough space to descend to the elbow with proper positioning

 

>>> As a special gift for you today, I'm including a video I've extracted right from "Mastering the Kettlebell" to help you solve these problems on the Get Up. 

 

 

Solving the issues above has been such a game changer for me over the years, and for many of the people I've worked with in programs like Mastering the Kettlebell and others, that I'm pumped to share them with you today.

 

Thank you for being a part of my community. I hope you enjoy your movement practice today, 

 

Mike

 

 

P.S.

To the men out there (and/or ladies with a special man in your life), I shared a few weeks ago a special event I'm facilitating coming up - the "Men of Movement, Hold Your Ground Retreat". You see, after researching and testing different methods on myself and others, that safely harness discomfort, I've found uncomfortable situations bring us face-to-face with the voice in our head that tells us it’s not worth it, we should quit, and who are we to be our own authority. And here's the truth, I want men to feel the courage of a warrior who holds their ground even when the odds are against them...men who know, to their core, what the values that they are willing to fight for are - which, in my opinion, is so important considering the times we are in.

 

If this event interests you and you feel ready for an experience like this alongside an amazing group of brothers, click here for more info and to set up a discovery call directly with me.

name: Greg Interview
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Mental health is a BIG topic today, and rightfully so. 

 

Our thoughts, and thus our mind, drive so much of how we experience life, both positively and negatively. 

 

In 30 minutes, I've got something special happening for you.

 

I'll be going LIVE on Instagram with Chek Practitioner and founder of Healing 4D for an interview on healing the mind, Greg Schmaus.

 

Greg has a very inspiring story of overcoming OCD, and the lessons he’s learned along the way during his healing journey can benefit all of us.

 

I've asked Greg to also share with us some tools and techniques we can use to reduce overwhelm prior to both competition and presentations at work - something I know I've experienced many times. 


The interview starts at 9amPST /12pmEST today, Thursday. 

You will be able to drop in questions for Greg right during the interview. 

 

*If you are unable to attend live, I will put up the recording afterward on my Instagram (@Mike.Salemi).

 

I hope to see you there shortly,
Mike

name: Greg Interview Follow Up
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In this morning's interview with Greg Schmaus, he shared so many gems that really hit home for me as well as for our community members. 

 

One of which is a new way to view performance - it was unlike anything I had heard before, and I now have a deeper and more expansive understanding of my relationship with performance over the years - both the beautiful, and challenging parts. 

 

He dives into this view of performance during the very first seconds of our interview, and I highly recommend you check it out here.

 

In this interview, Greg also discusses:

 

An easy way to become the observer in your meditations and bring healing to a racing mind
The connection between the heart and mind and what we so often forget
Powerful healing that can happen in the body using movement and shifting our state
And more!

 

Greg has created a special video for our community that comes directly from his new program, Healing the Mind A Journey to Wholeness 21 day online program.

 

You can get that here: healing4d.com/mike

Lastly, if you are interested in working with Greg one-on-one, please check out:  www.healing4d.com

 

I hope you enjoyed today’s interview as much as I did!

 

In health,

Mike

name: Breathing Workshop Announcement
text:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

Keeping calm and using oxygen efficiently is vital to performance. If you don’t believe me, try training without breathing...it’ll be a short workout! :)

 

If your body uses oxygen well, you will be able to perform better, longer. 

 

BUT, not many of us want to sit still and practice breathing for 30+ minutes. 

 

On Tuesday I’m offering a free workshop (usually $97). I know you’re interested in performance so be sure to register for this free workshop that will improve one of the most foundational elements to performance - how well your body uses oxygen.

 

And even if you can’t make it live, no worries, because I’ll email a link to a 72 hour replay.

 

 

Workshop Topic: Breathwork For Performance WITHOUT Taking Time From Training
 

Major benefits:

 

Improved concentration
Greater work capacity
Reduced breathlessness
Reduced anxiety (your body will be more calm)
Better sleep

 

How you get these benefits:

 

Train your diaphragm (your major breathing muscle), as well as improve your tolerance to C02. Better resistance to C02 buildup will help the release of oxygen from your lungs and blood into your tissues more readily.

 

Without taking time from your training:

 

I’ll show you not only what to do, but how to incorporate these protocols into your warmups and training.

 

Registration for this workshop is FREE: 

 

Click here and enter your email address to register. You’ll get the log-in details for attending and you’ll receive the 72 hour replay if you can’t make it live. 

 

DETAILS:

Date: Tuesday, 10/5/2021

Time: 9am PST/12pm EST

Duration: 90 min

Equipment needed: a set of lungs


 

See you Tuesday!

Mike

 

P.S. Improving how your body uses oxygen is one of the most foundational things you can do for your performance. This workshop will show you how to train your breathing without needing lots of dedicated breathwork time. Register for free even if you can’t make it live. I’ll send a 72 hour replay so you can watch later.
