name: Breathwork Workshop Follow Up
text:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

The impact breathwork has had on my life in recent years has been nothing short of incredible. 

 

I tend to look at the application of breathwork in three ways - for healing, for function, and for performance. And while there certainly is overlap between these three, I most often tailor my breathwork practice differently for each intention. 

 

This is a friendly reminder that tomorrow at 9amPST, I will be leading a workshop covering integrating breathwork with physical training, and it will be FREE!

 

Normally, these monthly workshops are $97, however this month I thought I'd do something special, and offer it at no charge, since this is something that anyone with a set of lungs can benefit from and it will be very supportive for the times we are in.

 

Here's the info below, as well as how to sign up:

 

Major benefits:

 

Improved concentration
Greater work capacity
Reduced breathlessness
Reduced anxiety (your body will be more calm)
Better sleep

 

How you get these benefits:

 

Train your diaphragm (your major breathing muscle), as well as improve your tolerance to C02. Better resistance to C02 buildup will help the release of oxygen from your lungs and blood into your tissues more readily.

 

Without taking time from your training:

 

I’ll show you not only what to do, but how to incorporate these protocols into your warmups and training.

 

Registration for this workshop is FREE.

 

Click here and enter your email address to register. You’ll get the log-in details for attending and you’ll receive the 72 hour replay if you can’t make it live. 

 

DETAILS:

Date: Tuesday, 10/5/2021

Time: 9am PST/12pm EST

Duration: 90 min

Equipment needed: a set of lungs

 

Hope to see you there,

 

Mike Salemi

Performance Specialist

www.mikesalemi.io

name: Bags and Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 10/6
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Here is your link to the workout from 10/6: 

https://vimeo.com/624956235/0a65f5e837

*This is also available in your Mighty Networks now

 

Here is Your Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (10/6): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (10/7): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down the videoed training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down:

Psoas Stretch x 45 sec x 2 ea
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

FRIDAY (10/8): Skill Development #1 and Stretching

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform the below superset, with the mouth fully closed throughout, resting as needed in between 
BB 1/2 Spin OR Spin with Half Step Over x 6 each side x 1-3
Take as many warm up sets and reps needed prior to the above BB exercise. Progressive warm ups include: Open Arm Side to Side Swing, Open Arm Side to Side Swing with Counter Balance, and Open Arm Side to Side Swing with Rotation
Knee Over Toe Lunges x 8 each side x 1-3 

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

Psoas Stretch x 45 sec x 2 ea
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

SATURDAY (10/9): Full Workout

Perform the workout as on Wednesday

 

SUNDAY (10/10):

Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout

Finish with this cool down:

Psoas Stretch x 45 sec x 2 ea
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

MONDAY (10/11): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Perform the Following Two Supersets:
SUPER SET 1: 3-5 Sets (Rest up to 45 sec)
 BB 1/2 Spin OR Spin with Half Step Over x 8 ea.
KB Open Palm Grip Bent Over Row x 10-15 
SUPER SET 2: 3-5 Sets (No Rest)
Half Kneeling KB Overhead Press OR Straddle Overhead Press x 6-10 ea
Bodyweight or KB Knee Over Toe Lunges x 6-10 ea.

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

Psoas Stretch x 45 sec x 2 ea
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

TUESDAY (10/12): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from the videoed training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down:

Psoas Stretch x 45 sec x 2 ea
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

Have fun with this,

Mike

name: Men of Movement 2
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

There’s a term for people who are so good at being what they are “supposed” to be. They’re predictable on almost everything because they’ve internalized expectations that come from the external culture.  




 

Here’s the truth:

 

Men won’t feel fully alive until their values and actions are rooted squarely in their own hearts and minds.

 

Trusting yourself about what you truly value and not caving to outside pressure is huge for self-respect.

 

How will your life change when you know yourself well enough to say “no” regardless of the pressure?

 

The good news is, you don’t have to wait to develop yourself until you’re in life and death circumstances. What you need is some intentional discomfort in the right places and the support to make new choices when that discomfort arises. 

 

Here is the plan:

Voluntarily face uncomfortable situations
Connect to your deeper strength that can withstand discomfort
Enjoy the self-respect that comes from sticking to what you authentically value

 

Hold Your Ground Retreat For Men

 

The Hold Your Ground retreat is happening October 28-31 at Belcampo Farms, sitting at the foot of Mount Shasta in Northern California. 

 

If you’re a man who wants to live confidently even when the pressure is on, the Hold Your Ground Retreat is for you. Click here to get the details along with booking a discovery call directly with me.

 

-Mike

 

P.S. Men want to feel powerful, but power, at least the kind I want to develop, is something you develop internally. You can’t buy it and you can’t get certified in it. Register for the Hold Your Ground retreat and live powerfully.

name: 11/3/21 Windmill
text:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

When your hands start tearing it doesn’t matter how much strength or endurance you have left in the tank. Then it takes a week or two (or three) for your hands to heal. 

 

INSTEAD, learn how to grip the kettlebell handle the right way to avoid tears. 

 

You’ll need to practice with a lighter kettlebell, but once you’ve got it down, your ability to perform in movements like the kettlebell snatch will improve. You’ll finally address the most common limiting factor - grip. 

 

In this under 5 minute video you’ll learn

 

Exactly where to put the handle in your fingers to keep your skin from tearing or blistering. 
The super-quick pull you’ll learn to transition where your hand is on the handle. 

And most importantly, you’ll be able to get a better training effect when the skin on your hands isn’t tearing off!

 

 

Happy training!

Mike
subject: Keep your hands from tearing in the KB snatch
previewHtml:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

When your hands start tearing it doesn’t matter how much strength or endurance you have left in the tank. Then it takes a week or two (or three) for your hands to heal. 

 

INSTEAD, learn how to grip the kettlebell handle the right way to avoid tears. 

 

You’ll need to practice with a lighter kettlebell, but once you’ve got it down, your ability to perform in movements like the kettlebell snatch will improve. You’ll finally address the most common limiting factor - grip. 

 

In this under 5 minute video you’ll learn

 

  • Exactly where to put the handle in your fingers to keep your skin from tearing or blistering. 
  • The super-quick pull you’ll learn to transition where your hand is on the handle. 

And most importantly, you’ll be able to get a better training effect when the skin on your hands isn’t tearing off!

 

 

Happy training!

Mike

name: Nurture 11/17/21 Coiled Swing
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

2-hand swing...no problem

 

1-hand swing...nailed it

 

Coiled swing...now we’re talking

 

Foundational movements are great because you can build on them. If you’ve been training for a little while, adding complexity to your movements will do wonders for your ability to move with precision, grace, and more power!

 

Training the coiled position has huge carry over for expressing strength as a human being. Locomotion - moving - starts with the coil. 

 

If you want to get more athletic, use this coiled swing. If you want to be able to better express the strength you build, use this coiled swing. 

 

Watch this ~5 minute video to see exactly how to perform the coiled swing.

 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: BF: Friday Specials List 3
text:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

When I started training seriously, my mindset was that I was going to work as hard as possible. No one would be more dedicated than I was.

 

With a mindset like that, I confused hard work with progress and developed the injuries to show for it. 

 

The programs I’ve created now are blueprints for what I call intentional training. Intentional training is a way for you to escape confusing hard work with progress. Instead, you’ll learn that hard work will get you further when it is applied strategically. Hard work should support more than exhaustion.

 

If you’ve been looking for how to get the best performance from your body, but without so much wear and tear, my programs are made for you. 

 

I especially recommend Kettlebell Lifestyle or Bags and Bells.

 

Click here to get the offer code for each program along with the link to more details. Time is running out!

 

Train intentionally,

Mike

name: Nurture 12/1/21 adv. swing progressions
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Kettlebell swings have got to be one of my all-time favorite, power-generating movements. The benefits I experience consistently leave me feeling solid and explosive afterwards. If you are reading this, then I'd imagine you too enjoy the swing, and are interested in ways to advance such a great exercise.

 

Ways to progress such as:

 

Make it more dynamic
Bring in more coordination 
Engage your brain more

The swing progressions in this week’s video will not only tax your muscles differently compared to the normal swing, they’ll also keep your brain active to coordinate everything. Movements like these progressions help you develop a nervous system more capable of quick, athletic movements. 

 

Watch the ~4 minute video here and give these progressions a try.

 

I hope you enjoy this one and keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 12/8/21 Farmer's Carrys
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

There is a concept of being "farm-boy" strong. 

 

You may not have known this, but growing up I spent a good deal of time hanging around garbage men, stone fabricators, and farmers and what I can tell you is the type of strength they possess will shock you. Their grip, back strength, and insane work capacity I continue to have massive respect for. 

 

One thing I learned from spending time with them is that getting strong can certainly come from things other than loading plates onto the bar. 

 

In today’s video, you’ll see 5 variations of the classic farmer’s carry. To get legit benefits, you do not have to go as heavy as possible. In fact, I challenge you to try these progressions with a lighter to moderate load and go for a longer time/distance.

 

Challenge your ability to maintain good posture - especially when fatigued. 

 

Watch this week’s video now and get farmer-strong! 

 

I hope you enjoy this one and keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

FRIDAY (12/10): Skill Development #1

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform the following as one individual station:
Spin OR Arm Throw x 20 seconds on x 20 seconds off x 4-8 sets
With this, I'd like you to pick one element within this movement and hone in on only one component and drill that in. In our last class for example, on the spin, we really dialed in the lowering phase, and keeping the lead arm close to the shoulder by pulling the elbow back. If this is your one weakpoint, that is the only thing that you'd focus on
Bent Over KB Row x 10-15 each arm

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

General ELDOA x 5/5

 

SATURDAY (12/11): Full Workout

 

 

SUNDAY (12/12): Recovery Day

Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout

Finish with this cool down:

General ELDOA x 5/5

 

MONDAY (12/13): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

3 Exercises, done in station (singular exercise, no circuit) format

Kettlebell Swings x 10 reps x 3-6 sets, with 30 seconds rest

Spin (either open palm grip or close palmed, inside grip) for 1 rep with a transitional element to the other side. For this, you would perform one swing and one transition to the other side. Here are a few ways to transition that we've covered in the past:

Spin-Pummel

Spin-Side Swing with Rotation

Spin-Low Side Swing (no rotation)

Spin-Side Swing Squat

Spin-Shoulder Load

Spin-Arm Throw

For this type of training, what I'd like you do do is:

1 Spin Left + Transition, 1 Spin Right + Transition, 2 Spin Left + Transition, 3 Spin Right + Transiiton, 3 Spin Left +Transition, 3 Spin Right + Transiiton

name: Balance Workshop Announcement
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

What good is a 700 horsepower engine in a Model-T? The suspension, brakes, and probably everything else wouldn’t be able to handle it. 

 

Gyms are full of people training to make a 700 hp engine without realizing the rest of their system can’t express that much energy. 

 

Fundamentals will turn that Model-T into a racecar, but what are the fundamentals??

 

Ask a gym bro and you’ll hear about deadlifts and squats…those are great, but true fundamentals will make you better at both of those lifts plus just about everything else. 

 

This month’s workshop will provide powerful benefits:

Improved stability creating more force generation (be stronger than you look)
Multiply your options for movement and exercise  
A more advanced nervous system that gives you reserves when performing fine motor patterns (perform with more precision longer)  
Not to mention that sports injuries happen late in the game once the nervous system has fatigued. That more advanced nervous system mentioned above is both practical and protective. 

Train This Fundamental

One of the biggest bang for your buck fundamentals is balance.

 

There are few people I've come across that know how to train and teach this topic better than my buddy Warren Williams.

 

I've asked Warren to come teach for us this Saturday, at 8:30amPST and it's going to be EPIC!

 

In this 90 minute virtual workshop you will learn how to maximize a variety of balance tools, progress versions of balance drills in all 3 planes of movement, and functionally incorporate balance training into your fitness regime.

 

This workshop will cover balance training with no equipment, as well as using a series of tools: totally barefoot, swiss ball, bongo board, wobble board, dura discs, hard foam rollers (any of the equipment above is recommended for you to get the most out of this workshop)

 

*If you cannot attend live, everyone will receive a viewing link for 72 hours.

 

Click here to register today, I promise you won't want to miss this!

 

Best,

Mike

name: Nurture 12/15/21  Tips KB Sport
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

One approach to becoming elite in a sport is to push as hard as possible. Always work harder. Always go for more. The word that comes to mind for that kind of training approach is…ouch. 

 

I learned a ton from competing in kettlebell sport. The competition is grueling and if you want to be elite, you have to keep at it for years. 

 

This week’s video is a peak behind the curtain of what it takes to become elite. The 6 tips I have are specifically for kettlebell sport, but you’ll see how they apply to training regardless of the sport. 

 

Top 6 Tips for Kettlebell Sport:

 

The Long Game Mentality
Prepare Your Body: Strength & Flexibility
Technique
Develop General & Specific Endurance
Increasing Loads
Training Cycles

Click here to watch this week's video, I hope you enjoy it! 

 


 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. One of the keys to me restoring my body following injuries and competing at an elite level in KB Sport while feeling great was the addition of the balance training and stabilization training that Paul Chek taught me.

 

This Saturday, I've got a very special 90 min virtual workshop happening. I'm bringing in CHEK Institute faculty member and performance specialist Warren Williams to share and teach Balance Training. You will learn how to maximize a variety of balance tools (barefoot, swissball, dura disc, wobble board, etc), progress versions of balance drills in all 3 planes of movement, and functionally incorporate balance training into your fitness regime. No equipment is needed to participate, but I suggest bringing at least one if you can.

 

Also, if you cannot attend live, you will receive a viewing link for 72 hours.

 

Click here to register. I hope to see you there!

 

In Health,

Mike

name: Nurture 12/22/21  Lowering Phase
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Tons can go wrong as you lower the kettlebell when performing a snatch. As you become more technically proficient in the lowering phase, you’ll get far more benefit and experience what this lift was actually designed to deliver. Instead of recovering from torn hands and a sore lower back, you’ll be accumulating quality volume, a bigger gas tank, more powerful "go" muscles (muscles on the backside of the body), and grip.

 

In this week’s video, I teach 2 styles to lower the kettlebell.

 

1

Over the top - the simplest method

 

2

Corkscrew - more technical, but more efficient 

 

Both methods are great IF you get it right.

 

Whichever method you use, practice at a lighter weight to lay down quality reps. It can take some practice to get the feel for these movements. Keep at it and soon it will be second nature. 

 

Click here to watch this week's Youtube technique breakdown:

 

Want to double up the benefits? While you’re on my YouTube channel, go back and watch The Kettlebell Snatch - Fix Blistering. You’ll be fixing the most common problems with the KB snatch. 

 

Keep training intentionally and happy holidays,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 12/29/21  Press Row Progression
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Being strong and being athletic overlap, but they’re different. Today’s video introduces two kettlebell progressions that train both. 

 

A classic strength combination is the push - pull because of how well those two movements complement and balance each other. Today, we’ll use an overhead press for the “push” movement and a row for the “pull”. 

 

Incorporating lower body movement during the press (in the case below, the Kettlebell Countered Sea-Saw Press) is one way to further integrate the movement and enhance the athleticism required. You'll need smooth, clean movement of your legs and hips while pressing. 

 

For the row (Coiled Lunge Stance Row), you’ll be holding strong in an isometric lunge position with your lower body while adding in a slight side bend and rotation of the spine during the pull. If you feel confident with both the classic lunge stance row, as well as the standing overhead press, give these two a go!

 

Watch today’s video by clicking here and train your body to perform. 

 


 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. I’ve got an exciting announcement coming up! I’ve been working on some new developments to one of my programs that I believe will be what many of you have been looking for. Keep your eyes open for it ; )

name: Nurture 1/5/22 Single Bell Tips
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Question:

How do you program the same few movements, performed for the same amount of time, using the same weight, but experience different results?

 

Answer:

Watch the under 5 minute video!

name: Fire Fighter Challenge Email
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

I’ve got a free breath challenge coming up specifically for firefighters.

 

Here’s what I believe about breath training for firefighters:

 

Every firefighter should know how to improve their lung capacity because your life could depend on it.

 

Being strong is important. Knowing the technical specifics of your job is vital. Breathing makes it possible.

 

Everything - especially under stress - is improved by training your breath.

Improved lung capacity
Reduced requirement of oxygen for the same amount of work
Clearer thinking because your body is less in a stressed state
And a whole ton more

Controlling your breath is how to keep your mind calm to focus on your task. 

 

In about 30 minutes, this free challenge will change the game for you:

 

Establish your baseline
How to use breath holds to increase CO2 tolerance and get more oxygen into the blood and to your tissues
The benefits of nasal breathing and exercises to use
Strategy for breath recovery 

"Unlock the Power of Breath" Challenge Details

When: Jan. 18 at 12:00pm Pacific

Where: Live virtual class

 

*A recording will be sent to you even if you can’t attend live. 

 

The challenge will give you techniques you can start using immediately without needing more information, training, or tools. For those who want more, there will be an opportunity to join a new fitness program with breath training built in. 

 

The benefits of training your breath come faster than traditional strength training results AND they support every job specific task firefighters perform (not to mention that better breathing means better recovery from all the stress).

 

You’ll be able to do what you’ve trained for longer and at a higher intensity with a practiced breathing strategy. 

 

[Register here for the free workshop]

 

See you January 18th,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. Breath training is absolutely key for firefighters. Feel free to forward this email to anyone you think would be interested. You can also forward the recording after the session. Thank you!

name: Nurture 1/19/22 kb drop and recover
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

It's no surprise that bodybuilders aren’t the best at athletic movement. Neither are most powerlifters. 

 

Both of them certainly do have high levels of muscle and strength, but typical training styles don’t usually prioritize essential athletic qualities: 

 

Rhythm
Timing
Fluidity

To me, the most beautiful displays of athleticism do so through expressing strength in conjunction with rhythm, timing and fluidity. 

 

When I see a gymnast for example, my brain goes "DAMN! That person moves athletically and with such grace!"

 

Today’s video covers the Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Drop & Recover, which I first learned from my mentor, Paul Chek, to help balance my body out from competing in Kettlebell Sport.

 



>>Click here for full video progression on this rad, athletic movement.

 

Also, respond to this email if you’d like to see more on the swiss ball ; )

 

Keep training intentionally and have a fantastic rest of your week,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. Did you know I'm offering a FREE Kettlebell Progressions workshop happening on February 1st?

When I see a gymnast for example, my brain goes "DAMN! That person moves athletically and with such grace!"

 

Today’s video covers the Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Drop & Recover, which I first learned from my mentor, Paul Chek, to help balance my body out from competing in Kettlebell Sport.

Also, respond to this email if you’d like to see more on the swiss ball ; )

 

Keep training intentionally and have a fantastic rest of your week,

name: Bags & Bells ELITE Plan+Recording 1/19
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Here is your link to the workout* from 1/19:

https://vimeo.com/667902759/12ae102127

*This is also available in your Mighty Networks now

 

Here is Your Weekly Recommended Training Plan:

 

WEDNESDAY (1/19): Full Workout

 

 

THURSDAY (1/20): Recovery Focus

Perform the cool down the videoed training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down:

L2/L3 ELDOA x 1 min

L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

FRIDAY (1/21): Skill Development #1

Perform the Core Temperature Warm Up and/or the Joint Warm Up to start
Perform the following as individual stations:
Bulgarian Bag Alternating Spins x 1L/1R for 4-6 each side x 1-3 sets
For this, you will perform one rep of a spin to the left, then immediately transition to the right for one spin. You will do this until you've completed 4-6 each side. The idea here is to improve how quickly and efficiently you can switch sides so that tomorrow when you perform your spin test you will reduce your time here. 
Butterflies x 20-50 x 1-3
Side of Hip Raises (Glute Medius) x 20-40 each x 1-3

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

L2/L3 ELDOA x 1 min

L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

SATURDAY (1/22): Full Workout

 

 

SUNDAY (1/23): Recovery Day

Easy walk outside/in nature (or anytime of day too) around your neighborhood for ~20-60 minutes remaining in nasal breathing throughout

Finish with this cool down:

L2/L3 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

MONDAY (1/24): Skill Development #2, Conditioning, and Stretching

Perform the Following:
Bulgarian Bag Spin Test Full x 10L/10R + 10 Push Ups x 5 Rounds

Once Completed with the Spin Test, Perform This Circuit:

Kettlebell Figure 8 Progression (work up into 2-5 working sets total at whatever progression you feel is right for you today), resting as needed:
Figure 8 x 6-8 each 
Figure 8 to Stand x 6-8 each
Fiture 8 to Upper Cut x 6-8 each
Figure 8 to Squat (Level II) 6-8 each
Figure 8 to Back Step Lunge (Level II) x 6-8 each
Abdominal Roll Ups with Rotation (Position Torsion x 10-20 total (if you are doing these with rotation, do half the reps to one side, and the other half to the other)
Kettlebell Bent Over Rows with Reciprocity x 8-12 each

Finish with this cool down as done in the workout:

I would suggest doing a stretch for chest and biceps today (while we did not get to that in class). 3 sets of 30 seconds (each side for chest) with 10 second rest for these.

L2/L3 ELDOA x 1 min

L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

TUESDAY (1/25): Recovery Focus
Perform the cool down from the videoed training session. Depending on your time availability, you can either solely do the core temperature warm up (marching in place), or if you have more time, also perform the Joint Warm Up as well prior to this cool down:

L2/L3 ELDOA x 1 min
L5/S1 ELDOA x 1 min

 

Enjoy and crush those spin tests!

Mike

 

P.S. Our next workshop will be on Tuesday evening, at 5pmPST on Feb.1st and be on kettlebell progressions. Mark your calendar!

name: Nurture 1/26/22 kb swing fix
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

The 2-Hand Kettlebell Swing is a staple in my training and carries many benefits. 

 

On the other hand, repeating a technique error over time for thousands of reps will lead to some trouble. 

 

Fortunately, locking in solid technique CAN be a simple fix. Even better, your practice reps to drill the fix add to the benefits you’ll get from the movement. 

 

Watch this video to get coaching on how to keep your shoulders and upper back in position on both the 2-Hand Swing and the Double Kettlebell Swing.

name: #2 KBL Live (to ALL)
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Hands down, the most common feedback I've gotten from people who have completed my Kettlebell Lifestyle program is that they want more! So, as a NEW offering launching next week, you can now train with me each week... live!  To make it easy for you to know if you'd like to join this new class - Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE - I’m offering a free taste of it through an upcoming workshop.

 

You are invited to join a free Kettlebell Progressions Workshop + Workout happening Tuesday (2/1) at 5pmPST. If you register, you’ll get access to the recording for 72 hours, so you don’t even need to attend live. 

 

You'll get the chance to experience so many of the principals I talk about often in action. Kettlebells are truly a versatile and powerful training tool. And like anything else, the more you know how to maximize the tool, the better your results will be. 

 

Helpful Info Regarding Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE Classes

What Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE will NOT do:

 

Make you as muscular as a bodybuilder
Make you a competitive powerlifter
Get you to qualify for the Olympics in weightlifting
Replace your training for specific sport applications
Beat you into the ground

Instead, it is designed to give you a powerful foundation you can build on however you want. 

 

Breath

How your body uses oxygen is foundational to both your performance and recovery.

 

Mobility

Targeted exercises and stretches prepare your body to exert strength, even in challenging positions. 

 

Athleticism

Brute strength is fun, but it’s only the beginning. 

 

Decompression 

Take care of your spine and joints to feel great.

 

 

Want A Taste? Register For The Free Workshop + Workout

Join me for this 75 minute workshop on Tuesday Feb. 1st starting at 5pm Pacific. I’ll coach you through a few kettlebell progressions and then we’ll use those exercises in the workout. Register even if you can’t make it live. I’ll send you a link to the recording good for 72 hours. 

Register now for the free Workshop + Workout

 

The day following this workshop marks the start of Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE - Wednesday Feb. 2nd. When you sign up for Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE, be sure to use the code LIVE50 to get 50% off your first month (that’s $28.50 for the first month). If you're ready now, you can sign up here!

 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi  

 

P.S. I know a lot of people feel a gap between their own workouts and what they know is possible with the right programming and coaching. This new class is how I want to make top notch programming and coaching available to almost any budget and schedule. 

 

These classes are fun and I have 2 levels you can follow so there is no need to be a fire-breathing kettlebell expert to join. Sign up now and use the code LIVE50 to get 50% off your first month. Plus there’s a 30-day money back guarantee. There’s no risk to join so I hope to see you there!

So, as a NEW offering launching next week, you can now train with me each week... live!  To make it easy for you to know if you'd like to join this new class - Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE - I’m offering a free taste of it through an upcoming workshop.

 

You are invited to join a free Kettlebell Progressions Workshop + Workout happening Tuesday (2/1) at 5pmPST. If you register, you’ll get access to the recording for 72 hours, so you don’t even need to attend live. 

 

You'll get the chance to experience so many of the principals I talk about often in action. Kettlebells are truly a versatile and powerful training tool. And like anything else, the more you know how to maximize the tool, the better your results will be. 

 

Helpful Info Regarding Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE Classes

What Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE will NOT do:

 

  • Make you as muscular as a bodybuilder
  • Make you a competitive powerlifter
  • Get you to qualify for the Olympics in weightlifting
  • Replace your training for specific sport applications
  • Beat you into the ground

Instead, it is designed to give you a powerful foundation you can build on however you want. 

 

Breath

How your body uses oxygen is foundational to both your performance and recovery.

 

Mobility

Targeted exercises and stretches prepare your body to exert strength, even in challenging positions. 

 

Athleticism

Brute strength is fun, but it’s only the beginning. 

 

Decompression 

Take care of your spine and joints to feel great.

 

 

Want A Taste? Register For The Free Workshop + Workout

Join me for this 75 minute workshop on Tuesday Feb. 1st starting at 5pm Pacific. I’ll coach you through a few kettlebell progressions and then we’ll use those exercises in the workout. Register even if you can’t make it live. I’ll send you a link to the recording good for 72 hours. 

Register now for the free Workshop + Workout

 

The day following this workshop marks the start of Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE - Wednesday Feb. 2nd. When you sign up for Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE, be sure to use the code LIVE50 to get 50% off your first month (that’s $28.50 for the first month). If you're ready now, you can sign up here!

 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi  

 

P.S. I know a lot of people feel a gap between their own workouts and what they know is possible with the right programming and coaching. This new class is how I want to make top notch programming and coaching available to almost any budget and schedule. 

 

These classes are fun and I have 2 levels you can follow so there is no need to be a fire-breathing kettlebell expert to join. Sign up now and use the code LIVE50 to get 50% off your first month. Plus there’s a 30-day money back guarantee. There’s no risk to join so I hope to see you there!

name: Nurture 2/2/22 locomotive
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

One of the many things that I appreciate about working with kettlebells is that when the training is intentional, it has the ability to build crazy levels of athleticism.

 

It's one of the only tools that, when you commit to training with it regularly, you can become strong AND mobile, muscular AND have high-level endurance... put simply, you can become a balanced warrior.

 

In today's video breakdown, I teach you a more advanced kettlebell locomotive movement that will transfer into enhancing athleticism.  I do suggest going light on the load, and focusing on the details of each progression.

 

Click here to watch the video below to learn the Locomotive Clean & Press.

 


 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi 

 

P.S. Yesterday was the first session of Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE. If you love learning new kettlebell techniques, Kettlebell Lifestyle LIVE is for you. The focus is teaching new movements, coaching the technique, and guiding you from warm up to decompressive stretches at the end. It’s a blast and I show progressive levels so there is a place for you whether you are newer to kettlebells or you’ve been training with them for years. Check out the details and sign up.

name: Nurture 2/16/22 cross body swing
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Legs, trunk, grip, stability, and coordination all trained in one exercise…I love kettlebells! 

 

I used to have a 600+ pound squat and deadlift BUT to be honest, nowadays my preference is to train like what you’ll see in this video. Don’t get me wrong, brute strength is great, but now that I’m not competing in powerlifting, I want to train, moving through every plane and direction while feeling incredible in the process.

 

The exercise today teaches your body how to express strength with precision, timing, and coordination. Notice the quick movements and the exact positions you have to hit to keep the kettlebell under control. 

 

I first learned this exercise from Paul Chek back while competing in Kettlebell Sport. Performing the Long Cycle (clean and jerk) so much in training, we used this movement to help me add more rotation into my regime and balance my body out.

 

Today’s video shows you 3 progressions to get to a cross body swing with a bottoms up lunge as a bonus. Talk about a great exercise!

 

Watch the video and practice the movement. 

 

I'll be working on my next series of videos very soon. Hit reply and let me know what topics you’d like me to cover in these weekly videos coming up. 

 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 2/23/22 TGU
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Strength without control isn’t useful or athletic. Enter the Turkish Get Up (TGU). Everything about this exercise is about strength under control. 

 

In today’s video I show an ascending pyramid format to progress the TGU. 

 

I feel great after doing this exercise. My shoulders and posture feel on point and I notice it in how I carry myself.  

 

Every exercise is an assessment. The TGU covers so many planes and patterns of movement, that you get an amazing look at stability, strength, and mobility on both sides of the body. 

 

One last thought, the TGU is a great prerequisite for advanced overhead lifts. You have to keep your elbow locked out at all times with the TGU which is essential for overhead lifts. 

 

Watch the video and carve out some time for training the Get Up this week!

 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 3/2/22 Straddle Press
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

A movement as fundamental as the press tends to get oversimplified and overlooked. As with any exercise, learning a few key points of technique will get you more benefit with less wear and tear. 

 

Today’s video shows 2 variations of the press. 

 

Variation 1 creates a stable lower body set up, so you can focus on the rack position and the proper finish position.

 

Variation 2 makes the movement a LOT more challenging! 

 

Watch the video below and work these presses into your training. 

 

Also, what would you like to see from me week to week? If you’d like me to cover something in these weekly videos, hit reply and let me know.

 

Thank you and keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 3/9/22 Isometric
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Almost everyone overlooks isometric holds. By incorporating isometrics into your training, here are just some of the benefits you'll be able to experience: 

 

Increased blood flow
Safety 
Increased muscle activation
Increased strength ~15 degrees above and below the hold
Breaking through plateaus
Getting results from an exercise that isn’t often done

 

My theory on why people rarely do isometrics is that it feels boring to hold a single position...and the fact that it is difficult!

 

One solution that you can explore while performing isometrics is to distract yourself from the isometric hold itself and integrate strength training components for other regions of the body - this week’s video shows you exactly what to do. The isometric hold this week is with the split squat, which is an amazing exercise all on its own. 

 

Follow the progressions in this video and note your progress.

 

I hope you enjoy implementing these into your training today. 

 

Keep training intentionally,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. Interested in training with me each week? Click here to learn more about weekly KBL LIVE classes. Our next training cycle starts on Wednesday!

Saunas are a fantastic training and recovery tool. 

 

Yes, you can do some gentle training in a sauna (watch the video for precautions!), but simply allowing your body to adjust to being in such a hot environment has a training effect. 

 

The human body adapts to its environment. Modern life has us primarily in comfortable, climate-controlled situations, which means the body doesn’t have to be as robust as it can be. Simply sitting in a sauna allows your body to adapt. You literally add capacity to your body by sitting in a hot room. It’s amazing. 

 

If you have access to a sauna or are interested in it, this video is for you!

 

Less is more in a sauna so be sure to proceed with caution. Watch this week’s video for my thoughts on how to make great use of a sauna. 

 

*The sauna I use is from Divine Saunas. 
 

Train intentionally,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. For the fellas out there looking to connect with like-minded and hearted men you can grow alongside, the next Men of Movement - Hold Your Ground Retreat is happening May 12-15th in Northern California. name: Men of Movement Sales  4/16/22
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Heads Up: this email is specifically for the men on my list

 

Many cultural factors teach men that they are supposed to be able to solve virtually any problem on their own (or be so financially successful they can pay for the best to come and solve it…or be so good at tons of skills they can figure it out in a frugal way). 

 

What happens as every man knows they aren’t actually able to live up to this image of what a man “should” be?

 

They come to feel inadequate.

 

Then they hide that feeling of inadequacy…

 

Through high performance

Through low performance

And everything in between

 

Really, we men find anything to avoid those uncomfortable feelings. But learning to feel is what allows a man to connect to himself.

 

We cannot feel what it is to be ourselves until we allow ourselves to feel.

 

Anything else is creating a mental model of what you think “yourself” should be and trying to live that model out. 

 

Inadequacy often comes from not being able to make yourself be who you aren’t.

You will never be who you aren’t. 

 

The Plan:

Connect to yourself.

Learn to feel.

Feel the grief & feel the pain.

 

Then you’ll learn through experience -step by step- to feel the strength of who YOU are rather than inadequacy for who you aren’t. 

 

The Men Of Movement Retreat

The goal of the Men of Movement retreat is to create a space for men to rewire and re-pattern their sovereignty through body, breath, and brotherhood. 

 

Learn to hold your ground.

Learn to know who you are and what you want.

Together we move.

Together we rise.

 

The Details:

Men of Movement retreat

Mt. Shasta, Northern CA

May 12-15, 2022

 

Click here to learn more and schedule your call to see if the retreat is right for you.
 

All the best,

Mike Salemi

name: Men of Movement Sales  4/25/22
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Heads Up: this email is specifically for the men on my list

 

The respected American poet, Robert Bly had powerful medicine for men. 

 

Watch this ~30 second clip

 

It's no shock that the feelings men often face around inadequacy are not pleasant ones. As a result, numbness can often take place inside. 

 

For so many of us men, this rings true. 

 

Inadequacy is enough to shut a man down. On the other hand, inadequacy is powerful enough to drive a man to high levels of achievement…but what we don't often see is that it comes at a cost.

 

The solution to the issue CANNOT be:

Do more
Follow this formula
Work harder
Suck it up
Copy the success of someone else
Etc. 

The solution is connecting to ourselves on an increasingly truthful level. 

 

There are principles for connecting to oneself, but the key is that everyone has to do it in their own way - authentic to them.

 

If a formula does help, it does so because the formula serves you. 

 

Remember this, you supersede any formula that someone may tell you.

 

We fellas tend to confuse this. We push for formulas and things like them because it allows us to operate and carry on while still being numb. 

 

In my experience, the way to address the sense of inadequacy is to learn to feel a wider spectrum of feelings, and to accept them as a natural part of being human.

 

The feelings that hurt, that ache, that are scary, are just there, AND the fun, exciting, and joyful feelings are there too. They come together as a package deal (emotions = energy in motion).

 

When you are no longer afraid of your feelings, you are in greater touch with yourself.

 

You are in touch with yourself because you are listening.

 

Of course, it doesn't happen all at once. It’s a process that continues with time. 

 

As the Men of Movement retreat comes up in May, we aim to create a container that allows men an opportunity to get reps at connecting with themselves. The activities, as well as the other men present moving towards a common goal, are there all help open to what's really going on inside.

 

We practice what is possible. 

 

Just like squatting with a barbell can feel awkward and uncomfortable when you first start. Practicing intentional reps and good technique, we are better able to make most any exercise feel great. 

 

The goal of the Men of Movement retreat is to create a space for men to rewire and re-pattern their sovereignty through body, breath, and brotherhood. 

 

Hold your ground.

Know who you are and what you want.

Together we move.

Together we rise.

 

Men of Movement Retreat

Mt. Shasta, Northern CA

May 12-15, 2022

 

I believe that we are more than our mistakes. AND we are more than what we accomplish. 

 

Click here and schedule a call if you’re interested. 

 

Wishing you all the best and hoping to hear from you soon,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 5/4/22 Halo
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

Exercise progressions are there to help methodically and intentionally make your body “smarter.” 

 

A smarter body moves with greater ease and control, AND continues to progress in complexity.

 

For example, it’s cool to do a standing broad jump. But if you have the capability to do a standing broad jump and stick the landing on a narrow balance beam, to me that demonstrates a body that has leveled up in "smartness."

 

In today’s video, we go over the halo. It’s a fundamental movement focusing on the shoulders. Add in the 2 progressions covered in this video and you'll experience training your body to be “smarter” with control, mobility, and coordination.

 

Click here and add these progressions in with the halo to get more benefit out of the same amount of time invested into your workout. 

 

Train intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 5/4/22 RecMin nasal
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

Often, it's the simple things that have the biggest impact. Breathing through your nose (NOT your mouth) may seem small but the benefits are huge.

 

Why does this small change have such a big impact?

 

Because it affects how oxygen is delivered to your tissues
Because it has a direct impact on your nervous system
Because you breathe thousands of times every day

Closing your mouth is a small change that carries BIG benefits. 

 

Breathing through your nose helps put your body into a parasympathetic state where it is better suited to recover. The fanciest post-workout protein shake can’t do that, but you can simply by closing your mouth. 

 

To start, focus on breathing through your nose in these 3 situations:

 

During the day
During conditioning workouts (especially during warm-ups)
While sleeping

I know…during the day and while sleeping pretty much means all the time! And while there are a few times when it's ok to breathe through your mouth while conditioning, those instances are rare, so basically keep it nasal as much as you can.

 

Here are a few of the benefits:

 

Greater ability to enter into a flow state
Increased work capacity
Improved recovery and restful sleep

Nasal breathing is your recovery minute for this week. Make it a habit.

 

Train (and recover) intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Bulgarian Bag Certification Interest
text:
Hey {first_name}, 

 

It's been approximately 12 years since I first picked up my Bulgarian Bag, and I am still impressed at how much it's given me, both as an athlete and as a coach. 

 

Truth be told, it's opened a lot of doors for me professionally, and that is one reason why I love sharing my knowledge and experience on this tool with others so they can also benefit.

 

Whether you are a coach or not, understanding how to use this tool safely and optimally can:

Enhance your movement skill
Add variety to training
Reduce injuries by becoming more proficient in often neglected patterns and planes of movement
Help you re-discover play in your training
Deliver a damn good training effect in a short amount of time
Set yourself apart from others in the gym/work environment if you are a coach/trainer

With the rise of virtual education, I figured I would gauge your interest here on hosting my next VIRTUAL Certification this coming August.

 

If you are interested in more details, click below:

Click Here to Apply

 

*NOTE: I've decided to do this certification differently than what I have offered in the past. Meaning you will be required to apply for it. This decision has come after lots of reflection on teaching this training tool widely around the US and internationally - not surprisingly, the best results come when the information is presented in a customized way to those who will attend. I'd love to get to know more, understand what experience (if any) you have, what your intention is for seeking to attend, if you're a good fit, and more. This will enable me to deliver something truly exceptional and unique just for YOU, which is what I love. 

 

Yours in health,

Mike

name: Bulgarian Bag August Cert Interest #2
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

Bulgarian Bag training is one of the best ways I know to develop overall athleticism and strength:

 

Grip (one of the most powerful but underrated aspects of strength)
Rotation (a punch, a throw, a kick etc. are all based on rotation)
Power & Power Endurance (move explosively, and be able to do so again and again) 

If you’re at all interested in the Bulgarian Bag, watch this ~5 min video about the certification and hear what people have said after experiencing it. 

 

I'm excited to share that I’ve got an online certification coming up at the end of August.

 

If you want functional strength - meaning that you can kick, throw, punch, run, and move like a bat out of hell - the Bulgarian Bag is a great tool. 

 

And we have a ton of fun!

 

Apply today and receive more details. There is an application process this time so I can learn the needs of each person attending and tailor the certification + a custom workshop to the specific needs of this group. 

 

I hope I get the opportunity to work with you soon,

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Nurture 6/23/22 Fully Body Circuit
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

Making progress in training is always easier when you have a few quality circuits/routines in your back pocket. 

 

Today’s circuit hits the upper body, lower body, back, and abs using three exercises

 

Tip: If you don’t have a Bulgarian Bag, substitute a kettlebell for exercise number 2 in this circuit. 

 

I recommend anywhere between 2 to 8 sets of this circuit, depending on your time, the weight you use, and how you’re feeling. 

 

Watch the full video for a demo and my recommendations on reps. 

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. Get certified with the Bulgarian Bag! I’ve got an online Bulgarian Bag certification + exclusive workshop coming up on August 27th which is the best way to get trained on the foundations. 

 

The Bulgarian Bag was invented to train wrestlers. It is a unique tool for building the kind of strength and conditioning that makes you stronger than you look. Functional training, to me, means that you can apply strength, balance, precision, timing, coordination, etc. in as many positions as possible…not only up and down like a squat or press. 

 

I’ve been using this tool for about 12 years and I can’t recommend it enough. It’s happening on Saturday August 27th. Click here to apply for the certification today.

name: Nurture 6/30/22 KB Essentials Deadlift
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

This week’s video is essential. Especially if you are newer to lifting, please make a point of watching and practicing this video. 

 

The deadlift represents the most essential movement pattern (i.e. bend pattern), that you will perform with a kettlebell. Practicing and using great technique is part of how you develop a body that is strong, stable, athletic and prepared for more advanced movements. Athletes have to make minute adjustments on the fly and practicing control of their body throughout this, and any lift, is a great way to support this ability. 

 

Watch today’s video breakdown and practice a few sets of this movement as you maintain awareness of your: spine, feet, shoulders and grip.

 

Own this deadlift technique and it will serve you for years. 

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

 

P.S. 4th of July sales are going down soon! Stay tuned for discounts on online programs - Kettlebell Lifestyle & Mastering The Kettlebell, PLUS 1-on-1 virtual Somatic Release Breathwork Sessions!

name: Bulgarian Bag Cert Promo Email #3
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

A powerful grip is truly practical strength. One of the primary ways we interact with the world is through our hands. 

 

If you need to express strength, chances are your grip is going to be an important aspect. The trouble is, most gym work isn’t that great at building a strong grip. 

 

If you’ve done heavy deadlifts before, you know that the first thing to give out is grip. That’s why people use lifting straps or a special grip for heavy deadlifts. If your hands start to slip, your brain compensates and reduces the force you can apply. 

 

Grip is a HUGE limiting factor. 

 

Now consider grip from the reverse perspective. If you find yourself in a situation where you have to grab someone to prevent them from doing harm to you or others, your grip strength is an unmistakable broadcast. Even before conscious thought has time to become words, they receive the signal of how powerful your grip is loud and clear. 

 

Talk about functional strength. 

 

My Favorite Way To Train Grip

 

I like dynamic movements. Working grip from every angle with special tools doesn’t appeal to me. Instead, I use a tool designed for wrestlers (a very grip intensive sport) so I’m building grip at the same time as I train all the other muscles to be scrappy and tough. 

 

The Bulgarian Bag swing - when done for higher reps - will work your grip like nothing else. The leather handle starts to get slippery and you have to crush the handles or it will go flying. 

 

Ask anyone who has trained with a Bulgarian Bag how their hands and forearms felt after some high rep swings. (They’ll tell you the grip training is amazing.)

 

A strong grip will also protect your shoulders and elbows when training with kettlebells, barbells, and pull up bars. 

 

The best way to learn the Bulgarian Bag is at a certification. At the certification, I’ll guide you through the curriculum created by the bag’s inventor who is also an olympic level wrestling coach. 

 

You’ll know what I mean about grip after the certification. 

 

The certification is virtual so you can join me from wherever you are and it is a lot of fun. To register, fill out the application form here. The application form will help me learn about your needs and tailor the certification to exactly who is showing up. 

 

Apply now and I’ll see you there. Your grip and how you interact with the world will thank you.

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

name: Bulgarian Bag Interest
text:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

If you’re like me, the idea of doing isolated grip training sounds too boring for me to program it into my training. The Bulgarian Bag is the perfect way to train grip while doing dynamic, full body movements. 

 

Here’s the main reason why:

 

Those handles… 

Your hands will get sweaty. At the same time, you’re spinning the bag 360 degrees which creates a lot of force pulling the bag away from you. You have to squeeze hard and keep focus on maintaining that killer death grip or the bag will go flying. 

 

Want to see what it looks like when you go all out to the point where forearms are clenching up? Click here to see high rep spins in action when I was challenged to test my max rep spins by the inventor of the bag. Watch from minute 8 if you’re short on time and notice how the set ends (hint: it was grip).

 

Want to develop your confidence and competence with this tool so you can train grip, along with your entire body in a new and exciting way? Come join the upcoming virtual Bulgarian Bag Certification I am running in August.

 

Bulgarian Bag Certification

Date: August 27th

Time: 7amPST to 4pmPST

*Virtual Certification - no travel required 

 

**Bonus 75 minute recorded workshop included when you sign up before August 1st. Click here to apply today.**

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi 

 

P.S. I’ve been using a Bulgarian Bag for about 12 years and I truly believe they are one of the best largely-unknown tools. I’ve tried tons of styles of training, but I stick with Bulgarian Bags. The best place to get the fundamentals down so you can make great use of a Bulgarian Bag is from a certification. Apply for my virtual Bulgarian Bag Certification coming up August 27th. Get the details and apply here.

name: Fear Paralyzes
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Lately, there have been many changes happening in my life.

 

For one, I recently got engaged :)

 

Two, I am going to be a father, HOLY SMOKES! 

 

And that’s not it…(read til the end)

 

With such big life changes happening, I feel now more than ever that everyday I am waking up a new man. 

 

Close friends have been asking me one question lately, “what is changing with the knowledge that you will be a father?”

 

While it keeps evolving, here are a few things that I’m present to:

 

A deeper sense of purpose and legacy
Testosterone feels like it’s at level 10+ lol
Heightened sense awareness
Love, gratitude, and awe for Lauren, my finance, is off the charts
Continuously in awe of how the miracle that is this baby is growing and Lauren is bringing it into the world
My gratitude for my mom and dad, all they’ve sacrificed and done for my brother and I all our lives, lands right in the center of my heart
I am more willing to connect with and grow through certain fears I’ve had for a long time. 

 

Circling back to the title of this email, I wrote that fear paralyzes…well, as I’m learning, that is the case - until it doesn’t.

 

There has been one fear I've had over the last 5 years that has really had my feet cemented into the ground…the fear of starting my own podcast. 

 

The truth is it’s not the podcast that scares me, it’s actually what I’ve allowed it to represent… and boy has it felt like a big a$$ monster. 

 

This monster has left me afraid:

 

To make mistakes where my voice will be heard in this way
Allow myself to be a beginner at something new
To express a difference of opinion with guests that may lead to a form of conflict (my personality has always been more of a peacemaker)
Suck at interviewing
Be great at interviewing
Receive negative feedback
Receive positive feedback

But, as I step into fatherhood, I’ve been doing more of an honest inventory of the man I am, and the man I am growing into. While the fear is still there, the pull towards being the best father I can be, has given me the courage to no longer let fear consume and paralyze me. 

 

I believe that sometimes what is in the way, IS the way. It's time that I step up into this opportunity to grow myself and simultaneously provide the best content and information I can by bringing in experts to help elevate your goals and dreams.

 

I am trusting my path, and I hope you find the strength to trust yours as well.

 

I’ll be sharing more over the next 6 weeks (podcast launches mid September) as I bring this new podcast creation to life, and I hope you’ll join me for it.

 

Wishing you all the best and stay tuned,

Mike

name: Inner Compass IG Live
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

As Carl Jung put it, “until you make the unconscious conscious, it will direct your life and you will call it fate."

 

(mic drop)

 

As a coach, so much of what we do is to support clients through this very process.

 

But this doesn’t only apply to client-coach relationships - bringing the unconscious conscious, which essentially heightens our level of self-awareness, applies to all people and relationships.

 

With this topic in mind, tomorrow at 5pm PST, I’ll be bringing on coach and friend, Jason Olivea for an IG Live interview. Jason co-developed a powerful personality assessment tool called InnerCompass. This is something I first took with Jason over 2 years ago, and the clarity and empowerment that both Lauren and I have received from it has been very helpful in our relationship, as well as our personal and professional lives.

 

The InnerCompass Personality Assessment invites people to come into contact with their core drives and motivations, which largely lie in the unconscious, per Carl Jung quotes above. We need a way to consider with curiosity and courage our shadow and habitual patterns which had served us in historical phases of life and yet do not serve us today due to the very different circumstances and challenges we face with life today.

 

The InnerCompass Assessment offers a Roadmap to navigate our inner life (i.e. the way we talk to ourselves and perceive the world) in a way that actually feels like I have a way to move forward without bypassing and divorcing the past.  

 

Join Jason and I tomorrow, Monday at 5pmPST, for a 30-minute discussion on making the unconscious conscious on IG Live (@Mike.Salemi).

 

Yours in health,

Mike

 

P.S. In case you missed this week's IG Live on Nature & Our Souls Purpose with Tim Corcoran, you can click here. People LOVED this discussion, and I know you will too.

name: Becoming Comfortable with Discomfort
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I understand that most people do not want to experience discomfort. And in many respects, I share that same sentiment.

 

BUT I've noticed there can be more to it than that if we so choose...

 

Over the years, parts of me have learned not only to see the value in discomfort, but also see its beauty and even enjoy it at times LOL.

 

Through discomfort, through adversity, and through testing our character, we can learn a great deal about ourselves and have a rare opportunity to rise up.

 

 

One of the keys, however, to using discomfort in a healthier, more productive way has to do with bringing intention into the equation.

 

Whether it’s public speaking for the first time, asking someone out on a date, taking a new martial arts class, playing an instrument, or learning a foreign language - whatever it is that makes you uncomfortable, offers a path to growth.

 

The next time there is something that you would like to explore but are experiencing fear or hesitation around it, I invite you to consider any or all of these questions:

 

Why do I, or parts of me, want to do this (be as honest as you can with yourself here)?
What would success look AND feel like?
How will other aspects of my life become better as a result of this?
Do I have anyone I can reach out to if I need support?
What tools do I have when things get hard?
On this one, I’ll remind you of something that we all have, that doesn’t cost any money, and something that is the anchor to helping us navigate any challenging experience - BREATH. 
Tip: Breathe low (belly), slow, and light (keep it nasal).

These questions have helped me more times than I can count to intentionally enter into discomfort and utilize it in a more productive manner.

 

Wishing you a great rest of your day,

Mike

 

P.S. Tomorrow is THE BIG DAY... my new podcast, The Path, drops! I’ll be reaching back out as soon as it does so you can be in the loop and catch the first episode with a special guest who I'm quite certain you have not heard before! ; )

 

P.P.S. If you enjoyed today’s email on becoming comfortable with discomfort and are a man (or have a special man in your life), the next Men of Movement Retreat happens Oct. 27-30th in Mt. Shasta, CA. We'll be doing deep, healing work together in community. Click here for more info or to hop on a call with me.

Hi {first_name},

 

I understand that most people do not want to experience discomfort. And in many respects, I share that same sentiment.

 

BUT I've noticed there can be more to it than that if we so choose...

 

Over the years, parts of me have learned not only to see the value in discomfort, but also see its beauty and even enjoy it at times LOL.

 

Through discomfort, through adversity, and through testing our character, we can learn a great deal about ourselves and have a rare opportunity to rise up.

 

 

One of the keys, however, to using discomfort in a healthier, more productive way has to do with bringing intention into the equation.

 

Whether it’s public speaking for the first time, asking someone out on a date, taking a new martial arts class, playing an instrument, or learning a foreign language - whatever it is that makes you uncomfortable, offers a path to growth.

 

The next time there is something that you would like to explore but are experiencing fear or hesitation around it, I invite you to consider any or all of these questions:

 

  1. Why do I, or parts of me, want to do this (be as honest as you can with yourself here)?
  2. What would success look AND feel like?
  3. How will other aspects of my life become better as a result of this?
  4. Do I have anyone I can reach out to if I need support?
  5. What tools do I have when things get hard?
    • On this one, I’ll remind you of something that we all have, that doesn’t cost any money, and something that is the anchor to helping us navigate any challenging experience - BREATH. 
    • Tip: Breathe low (belly), slow, and light (keep it nasal).

These questions have helped me more times than I can count to intentionally enter into discomfort and utilize it in a more productive manner.

 

Wishing you a great rest of your day,

Mike

 

P.S. Tomorrow is THE BIG DAY... my new podcast, The Path, drops! I’ll be reaching back out as soon as it does so you can be in the loop and catch the first episode with a special guest who I'm quite certain you have not heard before! ; )

 

P.P.S. If you enjoyed today’s email on becoming comfortable with discomfort and are a man (or have a special man in your life), the next Men of Movement Retreat happens Oct. 27-30th in Mt. Shasta, CA. We'll be doing deep, healing work together in community. Click here for more info or to hop on a call with me.

name: Episode 1 with Ya'acov
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

As the symbolic beginning of The Path Podcast, this is the perfect way to start.

 

Ya'acov Darling Khan has the wisdom of an elder and the humbleness of a friend. He is a modern-day shaman with over 30 years of experience teaching globally and is known for his down-to-earth strength, humility, and humor.

 

In this conversation, he shares the knowledge he has gleaned from his studies with gifted healers from around the world, from the Arctic to the Amazon. 

 

Ya'acov and I discuss:

• Using dance to transform self-consciousness into a conscious presence

name: Episode 2 Solocast
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

For years, much of my life revolved around Kettlebell Sport and the archetype of being an athlete. I dedicated an incredible amount of time, energy, and discipline towards my goal of being the best Kettlebell Sport lifter possible. Although my training and vision has evolved over time, that goal attracted me to some amazing experiences and lessons.

 

Looking back, one of the most memorable experiences involved attending a week-long training camp in St. Petersburg, Russia, run by members of the Russian National Kettlebell Sport Team. During that time, I learned invaluable lessons, not only in my training but also in life. Today I want to share them with you.

 

In Episode 2 of The Path Podcast, I discuss:

My trip to visit the Russian National Kettlebell Sport Team
Takeaways from training with the most elite athletes on the planet
How to become a kettlebell Master of Sport
The most essential component of physical training
My biggest lesson in becoming a better man

 

Click here to listen on Apple.

name: True Friends
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Today I got the opportunity to spend time with an old, dear friend.

 

It was heartfelt, real, and raw.

 

In our time together, I felt immense gratitude from him being what I call a true friend.

 

There are few people we can call a "true" friend.

 

People that will be there with you regardless what happens in life.

 

I want you to know that there are people out there who love you for being you - just as you are.

 

The beauty and challenge of being a human is that none of us are exempt from the trials and tribulations in life.

 

All we can do, in my opinion, is to keep putting one foot forward with the intention and effort to show up. Doing this consistently often pulls the right people to us. 

 

Match that with a pure intention to grow, heal, and connect and you’ve got a recipe for genuine expansion.

 

If you, or any man you know would like to share in a sacred space of healing together, come join us at the end of this month at my Men of Movement Retreat in Mt. Shasta, CA

 

I have no idea the transformation that is likely to place for you, but what I can say with certainty is that we’ve got your back, and will do all we can to support you. 

 

Click here to learn more about this unique experience.

 

Big love,

Mike

text:

name: Paul Chek's Tarot Workshop
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

The Tarot has been part of Paul Chek's personal and professional practice for many years. He even shared with us the spot in his library where he has 13 years of documented daily readings that his soul has shared with him through these powerful cards and archetypal symbols.

 


After wrapping up a podcast together (coming to The Path soon!) Paul guided me through a reading that blew Lauren and I away.

name: Episode 8  S. DiStefano  Episode
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Sal Di Stefano, co-host of the wildly popular podcast Mind Pump, is joining me today on The Path!

 

While Sal has an incredibly vast amount of knowledge and experience in the fitness industry, this conversation takes another direction. Sal and I share being first-generation Americans, coming from a culture steeped in family tradition and values. In this episode, we focus on the blending of traditional Italian culture with more modern times. There is a lot to be gained from maintaining values that have been passed down, as well as re-patterning generational cycles that no longer have a place today.

 

In Episode #8 of The Path Podcast, Sal and I discuss:

Challenging vs. maintaining traditional family roles
The pros and cons of cultural standards
Creating intentionality around the art of food
Connection and healing through generational gaps
Finding empathy for others’ experiences
What it means to be present as a parent

Click here to listen on Spotify.

Yours in health and strength,

Email: Support@mikesalemi.io

 

Also, last week I was stoked to share with you what a few clients had to say about their experience going through Kettlebell Lifestyle, now here's another incredible transformation you can read about from someone who came back to kettlebells after 3 years off!:

 

"A few months ago, I decided to get back to kettlebell training, after a 3 year hiatus. I made the mistake of picking up right where I left off, and threw out my back. I know better than to push myself so hard, but alas, it happens to the best of us. Needless to say I was hesitant to pick up a bell again. I saw that Mike Salemi rolled out his Kettlebell Lifestyle program and I decided to give it a try.

 

In the first section of the program, I was introduced to a proper daily warm up as well as a new stretching program. These two sections changed everything for me. I noticed that within the first 2 weeks, the residual pain in my low back and pelvis went away completely. My posture in my neck and low back improved massively.

 

The cues and attention to detail throughout the program made me feel like I was working one on one with a highly skilled trainer. The details in the stretches alone made me understand the importance of micro movements in the stretches I have been doing for years.

 

When I got into the main phases of the program, the program would adjust based on how I answered the morning questionnaire. This was amazing, as it made me realize that I can get a huge benefit from working less hard, if my body is under other types of stress. This program allows me to be less militant with following a program, and work better with my own daily limitations.

 

Overall, I have and will continue to recommend this program to my friends, family and clients who want to see lasting changes in how they move."

 

Allison Reynolds

Massage Therapist

 

I hope you and your family are having a wonderful holiday weekend,

Mike

name: Onnit Cert
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In my own physical training, the two tools that I use most are kettlebells and Bulgarian bags. 

 

Why is that? 

 

Considering that both are arguably the most versatile and portable functional training tools out there, in addition, simply the benefits of how you use them aids in our capacity to adapt to more of what life may throw at you is well any investment. 

 

Adaptability is defined as the ability to adjust to new conditions.

 

If you're receiving this email, I bet you can resonate with some of this reflection - that our fitness routines and workouts give us tools that help us to navigate life with greater confidence, resilience, and ease. 

 

When we get used to doing hard things, the hard things don't seem so overwhelming any more, and we learn to adapt.

 

At least, this has been true for me personally.

 

The fact that the Bulgarian Bag is a soft implement makes it a great choice for learning safely and makes the learning curve a bit more forgiving. 

 

The way it trains, rotation, lateral movement, grip, and muscular endurance I've experienced are hard to beat. 

 

That's why in the New Year, I've decided to hold the next in-person Bulgarian Bag Level 1 Certification at the mecca of human optimization and functional training - The Onnit Gym Headquarters in Austin, Texas on Monday, January 16th.

 

This certification will be an exceptional one. You will be surrounded by other students who are incredibly motivated to learn, as well as fitness industry leaders including Eric Leija (the Primal Swolger on Instagram), Aaron Alexander (of the Align Podcast), Kyle Kingsbury, and more. 

 

This special event includes your very own Bulgarian Bag to keep, as well as an additional virtual workshop before the course.

 

If this sounds like something you'd be interested in, click this link to find out more and register today!

 

We will be holding it on Martin Luther King Day weekend and the course will be held on Monday, January 16th.

 

If you've ever been curious to visit Onnit, learn the Bulgarian Bag, or train alongside rad people, click here.

 

I hope to see you there!

Mike

name: Episode 20 Steven Jaggers
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Breath is the only mechanism in the body that we do both consciously and unconsciously. It can be the access point to understanding parts of ourselves that we may have disconnected from over the years. I’ve always been interested in breathwork in regards to enhancing performance and now I’m aware of so many other applications like trauma healing and emotional release. This episode is a breathwork masterclass with the founder of somatic breathwork, Steven Jaggers. I know you’re going to learn a ton from this one!
 

In Episode #20 of The Path, Steven and I discuss:

Why it’s so hard to relax
Getting in touch with the mind muscle connection
Why we do inner emotional work
Healing is a process, not a place
Feeling, expressing, and dealing with anger
A new perspective on integration

 

Click here to listen on Apple.

 

Click here to listen on Spotify.
 

Yours in Health,

Mike

name: Episode 21 Justin Andrews
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Justin Andrews is one of the three co-hosts of the wildly popular fitness podcast, Mind Pump. Justin is really the resident expert on unconventional training at mind pump. In this episode, we break down the benefits of this kind of training for health, as well as how it can transfer to improving other aspects of life. Allowing kids to take their own risks and follow their own path
The biggest and most surprising lessons of parenthood
The camaraderie of sports
Unconventional training: What it looks like and how to start
Myths in the fitness industry
Fear of public speaking to speaking for a living & Learning to enjoy being a beginner

name: Baby Luca
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I am excited and blessed to share that two weeks ago, Lauren and our baby boy, Luca Valentino Salemi, was born. 

 

He came early and unexpected, and seeing him healthy has been the greatest gift of my life. 

 

In these past two weeks, I finally know what people have shared with me feels like - having a child is like having your heart outside of your body.

 

What I did not expect are some of the following:

Simply watching him has been healing for my inner child
My love for him and for Lauren has grown beyond my wildest dreams
I would do anything to protect him
Many parts of me do not wish to return back to work lol, as a result of loving every minute with him right now

In life, growth promoting events, whether perceived as "positive or negative", either happen to us, or we choose them.

 

Through stepping into fatherhood, I can say with conviction that I have a new level of purpose. 

 

Purpose in not just being a father, but protecting the innocence of children as a whole, and supporting fathers in their journey of stepping into this calling. 

 

I would like to share a little glimpse of our new nugget of joy.

 

As someone who has been a part of my community, I wanted to share that Laruen and I have decided to hold off on sharing more photos of him on Social Media as a personal preference. We feel he is so energetically porous right now, and we are simply loving being in our "cave" enjoying every moment. 

 

Thank you for being in this journey along with us. 

 

In the near future, we will release a podcast with Dr. Nathan Riley, the Holistic OBGYN discussing our birth story, and on The Path Podcast not long after that. 

 

In the meantime, we are sending you good energy, and want to thank you for all your support.

 

All my best,

Mike
