name: Illuminate
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Everywhere you look it’s easy to see people all rapidly disconnecting from old systems and structures we once relied on for guidance. People are starving for insight and information on how to live their lives, heal their bodies, soothe broken hearts, and be the place where cycles of trauma stop in their families.

 

By choice or by circumstance people are learning that they can't rely on the ways they used to receive guidance. They have to forge a new way forward. But how?

 

You and I know that the best and truest guidance comes within. They may not have experienced that yet.

 

The field of coaching has been on the rise in recent years and is currently seeing an explosion. Clients see the power of a dynamic coaching relationship to become a driving force in their own life. Coaches get to experience facilitating real, authentic, empowering change through their laptops… it’s easy to understand why it's such an expanding field. 

 

And if you're worried about industry saturation or not having enough room for you... think again...

 

In the United States alone the coaching industry was a 1.5 billion dollar industry in 2022 and that's projected to grow to 2 billion annually (yep, billion with a B) by the year 2030.

 

(This is where you come in...) 

 

There is a groundswell of people searching for the heart of service that you have... are you ready to rise to meet them?

 

If you desire to be a part of this global shift we're experiencing, now is the time to step into your capacity.

 

My friend Jator Pierre has seen his share of shifts over more than two decades of coaching. A globally recognized CHEK practitioner, National Board Certified Coach, and seasoned coach of over twenty years he’s seen it all and has helped thousands of people get to the roots of their symptoms to help them live the life they choose. 

 

With that knowledge has created something truly unique in a sea of bland, boring, fluff-filled online coach training programs. Illuminate is a 5-Month Coach Accelerator to provide you with the foundation you need for both you and your clients to thrive. 

 

If you desire clarity, confidence, and alignment in your coaching practice you’ll need a framework that is predictable, repeatable, and potent no matter the client's situation without being cookie-cutter, Illuminate was created to help you do just that. 

 

The time has come my friends...

 

If you are a coach (or desire to be) who wants to dive deeply into your purpose and step up in a big way... join me inside ILLUMINATE.

 

Illuminate is a 5-month Coach Accelerator that offers you a road-tested framework for guiding people into the role of leader of their own lives.

 

This is not your typical coach training.

 

Instead of me excitedly rambling on, why don't I just show you?

Check it out here.

 

It just launched today and I’m super excited for you to join me. We start Feb 20th.

 

See ya inside.

 

Talk soon friend!

Mike

name: Progress Can be Easy
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Progress feels DAMN good, AND doesn’t always need to be a struggle…It's been a long road, but progress on my right knee is finally happening.

 

Not long ago, I had a very honest conversation with Josh Trent on his podcast, Wellness+Wisdom, where I was open with knee issues I’ve been facing in recent years. Ever since that recording, I’ve been inspired to not only seek help but follow a recovery program that I was willing to stick to. 

 

One important thing I realized is that I’ve been standing in my own way. I had this story in my head that healing and resolving the knee pain needed to be hard, long, and tedious. 

 

In fact, I’ve held a similar story in many other areas as well, with the underlying theme being “things have to be hard” to be worthwhile or for me to “deserve” them.

 

Well, how much my knee has improved with such little hard “effort” has honestly been shocking to me.

 

Huge shoutout to my three main guys who have supported me in some way: Jonny Suarez, Justin Brien, and Brian Reynolds, and also the Marc Pro device (I’ll be sharing more on this unit in the near future). With each activity, I’ve literally been doing the minimum effective dose and just a few short minutes during the week, and WOW what an improvement. 

 

Jonny's pictured here, practicing TCM-Acupuncture, Justin's a Soma Therapist, and Brian's the TRE (tension & trauma release exercises) specialist.

 

What's been really refreshing is that progress doesn't always have to be a massive uphill battle. In fact, it can feel pretty effortless when you find the right approach. It's a big lesson I've learned and I'm thankful this has been my path.

 

This week on the Path Podcast, we're bringing on Jonny Suarez to dive deep into Men's Health and Hormone Optimization. If that's up your alley, you won't want to miss it.

 

Thanks for being there for me through this journey. Let's keep inspiring each other and lifting one another up.

 

- Mike

name: Men Retreat, Values
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

As men, we're often told to prioritize certain values such as success, self-reliance, and being decisive. However, it's crucial to identify and stand up for our authentic values, the ones that truly define us and give us purpose. By doing so, we can lead a fulfilling life.

 

To help you discover your authentic values, I wanted to share a condensed version of an exercise I take clients through: 

 

PART I

List out your top 5 core values as you know them.

 

If you've never explored your values, I HIGHLY recommend it. Many times in life when we experience stress, frustration, and pain, it's often because we are living in a way that is not in alignment with our values (or maybe we've never taken the time to get clear on them in the first place).

name: Men Retreat, Sweat Lodge
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I will never forget my first experience in a Sweat Lodge. It tested my spirit, along with the others around me, in a way I had not experienced before.

 

I felt as if a large weight was lifted off my back, and noticeable inner clarity arose.

 

In addition, I've found the Sweat Lodge to be helpful in my life for harnessing the inner resource needed to navigate times of overwhelm.

 

In my opinion, if we never touch our edges, not only will we not know what we're truly capable of, but also how we experience life can end up feeling dull, flat, or easily too much.

 

In this video, while in a sauna, I briefly explain some of the major differences between a sauna and a sweat lodge - something I’ve been asked multiple times by men who have an interest in the Men of Movement Retreat.

 

Photo: Sweat Lodge, Mt. Shasta, CA

One of the transformative sessions at this Men's event, led by a Native American elder, is a Sweat Lodge ceremony.

 

Although both the sauna and Sweat Lodge involve intense heat, there are SIGNIFICANT differences between experiencing the two.

 

I hope you enjoy this video mini-breakdown discussing this very thing.

 

Yours in health and strength,

Mike

 

P.S. At the Men of Movement retreat coming up June 8 - 11, the Sweat Lodge we partake in is a rite of passage guided by a Native American elder who has been running Lodges for over 40 years. There are still 5 available spots -  schedule a call with me if you are a man interested in addressing the overwhelm and isolation that is all too common today.

name: KB Snatch
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

The Kettlebell Snatch is primarily used as a power-endurance exercise. It integrates the lower and upper body, builds the muscles of the lower back, glutes, hamstrings, rhomboids, traps, shoulders, and more.

 

The Snatch is a progressive movement from the Clean and involves similar mechanics, except now rather than the kettlebell finishing in the Rack Position, the terminal point is in the Overhead Lockout, also known as Fixation Position. 


The most challenging part: Intentional positioning and timing of hand insertion to enter into the overhead lockout position (this is pictured during the second row of photos below).

 

Technique Points for the element of hand insertion:

Hand insertion during this movement happens at approximately chest level and 10 o’clock
To redirect the kettlebell back, a slight leaning back, pull from the shoulder + arm, and to a degree trunk rotation takes place. As you "meet" the kettlebell by actively inserting your hand through the window, the shoulder protracts and arm straightens a bit.
Keep fingers and palm open as you insert your hand
Kettlebell handle should finish at a 45-degree angle into the heel of the palm 
Once the hand is fully inserted, it's the kettlebell’s momentum that should carry it effortlessly into the Overhead Lockout Position
Also, aim to bring the kettlebell up the centerline of the body and allow the kettlebell's momentum and the mechanics of the movement to do most of the work to get the kettlebell overhead.

By following some of these tips, you can more safely and effectively perform the Kettlebell Snatch.

 

I hope you have a fantastic weekend and enjoy your training,

Mike

name: Finding the Levity
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

When it comes to exploring and working with things like our inner critic, limiting beliefs, and all the other aspects of our inner world, many times it can feel heavy, dense, and uncomfortable. 

For a LONG time I kept pushing to grow in a way that for the most part primarily involved an energy of seriousness and intensity - something that I still need to be mindful of at times. 

As I started finding levity in this work (side note - finding a partner who loves to play like Lauren is teaching me a lot in this regard 🙏), I realized that it is a vital medicine for life. 

As we embrace levity and play in/around deeper inner work, a few things come up with how it can be an ally:





Safety: Play can create a safe space for exploring deeper aspects of oneself, reducing fear and allowing us greater ease when stepping into something uncomfortable.
Creativity: Playfulness sparks imagination and fresh insights, unveiling hidden patterns and alternative solutions.
Emotional release: Playful activities can provide a healthy outlet for emotions, freeing us from tension and fostering processing.
Self-reflection: A lighthearted approach can encourages curiosity and openness, leading to greater self-awareness and insight.
Resilience: Playfulness can cultivate adaptability and resilience, helping us navigate challenges and embrace personal growth.
Joy and well-being: Levity injects joy, pleasure, and fun into inner work, which can make it more sustainable.
Integration: Play aids in integrating and embodying insights, bridging the gap between understanding and lasting change.

As a general theme, balancing playfulness with respect for the depth of inner work can be incredibly powerful and freeing.

As we head into the weekend I hope you are able to enjoy some light, fun activities filled with laughter alongside those people you care about most.

 

Wishing you all the best,

 

Mike Salemi

name: Educational Email 2
text:
Hi {first_name},

As promised last week, here is the email I created just for you where we explore the Kettlebell Push Press.

The Kettlebell Push Press has to be one of my favorite integrated pressing movements. The goal with this exercise is to begin utilizing power from the legs to drive the kettlebell into the Overhead Lockout Position.

 

Today we’ll be going into a step-by-step “how-to” on this movement, along with a few tips. 

 

When first learning, I like to break it up into two variations. 

 

Variation One

Heels Remain Down 

 

 

This first classic Push Press Variation is quite simple. As you dip and drive with the legs to propel the kettlebell upward, your heels will remain down the entire time. This tends to be good for people who are new to the movement entirely and are making their first progression from the Standing Strict Overhead Press, into this more dynamic and full body movement . 

 

Variation Two

Heels Rise

 

 

This second, more advanced variation requires even more total body integration, timing, power, and coordination. One thing to notice on this version is that you’ll be coming up powerfully onto the balls of the feet. This will involve more movement to take place around the ankles, forcing the calves to assist to a greater degree in the force generation sequence.

 

Let’s now break down the steps of this type of Push Press (version two):

 

Set up as for a Standing Overhead Press
While in the Rack Position, it is ideal to depress the loaded shoulder to the point at which the elbow rests on the pelvic/iliac crest, while maintaining a lengthened spine; however, do not force it
Dip body straight down 
Propel kettlebell powerfully into the Overhead Lockout Position with your legs, while extending up onto the balls of your feet
As the kettlebell enters the Overhead Lockout Position, heels should return to the floor
Lower kettlebell back into the Rack Position maintaining control
 

Additional Tips
 

Control the first dip. The first dip is the initial point when the body descends down,  pre-loading the acceleration phase. The idea here is to lower down quickly, however while maintaining control at all times. 

Timing the heels with the lockout. Most people will experience difficulty with the timing involved in this variation of the Push Press. Aim to have the have your heels return back to the floor around the same time as the arm/elbow lock out overhead. 
 
When to press. During a Push Press, majority of the work is done by the legs (via triple extension of the ankles, knees, and hips). It’s only the final ~1/4 of the movement overhead that the arms come in to press the kettlebell into the lockout position. 

 

Toss either Push Press variation one or two into your training and work on the details discussed above and I guarantee you’ll become a more functional overhead athlete as a result : )

 

Stay strong my friend,

Mike


 

P.S.  Next week we’ll head into discussing 3 simple things you can do to improve the effectiveness of your stretches. 

 

 

P.P.S. Check me out on Instagram @Mike.Salemi where I give more helpful information on wellness and performance throughout the week. You might even catch some tips on my Story on how to create the perfect espresso shot  ; )

name: Men of Movement Alumni
text:
Men of Movement Alumni!

 

I hope each of you are doing awesome!

 

As you may be aware, the next Men of Movement Retreat is coming up June 8-11th back out in Mount Shasta.

 

While you can expect key aspects similar to past events (Sweat Lodge, breathwork, and Ya'acov's Movement Medicine Ceremony for example) there are LOTS that will be new and different at this upcoming one. I believe we have 9 new sessions!

 

Getting in touch with the wisdom held inside the body through unique embodiment work, specialised breathwork practices, physicality exercises, the Enneagram, and much more will all be intertwined at this event. 

 

It's a time with no cell phones, to get out in nature with our brothers, and dive in together so that we can experience greater connection, healing, and growth. 

 

If you are feeling the call to join us, I'd love to have you. I will be offering this at a discounted rate for past participants. If you are interested please respond to this email and I can get you more information. 

 

Wishing you and your families all my best and big love,

Mike

 

 

P.S. 

A former teacher of mine, Anat Peri, runs an excellent program called Training Camp for the Soul. She is holding an event in June (7-11th) and while it is co-ed, I wanted to share it with you as I was speaking with her and if you have a wife/girlfriend/partner who is interested, feel free to reach out to Anat directly. She mentioned that for any of your ladies interested in joining her Soul Liberation Retreat, she would be happy to offer $300 off. You can email her here (anat@trainingcampforthesoul.com) and mention you are from our Men of Movement group to get the discount.

name: Episode 38 Jator Pierre
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Jator Pierre is back on the Path podcast today! With 25 years of experience as a holistic coach, Jator has been a close friend and mentor to me for a decade. Over the past four months, I've had the privilege of participating in Jator's transformative Illuminate coaching program, which has inspired today's discussion on self-sabotage.

 

During our conversation, Jator sheds light on the nature of self-sabotage, explores the reasons behind our self-defeating tendencies, and provides guidance for healing and personal growth. This is an opportunity to discover how to expand your emotional capacity, harness the power of language to honor each moment, and overcome the obstacles that prevent us from living the life we truly desire.

Episode #38

with Jator Pierre

 



	

An unconventional idea of self-sabotage

 


	

The critical aspects of how we speak to ourselves and about ourselves

 


	

The difference between overt and covert behavior patterns

 


	

Breaking the hypnotic trance of our repetitive actions

 


	

Moving from unwanted behavior to empowered action

name: Beginner Workout B.Bag
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I just returned back from Boise, Idaho, which is the headquarters of Suples Training Systems - the creators of the Bulgarian Bag.

 

It was a jam-packed, exciting 36 hours filled with:

Podcasting with Olympian and legend, Ivan Ivanov
Training on the Bulgarian Bag and Throw Dummies
Learning new skills and olympic-level coaching philosophies
Watching the best wrestlers in the state of Idaho
Teaching a FREE workout on Instagram
Fun hanging out with the Suples team and family

Ivan Ivanov is an Olympian in Greco-Roman Wrestling, and was the former US Olympic coach. In addition to that, he developed Suples Training Systems, which makes some of the industry's best and most unique functional training tools - with solid education to go with it. 

 

While at Suples, myself, and two other Suples Pro Instructors, Magdalena Ivanova and Holly Lewis offered a free beginner-friendly workout. This was followed by a "round table" discussion on preparation for the Bulgarian Bag Championships happening in September.

 

The beginner-friendly workout can be viewed here in it's entirety. 

After the workout, you'll get to hear top tips from each of us in preparation for the Championships if you're interested in competing. This was followed by open Q+A.

 

I hope you enjoy the free Bulgarian Bag workout!

 

Wishing you all the best,

 

Mike Salemi
Performance Specialist, Men's Coach,

& Host of The Path Podcast

name: Episode 39 Anat Peri
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Today on The Path, we are joined by Anat Peri. Anat is an inner child expert with over 18 years of experience in the self-development space. Through her mentoring and Training Camp for the Soul program, Anat has empowered coaches and individuals to achieve emotional wellness and explore new possibilities in life. name: Educational Email 3
text:
Hi {first_name},
 

I received a great response from last week’s kettlebell email “Push Pressing Your Way to the Top.” Here’s another one on a topic that I’m excited to share with you - stretching and flexibility!

 

No matter which stretches you are performing to improve posture, performance, or recovery, below are 3 things you can do to immediately make big strides in your personal stretching practice. 

 

But, first let’s briefly discuss what flexibility is and how it differs from mobility - two terms that both relate to the topic of stretching that often get confused with one another.

 

Generally speaking, flexibility refers to the ability of a muscle to lengthen (more so passive in nature).  This differs from mobility - mobility is the combination of flexibility AND strength through a given range of motion. Mobility therefore integrates the nervous system, and body control is the desired end result. This element of control is very important to reduce injury risk, as well as help you become a more functional and resilient mover. 

 

 

So what are the 3 things you can do to improve both your flexibility AND mobility right now?

 

1. Raising Your Core Temperature Before Stretching 

 

The tissues of our body respond very well to heat. Thus performing stretches when the body is warm can go a long way to helping you get more out of them, and also reduce your risk of injury. I enjoy performing a brief core temperature warm up (for example, a brisk walk, marching in place, an easy row, etc. for around to 4-10 minutes). The idea here is to gradually get a light sweat going, and then move into your stretching routine. Often times I find it beneficial to also wear layers, such as sweat pants and a sweater during this time. 

 

2. Stretching Before Bed

 

I often get asked, “Mike, when is the best time to stretch?” What I’ve found is that stretching immediately following training, as well as before bed are both fantastic and produce noticeable results. Before bed is a critical time because our bodies are under the selective pressures of gravity to a much lesser degree and our postural muscles are not actively engaged. See what happens when you make this a regular part of your evening practice and shoot me a message with how it went!

 

3. Duration & Active Components 

 

a) Duration. In order to have a more substantial long-term effect on the flexibility of our tissues, I suggest holding stretches for longer duration. Usually I recommend approximately 90 seconds total of a stretch (or longer if needed) to start. You can do this in one shot, or break it up into 3 sets of 30 seconds with a short 10 second rest in between. Especially when combined with active components, these longer static stretches tend to produce longer term quality changes in flexibility and mobility. 

 

b) Active Components. Involving the nervous system to build strength and control across a range of motion requires an active component.  When doing this, the effort level doesn’t need to be intense, in fact I find it is best to ramp up the effort gradually during stretches and work closely with the breath.

 

Below is one example of a sequence you can try with any stretch:

 

Find your natural end-range for a given stretch
Relax into it and hold: (~60-90 seconds total)
Contract and activate the muscle you are aiming to stretch: 10-30 sec
Relax and go deeper: 10-30 sec
Contract and activate (starting from this newly acquired end-range): 10-30 sec
Relax & go deeper: 10-30 seconds
Repeat 1-3 more times with the same contract-relax sequence

I hope you found today’s tips on stretching helpful. Remember, quality (as with everything) is always preferred to over quantity. Thus, when performing your stretches, I suggest picking the 2-5 stretches that are likely to have the biggest positive impact on your health and performance, and sticking there for few weeks. If you have additional time on your hands, do this multiple times a day; as your flexibility and mobility improve, gradually add another stretch or two into the mix.

 

Wishing you happy stretching,

Mike

 

P.S. Check me out on Instagram @Mike.Salemi where I give more helpful information on wellness and performance throughout the week.

 

P.P.S.  Next week we’ll head into discussing "When to train, and when to back off ".

name: Announcement of July 4th Offer
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Almost daily, I see the struggles and internal battles faced by many men today, ones they largely live out in silence.

 

The weight of societal expectations, the masks worn to conceal vulnerability, the longing for genuine brotherhood, and the sense of feeling purposeless is real.

 

With this in mind, on July 4th  I am opening the doors to joining a new opportunity tailored for men who have been experiencing the burden of expectations, unexpressed emotions, the yearning for fulfillment, and the desire to live a life driven by purpose and integrity. 

 

Exploring these areas isn’t always the most "comfortable,” however, if you’re like me, I imagine you might agree that the greatest transformations come when we fully touch our edges. 

 

I’ve found two key ingredients to be incredibly helpful with this - curiosity and courage. And if I were to add one more, of which the impact cannot be understated, it would be quality brothers to go on the journey with.

 

This program, which opens for early enrollment on the 4th, provides a unique structure of masculine embodiment, Storywork, breathwork, 1:1 coaching, and more. 

 

It is time to shift the narratives that no longer serve our growth as men, and wholeheartedly embrace our true potential. 

 

If you feel called to this message of rising up and stepping firmly into your unique power from a grounded place, save the date - July 4th.

 

Together, we will pave a new way forward—one characterized by depth, purpose, and integrity, and brotherhood.

 

Stay tuned for more details coming.

 

Thank you,

Mike

name: Every a Perfect Time
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Too often, we find ourselves held back by thoughts of not being enough or not being ready. These self-imposed limitations become energy blocks that hinder us from pursuing our goals and dreams.

 

But here's the truth: waiting for the perfect moment will only keep us stuck in the same place. It's when we take action, even in the face of doubt, that we create the momentum necessary for growth.

 

It's sometimes about taking a leap of faith and betting on ourselves. When we embrace this mindset, incredible things can happen.

Speaking of incredible things, I've been working with my head down over the past few weeks on a project that I believe will have a profound impact on your life. It's designed to empower individuals like you to unlock your true potential and live authentically.

 

 

 

 

I'm excited to share all the details with you tomorrow. So, mark your calendar and keep an eye on your inbox for an email that could be a game-changer.

 

Best regards,

Mike

name: Educational Email 4
text:
“Should I train today? 

“If so, how much?”

“If not, should I take today completely off, or do something else?” ?

 

Hi {first_name}, these are all questions I hear often and have even asked myself many times over the years. 

 

If you’re like me, you’re hungry to reach the next level in your health and physical performance. Not surprisingly though, with this strong drive can come a few undesired consequences - especially if we are not aware of what our body is attempting to tell us along the way. 

 

Here’s a personal story to help illustrate this... 

 

I recall when I was about 19 years old training harder than ever for a Powerlifting competition. This was an in-house competition solely amongst the 18 members of our tight-knit basement Powerlifting team. We would run this competition once a year, and it was called “The Extravaganza.”

 

605lb Squat at 19 yrs old, 178lbs bodyweight

 

Using a total from a cumulative one-repetition maximum on the Squat, Bench Press, and Deadlift (3 attempts given on each lift), we would account for bodyweight and use a formula to determine who was the pound-for-pound strongest in the gym. 

 

I had been working my tail off for years and came as close as 2nd place the year prior. Winning the Palace Gym “Extravaganza” would have meant more to me than any large competition I would ever enter.  We were like a family - the type of family that wants to take each-others heads off for the sake of winning and holding bragging rights for a year ?. 

 

After a few brutal training cycles, I came in feeling ready. Programming, training sessions, the de-load phase, and weight cut were all dialed in. I ended up going 9 for 9 that day, finishing with a 605lb Squat, 430lb Bench Press, and 615lb Deadlift...winning my first ever Palace Gym Extravaganza.  

 

I felt so high after the win, yet rather than taking some much-needed rest to allow my body and mind to reset, I took only 2-3 days off and then it was back at it - nearly at full steam. 

 

What I later observed in myself was a pattern. Push hard for months, test myself, allow the bare minimum rest time, and then do it all over again. Over time this caught up with me. What followed not long after was discovering that I was in Stage 3 adrenal fatigue, had fungal and parasite infections, and a bacterial infection called H. Pylori - something that was causing painful stomach ulcers.

 

You see, on the surface, I appeared healthy, yet over time the continual grind without paying attention to the signs left me in a low state of vitality.  It got so bad that I had to take nearly 6 months completely off from training to allow my body to heal as I worked to restore my gut health. 

 

If it’s one thing I’ve learned over the years, it’s that the body is ALWAYS talking and dropping little (and sometimes big) clues for us to wake up to the reality of what is.

 

Today, in my coaching practice, I tend to see one of two people. The first is the under-trained and often injured client, and the second is the overtrained, and often bandaged-up person.

 

In this email, I’d like to focus on the overtrained person, and how to develop a more intuitive approach to training, as it relates closely to my own story above.

 

Specifically speaking to the topic of “when to train, and when to back off”, here are a few self-check-in questions you can ask yourself to help guide this:

 

“Am I tired today, honestly?” 
“Am I excited and motivated to train?” 
“Has my muscle and joint soreness recovered from the last session?”

 

While there are plenty more questions we could ask here, these 3 simple “yes or no” ones are plenty to get the ball rolling. When you test these on yourself, I suggest writing them down in a journal and making it a habit so that you can begin to identify patterns. The best time to ask yourself these questions is when you first wake in the morning. 

 

It would be beneficial if you write them down and add in what type of training you did that day as well. You can get super detailed here with sets, reps, exercises, etc., or simply write if the training that day was easy/restorative, medium difficulty, or hard and taxing. The idea here is to log how you are feeling inside, and ultimately develop a better intuitive guide for what you choose to energize outside. In time, explore modifying your workouts based on the magnitude of how you are feeling in relation to each question, or a combination of questions. A sample of how I would approach the following two scenarios for myself, or a client, would be the following:
 

Poor Day

 

“Am I tired today, honestly?” - YES
“Am I excited and motivated to train?” - NO
“Has my muscle and joint soreness recovered from the last session?” - YES

 

Training Modification - Either take the day fully off and go for a 20-30 minute walk outside or cut the sets in half of what you would normally do in a training session. 

 

Good Day 

 

“Am I tired today, honestly?” - NO
“Am I excited and motivated to train?” - YES
“Has my muscle and joint soreness recovered from the last session?” - YES

 

Training Modification - None, go get some!

 

I think we’ll stop here and continue back on this topic next week in Part II. We’ll look deeper into what happens when we miss out on listening to our body for too long, and the signs of overtraining begin. 

 

Oh! And drop me a line if you experiment with the three questions as a part of your morning routine and you feel like sharing : )

 

Sending good vibes for happy and healthy training, 

Mike

 

P.S. You may recall a few weeks back I sent out a brief survey to better understand what programs and education you wanted to see most. Well, I took that to heart and have been working nearly full-time since then on creating an incredible program based off of just that. You see, an overwhelming majority of responses came in seeking a kettlebell workout program with a longevity focus. Now, this gets me SUPER excited! In many of my conversations with people since then, I have really been inspired to push the limit of what’s possible to create something unique, useful, and powerful for you in this regard. Stay tuned, as you’ll be the first to know what’s coming…

In the meantime, follow me on Instagram @Mike.Salemi for more regular tips on healthy living and high performance.

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 2
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Today, I want to address something that many of us men find ourselves entangled in: the trap of "busy work."

 

Have you ever felt trapped in a never-ending cycle of busyness? I can certainly relate. In truth, more often than not, busy work only drains our precious time and energy.

 

As men, we often carry the weight of numerous responsibilities, commitments, and obligations, leaving little room for what truly matters. Unfortunately, this constant busyness can hinder our growth, strain our relationships, and leave us feeling unfulfilled.

 

What if we took a moment and explored where this pattern of busyness originated? Why do so many of us find ourselves caught in the web of busy work?

 

In my experience, one significant reason is the desire to be seen and validated by the outside world, especially the father figures in our lives. We engage in busyness to feel as if we matter, and at times it can even serve as a means of escape, a way to avoid facing parts of ourselves. 

 

Paradoxically, while we remain stuck in the same place, we can craft a narrative of victimhood, believing that no matter how hard we try, our circumstances remain stagnant in finances, relationships, health, and more.

 

Could it be that our past will continue to shape our future if we fail to uncover the ways in which certain aspects of our lives benefit from maintaining these behaviors?

 

This journey of self-discovery requires courage, my friend. The courage to be different, to step into unfamiliar territory, even when it feels scary. It's okay to acknowledge and embrace our emotions, allowing ourselves to feel fully.

 

Yesterday, I announced the early launch of my new program "Path to Inspired Action: Empowering the Authentic Man Within" - a sacred space where vulnerability becomes strength, and genuine connections are forged.

 

Imagine a life where every action you take is a true reflection of your authentic self. Picture waking up each morning with a sense of purpose that electrifies your very being. Through heartfelt conversations, embodiment practices, and personalized guidance, you will embark on a transformative journey that leads to your authentic power and the man you were destined to become.

 

Spots in the "Path to Inspired Action" program are intentionally limited. This ensures an intimate and impactful experience for each participant, fostering a supportive community that will walk alongside you on this transformative journey.

 

If you feel called to take a step forward in this way, complete the short application form.

 

I am here, humbled and honored, ready to guide you toward a life of authenticity and inspired action.

 

Your transformation awaits,

Mike

This journey of self-discovery requires courage, my friend. The courage to be different, to step into unfamiliar territory, even when it feels scary. It's okay to acknowledge and embrace our emotions, allowing ourselves to feel fully.

 

Yesterday, I announced the early launch of my new program "Path to Inspired Action: Empowering the Authentic Man Within" - a sacred space where vulnerability becomes strength, and genuine connections are forged.

 

Imagine a life where every action you take is a true reflection of your authentic self. Picture waking up each morning with a sense of purpose that electrifies your very being. Through heartfelt conversations, embodiment practices, and personalized guidance, you will embark on a transformative journey that leads to your authentic power and the man you were destined to become.

 

Spots in the "Path to Inspired Action" program are intentionally limited. This ensures an intimate and impactful experience for each participant, fostering a supportive community that will walk alongside you on this transformative journey.

 

If you feel called to take a step forward in this way, complete the short application form.

 

I am here, humbled and honored, ready to guide you toward a life of authenticity and inspired action.

 

Your transformation awaits,

Mike

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 4
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

After taking nearly six months off from regular cold plunges, today marks exactly one week of this ritual added back into my daily commitments.

 

I forgot two things:

How good I feel after
Just how challenging it is!

When I initially step into the water, it seems to always brings me face to face with a range of emotions - to name a few:

 

Fear
Anxiety
Anger
Overwhelm
Frustration

And then you have the sensations:

Cold
Tingly
Numb
Shivering 

Thinking back to my initial plunge last week, the dominant two emotions (by a landslide) were fear and anger. 

 

Anger that it was much harder than I remember, and I didn't feel prepared.

 

Anger of wanting to get out, and not giving myself that option.

 

Anger that I wouldn't be able to maintain my control and cool while my son was watching.

 

Fear of what if I made the water too cold, and something bad was going to happen.

 

It's wild to think how all the rational parts of my brain in those initial few seconds completely went away. 

 

It was pure survival, and near panic.

 

I found it hard to regulate my breath and my mind.

 

There was no calm, nasal breathing. 

 

There was no stoic Mike.

 

There was simply an internal “holy shit!"

 

It was sure humbling.

 

But then a few things happened.

 

The first was that once I passed the 30-second mark, the magnitude of the discomfort started slowly to reduce.

 

I started regaining control over my breath.

 

And every second that I stayed in, was also another second that brought my time in the water closer to completion.

 

When I got out, there was an immediate sense of accomplishment, and no doubt, a surge of energy.

 

The thing I enjoy about the cold is that it is what it is.

 

There is no pretending with it.

 

It’s not trying to be anything other than it is, and you know exactly what you’re going to get.

 

The cold always delivers.

 

I've realized that the cold is one reliable way we can train ourselves to develop a greater range and capacity to hold and experience our emotions.

 

To stay with them, and not collapse. 

 

Rather, remain heart-open, even in the discomfort.

 

This is a skill that can be developed, and what’s even more powerful is when we do so in community.

 

Of course, others can't do the work for you, or me for that matter, however, when we gather in a group, the power of the experience can grow exponentially.

 

And that is one reason that speaks to the power of aligning with other men on this path and going through the process of transformation together. 

 

In my upcoming small group, virtual program that will be running at the end of September, I will be bringing together 12 motivated men to step into this same energy.

 

Going through a process where you can meet your edges in a community of brothers is what the journey is all about.

 

It is called The Path to Inspired Action: Empowering the Authentic Man Within.

 

Right now we are taking early enrollment, and since it is a small group virtual experience, it will fill up.

 

If you are interested in learning more, click here.

 

Wishing you a badass day,

Mike

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 5
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Today, I'd like to shed light on a crucial but often overlooked element in transformational work.

 

While we often acknowledge the power of words and how they shape our stories and reality, there's more...something that goes farther than speaking a story outloud, or through a tool like journaling.

 

Enter the concept of embodiment, which is increasingly gaining recognition and significance today, especially in men's work, and for good reason.

 

It can be helpful to look at it in two ways:

Taking these more etherial concepts such as love, presence, radiance, and consciousness and having them felt through the body. It's when these traits emanate so profoundly from our bodies that others can feel them.
When a person places awareness, breath, and feeling attention deeply within their own bodies. This often happens naturally during heightened emotional states, but it's also something that can be honed through practice over time.

One key takeaway is that through embodiment work, we can truly FEEL our bodies - grounded in our feet, legs, and heart, rather than solely residing in our heads. It can open up vast opportunities for deepening our connection to ourselves, the world around us, our health, and intimate relationships.

 

This is a big reason why I've been diving into embodiment practices and studying the work of someone like John Wineland in recent years. The impact has been very special, to say the least.

 

In the upcoming 6-week group virtual program, "The Path to Inspired Action: Empowering the Authentic Man Within," we will incorporate embodiment practices each week in different ways. Without these practices, I've observed that much of this type of work tends to lose its deep and lasting impact for men.

 

Through daily practice, combining the body, mind, and heart accompanied by the breath, we can achieve more sustainable changes in our lives.

 

We have limited availability, accepting only the most motivated 12 men into this program, which will commence at the end of September.

 

Applications are already coming in, and if you feel connected to this message, I invite you to click here to learn more and start the application process.

 

Thank you for taking the time to read this email. I appreciate you and look forward to the possibility of embarking on this journey together.

 

Best regards,

Mike

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 6
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I wanted to share a recent experience that left a profound impact on me and deepened my understanding of the importance of men's work.

 

Just yesterday, I had the privilege of recording a podcast episode for the Path alongside Ted Riter, a remarkable teacher, and guide who leads one of the men's groups I am actively involved in.

 

Before we began recording, Ted and I engaged in casual conversation, getting to know each other better. Little did I know that a simple question he posed would leave me truly reflective and searching within myself for an authentic answer.

 

He asked me, "Why men's work?" It was a moment of introspection that caught me off guard, yet it held incredible significance.

 

Just before this encounter, I had been discussing my goals to simplify certain aspects of my business. In response to his question, I realized that while I could have provided a quick, almost automatic answer, there was a profound shift within me that craved deeper exploration.

 

Honoring the significance of the question and the respect I hold for Ted, I shared that I needed time to sit with his question.

 

In the days that have followed that conversation, my response remains remarkably unchanged. However, what has shifted is the depth of emotion and meaning attached to it.

 

My passion for men's work stems from experiencing and seeing it firsthand as a powerful tool for healing generations and leaving a lasting impact on the fabric of the family.

 

I have witnessed incredible transformations in men who have wholeheartedly committed themselves to this journey.

 

In more times than I can count, I've been humbled to witness family structures being revitalized, with newfound honesty, vulnerability, and responsibility.

 

Some men have embraced the role of being more present fathers, recognizing the need for emotional connection and nurturing in their relationships with their children.

 

In others, their journeys have led them to pursue new careers that align with their soul's purpose, nourishing their sense of fulfillment.

 

Many have embarked on a profound journey of self-acceptance, reconnecting with their childlike innocence and extending forgiveness to those who have deeply hurt them, as well as themselves.

 

Some have completely re-examined their relationship with food and self-care in a more positive way.

 

In all this, what I find most important is how the impact of this work extends far beyond one person.

 

Through deep introspection, unwavering commitment, and the courage to take inspired action, it is not solely our lives that undergo a profound shift, nor is it solely those in our immediate surroundings who benefit. It is the generations that came before us, and the generations that will follow, who experience the ripples of our journey.

 

This, my friend, is the Path of Inspired Action, and I am wholeheartedly dedicated to this path of supporting mem. I am reaching out to invite other like-minded men to join me in a 6-week, virtual group coaching program and accelerated dive into empowering the authentic man within.

 

Together, as a brotherhood, we can embark on a transformative journey that will amplify our impact on ourselves, our families, and generations to come.

 

If you feel a resonance with these words and wish to join alongside a group of dedicated brothers, I warmly invite you to reach out.

 

Click here to learn more about this virtual group coaching program and submit your application.

 

Thank you for taking the time to read this message. May your weekend be filled with joy and fulfillment.

 

Warm regards,

Mike

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 7
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Have you ever said, or felt the following:

 

"I am frustrated, I’m trying so hard, but the people in my life don’t really seem to see me."

 

"No matter what I do, it’s not enough."

 

"The same shitty patterns from past relationships keep happening and I don’t know what to do."

 

Want to know something?

 

In addition to having conversations each day with men, experiencing many of these exact challenges, I too, have experienced every single one of them at some point in my life.

Be curious about everything.

name: Educational Email 5
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Happy 2020! I am thrilled about the New Year and I hope you are too! My main focus in 2020 is elevating how I serve and support your goals.

 

Last week we opened a discussion around how to begin tuning in to our inner awareness to help determine the day(s) ideal for harder training, and those more suitable for rest and recovery.

 

Since then, I’ve received a handful of messages from people who found the tips very helpful, and are now starting their morning with the three simple questions I shared. SO RAD!  

 

So, overtraining...what is it exactly?

 

There are a few different definitions out there when it comes to overtraining, but the definition I’ll use here that I found clear, concise, and will touch on below comes from AceFitness: 

 

Overtraining is: constant intense training that does not provide adequate time for recovery.

 

 

Physical signs of overtraining include:

 

Decreased performance
Loss of coordination
Prolonged recovery
Elevated morning heart rate
Elevated resting blood pressure
Headaches
Loss of appetite
Muscle soreness/tenderness
Gastrointestinal disturbances
Decreased ability to ward off infection
Increased incidence of musculoskeletal injuries
Disturbed sleep patterns

 

Any of this sound familiar at one point in your life? Maybe right now?

  

Thinking back to one of the most valuable pieces of advice Holistic Health Expert and mentor, Paul Chek, shared with me during our coaching together was this - “if you can’t walk into the gym, and honestly exceed your last performance by 1-3%, then you don’t belong in there.” Simple, yet POWERFUL - especially when applied regularly.

 

 

 

These wise words he shared came from renowned Olympic Track Coach Charlie Francis. I’ve found this to be extremely valuable and is still one question I ask myself often to determine what type of training day it will be. 

 

Many of the tools I use for how to become a more balanced athlete, coach, and individual came from lessons learned while working with Paul and the education received from the Chek Institute. For this, I am incredibly grateful.

 

In my opinion, the New Year is all about learning from the past, letting go of what no longer serves us, and creating new beginnings. If we take this and think about how awareness is a prerequisite for change, then the more mindful we are, the greater the propensity for positive change to occur and last. 

 

Below are a series of questions to reflect deeper upon that can help guide your inner compass:

 

Is my sleep getting worse?
Am I experiencing nagging injuries that simply won’t heal no matter my efforts?
Am I moody often?
Is it taking longer for me to feel warmed up on a consistent basis?
Am I losing my appetite?
Am I regularly feeling stressed and beginning to store unwanted body fat?
Do I regularly feel run-down?
Do weights that used to feel light and easy, now feel hard and challenging 
Are my digestion and elimination continually poor? (example - skinny poops, never feeling complete after a bowel movement, or food feels like it sits heavily in the gut for a long time) 

 

I’d encourage you to check-in with these questions regularly. The result after 1-2 weeks can be a BIG eye-opener. 

 

If you start asking yourself any of the questions I’ve listed in Part I and/or Part II of this email, I trust that you’ll begin developing a deeper relationship with yourself, and a more intuitive approach to your fitness and performance training too! 

 

If reflecting upon questions like this is completely new, I encourage you to remember to have fun with it and remain curious. Over time your intuitive muscles will grow stronger and stronger - just like the first time you picked up a barbell or kettlebell and started deadlifting or swinging ; )

 

Lastly, if you are feeling constantly exhausted and potentially overtrained, you have lots of options. Explore going for a daily easy walk, taking a restorative yoga class (Yin and Hatha are great for this), or simply taking more dedicated total rest days a week and doing something playful with friends or family.

 

I hope this helps guide you to develop a deeper connection with your body and determine when to train, and when to back off.

 

Wishing you a wonderful New Year full of great beginnings!

 

Best,

Mike

 

P.S. 

 

If you’re reading this, you’re more than likely aware of this fact - in a balanced training program, the physical component can only be but one aspect in the larger plan. Health and longevity require consideration of the entire person and customizing a plan of action that meets your needs at any given moment.  That’s why in my next program, while it will be kettlebell workout focused, there is SO much more to it than that. I am calling it Kettlebell Lifestyle - the program that listens to you. In my next email, you’ll get an inside look at what it’s all about. 

 

In the meantime, follow me on Instagram @Mike.Salemi for more regular tips on healthy living and high performance.

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 8
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I wanted to take a moment today to emphasize the profound impact that questions can have in ANY conversation.

 

The art of asking the right questions cannot be understated, as it holds a unique power in fostering understanding, curiosity, and tends to be more disarming by nature.

 

Questions possess a feminine energy, characterized by their inviting and undefended nature. They create a space for exploration and inner discovery, allowing individuals to delve into their thoughts and emotions.

 

On the other hand, statements carry a more assertive, masculine energy, often placing us in a defensive stance.

 

I invite you to reflect on a past experience when a family member genuinely posed a question during a conversation that held great importance or an emotional charge.

 

Do you recall how that felt?

 

What emotions and thoughts arose within you?

 

In contrast, can you recall a time when that same family member simply told you what to do.

 

Did you notice how much easier or quicker it was to become defensive in the face of statements?

 

This is precisely why, in the coaching process, questions are invaluable - especially when they are from a heart-centered place, and guided skillfully.

 

While statements do have their place, particularly in consulting roles, coaching focuses on empowering individuals to arrive at their own conclusions.

 

By asking the right questions, we unlock the doors to our subconscious and unconscious minds, revealing a treasure chest of insight.

 

Allow me to share a simple practice that has aided me in processing challenges in a more productive way, rather than getting caught in the loop of dwelling on the past:

Reflect on the positive and negative consequences associated with the situation/challenge.
Consider what this situation/challenge represents to you.
Identify the most dominant feeling and sensation that arises within you.
Explore how a part of you might benefit from this behavior or challenge.

While these questions themselves can be life-changing, their potency is greatly influenced by our state of mind when answering them.

 

If we approach them when we are busy or distracted, for instance, we may not receive the answers we seek. Therefore, I recommend creating a supportive environment for introspection before diving into these inquiries.

 

This could involve:

Slow breathing for 1-5 minutes
Taking a leisurely walk 
Lighting a candle or incense
Playing calming music.

In the upcoming Path to Inspired Action Program, we harness the power of questions throughout to guide you towards your own answers.

 

I want to emphasize that my role as a coach is not to tell you what I think you should do. That would be both arrogant and disrespectful, assuming that I possess greater knowledge of how you should live your life, which I certainly do not.

 

If you are interested in embarking on a transformative journey to uncover your true desires and learn how to take continual inspired action, I encourage you to click here to learn more about the program and apply today - spots are limited to 12 total.

 

The Path to Inspired Action is a small group men's experience, conducted virtually, and incorporates powerful tools and techniques that I have honed over the years as a dedicated student and coach.

 

I wish you a fulfilling and productive day ahead,

 

Warm regards,

Mike

 

P.S.

Early discounted pricing ends at the end of July, so if you are feeling the call, I highly suggest checking it out here today.

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 9
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Clarity, as I've come to realize, is an incredibly powerful tool that can enhance every aspect of our lives – be it at work, in relationships, or when striving for better health.

 

It's like a superpower that guides us towards our true purpose and potential.

 

About three years ago, I experienced a profound shift in my life when I devoted four days to sit and reflect in the quiet of nature. During this intentional space, I examined what was working well in my life and where I felt unfulfilled.

 

It took honesty and courage to confront my self-defeating thoughts and beliefs, but it was a necessary step towards the clarity I sought.

 

With this new clarity and direction in life – creating spaces where men can embrace their true selves, vulnerabilities, and imperfections, knowing they are genuinely loved and supported, I found the answers I was looking for.

 

As I discovered, having the right people in your corner, those who offer honest and constructive feedback, can be invaluable on this journey of self-discovery.

 

The Path to Inspired Action Program is designed to provide you with the tools and guidance to gain the clarity you need to pursue your deepest aspirations. Over six weeks, we will work together in a collaborative environment to uncover what truly matters to you and how you can create positive change in your life.

 

I understand that stepping out of your comfort zone can be tough, but remember that growth often requires touching our edges. The program aims to push you forward, helping you break free from the monotony of the same old patterns and embrace inspired action.

 

If you're intrigued and ready to embrace positive change, I invite you to join me and a group of like-minded individuals on this transformative journey.

 

The program commences on October 1st, and early discounted pricing is available until July 31st.

 

Take the first step towards a clearer and more purposeful life by clicking on this link to learn more and apply for the Path to Inspired Action Program.

 

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions or would like to know more about the program. I'm here to support you on this empowering path.

 

Wishing you clarity and inspiration,

Mike

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 10
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I believe that within each man lies a dormant force of power, wisdom, integrity, and direction—a sleeping giant waiting to be awakened.

 

As men, we all possess this potential, and it's essential to recognize its existence within us. When this sleeping giant stirs, incredible transformations occur, allowing us to tap into our true capabilities and lead more fulfilling lives.

 

At times, however, we might find ourselves slipping into comfort zones, causing the giant to retreat into its cave. We may feel overly relaxed, unenthusiastic, and disconnected from our purpose. Recognizing these signs can be the first step towards change.

 

The sleeping giant is recognizable when:

We become too comfortable and resist challenges.
Our energy and motivation feel diminished.
We spend excessive time on social media and entertainment.
Our physical well-being and intimate relationships are affected.
We avoid meaningful conversations for fear of conflict.
We struggle with setting healthy boundaries.

Despite being dormant, it's crucial to remember that a giant still resides within us, ready to awaken and empower us to:

Embrace challenges and take calculated risks.
Prioritize our purpose and values above all else.
Honor our commitments and be reliable to others.
Cultivate physical strength and resilience.
Experience deep and meaningful connections.
Engage in radical self-honesty.
Lead by example and inspire those around us.
Appreciate our achievements and worth.
Take responsibility for our actions and their consequences.
Release trivial concerns and forgive ourselves and others.

The sleeping giant is a powerful force that resides within all of us just waiting to come alive and transform into the wild man, as poet Robert Bly described in his book Iron John.

 

The journey to Inspired Action involves awakening this potential within ourselves, acknowledging the essential aspects of our being, and rising to embrace our true selves.

 

As we head on this path of self-discovery and growth, we also unconsciously grant others the permission to explore their own hidden potential, creating a supportive environment for personal development and transformation.

 

If you resonate with the idea of awakening the sleeping giant inside and embarking on a journey of self-discovery, I invite you to join our upcoming small group virtual coaching program, limited to just 12 men, commencing on October 1st.

 

Early discounted pricing for the program, The Path to Inspired Action is available until July 31st.

 

Click here to learn more about the program and secure your spot today.

 

I genuinely hope to see you there, ready to unleash your untapped potential.

 

Best regards,

Mike

  • Honor our commitments and be reliable to others.
  • Cultivate physical strength and resilience.
  • Experience deep and meaningful connections.

  • Release trivial concerns and forgive ourselves and others.

The journey to Inspired Action involves awakening this potential within ourselves, acknowledging the essential aspects of our being, and rising to embrace our true selves.

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 12
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Over the past 4 years, I've incorporated a simple practice into starting my day that has made a significant impact on how I feel and approach life. It's become my go-to morning "bread and butter", and I'm excited to invite you to experience its benefits too.

 

This morning routine is easy to follow, takes approximately 10 minutes, and requires no special skills or equipment.

 

All you need is the commitment to yourself and this practice, which I've found to be incredibly rewarding each time I perform it and thus create a win to start the day.

 

Click here to access the routine.

 

As men, we often face the challenge of not feeling our best first thing in the morning. We might wake up feeling tight, stiff, and lacking energy, making it challenging to engage with the day ahead.

 

However, I've discovered that by integrating a few essential activities into our mornings, we can experience a remarkable shift in our physical and mental state:

Warm up the body (it's easier than you might think).
Move the spine (the spine is KING)
Get the synovial fluid moving to lubricate our joints - imagine you're "greasing the hinges."
Open up the lungs through focused breathwork.
Become aware of your positioning and posture.
Engage and wake up the abdominals - for improved digestion, trunk stability, and strength

To help you get started on this transformative journey, I'm sharing the exact morning routine from my Kettlebell Lifestyle Program.

 

Click here to access the routine.

 

You can find this entire program incorporated as one element in the Elite Package of The Path to Inspired Action. 

 

By consistently following this routine, you'll notice improvements in various aspects of how your body-mind performs.

 

Pay attention to how these areas are impacted: increasing energy levels, alertness and focus, how your joints feel more "greased" and agile, and your confidence and readiness to face the day elevates. You might also find that you can handle life's challenges with greater ease and resilience.

 

I'd love to hear about your experience with this morning routine, so feel free to share your thoughts with me by responding to this email.

 

And speaking of The Path to Inspired Action, we're currently offering early discounted pricing for three more days until July 31st.

 

Don't miss this opportunity to join the program and be a part of a group of dedicated men committed to self-development and contributing to each other's success.

 

Click here to learn more and apply today.

 

The applicants we've received so far have been exceptional! Men from all different stages in their self-development journey, all united by a shared willingness and commitment to growth.

 

If you resonate with this energy and want to make a meaningful change in your life, I encourage you to fill out an application and schedule a discovery and coaching call with me.

 

Let's rock this thing together!

 

I hope you find the morning routine gift helpful and that you'll apply it in your daily life. Remember, small changes in our routines can lead to significant transformations.

 

Best regards,

Mike

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement 13
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Whether it be a deep meditation, retreat, plant medicine journey, or something else, we are often told, or assume, that transformation only happens during the experience itself.

 

However, I strongly believe that the journey to transformation begins long before the actual event and continues well after it's over.

 

Allow me to explain why...

 

Transformation is a deep, profound process, and it starts from that pivotal moment when we decide to take a step towards change.

 

It's that first conscious step that sets everything in motion. And to maximize the potential of any transformative experience, I've come to understand four crucial components:

Preparation: Set an intention, and engage in the imagination process. This could come through meditation, being in nature, journaling, mandala art, etc.
Effort: Honest, heartfelt effort is what propels us forward on this path. It's about committing fully with heart, body, and mind
Courage: Especially when faced with challenges or fears, having the courage to continue on is what unlocks true growth and self-discovery.
Surrender: Being patient and open to the unfolding of the experience allows us to embrace life and the experience more fully.

And there is ONE more...

 

One that cannot be understated, and that is support - especially a solid group of brothers who have got your back.

 

That's why I'm excited about the kick off of The Path to Inspired Action, starting October 1st - a 6-10 week virtual coaching program exclusively designed for men who are ready to embark on a life-changing journey of transformation.

 

In less than 72 hours, the early price for this program will end, and I don't want you to miss out on this opportunity to take aligned, inspired action.

 

By participating in this Program you will:

Uncover and overcome the barriers that have been holding you back from reaching your highest potential.
Nurture neglected aspects of yourself that need attention and care.
Release stagnant energy and create a positive flow in your life.
Gain clarity on the necessary actions to move forward in life with alignment and inspiration.
Receive honest and valuable feedback from other participants.
Connect with a supportive group of like-minded individuals who can become your new friends and brothers on this journey.

Click here to apply and embark on this life-changing path - let's take this first step together!

 

I'm looking forward to seeing you in The Path to Inspired Action program!

 

Best regards,

Mike

 

P.S.

In my last email I shared a free gift with you - the morning routine I've used regularly  for the last ~4 years. It takes less than 10 minutes to do and is one of the routines in my program Kettlebell Lifestyle, which is included in the Elite Package of The Path to Inspired Action.

 

To get my morning routine for free, click here.

name: Bulgarian Bag Email
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In recent years, the fitness industry has seen a surge in the term "movement," largely signifying a shift from machine-based, isolated workouts to more functional training approaches.

 

Movement is about integrating diverse physical activities that respect real-life motions, emphasizing core strength, flexibility, balance, and coordination - just to name a few.

 

To be movement-minded in my opinion, means focusing on holistic fitness routines that enhance overall functionality, adaptability, and agility for better everyday challenges.

 

If you share this mindset, you'll understand the significance of the Bulgarian Bag, a unique tool that amplifies your capabilities beyond typical gym routines.

 

However, owning a Bulgarian Bag isn't enough; like with anything skill based, solid guidance is key.

 

This is a big reason I've invested so much time learning directly from Ivan Ivanov, former Olympian and Olympic coach, to bring you authentic expertise.

 

Witnessing and being a part of Ivan's coaching first hand is inspiring, to say the least, and I'm committed to sharing both the tool and the essential education behind it.

 

My journey with the Bag combines Ivan's teachings with my passion for longevity, and holistic high performance.

 

If you're intrigued, I invite you to explore three upcoming opportunities to work with me and embrace a unique experience.

 

 #1 Bulgarian Bag Championships 

On September 23rd, in Boise, Idaho for those individuals who love pushing their boundaries and are seeking community in their fitness pursuits, check out the upcoming Suples Bulgarian Bag Championships. If you are interested in learning more and competing, click here.

Note, registration closes August 12th.

 

I will be personally coaching a small group at the Championships. If you would like to receive programming, and coaching as a part of Team Salemi at the competition, please reply to this email notifying me of your interest. 

#2 Bulgarian Bag LVL I Certification at ONNIT! 




 

On August 26th, in Austin, Texas I will be collaborating with Onnit Gym, and various industry leaders (like Primal Swolger!), to hold this one-day immersive experience.  If you're a fitness enthusiast who desires to master an innovative training tool that challenges your body in unconventional ways, this immersive certification offers the techniques and insights you need to revitalize your routine and achieve new heights of performance.

Click here to sign up.




#3 [30-Day] Bulgarian Bag Program: Waitlist

The eagerly anticipated 30-day online Bulgarian Bag program is on the horizon. Designed for individuals who prioritize strength and movement without spending copious time training, this program will empower you to achieve your goals on your terms.

 

My aim is for the program to be released in late fall, you can sign up below to be notified of progress and exclusive pricing for being on the waitlist.

Click here to sign up.

 

In closing, these 3 opportunities are meticulously crafted to cater to the aspirations of those who seek innovation, community, and tangible results from their fitness pursuits.

 

Committed to your success,

 

Mike Salemi

name: Educational Email 6
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Let's be real. 

 

Walking into the gym feeling like a determined warrior every session just isn't the way things go. 

 

Heck, it's life.

 

But, what if there was a way when you're feeling less than your best, that you could get in the gym and know you're supporting your body's resources, instead of draining them?

 

What exactly might training like this look like?

 

 

In my prior two emails, we covered “when to train and when to back off.” Today we'll go one step further... I'm going to teach you a kettlebell and bodyweight energizer that you can use anytime in situations like the one I mentioned above. You can do this at home, the park, the gym - anywhere. 

 

Should I also add that it won't take you more than 15 minutes to complete??

 

Here it is:

 

Kettlebell Snatch Energizer (Super-set)

Single Arm Kettlebell Snatch - Forward Lunge Combo
Spinal Roll Down with Chest Opener

 

Weight: Light 

 

Reps: 5 Left / 5 Right + 5 Spinal Roll Downs with Chest Opener

 

Rest: None (back-to-back exercise supersets)

 

Duration: 5-8 minutes

*Remember to get in a quick warm-up in first

 

To help your success with this workout-work in combination, I just created and posted a nearly 8-minute video on my Instagram TV covering this. Here is the link

 

When you attempt the kettlebell snatch-lunge, if it feels too advanced for where you're currently at, don’t worry. Here are two other options to explore:

 

Regression I (Intermediate Level)

Single Arm Kettlebell Clean - Forward Lunge Combo
Spinal Roll Down with Chest Opener

 

Regression II (Beginner/Intermediate Level)

Single Arm Kettlebell Swings
Spinal Roll Down with Chest Opener

 

Weight, Reps, Rest & Duration: Same as prescribed for the Snatch

 

This concept of working in I feel is paramount to experiencing high levels of performance and well being. In a session like this (while it is a hybrid type of training), the idea is still to cultivate energy in the body and feel uplifted afterward.

While journaling yesterday, exploring what comes to mind when I think of an unstoppable man was the theme. And wow, I was surprised how much poured out!

 

Here is that entry...

 

"There is NO stopping a man who…

 

Is fiercely driven by his purpose.

 

Engages in regular honest self-evaluation.

 

Acts in service of his family.

 

Trusts his gut and intuition.

 

Lives from his heart.

 

Rain or shine shows up.

 

Maintains a high standard of integrity.

 

Listens intently.

 

Receives council from other wise men.

 

Is meticulous with how he speaks to himself.

 

Is physically strong and fit.

 

Knows how to regulate his own nervous system.

 

Breathes into his balls.

 

Communicates clearly

 

Recognizing when he may collapse, he still makes a heart-felt effort to remain open.

 

Takes ownership and responsibility for the life he is living and creating moment to moment.

 

Recognizes vulnerability and emotional capacity is a superpower for growth and connection.

 

Admits when he’s made a mistake, and is not too proud to apologize.

 

Hold his partner close, through the depths of her emotions.

 

Is committed.

 

Loves fully, and unapologetically.

 

Has learned that he doesn’t have to do it all himself.

 

Plays all out."

 

Sending love and respect for a great rest of your week,

Mike

name: Educational Email 7
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

In last week’s email, the focus was placed on an energizing workout-work in combo designed to increase your health and vitality. I hope you loved trying it out!

 

Now, if it’s one element that relates closely to both working out and working in, it is this week’s topic on breathing. 

 

Breathing is a critical factor in building health and high performance. With proper breathing, we can energize the body, remove toxins, pump the discs of the spine, and much more. 

 

Although there are many breathing strategies, each with a specific purpose and intent, the one I will discuss here is that of a more natural, relaxed breathing rhythm. With it, we aim to activate the parasympathetic nervous system - responsible for rest, repair, and digestion functions in the body. 

 

 

 

In this video, former USA Taekwondo National Team Member, TJ Curry, meets up with me in the gym. We touch on various aspects related to the mechanics of breathing, specifically focused around the diaphragm - a key respiratory and spinal stabilizing muscle.

 

Additional note on performance -  the middle back (thoracic spine) plays a significant role in healthy shoulder function during overhead lifting. Faulty breathing, which can be coupled with a stiff middle spine, can negatively impact overhead movements. Retrain your breathing, and you may likely see a surprising improvement in these lifts as a result. 

 

Helpful Tips:

 

During inhalation, the belly rises and expands
During exhalation, the belly descends and narrows
The first ⅔ of the breath should  initiate from the belly
Breathe in and out through the nose (this excites parasympathetic nerve endings, responsible for putting us into a more restful and relaxed state)
The breath should not feel forced

 

If you are having difficulty performing a quality, effortless inhalation-exhalation cycle in the standing position, I suggest taking your time with the following sequence below. 

 

Progressions

 

Laying on Your Back
Seated
Half-Kneeling
Standing

 

 

Do this daily and spend 3-7 days working through each progression. I suggest 20-30 slow breaths for approximately 4 seconds on inhalation, and 4 seconds on exhalation when starting out.

 

I hope you enjoyed today’s email on breathing. By retraining your breathing rhythm in this way, not only will your stress levels reduce, energy increase, but also your deep core muscles will be primed for all your loaded lifting movements.

 

Wishing you a wonderful day!

Mike

 

P.S.

Last week I shared a neat gift with you - a downloadable PDF plus 10+ minute instructional video titled, “3 Biggest Kettlebell Snatch Mistakes.” In case you missed it, click here. Once you grab yours, you’ll also be notified of the upcoming release of my new Kettlebell Lifestyle workout program! : )))


Click here to get the guide ( and video )
https://programs.mikesalemi.io/get-guide-and-tutorial-video

 

Resources:

1. Calais-Germain, Blandine. Anatomy of Breathing, Eastland Press, Inc. 2006

2. CHEK Institute and Dan Hellman. Heavy Breathing -The Science and Practice of Respiration During Resistance Training, IDEA Personal Training Institute, Feb. 25-28, 2010

name: Path to Inspired Action: Announcement V2
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Have you ever experienced that sweet gratification of knocking out tasks or achieving a certain goal?

 

It's a damn good feeling, isn't it?

 

For many of us, checking off those to-dos is a source of motivation and a sense of accomplishment.

 

I frequently say that as men, when we lay our heads down on a pillow at night, if we accomplish our duties, roles, and commitments according to OUR unique scoreboard, it is a good indicator that it was a solid day.

 

However, it is critical to recognize that executing tasks needs to be accompanied by one key thing - discernment.

 

I know this to be true because this is something I personally have struggled with for years.

 

I used to hide in tasking and busyness.

 

And it wasn't until I worked with a coach that he pointed out this repetitive pattern I had been living out for years.

 

 

At this new stage in life with a family, working tirelessly and non-stop hours, I've realized has greater consequences.

 

A big lesson came from this...

 

Discernment of which tasks are essential to engage with on a daily basis is critical.

 

Questions you can ask yourself:

Are these tasks I engage with truly moving me forward in life in a meaningful and noticeable way?
Are they contributing to increased revenue in my businesses?
Are they giving me more quality time with my family?
Are they enhancing my overall health, vitality, and physical performance?
Why are they important to me in the first place?

I understand the allure of staying busy, but it's a continual process for both men and individuals I support to not merely complete tasks but to choose them wisely.

 

Failure to exercise discernment may result in finding yourself in the same position 1 year from now, 3 years from now, or even 5 years from now.

 

It often takes a step back from the daily grind to recognize that we've become so immersed in it that we've neglected to seek a higher perspective and fresh air.

 

The true value lies in using your time judiciously, ensuring that every minute spent brings you closer to the things that yield what really matters, such as freedom, connection, and vitality.

 

This is where the GOLD is.

 

In my upcoming Path to Inspired Action Program, we will do just this.

 

Over the course of 6-10 weeks, we will unearth the hidden aspects of yourself that may be holding you back. With newfound awareness and the support of a community of like-minded men, you can take the needed aligned and inspired action in your life.

 

This program combines group online experiences, along with one-on-one sessions to guide you on a journey of action and empowerment.

 

Join us starting Monday, October 2nd.

 

To learn more about the program, apply, and secure your spot, please click here.

 

Best regards,

Mike

 

P.S. Stay tuned for a special gift coming this Monday - a specific breathwork protocol that has been a game-changer for me. Whether it's the start of your day, during travel, or whenever you find yourself in a rut, this practice can help you manage overwhelm, anxiety, and overall stress. I can't wait to share it with you!
