name: Path to Inspired Action: Breathwork Gift
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Throughout my journey, I've explored various breathwork techniques and embodiment practices that have been profound tools for my healing and growth.

 

I’ve used breathwork over the years for various reasons, some of which include:

 

Performance
General Health
Mindfulness
Grounding
Emotional Release
Altering States
And more...

Depending on the specific objective of the practice, elements like the intention, mechanics, pacing, duration, etc., can all vary.

 

As mentioned, the application of breathwork in my life, as well as in the lives of the people I work with, has been deeply transformative.

 

Somatic breathwork, in particular, stands out as one powerful modality that can help release stress and pressure, connect us deeply with our emotions, express ourselves authentically, and restore us to inner calm.

 

It can bring about an opening, relief, and a balancing of the nervous system that empowers you to create a sense of safety within your body - which, in my opinion, is a prerequisite to any form of healing.

 

With this in mind, while the Somatic Release Breathwork I incorporate into my programs and in-person experiences is a deep ceremonial process, there is a distilled, much shorter version that you can use whenever you need to release stress, gain clarity, and re-harmonize your nervous system on a daily basis.

 

As a gift, I am including this video that you can follow along with.

 

Feel free to customize this practice by adjusting the number of breaths. However, I find it works best if you maintain the alternating pattern of mouth breathing (up-regulating) and nasal breathing (down-regulating).

 

I will share some tips at the beginning of the video and will include a few more below.

 

Breathwork Protocol Format:

Set an intention.
Perform 30 clearing breaths (open mouth, faster pace).
Hold your breath (moderate duration at the top of the inhale).
Follow with 30 calming breaths (nasal breathing, slower pace).
Hold your breath (moderate duration at the bottom of the exhale).

In terms of mechanics, the breathing should occur in three dimensions, expanding front and back, laterally (sideways) in the belly and ribcage, and finally with some elevation in the chest at the end.

 

The breath should be smooth and circular, meaning it flows seamlessly from inhale to exhale - except during the short breath hold (if you have any blood pressure issues, I suggest omitting the holds).

 

I recommend doing this practice while seated or lying down. If you feel dizzy, slow down the pace of your breath. Avoid standing up quickly afterward, and gradually exit the practice.

 

Journaling for a few minutes afterward can be very supportive too.

 

This practice is intended for daily/anytime use and is not meant to open up a deep internal/emotional process. However, be aware that certain emotions may surface as breathing is powerful, so please listen to the wisdom of your body and navigate this practice mindfully. Proceed at your own pace and engage at a level that feels supportive to you on that given day.

 

Wishing you a fantastic rest of your week and I hope you love this!

Mike

 

P.S.

If you're interested in delving deeper into breathwork and embodiment practices, consider joining my upcoming men's virtual program, The Path to Inspired Action, as well as the Men of Movement: Initiation Experience on Nov. 10-12th.

 

The group Path to Inspired Program begins on Monday, October 2nd, and we have already assembled an exceptional group of men for the program. If you're ready to level up, be supported, and support other men on their journey, now is the time to join. Click here for more info and to hop on a call with me today.

name: Path to Inspired Action: V2.3
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

If you're like me, sometimes living out perfectionistic tendencies is a double-edged sword. In some ways, it can feel incredibly stressful, like life requires a ton of self-responsibility to do things the "right way", and at other times it can indeed be a superpower.

 

Today, we'll be unpacking the perfectionist's dilemma...so get ready ; )

 

In my personal experience and coaching around perfectionism, I've found understanding the Ennegram to be incredibly helpful. The Ennegram encompasses 9 distinct personality types that we all possess to varying degrees, based on our life experiences since childhood.

 

Within these 9 types, there's one known as our Core Type, which serves as the driving force behind our unconscious motivations in life. This core type is fueled by a fundamental fear, belief, and desire, 

 

It's the lens through which we view ourselves, and the world.

 

One of the biggest insights I've gained and use in my coaching practice to determine someone's unique psychological fingerprint (using the Inner Compass System), is that how we draw upon the other eight types serves as coping or compensation strategies to manage the fundamental fear, belief, and desire of our Core Type.

 

Now that we've touched on a few Enneagram basics, let's return to the Perfectionist's dilemma.

 

The Perfectionist corresponds to Type 1 in the Enneagram system, also known as the Improver, Fixer, Moralist, and Reformer, to name a few.

 

As with all types, there are inherent pros and cons (light and shadow), with varying levels of functionality that we shift between throughout the day, depending on life's challenges and our current state.

 

Generally speaking, individuals who lead as a Core Type 1 are conscientious, responsible, disciplined, orderly, and serious.

 

Their motivations are as follows:

 

FEAR of making mistakes, being imperfect, or being "bad".
DESIRE to be good, virtuous, and have integrity.
CORE BELIEF centered around being good or okay if they do what's right (according to their defined values, and inner code).

 

At their best, they are discerning, wise, principled, and fair, but they can sometimes fall into traps of rigidity, perfectionism, criticism, and judgment (of self/others)

 

I have a deep connection with this Enneagram type because I've learned to get my needs met (physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual) by leading with it at my core.

 

While the Inner Compass System, and the Enneagram, offer far more depth than I can share here today, even a basic understanding is incredibly empowering for personal growth and healing.

 

One thing I found incredibly intriguing is that approximately 80%+ of those who've joined the Path to Inspired Action Program have Type 1 as their Core Type! 

 

Everyone entering the program takes the Inner Compass assessment as part of the pre-course work, followed by a one-on-one interpretation session with me. 

 

An important thing to note is that this system is NOT meant to put you in a box. In fact, it's meant to uncover the box that you're already in, and help empower your way out - especially when you feel stuck, unfulfilled, less than vital, and simply challenged in life.

 

In many one-on-one interpretations over the past year, people have shared it was one of the biggest game changers for obtaining powerful new awareness of themselves, how to get out of their own way, and move forward in life intentionally. 

 

This personalized information can illuminate numerous blind spots as you journey toward becoming the best version of yourself.

 

If this resonates with you or if you're seeking to explore the drivers behind your struggles, communication style, relationships, financial outlook, and more, I highly recommend my men's virtual group Program starting on October 2nd—The Path to Inspired Action.

 

While the program is open to anyone, and there is a defined structure, I will be tailoring it to the individuals who join.

 

We will use tools such as: Somatic Breathwork, Storywork, Inner Compass Assessment, embodiment practices, shamanic techniques, and more, through this 7-11 week program (depending on your chosen path).

 

If you're interested, please note that enrollment closes this Sunday. To jump on this opportunity, schedule a free call with me today. I'm accepting applications for review until Saturday evening, with final interview calls taking place on Sunday.

 

If this sparks your interest and you desire support alongside other men in discovering your true self, achieving greater internal freedom, and living the life you most desire, I'm here for you.

 

Let's rock this transformative journey together!

 

Click here to apply today - less than 48 hours left!

 

Warm regards,

Mike

name: Leadership
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

When we think about leadership, it's easy to picture individuals who possess those natural qualities that seem to make leading effortless. They're the ones who have a clear vision, aren't afraid to speak their minds when it counts, and support their team unconditionally.

 

But here's the thing – and while there are those that may disagree, to be a leader, a guide, it is a skill you can nurture and develop over time, no matter where you start.

 

Even if you're an introvert, you can step up and become an incredible leader.

 

However, let's be real for a moment: being a leader isn't all sunshine and rainbows. It comes with a hefty dose of responsibility and ownership.

 

Sometimes, it might feel like life isn't fair, especially when you're tackling tasks or conversations that no one else wants to touch. But that right there is a fundamental part of what leadership is all about.

 

What you may not already know, is that you are already a leader - and it all begins from within.

It starts with knowing yourself, working on yourself, and digging deep to understand the people around you on a more human level. It's about learning how to guide and inspire effectively.

 

Leading from within – or as we tend to say in our Men for Movement retreat experiences, "Leading From The Middle" – isn't just a role. It's a way of life.

 

When us men lead with heart, and hold ourselves accountable, even when we feel like collapsing, that's the real call to leadership. From that place you will lead those around you in a more potent way.

 

If you're looking to level up your leadership game alongside your fellow brothers, our next retreat is happening from November 10 -12th in beautiful Mount Shasta, California.

 

Click here to apply today.

 

I can't wait to have you with us on this incredible journey with us.

 

Love & Respect,

Mike

text:
Hi {first_name},

 

15 years ago if you’d ask me if I’d ever imagine myself in the Middle East about to teach to a group of motivated trainers on health and performance, I’d say heck no!

 

Yet, here I am at TFB Fitness in Kuwait, reflecting on what a wild ride it’s been...

 

             Mike Salemi ( 20 years old )

 

This picture dates back to when I was the co-head strength and conditioning coach for the Division 1 Men’s Tennis Program at Santa Clara University.

 

I remember this being a BIG step for me. I was nervous, excited, humbled and honored all at the same time. 

 

I recall studying non-stop, at times falling asleep at my desk, reading books on performance training. I put so much pressure on myself to do everything I could to add value to the team and help ensure they were prepared physically to perform to their potential.

 

The team put in solid work that year and deserved their results, as they outperformed their best ranking to date.

 

I am so proud of that group and grateful they trusted me as their coach. I learned a tremendous amount about myself in the process and what it takes to be an effective coach.

 

If you’re reading this email, it means you are trusting my knowledge and experience in some way to support your health and performance goals. For this, I am incredibly grateful…it means a lot. 

 

This is also why I literally have goosebumps about sharing this next announcement with you. 

 

Today, on January 18th, the next phase in my journey has begun, and I’d love for you to be a part of it.

Build a body that will perform and last for decades to come with Kettlebell Lifestyle.

With you in health and happiness!

name: Bulgarian Bag Pre-Order 1
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

I'm excited to share the story behind the Bulgarian Bag today and why being a part of its lineage is truly something special—one that sets it apart from the rest...

 

The Origin Story

The journey of the Bulgarian Bag began in Marquette, Michigan, 15+ years ago where Ivan Ivanov, while coaching at the Olympic Training Center Campus for Wrestlers, sought a unique training tool that could help his needs as a coach.

 

His vision was ambitious - he needed:

To train his athletes in a way, functionally, that no other tool could - suitable for multi-pattern and plane movements used in wrestling
To build high levels of muscular endurance
A versatile implement that would not damage floors/mats
Something that could be used with little to no set-up, both during and after practice
A way to foster team camaraderie and competitiveness while conditioning
A tool that allowed his creativity to be unleashed and design innovative, fun, and challenging workout protocols

 

The result?

 

A testament to Ivan's dedication, the Bulgarian Bag emerged as not just a product, but a culmination of blood, sweat, and tears. Ivan not only created a revolutionary piece of fitness and performance equipment but also developed time-tested training methodologies.

A Family Business

Suples isn't just a global company, it is a passionate family business. Having experienced the dynamics of a family-run business myself for much of my life, I understand the commitment and sacrifices that go into every endeavor.

 

There are no fixed working hours; it's about showing up, doing what's necessary, and supporting each other to provide the best for our customers.

 

Suples stands out as one of the most innovative companies I've had the pleasure of working with. Representing them globally and integrating my personal experience with a tool like the Bulgarian Bag fills me with pride.

 

The Authenticity Factor

While there may be knock-off bags out there, there is only one Original Bulgarian Bag. Crafted in Bulgaria at their factory run by Ivan's brother, these bags carry with them not just the product, but the essence of a culture steeped in human potential and teamwork.

 

More Than a Product

The Bulgarian Bag is not just a fitness tool; it's an entryway into a rich history of individuals striving for performance, health, and fitness together. Being a part of this story and lineage means something profound.

 

NEWS: 30-Day Bulgarian Bag Online Program Is Coming!

I'm thrilled to announce that my long-awaited Bulgarian Bag Online Program, Athleticism for Life, will be available for pre-order at a big discounted price starting next week on Black Friday.

 

This Suples Approved Program is a result of many hours of dedication and will be accessible for you to start training on January 1st. 

 

To secure your pre-order at a special rate, make sure to act before Cyber Monday when the cart closes.

 

While I will be sending more emails as we get closer, the best way to make sure you don't miss out, is to get on the waitlist by clicking here.

 

If you're eager to get your hands on a Bulgarian Bag and gear up for the January 1st access, use the code TEAMSALEMI10 by ordering here (note, this code will only work for US orders).

 

Let's gooooooo!

 

Yours In Strength,

Mike




P.S.

name: Form Welcome
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

Congratulations on starting Kettlebell Lifestyle! This program is designed to be different from most training plans. Usually, most plans are exclusively focused on the sets and reps, but if you want your whole body to be strong and feel great, you’ll need more. 

 

While working muscles hard can deliver clear feedback in the form of sore muscles, it isn't the most important thing. In fact, the more important progress comes when you learn to feel the effect of your training on your energy levels, movement abilities, level of fitness, and overall health.  

 

Here are some of the features of Kettlebell Lifestyle (KBL) designed to help you improve performance by learning to notice and cultivate what makes sustainable performance possible. 

 

Onboarding Questions  

These 12 questions will place you into the appropriate level. Pay attention to the questions because they are written to help you gain awareness around your current level. Then keep your eye out for the weekly bonus material sent by email each week. Some of the bonus topics are sure to address issues the onboarding questions bring up.

 

*Note about shift workers and trainers

Shift workers will likely need to use the Self-Guided route due to their schedule and the demands of shift work on your body as opposed to immersion. 
Trainers with high levels of physical experience may prefer the Self Guided route as opposed to Immersion.

 

Daily Training Readiness Assessment

Each day you’ll be prompted to answer 5 questions that gauge how ready your body is for the stress of training. The importance of adjusting your training based on how your body feels is one of the biggest keys to longevity. 

 

Your answers will customize the volume (namely sets) of your training for the day. 

 

*Note:

The personalized changes for your training plan show up in the written workout located under the guided workout video.

 

The table below reflects 100% volume:


 

The table below reflects reduced volume by reducing the number of sets:


 

The video workout will always shows the workout with 100% volume for someone who was feeling great that day. Look at your chart and follow your personalized workout. 

 

If your answers show that training would be a detrimental stress for your body, the chart will tell you to suggest to other alternatives such as: Working In, Stretching, or a Total Test Day. But don’t fear! That day’s workout will show up next time and you’ll pick up without missing anything. 

 

What to expect over the next 9 weeks:

Bonus videos will be emailed each week for 8 weeks
The Onramp is purposely designed to strengthen muscles that are often weak AND gently prepare your body so that you start the program with an EXCESS of energy. Resist the urge to push hard during the Onramp! 
3 following phases will build: foundations,  then layer in more dynamic movements and improved conditioning, and finally end with performance. 

 

What to do when you finish:

This program is designed so you can go through it again and again. In addition, you’ll be emailed a resource toward the end of the first 9 weeks that will guide you through adapting KBL to specific goals such as improving cardio, strength, or muscle mass. 

 

Reach out at this email address or on social media if you have any questions.
 

Enjoy how you feel when you train intentionally!

-Mike

While working muscles hard can deliver clear feedback in the form of sore muscles, it isn't the most important thing. In fact, the more important progress comes when you learn to feel the effect of your training on your energy levels, movement abilities, level of fitness, and overall health.  

 

Here are some of the features of Kettlebell Lifestyle (KBL) designed to help you improve performance by learning to notice and cultivate what makes sustainable performance possible. 

 

Onboarding Questions  

These 12 questions will place you into the appropriate level. Pay attention to the questions because they are written to help you gain awareness around your current level. Then keep your eye out for the weekly bonus material sent by email each week. Some of the bonus topics are sure to address issues the onboarding questions bring up.

 

*Note about shift workers and trainers

  • Shift workers will likely need to use the Self-Guided route due to their schedule and the demands of shift work on your body as opposed to immersion. 
  • Trainers with high levels of physical experience may prefer the Self Guided route as opposed to Immersion.

 

Daily Training Readiness Assessment

Each day you’ll be prompted to answer 5 questions that gauge how ready your body is for the stress of training. The importance of adjusting your training based on how your body feels is one of the biggest keys to longevity. 

 

Your answers will customize the volume (namely sets) of your training for the day. 

 

*Note:

The personalized changes for your training plan show up in the written workout located under the guided workout video.

 

The table below reflects 100% volume:


 

The table below reflects reduced volume by reducing the number of sets:


 

The video workout will always shows the workout with 100% volume for someone who was feeling great that day. Look at your chart and follow your personalized workout. 

 

If your answers show that training would be a detrimental stress for your body, the chart will tell you to suggest to other alternatives such as: Working In, Stretching, or a Total Test Day. But don’t fear! That day’s workout will show up next time and you’ll pick up without missing anything. 

 

What to expect over the next 9 weeks:

  • Bonus videos will be emailed each week for 8 weeks
  • The Onramp is purposely designed to strengthen muscles that are often weak AND gently prepare your body so that you start the program with an EXCESS of energy. Resist the urge to push hard during the Onramp! 
  • 3 following phases will build: foundations,  then layer in more dynamic movements and improved conditioning, and finally end with performance. 

 

What to do when you finish:

This program is designed so you can go through it again and again. In addition, you’ll be emailed a resource toward the end of the first 9 weeks that will guide you through adapting KBL to specific goals such as improving cardio, strength, or muscle mass. 

 

Reach out at this email address or on social media if you have any questions.
 

Enjoy how you feel when you train intentionally!

-Mike

text:
Hi {first_name}!

 

Thank you for joining the Kettlebell Lifestyle 5 Day Morning Routine Challenge! I'm so stoked to share this with you, it's going to be incredible!

 

Here's what you can do to get the most out of your experience: 

 

MOST IMPORTANT: Add this email to your contact list so you don’t miss any important details heading into and during the challenge.

A preview of each day
Reminders
Special updates on prizes

I look forward to seeing you in the live meetings and interacting with you in the group.

 

Wishing you a wonderful day!

Mike Salemi

name: Thank you for joining
text:
Hi {first_name}!

 

Thank you for joining the 15 Minute Feel Good Challenge!

 

Today most of us are spending much more time at home. With that in mind, finding (and more importantly starting) practices that improve our quality of life in a short amount of time are VERY needed, and I want to help.

 

 

While a picture of my pup Basil has nothing officially to do with this challenge, who doesn't love puppies and WOW can being around animals help elevate our mood and help make us feel good!  

 

 

 

 

 

 

Here's what you can do to get the most out of your challenge experience: 

 

IMPORTANT: 

1. Join the private Facebook Group where you’ll be able to watch and follow along live (recordings will be kept in the group for later viewing).

2. Add this email to your contact list so you don’t miss any important details.

3. Block out 30 minutes (the additional time is for discussion and any teaching components that will happen on certain days before the 15-minute routine begins) 

4. Show up for the live calls on Facebook starting October 22nd at 9amPST / 12pm EST

5. If you know anyone who would be interested in joining, please send them over to www.kettlebelllifestyle.com/feelgoodchallenge.

 

Once the challenge begins, you can expect the following emails so you are prepared:

A preview of each day
Reminders on any light (fun!) homework that will be shared
Special updates on prizes
Tips on how to continue to use what you learn after you finish the challenge

 

I truly believe that in just 15 minutes of focused effort you CAN create and build momentum to embody doing “less but better”. This will help you build your mental and physical strength and openness that we all need nowadays to thrive. 

 

I look forward to seeing you in the Facebook Group!

 

Wishing you all the best,

Mike Salemi

name: Email #1: What You Need to Know
text:
Hello {first_name},

 

Congratulations on starting Kettlebell Lifestyle! This program is designed to be different from most training plans. Usually, most plans are exclusively focused on the sets and reps, but if you want your whole body to be strong and feel great, you’ll need more. 

 

While working muscles hard can deliver clear feedback in the form of sore muscles, it isn't the most important thing. In fact, the more important progress comes when you learn to feel the effect of your training on your energy levels, movement abilities, level of fitness, and overall health.  

 

Here are some of the features of Kettlebell Lifestyle (KBL) designed to help you improve performance by learning to notice and cultivate what makes sustainable performance possible. 

 

Onboarding Questions  

These 12 questions will place you into the appropriate level. Pay attention to the questions because they are written to help you gain awareness around your current level. Then keep your eye out for the weekly bonus material sent by email each week. Some of the bonus topics are sure to address issues the onboarding questions bring up.

 

*Note about shift workers and trainers

Shift workers will likely need to use the Self-Guided route due to their schedule and the demands of shift work on your body as opposed to immersion. 
Trainers with high levels of physical experience may prefer the Self Guided route as opposed to Immersion.

 

Daily Training Readiness Assessment

Each day you’ll be prompted to answer 5 questions that gauge how ready your body is for the stress of training. The importance of adjusting your training based on how your body feels is one of the biggest keys to longevity. 

 

Your answers will customize the volume (namely sets) of your training for the day. 

 

*Note:

The personalized changes for your training plan show up in the written workout located under the guided workout video.

 

The table below reflects 100% volume:


 

The table below reflects reduced volume by reducing the number of sets:


 

The video workout will always shows the workout with 100% volume for someone who was feeling great that day. Look at your chart and follow your personalized workout.

While working muscles hard can deliver clear feedback in the form of sore muscles, it isn't the most important thing. In fact, the more important progress comes when you learn to feel the effect of your training on your energy levels, movement abilities, level of fitness, and overall health.  

 

Here are some of the features of Kettlebell Lifestyle (KBL) designed to help you improve performance by learning to notice and cultivate what makes sustainable performance possible. 

 

Onboarding Questions  

These 12 questions will place you into the appropriate level. Pay attention to the questions because they are written to help you gain awareness around your current level. Then keep your eye out for the weekly bonus material sent by email each week. Some of the bonus topics are sure to address issues the onboarding questions bring up.

 

*Note about shift workers and trainers

  • Shift workers will likely need to use the Self-Guided route due to their schedule and the demands of shift work on your body as opposed to immersion. 
  • Trainers with high levels of physical experience may prefer the Self Guided route as opposed to Immersion.

 

Daily Training Readiness Assessment

Each day you’ll be prompted to answer 5 questions that gauge how ready your body is for the stress of training. The importance of adjusting your training based on how your body feels is one of the biggest keys to longevity. 

 

Your answers will customize the volume (namely sets) of your training for the day.

name: Email #7: The Power of Play
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Play is the best way to teach your body how to move. 

 

It doesn’t matter if you’re a kid or an adult, playing is powerful. Playing is the state of mind when you are simply enjoying what you’re doing.

 

Adults are the worst at play, but the time you invest into training can be even more valuable by approaching it with play. 

  

Today, Brooks Meadows (former owner of the gym Recess, which was designed around play!) helps we adults recalibrate to versions of ourselves that have more fun. 

 

1. What is play?

2. Why is play important?

3. How can we do it?

 

Click here to watch the full video.

 

Have a great day!

Mike

name: Email #9: Lizzy Smith's Story
text:
Hi {first_name},

 

Skill development days are important.

 

Training should make your body smarter. When done properly, training allows you to teach your body to move with more fluidity as well as strength. The more ways your body practices stringing together movements, the better you can navigate the unpredictable nature of life. 

 

This week brings you the real life inspiring story of  para-olympic athlete, Lizzy Smith. Lizzy has one prosthetic arm and competes in the 100m Freestyle, 100m Backstroke, 100m Butterfly, and 200m IM events.

 

Watch this 3 minute video to see how the Weck method skills taught in KBL have been helpful for Lizzy’s performance and can help you too. 

 

Click here to watch the full video.

 

Wishing you all the best,

Mike

name: Email 1
text:
Hi,

 

Congratulations on completing your kettlebell generator and uncovering which three kettlebells to start with.

 

Weight number one is a great choice when first getting familiar with classic kettlebell movements, as well as developing a good base level of skill.

 

Weight number two is great for most upper body lifts, as well as progressing beyond your suggested weight (number one), more focused on technique development.

 

Weight number three is excellent for lower body lifts, as well as more strength development once you've established a foundational level of proficiency.

 

If you’re only going to buy one weight, I recommend getting #2. 

 

If you get 2 of the 3 weights, choose based on your training history. 

 

New to training with weights, go for #s 1 and 2. These two weights will allow you to develop great technique safely and you’ll get plenty of muscular challenge. 

 

Experienced with weights but new to kettlebells, I recommend going with weights 2 and 3. 

 

Stay tuned for another email that will include four tutorial videos on how to get started with the following fundamental lifts:

 

Two-Hand Deadlift
Goblet Squat
Half-Kneeling Overhead Press
Two-Hand Swing

Enjoy getting started with your kettlebells!

- Mike

name: Email 2
text:
Hello {first_name}, 

 

Burning calories is easy. 

 

Getting yourself tired and sore is easy. 

 

Training - actual training - takes insight into how the body works and recovers. 

 

When I was in my teens and early 20s, I was a competitive powerlifter and I trained incredibly hard for that goal.

 

It was tough training, BUT longevity and feeling good were not part of the plan...and I paid for it with injuries as a result.

 

It was once I began competing in Kettlebell Sport that I chased down information on how to have both performance and longevity.

 

This information is how I was able to keep competing and win. It’s how I was able to turn training stress into positive adaptation.

There are TONS of benefits to exercise…however, an essential part to not forget is this - recovery. 

 

I have a simple idea: by focusing on consistency, technique, AND recovery you can be as much of a badass as you want without the wear and tear that is standard in today’s fitness culture. 

 

Stick around and I’ll keep sending you the information you need to get what you want out of training.

Access the workout here. 
 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

Hello {first_name},

 

Did you know that people who forage for wild foods and herbs will take some from an area, but they’ll be careful to leave plenty behind so there will be great harvests year after year?

 

There are many parallels here with regards to our fitness....

 

Your body is its own ecosystem. If you deplete its energy week after week, it won’t be able to produce like it could before. 

 

But if you harvest responsibly, you’ll have energy whenever you need it. 

 

That’s why I choose to workout intelligently and methodically, because it means I’ll be able to push it - whenever I want or need to. 

 

So what exactly goes into well-rounded workouts (regardless of your goal) so you can stay strong and feel great for decades instead of just your 20s? 

 

 

The 4 Elements of Well-Rounded Training

 

The exercises, weights, and volume will change based on your goal, however the fundamentals stay the same. 

 

Personalization 

At its core, personalization is about taking responsibility for your continued progress. You learn what signs and symptoms to pay attention to and how to modify training so that your training stress doesn’t overtake your ability to recover. Learning to see how life outside the gym affects your training AND exactly how to adjust your training to continue to make progress is key.  

 

Preparation: A Core Temperature & Joint Warm Up

Warm ups are hugely underrated. A core temperature warm up gradually raises body temperature, circulating blood from the heart to the tissues, generating warmth, as well as exercising the respiratory system. 

 

A quality joint warm up prepares the proprioceptors (directly tied to the intelligence of your tissues such as ligaments and promotes body awareness) and triggers your joints to release synovial fluid (joint lubricant). In addition, we use movements to increase specific body control and range of motion where one part of the body is fixed, (for example the lower body) while another part (upper body in this case) is performing more targeted movements. 

 

The spine and ribs have tons of small muscles, tendons, ligaments and joints. If these joints are tight they essentially get "bound" together, leading to compensations. In regular English, your body will allow you to get your arms over your head even if doing so is like running your car without oil. The joint warm up keeps these joints and tissues from being stiff and bound up which means you’ll feel better and move better. 

 

This does not take but a few minutes to perform and will pay you dividends if you perform it consistently.

 

Skill Based Training

In my programs, proper biomechanics, methodical progressions, and the integration of the nervous system are how I develop skill. You’ll not only train strength, you’ll practice the skill of being strong with precision and accuracy. 

 

Knowing the feel of proper biomechanics and honing the ability to express strength with precision enables effective transfer to other tools and other sports. Not to mention that being skilled in your movement avoids unnecessary wear and tear on your body. 

 

Recovery & Cool Down

After your workout you have the opportunity to guide your body from the stress and sympathetic state (fight or flight) of training to one that is more parasympathetic (rest & digest) where you can recover. The more time you spend in recovery mode, the better your results will be. 

 

The tight, achy bodies so many people have is because they haven’t learned how to bring their bodies back to a more de-stressed baseline. The emphasis on breathing, working in, skill development days, and targeted stretches are all part of cooling down and bringing your body into balance. 

 

Maybe you're saying, "Mike…I don’t have time for all that."

 

Including each of these 4 elements into your training is what makes the difference between someone looking back on their glory days and someone else who is a badass throughout the aging process. 

 

     Strong and energetic in my 80’s…yes, please. 

     Strong and energetic now…of course. 

 

In Kettlebell Lifestyle, there are follow-along videos for each one of these aspects. Doing the warmup all the way through to cool down, i.e. all 4 elements, only takes 40 mins to 1 hour, that's it.

 

Include these 4 elements and it doesn’t matter which style of training you like. Bodybuilding, kettlebells, powerlifting, Olympic lifting, CrossFit, endurance sports, whatever…these 4 elements will keep you going. 

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi 

 

P.S. Kettlebell Lifestyle has follow-along videos for each of these 4 elements for each workout day. By the end of the program, you will have these elements so ingrained that you won’t have to think about them. You’ll know how to warm up, personalize, develop skill, and decompress. Here’s to a lifetime of being strong and energetic!

 

 

In case you were curious...

LIFETIME ACCESS to a 9 week, follow along video program. I spent months testing and tweaking these workouts and how you progress from one phase to the next. One time through is great, but repeating the program (and charting your continued progress) is even better. There are 9 weeks of training included for beginners, and 9 weeks for the intermediate level. 

 

On Ramp

Build your energy stores to set yourself up for progress while getting familiar with the platform.

 

Phase 1  

Bring up weak points and create a strong foundation.

 

Phase 2 

Layer in skill development with more dynamic movements to increase conditioning.

 

Phase 3 

This phase is performance using more rotation with challenging workouts to emphasize strength, speed, mobility, coordination, strength endurance, power, and more.

Hello {first_name},

 

It's a fact of life that we can’t give what we don’t have, or fully benefit from working out when we don’t have the energy to recover. 

 

Movement as a whole is great for the body. Challenging training, however, I believe must be adjusted based on what is going on in your life and how you feel. 

 

Poor night of sleep, emotional exhaustion, recovering from being sick, physically exhausted…there is so much more outside of the gym. 

 

One of the most important principles in training is how to adjust your workouts to fit how you show up that day. I cannot overemphasize how important this personalization is if you want great results for decades. 

 

The Quick and Easy Way to Check in With Your Body

 

In Kettlebell Lifestyle, I use 5 questions to help you scan your body and get real information on your training readiness for the day:

 

Did I wake up today feeling tired, honestly?
How recovered does my body feel following the prior workout?
Did I wake up with water retention, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation?
My overall stress level today is?
My willingness and motivation level for training today is?

Based on your answers, your workout automatically adjusts the training volume for your session that day. I will include a snapshot below of one modified workout.

 

Feeling Good

 

*In this example, the “sets” column shows full volume


 

Feeling OK

 

 


*In this example, the “sets” column has changed, reducing the total volume 


 

Feeling Beat Down

 


*In this final example, the workout is paused ( you will have a personalized stretching program as well as active meditation option instead ) and you won’t miss a thing when you come back to training the next time

 

Movement everyday is medicine for your body, and adjusting how you train based on an honest assessment of how you feel is true wisdom. 

 

Properly warming up, adequate technique covering the primary movement patterns, and cooling down are super important, but I say the skill of knowing when and how to adjust your training based on how you feel is the PRIMARY skill for training longevity. 

 

Start checking in with yourself and adjust your training accordingly, and watch what happens ; )

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

text:
Hello ____,

 

Watching gymnasts is amazing. They make everything look easy which is funny because what they are doing is incredibly difficult. 

 

Watching the men on the rings hold an Iron Cross - common in the gymnastics world - has made many of us men feel like we can pull that move off no problem…only to find how difficult it is. 

 

No gymnastics coach ever got a beginner gymnast and told them to go do an Iron Cross. Instead, they worked on progressions to the point where holding an Iron Cross was possible. 

 

Kettlebell Lifestyle follows the same principle. 

 

Lay the foundation > build > perform 

 

Here’s an example straight from the course:

 

Track 1 (Beginner)

 

Side of hip raises
 

Static alternating side lunge

 

 

Alternating halo side lunge combo

 

Explanation:

The glute medius is targeted in the Side of Hip Raises which is important to stabilize the hip in single leg and lateral movement. Essential for ANYTHING athletic. The Static Alternating Side Lunge moves from an isolated movement to an integrated movement.  The Alternating Halo Side Lunge Combo adds weight, integrates the upper and lower body, becomes more dynamic, trains balance, coordination, timing etc.

Track 2 (Intermediate)

 

Hand to Hand Swing

 

Single Arm Clean

 

RMT Clean

Watching gymnasts is amazing. They make everything look easy which is a paradox, because what they are doing is incredibly difficult. 

 

For example, watching men on the rings hold an Iron Cross (a movement fairly common in the gymnastics world) - may have made many of us men feel like we can pull a move off like that…only to find out when we try at our local neighborhood park, how wildly difficult it is LOL.

 

No gymnastics coach ever told their athlete to go do an Iron Cross as a beginner. Instead, they worked on progressions sustained over time, to the point where holding an Iron Cross was possible. 

 

Kettlebell Lifestyle follows the same essentail principle. 

 

Lay the Foundation > Build > Perform > Sustain

 

Here’s an example straight from the course illustrating a basic progression (I will explain further as you read on):

 

LEVEL 1 (Beginner Track)

Side of Hip Raises


Static Alternating Side Lunge

Alternating Halo Side Lunge Combo

 

Progression Explained:

The glute medius is targeted in the Side of Hip Raises which is important to stabilize the hip in single leg and lateral movement. Essential for ANYTHING athletic. The Static Alternating Side Lunge moves from an isolated movement to an integrated movement.  The Alternating Halo Side Lunge Combo adds weight, integrates the upper and lower body, becomes more dynamic, trains balance, coordination, timing, etc.

 

 

LEVEL 2 (Intermediate Track)

Hand to Hand Swing

 

Single Arm Clean

 

RMT (Rotational Movement Training) Clean

Progression Explained:

The Swing itself is a ballistic hinge movement and is the basis of many advanced movements in Kettlebell lifting. Adding the Hand to Hand Swing is a ballistic hinge movement that works coordination, gets you comfortable with timing, and works single-arm training in preparation for the Clean. The Clean is a BIG step in integrating the upper and lower body and a chance to practice "hand insertion". The RMT (rotational movement) Clean takes each of these elements up a notch with more rotation, coordination, timing, and significantly more integration between the upper and lower body.

 

The Bottom Line

 

Progressions yield better results, period. Even if you are already strong and used to tough workouts, following a progression rather than just diving in the deep end works better in the long-run - trust me.

 

Combine intelligent recovery with progressions and you have…Kettlebell Lifestyle. 

 

Try the free follow-along workout from KBL today (if you haven’t already) and see if KBL is a fit for you. If it is, click here and use the code KBRoadmap for $100 off. 

 

Train Intentionally,

Mike Salemi

Hello {first_name},

 

Movement is good for everybody. 

 

This is not a controversial statement.

 

Add to that the idea of “use it or lose it” and it’s even more obvious why some sort of movement practice is not just helpful, but necessary if you want to live to your full human potential. 

 

Thousands of years ago consistent movement was baked into everyday life. There was ZERO need to think about it for most people just like most of us don’t have to think about going to work. It’s how we survive so we do it. 

 

That said, many of us get bogged down on what kind of exercise to do. 

 

So how do you choose what type of exercise?

 

One way is to look around at what other people do and see how their results are.

 

          Some are committed to heavy weights, often done at commercial gyms.

          Then there are endurance activities like cycling, running, swimming, etc. 

          CrossFit is another popular style of mixed training.

          At-home bodyweight focused training is common as well.

 

Now take a closer look. Regardless of the type of exercise someone enjoys, the people who are able to keep it up for years have one thing in common -  they know how to recover. 

 

Recovery is the key.

 

Without recovery you’ll end up an achy, injured, stiff person who has more trouble getting around and doing normal activities. Interestingly, that’s true whether someone trains a lot before their body gives out or doesn’t train at all and loses it through lack of use. 

 

Here’s the point, if you learn how to build recovery into your training, you are golden REGARDLESS of the type of training you find enjoyable. 

 

Powerlifting
Olympic lifting
Bodyweight training
Biking
Swimming
Long walks on the beach
Kettlebells
Bodybuilding
Running
Martial arts or MMA

All of these (and others) are great. You should perform the type of exercise you enjoy…as long as you recover from it.

 

Kettlebell Lifestyle is a roughly 9 week program (it can be longer depending on how you use it, and it’s perfect for going through the program multiple times) that ingrains recovery principles into you. 

 

By the end of the program you’ll know what to do so your body can recover and positively adapt to whatever form of training you choose to do. 

 

“Before I used to be a basketball player, tennis player in high school and college. Very athletic and mobile. After that I started doing strength training and I was actually more restrictive in some areas…I wasn’t as able to move as quickly as I used to. With Kettlebell Lifestyle, mobility flexibility strength training, conditioning…my lifts are more explosive and I feel more dynamic.” 

-John N.

 

“I’ve never really come across a program that is so versatile: that you can do multiple times, that you can approach different ways, that literally is tailored toward how you’re feeling that day and what type of training that your body and your mind are capable of in that moment.”

-Taylor Laforce

-Wade Bruffey

Hi {first_name},

 

I’ve done many workouts in my life...workouts where my whole body felt CRUSHED. Often times, these workouts took so much energy that it took me a week to return to feeling half-way decent.

 

While I do like to challenge myself, I have learned there can be a better way to sustain progress for the long run and have fun along the way. 

 

With the principles I used in developing Kettlebell Lifestyle, people will often experience a new post-workout feel. I often hear they actually forget they had a workout because, rather than feeling depleted, they feel amazing.

 

It’s not like the workout was easy. In fact, sometimes the next day they'll be quite sore, BUT that deep feeling of being crushed just isn’t there. 

 

There’s the old phrase “work smarter not harder.” It’s good advice. 

 

The thing is, hard work can feel great. 

 

Hard work is necessary sometimes, so I don’t like to pit the two against each other. Instead, I like to work more intelligently so that my body is ready, willing, and able to work hard whenever I need or want to. 

 

The secret sauce is combining recovery into your training. 

 

You don’t have to do years of research and get certifications.. 

 

All you have to do is follow along...

 

Over the course of Kettlebell Lifestyle you’ll end up memorizing the recovery tactics I use. It will be second nature for you to incorporate them into your training. 

 

Your body is sophisticated.
Your training should be sophisticated too…
It should, however, also be easy to follow.

And there you have Kettlebell Lifestyle in a nutshell. An easy-to-follow program that will teach you the skills to blend training with recovery. You’ll get better results and feel better. That is my promise.

Hi {first_name},


I'd like to personally welcome you to the inner circle team : )


Here is where I provide valuable information designed to help you progress towards mastering the kettlebell, and also becoming a higher performer in many aspects of life. 


I'll be sharing tips that have helped me become a sought-after performance coach, as well as create the lifestyle I’ve dreamed of for years.

What I've learned has helped me attract more of the right clients, retain existing clients, deliver results, and develop strategies to earn more while working less.


I’m truly excited that you’re joining me in this journey to not only uncover things that can scale your training skills, but also business too.


…as I've learned from many successes and failures the dedicated work it takes to develop a long-lasting coaching business.




That's why I'm excited to share more useful information with you in the next couple of days.


Be sure to look out for my next email coming tomorrow.


Thank you and welcome to the team once again,

Mike Salemi

name: Email 2
text:
Hi {first_name},


As a trainer, I recall experiencing many challenges early on, and sometimes I can't believe the road it's taken to finally get here.




It's humbling looking back, and today when I see another trainers and coaches struggling with similar challenges, I can relate.

And when I say “struggling”, some of the problems I faced involved:




Attracting the right clients
How to consistently deliver more value to existing clients 
Solving complex cases
Being better with time management skills 
Learning to take care of my own health first, especially when having to work long hours




In fact, in more times than I'd like to admit, my efforts to grow my business in those days felt like I was running into a wall at times. 


Looking back I realize I was lacking clarity around my overarching dream, who I was serving, and how I could serve them best. Progress therefore felt as if  it was happening at a snail's pace, and each day felt like I was stuck living out the same routine. 


I remember putting tons of energy into the business. But still, it wasn’t giving me the outcome I desired.


After years of hard work, I understood these key components to success - aligning every part of your being with purpose, and taking care of your body so you can foster a healthier mindset is critical. With these things, I believe it is possible to achieve nearly anything. 


In my experience, these elements are also intimately connected to self-confidence. In order to grow this confidence as a trainer (once clear on why, who you're serving, how you'll serve them, and with the vitality to do all this well), in my opinion, the priority should be to master a skill set that delivers unprecedented results to these clients you seek to help.

 
If you're reading this email, more than likely you are interested in kettlebell training for health and performance - whether you are a trainer or simply an avid fitness enthusiast. With this in mind, I've created a special program for you to learn at a high-level just about everything there is to know about kettlebell training.


In my Mastering the Kettlebell Program I give you a road map on how to move step-by-step towards mastering this incredible tool (for developing strength, power, endurance, flexibility, and coordination) to become a true leader in fitness and performance training.


Developing the authentic knowledge and experience that went into it wasn't easy. In fact, for a number of reasons I almost quit, many times...but I'm forever grateful that I didn't because after so many trials and errors I finally created something that changed the game for me as a teacher and the results of my clients. 


Once I got to a place where I felt I had enough real world knowledge and application that I could deliver everyday at the highest level, more devoted clients started seeking me out for training. Life started becoming more and more interesting and enjoyable.  


Are you interested in achieving similar, or even better results?


If so, then wait for my email tomorrow. In it, I’m going to show you exactly how you can do it!


Regards,
Mike Salemi

name: Email 3
text:
Hi {first_name},




I can’t believe I’m going to share this with you…

So, essentially I’ve been through just about every kettlebell system out there, and early on I allowed myself to fall into the belief that each one was the only way to achieve the highest performance possible. All too often I would follow blindly what other so-called leaders would say and completely disregard my own inner voice and felt experience. 

I won’t say they did not provide good value, it’s just that in my experience they were very geared towards one main objective, and not utilizing the kettlebell to its fullest potential.

What I found after more than a handful of kettlebell certifications, training a ton myself, and working with respected coaches during this time, was that when seeking to develop high levels of power and strength with a kettlebell, there is a specific technique that is optimal.

On the other hand, when seeking to develop respectable levels of strength-endurance it's all about energetic efficiency, and there's in fact another, contrasting technique style that is more favorable. 

Without getting too technical, what I discovered when diving into these new ways to lift a kettlebell, my mind opened - helping me tremendously during my early development.

BUT I was still craving more, and knew I needed to level-up in order to distinguish myself as a real leader in the kettlebell industry beyond any one system or school of thought. 




Years went by, I kept on learning and refining my training techniques and application.

And then around this time I discovered Kettlebell Sport and started competing.

But everything was taken to an entirely new level when I went to the birthplace of Kettlebell training, Russia, and trained with members of the Russian National Team.

That’s when it hit me, there’s a lot more to kettlebell training, than I ever expected and had studied to that point.

I started discovering a level of depth to kettlebell training that was barely available in United States at the time.

I spent countless hours training and trying to reach the elite ranking in kettlebell sport, a ranking called “Master of Sport” but fell short competition after competition. 

The reason for my shortcoming as an athlete was not due to lack of effort but rather an injury to my left forearm that no practitioner/therapist could figure out.

After over three years of exhausting everything possible to remedy the loss of feeling and swelling that would occur in my left forearm, forcing me to set the kettlebells down during any hard effort in competition or training - I started working with Holistic Health Practitioner and rehab specialist Paul Chek.

During 2.5 years of dedicated work with Paul, I truly came to understand how complex and integrated the human body is. The rehab process involved everything from balancing my physical body to my mental-emotional self-management.




The ultimate goal was to achieve lifelong high performance, injury-free and all while loving the process.

And then finally…

I achieved the ranking “Master of Sport” in the Long Cycle event (Double 32kg Clean and Jerks in 10 minutes, performed continuously). Hi {first_name},


I can’t believe I’m going to share this with you…

So, essentially I’ve been through just about every kettlebell system out there, and early on I allowed myself to fall into the belief that each one was the only way to achieve the highest performance possible. All too often I would follow blindly what other so-called leaders would say and completely disregard my own inner voice and felt experience. 

I won’t say they did not provide good value, it’s just that in my experience they were very geared towards one main objective, and not utilizing the kettlebell to its fullest potential.

What I found after more than a handful of kettlebell certifications, training a ton myself, and working with respected coaches during this time, was that when seeking to develop high levels of power and strength with a kettlebell, there is a specific technique that is optimal.

On the other hand, when seeking to develop respectable levels of strength-endurance it's all about energetic efficiency, and there's in fact another, contrasting technique style that is more favorable. 

Without getting too technical, what I discovered when diving into these new ways to lift a kettlebell, my mind opened - helping me tremendously during my early development.

BUT I was still craving more, and knew I needed to level-up in order to distinguish myself as a real leader in the kettlebell industry beyond any one system or school of thought. 


Years went by, I kept on learning and refining my training techniques and application.

And then around this time I discovered Kettlebell Sport and started competing.

But everything was taken to an entirely new level when I went to the birthplace of Kettlebell training, Russia, and trained with members of the Russian National Team.

That’s when it hit me, there’s a lot more to kettlebell training, than I ever expected and had studied to that point.

I started discovering a level of depth to kettlebell training that was barely available in United States at the time.

I spent countless hours training and trying to reach the elite ranking in kettlebell sport, a ranking called “Master of Sport” but fell short competition after competition. 

The reason for my shortcoming as an athlete was not due to lack of effort but rather an injury to my left forearm that no practitioner/therapist could figure out.

After over three years of exhausting everything possible to remedy the loss of feeling and swelling that would occur in my left forearm, forcing me to set the kettlebells down during any hard effort in competition or training - I started working with Holistic Health Practitioner and rehab specialist Paul Chek.

During 2.5 years of dedicated work with Paul, I truly came to understand how complex and integrated the human body is. The rehab process involved everything from balancing my physical body to my mental-emotional self-management.


The ultimate goal was to achieve lifelong high performance, injury-free and all while loving the process.

And then finally…

I achieved the ranking “Master of Sport” in the Long Cycle event (Double 32kg Clean and Jerks in 10 minutes, performed continuously). More recently, also "Master of Sport" in Biathlon (Snatching 10 minutes and Jerking 10 minutes continuously) becoming one of only approximately six Americans to do so in both categories in the professional 32 kg kettlebell division.

text:
Laying the necessary foundation for all ballistic movements







The Deadlift

The deadlift is one of the most integral components to successful kettlebell lifting. Learning to hinge while maintaining proper spinal alignment via a stable core, not only makes this movement excellent on its own, but also magnifies its importance as a prerequisite heading into dynamic ballistic lifts such as swings, cleans and snatches.




In this section you'll be taken through a guided series of pre-checks to help you identifying any movement limitations that may exist, as well as how to address them yourself. Then, enjoy progressing into the loaded two hand deadlift. Continue onward and you'll further develop your coach's eye as we look at some of the most common errors on this lift and how to solve them. Lastly, we'll explore together a variety of deadlift variations that are presented in increasing level of difficulty and complexity. Oh, and if you're curious about programming, go to the "Tips for Training" section tab where you'll find helpful information. 




As a bonus, I've also included an additional section on the Single Arm Single Leg Deadlift. Single leg balance, pelvis, and core stability through this bend pattern movement transfers well into many work and sport environments. It's in fact a movement that shows up in many of my one-on-one client programs as well.

name: Email 3
text:
The most iconic of all kettlebell movements 

The Swing




The kettlebell swing has to be the single most common movement that people think of when it comes to kettlebells, and for good reason. Due to the unique construction of the kettlebell, this tool is perfect for maximizing repetitive ballistic lifts and powerfully conditioning the entire body!




What few people know, however is that there are in fact two broad classifications of swing techniques - one you can think of as what would be needed to develop a fast sprinter, and the other related to what would be needed to train a strong 800 meter, or longer distance runner.




The first video, Choosing Your Swing Technique, aims to explain the main differences between these two, and where I suggest starting your journey. Don't over think it though, the most important thing is to start laying down reps and get started right away!




Depending on which technique you chose, you'll first head into the Pre-Checks section, similar to what you experienced with the deadlift section, except now with application and additional information geared towards the kettlebell swing. Following the pre-check section, you'll be taken into progressions for the loaded kettlebell swing (again separated by specific technique - either Russian or Pendulum).




Within the common errors section, I've explained in detail the most frequent mistakes that relate to both swing types. You will see the main tutorial related to the more popular Russian Swing, and then I provide an additionally videos demonstrating the what the Pendulum version would look like as well. 




Lastly, we go into kettlebell swing variations related to each technique. As you develop your coach's eye and experience under the bells, the difference between these two should look, and more importantly feel very different. I hope you'll enjoy these sections.




When it comes to programming, don't forget to check out the "Tips for Training" section. Here you'll find tons of helpful tips, as well as a done-for-you program unique to each swing technique.

name: Email 4
text:
A fantastic lower and upper body integrated movement

The Clean




The kettlebell clean is the movement where we truly start integrating the lower and upper body. This lift tends to give beginners the most trouble due to a new technical element being introduced called "hand insertion" - where the hand fully inserts through the kettlebell window as we enter the rack position. Often times when done incorrectly, the kettlebell will painfully bang on-top of the forearms. Step-by-step you'll learn helpful progressions to expedite the learning curve; just remember that learning a new skill like this takes time. Trust the process and it will get smoother and smoother, I promise!




This section is laid out similarly to our prior swing section and begins with a Choosing your Clean Technique video. In general, I suggest continuing on with the same technique (Russian or Pendulum) as you utilize during the swing section to keep things simple and consistent for the time being. Following this section are clean pre-checks, progressing into the loaded clean, common errors, variations, and programming tips for training unique to each technique. 




If you happened to skip straight to this section when opening the program, I highly suggest watching the Choosing your Clean video first. It will put into context and guide you best especially as you move through all the ballistic movements - swings, cleans and, snatches.

name: Email 5
text:
Where technical mastery shines




The Snatch




The kettlebell snatch is often viewed as the most technical of all classical kettlebell lifts, and you're about to about to learn why in this section. That's not said to discourage you by any means, but rather to tell you honestly that even in my own training and with my most dedicated students, this is one particular lift that I feel never ceases to leave room for improvement. It is for this reason, the process of continually becoming a more technical, powerful, and well rounded lifter, that I LOVE the snatch and I hope you will too! 




Grip, cardio, leg development, back development, and more are all tested and conditioned during this fantastic movement. You can think of the snatch as a clean, only to a higher destination point. Thus, if you really practice your cleans in the prior section (especially with regards to "hand insertion") it will pay off here. 




This section begins with a Choosing your Snatch Technique video. Just like the clean, and in general, I suggest continuing on with the same technique (Russian or Pendulum) as utilized from the clean and swing sections for consistency purposes when learning. Following this section are snatch pre-checks, progressing into the loaded snatch, common errors, variations, and programming tips for training unique to each snatch technique.

name: Email 6
text:
Where strength and power meet

Overhead Press and Jerk




The standing overhead strict press is one of the best upper body strength builders you can do with a kettlebell, and is the path I highly recommend starting first prior to jerks. Once your overhead press is rock solid, we'll take this strength base, and ramp up the athleticism to a high degree increasing the speed of movement, as well as incorporate a quick change of direction with the jerk.




The construction of the kettlebell, with its offset center of mass, makes it a very special training tool to use when performing overhead lifts in particular. You may find the way you grip the kettlebell and position it to be more ergonomic for the wrist than for instance a barbell or dumbbell - not to mention with a good portion of the mass of the kettlebell concentrated behind the forearm, it can also help you enter a more well aligned overhead shoulder/arm position.




The overhead press and jerk are complete with their own progressions, common error sections, variations, and programming tips for training.

text:
Complexity with strength and grace

Turkish Get Up




Next to the kettlebell swing, the Turkish Get Up is arguably the lift that people love most in kettlebell training. It is a full body movement that trains pressing, rotation, bending, and lunging, AND involves all three planes of movement - sagittal (front-to-back), frontal (side-to-side), and transverse (rotation). If there was ever a total body big-bang kettlebell exercise it is this. 




Due to its complexity, there is a tremendous amount of information you are going to learn about yourself and gain from practicing this movement. To start, you'll be taken through the pre-check section, progressions into the bodyweight and loaded movement (along with bonus videos like a neat challenge!), common errors, variations and programming tips for training.




As an added bonus, included is another movement (the windmill), with full video and text breakdowns. The kettlebell windmill is not only an excellent movement for functional core stability, but also it trains the shoulder and hip complex like no other!




Have fun enjoying this movement and the associated sections in the program.

name: Email 2
text:
Laying the necessary foundation for all ballistic movements







The Deadlift

The deadlift is one of the most integral components to successful kettlebell lifting. Learning to hinge while maintaining proper spinal alignment via a stable core, not only makes this movement excellent on its own, but also magnifies its importance as a prerequisite heading into dynamic ballistic lifts such as swings, cleans and snatches.




In this section you'll be taken through a guided series of pre-checks to help you identifying any movement limitations that may exist, as well as how to address them yourself. Then, enjoy progressing into the loaded two hand deadlift. Continue onward and you'll further develop your coach's eye as we look at some of the most common errors on this lift and how to solve them. Lastly, we'll explore together a variety of deadlift variations that are presented in increasing level of difficulty and complexity. Oh, and if you're curious about programming, go to the "Tips for Training" section tab where you'll find helpful information. 




As a bonus, I've also included an additional section on the Single Arm Single Leg Deadlift. Single leg balance, pelvis, and core stability through this bend pattern movement transfers well into many work and sport environments. It's in fact a movement that shows up in many of my one-on-one client programs as well.

name: Email 3
text:
The most iconic of all kettlebell movements 

The Swing




The kettlebell swing has to be the single most common movement that people think of when it comes to kettlebells, and for good reason. Due to the unique construction of the kettlebell, this tool is perfect for maximizing repetitive ballistic lifts and powerfully conditioning the entire body!




What few people know, however is that there are in fact two broad classifications of swing techniques - one you can think of as what would be needed to develop a fast sprinter, and the other related to what would be needed to train a strong 800 meter, or longer distance runner.




The first video, Choosing Your Swing Technique, aims to explain the main differences between these two, and where I suggest starting your journey. Don't over think it though, the most important thing is to start laying down reps and get started right away!




Depending on which technique you chose, you'll first head into the Pre-Checks section, similar to what you experienced with the deadlift section, except now with application and additional information geared towards the kettlebell swing. Following the pre-check section, you'll be taken into progressions for the loaded kettlebell swing (again separated by specific technique - either Russian or Pendulum).




Within the common errors section, I've explained in detail the most frequent mistakes that relate to both swing types. You will see the main tutorial related to the more popular Russian Swing, and then I provide an additionally videos demonstrating the what the Pendulum version would look like as well. 




Lastly, we go into kettlebell swing variations related to each technique. As you develop your coach's eye and experience under the bells, the difference between these two should look, and more importantly feel very different. I hope you'll enjoy these sections.




When it comes to programming, don't forget to check out the "Tips for Training" section. Here you'll find tons of helpful tips, as well as a done-for-you program unique to each swing technique.

name: Email 4
text:
A fantastic lower and upper body integrated movement

The Clean




The kettlebell clean is the movement where we truly start integrating the lower and upper body. This lift tends to give beginners the most trouble due to a new technical element being introduced called "hand insertion" - where the hand fully inserts through the kettlebell window as we enter the rack position. Often times when done incorrectly, the kettlebell will painfully bang on-top of the forearms. Step-by-step you'll learn helpful progressions to expedite the learning curve; just remember that learning a new skill like this takes time. Trust the process and it will get smoother and smoother, I promise!




This section is laid out similarly to our prior swing section and begins with a Choosing your Clean Technique video. In general, I suggest continuing on with the same technique (Russian or Pendulum) as you utilize during the swing section to keep things simple and consistent for the time being. Following this section are clean pre-checks, progressing into the loaded clean, common errors, variations, and programming tips for training unique to each technique. 




If you happened to skip straight to this section when opening the program, I highly suggest watching the Choosing your Clean video first. It will put into context and guide you best especially as you move through all the ballistic movements - swings, cleans and, snatches.

text:
Where technical mastery shines




The Snatch




The kettlebell snatch is often viewed as the most technical of all classical kettlebell lifts, and you're about to about to learn why in this section. That's not said to discourage you by any means, but rather to tell you honestly that even in my own training and with my most dedicated students, this is one particular lift that I feel never ceases to leave room for improvement. It is for this reason, the process of continually becoming a more technical, powerful, and well rounded lifter, that I LOVE the snatch and I hope you will too! 




Grip, cardio, leg development, back development, and more are all tested and conditioned during this fantastic movement. You can think of the snatch as a clean, only to a higher destination point. Thus, if you really practice your cleans in the prior section (especially with regards to "hand insertion") it will pay off here. 




This section begins with a Choosing your Snatch Technique video. Just like the clean, and in general, I suggest continuing on with the same technique (Russian or Pendulum) as utilized from the clean and swing sections for consistency purposes when learning. Following this section are snatch pre-checks, progressing into the loaded snatch, common errors, variations, and programming tips for training unique to each snatch technique.

text:
Where strength and power meet

Overhead Press and Jerk




The standing overhead strict press is one of the best upper body strength builders you can do with a kettlebell, and is the path I highly recommend starting first prior to jerks. Once your overhead press is rock solid, we'll take this strength base, and ramp up the athleticism to a high degree increasing the speed of movement, as well as incorporate a quick change of direction with the jerk.




The construction of the kettlebell, with its offset center of mass, makes it a very special training tool to use when performing overhead lifts in particular. You may find the way you grip the kettlebell and position it to be more ergonomic for the wrist than for instance a barbell or dumbbell - not to mention with a good portion of the mass of the kettlebell concentrated behind the forearm, it can also help you enter a more well aligned overhead shoulder/arm position.




The overhead press and jerk are complete with their own progressions, common error sections, variations, and programming tips for training.

Where strength and power meet

​Overhead Press and Jerk

The standing overhead strict press is one of the best upper body strength builders you can do with a kettlebell, and is the path I highly recommend starting first prior to jerks. Once your overhead press is rock solid, we'll take this strength base, and ramp up the athleticism to a high degree increasing the speed of movement, as well as incorporate a quick change of direction with the jerk.


The construction of the kettlebell, with its offset center of mass, makes it a very special training tool to use when performing overhead lifts in particular. You may find the way you grip the kettlebell and position it to be more ergonomic for the wrist than for instance a barbell or dumbbell - not to mention with a good portion of the mass of the kettlebell concentrated behind the forearm, it can also help you enter a more well aligned overhead shoulder/arm position.


The overhead press and jerk are complete with their own progressions, common error sections, variations, and programming tips for training.

name: Email 7
text:
Complexity with strength and grace

Turkish Get Up




Next to the kettlebell swing, the Turkish Get Up is arguably the lift that people love most in kettlebell training. It is a full body movement that trains pressing, rotation, bending, and lunging, AND involves all three planes of movement - sagittal (front-to-back), frontal (side-to-side), and transverse (rotation). If there was ever a total body big-bang kettlebell exercise it is this. 




Due to its complexity, there is a tremendous amount of information you are going to learn about yourself and gain from practicing this movement. To start, you'll be taken through the pre-check section, progressions into the bodyweight and loaded movement (along with bonus videos like a neat challenge!), common errors, variations and programming tips for training.




As an added bonus, included is another movement (the windmill), with full video and text breakdowns. The kettlebell windmill is not only an excellent movement for functional core stability, but also it trains the shoulder and hip complex like no other!




Have fun enjoying this movement and the associated sections in the program.

name: Email 8
text:
Let's get our lower body and pulling training on!

Squatting, Lunging and Rowing




In my opinion, the squat and lunge may be two of the most underrated movements when it comes to kettlebell training. The movements patterns associated with them are absolutely critical in daily life, and in many work and sport environments - not to mention the nature of the kettlebell makes it incredibly easy to scale progressions/regressions. Whether it's by utilizing a different grip or orientation of the kettlebell, there is a ton of variety and benefits you can experience by implementing kettlebells into your lower body training. 




In the program there are complete sections on squatting, lunging, and rowing. You'll find tabs for each movement with pre-checks, progressing into loaded movements, common errors, and variations. While each of these three movements contain programming tips for training, I have written a full done-for-you program focused on the squat. This will set you up for successful squatting well into the future with many lower body movements; not to mention help you reach your performance benchmarks...stay tuned for the next email to learn more about this! ; )

text:
Let's round-out our training with these very special 


Free Bonuses





As you've seen by now, the way Mastering the Kettlebell has been designed was to provide you all the tools needed to have a truly well-rounded understanding of kettlebell training. I'm confident that the knowledge and experience gained as a result of going through this program will set you apart from 99.9% of lifters and coaches in the fitness world. 




While Mastering the Kettlebell is incredibly comprehensive, I felt I just had to give you more. Paul Chek, one of my greatest mentors and coaches, was kind enough to share an 8 part series on a fascinating topic that he calls "Working In". If you are new to this topic, it has been without a doubt the biggest "secret" I've learned over the years for long-lasting athletic performance.  Additionally, in this section you'll find a talk given by respected Upper Cervical Chiropractor and kettlebell coach Dr. Drew Vercellino, AND two more multi-part lectures on program design and posture. 




Lastly, you'll find a section titled "Performance Benchmarks". In this section are lift-specific charts categorized by gender, bodyweight, and kettlebell weight with markers to gauge your objective improvements. It may take some time, however, if you are able to complete your level 3 benchmark, you will be in a great position to take your kettlebell lifting as far as you'd like - performing a myriad of advanced lifts, and really test your grit with kettlebell challenges you may find exciting to train for in the future.




If you are a trainer looking for continuing education units, I have a great surprise for you. Very soon you'll be able to qualify for CEUs with Mastering the Kettlebell in many of the most respected Personal Training Organizations around the world. Stay tuned for an online exam coming soon you may take upon completion of the program to earn your credits.
